    pub fn set_page_mail(&mut self, f: PageMailHook) {
        self.buddies.page_mail = Some(f);
    }

    /// the messages that waited for persona `me` (lower case), for its page, and gone from the store (a sender blocked
    /// since is left out)
    fn take_page_mail(&mut self, me: &str) -> Vec<PageMail> {
        let Some(l) = self.buddies.lists.get_mut(me).filter(|l| !l.m.is_empty()) else { return Vec::new() };
        let mail = std::mem::take(&mut l.m);
        self.buddies.mail -= mail.len();
        self.buddies.mark(me);
        self.touch_lists();
        let now = self.bnow();
        mail.into_iter()
            .filter(|m| now - m.t < MAIL_DAYS * DAY_MS && !self.buddies.blocks(me, &lower(&m.from)))
            .map(|m| PageMail { from: m.from, body: m.body, t: m.t })
            .collect()
    }

    /// A friend's message of persona `mk` (lower case) that reads as a slur (nfsu2-names `chat_slur`, as the lobby's
    /// chat): it reaches no one (its sender is told it went), and the lobby's `slur_lines` of them in its
    /// `slur_window_ms` turn the persona's messages off for its `slur_mute_ms`, the log says so.  True: it reads as one
    fn msg_slur(&mut self, mk: &str, who: &str, body: &str, group: Option<&Arc<str>>) -> bool {
        let Some(word) = nfsu2_names::chat_slur(body).map(str::to_string) else { return false };
        let (now, l) = (self.bnow(), self.lobby.l);
        let (times, until) = self.buddies.msg_slurs.entry(mk.to_string()).or_default();
        let muted = l.slur_said(times, until, now);
        let off = nfsu2_util::js::number_to_string(l.slur_mute_ms / 1000.0);
        let then = if muted { format!("; messages off for {off} s") } else { String::new() };
        let word = serde_json::to_string(&word).expect("a string");
        (self.log)(&format!("[online] \"{who}\": a message with {word} in it, sent to no one{then}"), group.map(|g| &**g));
        true
    }

    /// persona `mk`'s (lower case) messages are off now (`msg_slur`)
    fn msg_muted(&mut self, mk: &str) -> bool {
        let now = self.bnow();
        let Some(x) = self.buddies.msg_slurs.get(mk) else { return false };
        if x.1 > now {
            return true;
        }
        if x.0.iter().all(|t| now - t >= self.lobby.l.slur_window_ms) {
            self.buddies.msg_slurs.remove(mk);
        }
        false
    }

    /// The page of persona `me` sends its friend `name` a message (`FriendAsk::Send`): to the friend's EA Messenger
    /// when it is logged in there, else to its pages (`PageMailHook`), else it waits (`MAIL_DAYS`).  "sent", "kept",
    /// "none" (not friends), "empty", "off" (its messages are off: `msg_slur`), "full" (no room for it to wait)
    fn page_send(&mut self, me: &str, group: &Arc<str>, name: &str, body: &str) -> &'static str {
        let (mk, k) = (lower(me), lower(name));
        let body = clean_text(body, PAGE_MSG_LEN);
        if body.is_empty() {
            return "empty";
        }
        if self.msg_muted(&mk) {
            return "off";
        }
        self.buddy_fetch(&k);
        let Some(to) = self.buddies.list(me).and_then(|l| l.b.get(&k).cloned()) else { return "none" };
        // one that reads as a slur, or to a friend that blocks the sender: its sender sees it go, nobody gets it
        if self.msg_slur(&mk, me, &body, Some(group)) || self.buddies.blocks(&k, &mk) {
            return "sent";
        }
        let now = self.bnow();
        let o = self.buddies.online.get(&k).copied().filter(|o| self.buddies.conns.get(o).is_some_and(|x| x.persona.is_some()));
        let done = if let Some(o) = o {
            let rec = fields![("USER", me), ("BODY", body.as_str()), ("SUBJ", ""), ("TYPE", "C"), ("TIME", (now / 1000.0).floor())];
            if self.bsend(o, "RECV", &rec, "").is_ok() { "sent" } else { "full" }
        } else if self.page_mail_to(&k, &PageMail { from: me.to_string(), body: body.clone(), t: now.floor() }) {
            "sent"
        } else if self.keep(&k, Mail { from: me.to_string(), body, subj: String::new(), kind: "C".into(), t: now.floor() }) {
            "kept"
        } else {
            "full"
        };
        let how = match done {
            "sent" => "got it",
            "kept" => "away, it waits",
            _ => "no room for it",
        };
        (self.log)(&format!("[online] \"{me}\" sent \"{to}\" a message ({how})"), Some(group));
        done
    }

    /// the messages that waited for persona `me` (lower case), to connection b, and gone from the store (a sender
    /// blocked since is left out)
    fn deliver_mail(&mut self, b: u64, me: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
        let Some(l) = self.buddies.lists.get_mut(me).filter(|l| !l.m.is_empty()) else { return Ok(()) };
        let mail = std::mem::take(&mut l.m);
        self.buddies.mail -= mail.len();
        self.buddies.mark(me);
        self.touch_lists();
        let now = self.bnow();
        for m in mail {
            if now - m.t >= MAIL_DAYS * DAY_MS || self.buddies.blocks(me, &lower(&m.from)) {
                continue;
            }
            let rec = fields![("USER", m.from), ("BODY", m.body), ("SUBJ", m.subj), ("TYPE", m.kind), ("TIME", (m.t / 1000.0).floor())];
            self.bsend(b, "RECV", &rec, "")?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// the AUTH tried again
    pub fn buddy_retry(&mut self, b: u64, f: FieldMap) {
        let Some(x) = self.buddies.conns.get(&b) else { return };
        if !self.conn_open(x.conn) || x.persona.is_some() {
            return;
        }
        let _ = self.buddy_message(b, "AUTH", &f);
    }

    fn buddy_message(&mut self, b: u64, kind: &str, f: &FieldMap) -> Result<(), String> {
        let with_id: Fields = match f.get("ID") {
            Some(id) => fields![("ID", id)],
            None => vec![],
        };
        let wid = |mut extra: Fields| {
            let mut v = with_id.clone();
            v.append(&mut extra);
            v
        };
        let x = &self.buddies.conns[&b];
        if kind == "AUTH" {
            if x.persona.is_some() {
                return self.bsend(b, "AUTH", &fields![("TITL", "EA MESSENGER")], "logn");
            }
            // the lobby's key for this browser's persona: the only thing that says who this is
            let key = f.str("LKEY").to_string();
            let vip = x.vip;
            // the first of this browser's live sessions with this key (a session of another browser never counts)
            let s = if key.encode_utf16().count() >= 24 {
                self.lobby.of_vip(vip).iter().copied().find(|id| {
                    let y = self.lobby.s(*id);
                    y.vip == vip && y.lkey.as_ref().is_some_and(|l| !l.is_empty() && l.starts_with(&key))
                })
            } else {
                None
            };
            let Some(s) = s else {
                let x = self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).expect("held");
                x.tries += 1;
                // the lobby login may finish a moment later
                if x.tries <= 6 {
                    self.set_timeout(500.0, Action::BuddyRetry(b, f.clone()));
                    return Ok(());
                }
                return self.bsend(b, "AUTH", &fields![("TITL", "EA MESSENGER")], "pass");
            };
            if let Some(t) = self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).and_then(|x| x.login_timer.take()) {
                self.timers.clear(t);
            }
            let persona = self.lobby.s(s).persona.clone().unwrap_or_default();
            let k = lower(&persona);
            if let Some(old) = self.buddies.online.get(&k).copied().filter(|o| *o != b)
                && let Some(conn) = self.buddies.conns.get(&old).map(|x| x.conn)
            {
                self.conn_destroy(conn, "logged in again");
            }
            if let Some(x) = self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b) {
                x.persona = Some(persona.clone());
                x.key = k.clone();
            }
            self.buddies.online.insert(k, b);
            let owner = self.lobby.s(s).owner.clone();
            self.lists_at_login(&persona, owner);
            self.seen_list(&persona);
            // (requests and messages that waited too long go, at most once an hour)
            let now = self.bnow();
            if now - self.buddies.pruned >= 3_600_000.0 {
                self.buddies.pruned = now;
                if self.buddies.prune(now) {
                    self.touch_lists();
                }
            }
            return self.bsend(b, "AUTH", &fields![("TITL", "EA MESSENGER")], "");
        }
        if kind == "PING" {
            return self.bsend(b, "PING", &[], "");
        }
        if kind == "DISC" {
            self.buddy_gone(b);
            let conn = self.buddies.conns[&b].conn;
            self.conn_end(conn);
            return Ok(());
        }
        let short = jsx::slice16(kind, 4).to_string();
        let Some(bp) = self.buddies.conns[&b].persona.clone() else { return self.bsend(b, &short, &[], "auth") };
        let me = lower(&bp);
        let group = self.buddies.conns[&b].group.clone();
        let list_of = |f: &FieldMap| if f.str("LIST").to_uppercase() == "I" { "I" } else { "B" };
        let list_field = |f: &FieldMap| if f.has("LIST") { list_of(f) } else { "B" };
        match kind {
            "EPGT" => self.bsend(b, "EPGT", &wid(fields![("ENAB", "N"), ("ADDR", "")]), ""),
            "RGET" => {
                let now = self.bnow();
                if !self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).expect("held").heavy.take_at(now, 1.0) {
                    return self.bsend(b, "RGET", &with_id, "full");
                }
                let which = list_field(f);
                // the entries: name, ATTR (a request's letter, none for a friend or a blocked one)
                let mut rows: Vec<(String, &'static str)> = Vec::new();
                let bs = &self.buddies;
                let l = bs.lists.get(&me);
                if which == "I" {
                    rows.extend(l.into_iter().flat_map(|l| l.i.values()).map(|n| (n.clone(), "")));
                } else {
                    rows.extend(l.into_iter().flat_map(|l| l.b.values()).map(|n| (n.clone(), "")));
                    if f.str("PEND").eq_ignore_ascii_case("Y") {
                        let friend_or_asked = |k: &str| l.is_some_and(|l| l.b.contains_key(k) || l.r.contains_key(k));
                        for (k, (n, t)) in l.into_iter().flat_map(|l| l.r.iter()) {
                            if now - t < ASK_DAYS * DAY_MS && !l.is_some_and(|l| l.b.contains_key(k)) {
                                rows.push((n.clone(), I_ASKED));
                            }
                        }
                        let mut askers: Vec<&String> = l.into_iter().flat_map(|l| l.q.keys()).collect();
                        askers.sort();
                        for k in askers {
                            if let Some(n) = bs.request(k, &me, now)
                                && !bs.blocks(&me, k)
                                && !friend_or_asked(k)
                            {
                                rows.push((n.to_string(), ASKED_ME));
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
                self.bsend(b, "RGET", &wid(fields![("SIZE", rows.len())]), "")?;
                for (n, a) in &rows {
                    let mut r = wid(fields![("USER", n), ("LIST", which)]);
                    if !a.is_empty() {
                        r.extend(fields![("ATTR", *a)]);
                    }
                    self.bsend(b, "ROST", &r, "")?;
                }
                if which == "B" {
                    for (n, _) in &rows {
                        let p = self.presence_of(&lower(n), n);
                        self.bsend(b, "PGET", &p, "")?;
                    }
                    // the messages that waited, a moment later (`MAIL_WAIT_MS`)
                    let waiting = self.buddies.lists.get(&me).is_some_and(|l| !l.m.is_empty());
                    if waiting && self.buddies.conns[&b].mail_timer.is_none() {
                        let t = self.set_timeout(MAIL_WAIT_MS, Action::BuddyMail(b));
                        self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).expect("held").mail_timer = Some(t);
                    }
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            // (RADD LIST=B: a friend request, as RADM below)
            "RADD" | "RDEL" | "RDEM" if kind != "RADD" || list_field(f) == "I" => {
                let which = if kind == "RDEM" { "B" } else { list_field(f) };
                let who = strip_at(f.str("USER")).to_string();
                if !valid_name(&who) || lower(&who) == me {
                    return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "user");
                }
                let k = lower(&who);
                if which == "I" {
                    if kind == "RADD" {
                        if !self.block(&bp, &group, who) {
                            return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "full");
                        }
                    } else if self.buddies.block_remove(&me, &k) {
                        self.touch_lists();
                    }
                    return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "");
                }
                // a friend taken off, or the request taken back: on neither side any more
                self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "")?;
                self.unfriend(&bp, &who)
            }
            "RADM" | "RADD" => {
                // a friend request (Send Friend Request): it waits for the persona's answer, RRSP.  RADD LIST=B too,
                // which the game never sends: until the 2026-11-05 security audit it put the persona on this one's
                // list at once, unasked, and the free-roam hub then told this one where the persona played
                let who = strip_at(f.str("USER")).to_string();
                let k = lower(&who);
                if !valid_name(&who) || k == me {
                    return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "user");
                }
                let now = self.bnow();
                // (friends both ways already; a name on this one's list alone is asked as any other)
                let back = self.fetch_back(&me, &k);
                let (friends, full, asked_full) = match self.buddies.list(&bp) {
                    Some(l) => (
                        l.b.contains_key(&k) && back,
                        l.b.len() >= MAX_FRIENDS && !l.b.contains_key(&k),
                        l.r.len() >= MAX_ASKED && !l.r.contains_key(&k),
                    ),
                    None => (false, false, false),
                };
                if friends {
                    return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "");
                }
                if full {
                    return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "full");
                }
                // two requests that cross (the asked one asks back) make friends
                if self.buddies.request(&k, &me, now).is_some() {
                    self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "")?;
                    return self.befriend(b, &who, "asked back");
                }
                if asked_full || !self.make_list(&bp, &group) {
                    return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "full");
                }
                self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "")?;
                // the asked persona's presence for the asker's new entry (PRES=Y; else the game shows it offline)
                let p = self.presence_of(&k, &who);
                self.bsend(b, "PGET", &p, "")?;
                // (a persona that blocks the asker never hears of it)
                if self.buddies.blocks(&k, &me) {
                    return Ok(());
                }
                self.asked_list(&who);
                self.buddies.ask(&me, k.clone(), who.clone(), now.floor());
                self.touch_lists();
                (self.log)(&format!("[online] \"{bp}\" asked \"{who}\" to be friends"), Some(&group));
                let Some(o) = self.buddies.online.get(&k).copied() else { return Ok(()) };
                // to the asked one: the asker, as a request that waits for its answer (R: the player's menu then
                // offers to answer it, Accept, Decline or Block, 0x4D5190/0x4A1B50), then the asker's presence for
                // that entry
                self.bsend(o, "RNOT", &fields![("USER", bp.as_str()), ("CHNG", "A"), ("ATTR", ASKED_ME)], "")?;
                let p = presence(&self.buddies.conns[&b]);
                self.bsend(o, "PGET", &p, "")
            }
            "RRSP" => {
                // the answer to a friend request: Y accept, N decline, B block
                let who = strip_at(f.str("USER")).to_string();
                let k = lower(&who);
                let now = self.bnow();
                self.buddy_fetch(&k);
                let asker = self.buddies.request(&k, &me, now).map(str::to_string);
                self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "")?;
                // (one that waited too long goes too)
                if self.buddies.unask(&k, &me) {
                    self.touch_lists();
                }
                let Some(asker) = asker else { return Ok(()) };
                let answer = f.str("ANSW");
                let a = answer.chars().next().map(|c| c.to_ascii_uppercase());
                if a == Some('Y') {
                    return self.befriend(b, &asker, &format!("ANSW={}", clean_text(answer, 8)));
                }
                if a == Some('B') {
                    self.block(&bp, &group, asker.clone());
                }
                (self.log)(&format!("[online] \"{bp}\" declined \"{asker}\"'s friend request"), Some(&group));
                match self.buddies.online.get(&k).copied() {
                    Some(o) => self.bsend(o, "RNOT", &fields![("USER", bp.as_str()), ("CHNG", "D")], ""),
                    None => Ok(()),
                }
            }
            "PADD" | "PDEL" => {
                // the Messenger's "All" list: players this one searched for or met (in memory only); their presence
                let who = strip_at(f.str("USER")).to_string();
                self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "")?;
                if !valid_name(&who) {
                    return Ok(());
                }
                let x = self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).expect("held");
                let k = lower(&who);
                if kind == "PDEL" {
                    if x.met.remove(&k)
                        && let Some(s) = self.buddies.met_by.get_mut(&k)
                    {
                        s.remove(&b);
                        if s.is_empty() {
                            self.buddies.met_by.remove(&k);
                        }
                    }
                    return Ok(());
                }
                if x.met.len() < MAX_LIST && x.met.insert(k.clone()) {
                    self.buddies.met_by.entry(k.clone()).or_default().insert(b);
                }
                let p = self.presence_of(&k, &who);
                self.bsend(b, "PGET", &p, "")
            }
            "USCH" => {
                // Search: personas online now or known from their races whose name starts with the text (at most
                // MAXR, 20)
                let now = self.bnow();
                if !self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).expect("held").heavy.take_at(now, 1.0) {
                    return self.bsend(b, "USCH", &wid(fields![("SIZE", 0)]), "");
                }
                let q = jsx::slice16(&lower(strip_at(f.str("USER"))), 15).to_string();
                let max = 20i32.min(1i32.max(jsx::to_int32(f.num("MAXR", 20.0)))) as usize;
                let mut found: IndexMap<String, String> = IndexMap::new();
                if !q.is_empty() {
                    // (by_persona's keys are its sessions' personas in lower case: none made again for each)
                    for (k, s) in &self.lobby.by_persona {
                        if k.starts_with(&q)
                            && let Some(p) = &self.lobby.s(*s).persona
                        {
                            found.insert(k.clone(), p.clone());
                        }
                    }
                    for n in self.stats.starting_with(&q, max + 1) {
                        found.insert(lower(&n), n);
                    }
                }
                found.shift_remove(&me);
                let mut names: Vec<String> = found.into_values().collect();
                names.sort();
                names.truncate(max);
                self.bsend(b, "USCH", &wid(fields![("SIZE", names.len())]), "")?;
                for n in names {
                    self.bsend(b, "USER", &wid(fields![("USER", n)]), "")?;
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            "PSET" => {
                let show = jsx::slice16(f.get("SHOW").unwrap_or("CHAT"), 8).to_string();
                let stat = jsx::slice16(f.str("STAT"), 64).to_string();
                let prod = clean_text(f.str("PROD"), 64);
                self.bsend(b, "PSET", &with_id, "")?;
                let x = self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).expect("held");
                if x.told.is_some() && show == x.show && stat == x.stat && prod == x.prod {
                    return Ok(());
                }
                x.show = show;
                x.stat = stat;
                x.prod = prod;
                self.presence_changed(b)
            }
            "SEND" | "GINV" | "GRSP" | "GRVK" => {
                let to = strip_at(f.str("USER")).to_string();
                let k = lower(&to);
                let o = self.buddies.online.get(&k).copied();
                let t = self.bnow();
                let x = self.buddies.conns.get_mut(&b).expect("held");
                // messages and invites: 2 a second, a burst of 5 (over that: "full", the connection stays)
                x.msgs_v = 5f64.min(x.msgs_v + (t - x.msgs_t) / 500.0);
                x.msgs_t = t;
                if x.msgs_v < 1.0 {
                    return self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "full");
                }
                x.msgs_v -= 1.0;
                self.bsend(b, kind, &with_id, "")?;
                // a message that reads as a slur, or one while the sender's are off, reaches no one (`msg_slur`)
                if kind == "SEND" && (self.msg_muted(&me) || self.msg_slur(&me, &bp, &clean_text(f.str("BODY"), 500), Some(&group))) {
                    return Ok(());
                }
                // away: a message from a friend goes to its pages, or waits for the persona (an invite is forgotten)
                let Some(o) = o.filter(|o| self.buddies.conns.get(o).is_some_and(|x| x.persona.is_some())) else {
                    if kind == "SEND" && valid_name(&to) {
                        self.keep_mail(&k, &bp, f, t);
                    }
                    return Ok(());
                };
                // this sender is blocked
                if self.buddies.blocks(&k, &me) {
                    return Ok(());
                }
                let bp2 = self.buddies.conns.get(&b).and_then(|x| x.persona.clone());
                if kind == "SEND" {
                    let rec = fields![
                        ("USER", bp2),
                        ("BODY", clean_text(f.str("BODY"), 500)),
                        ("SUBJ", clean_text(f.str("SUBJ"), 64)),
                        ("TYPE", jsx::slice16(f.get("TYPE").unwrap_or("C"), 4)),
                        ("TIME", (t / 1000.0).floor())
                    ];
                    self.bsend(o, "RECV", &rec, "")
                } else {
                    // a game invite and its answers: the game's own fields, the sender named by the server
                    let mut rec = fields![("USER", bp2)];
                    let passed =
                        f.0.iter()
                            .filter_map(|(k, v)| Some((k, v.as_ref()?)))
                            .filter(|(k, _)| !["USER", "ID", "LKEY"].contains(&k.as_str()));
                    rec.extend(passed.take(12).map(|(k, v)| (std::borrow::Cow::from(k.clone()), V::S(clean_text(v, 128)))));
                    self.bsend(o, kind, &rec, "")
                }
            }
            _ => self.bsend(b, &short, &with_id, ""),
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    // buddies.json of before read leniently and moved onto the shelf, one file a list, each request on both lists
    #[test]
    fn buddies_json_moved_onto_the_shelf() {
        let friends: Vec<String> = (0..260).map(|i| format!("\"Friend{i}\"")).collect();
        let many = format!(r#"{{"personas":[{{"name":"Many","seen":"2026-03","B":[{}]}}]}}"#, friends.join(","));
        let most = format!(r#"{{"v":4,"name":"Many","seen":"2026-03","B":[{}]}}"#, friends[..MAX_FRIENDS].join(","));
        let mail: Vec<String> = (0..25).map(|i| format!(r#"{{"from":"Friend1","t":{i},"body":"m{i}","subj":"","type":"C"}}"#)).collect();
        let lots = format!(r#"{{"v":3,"personas":[{{"name":"Inbox","seen":"2026-10","B":["Friend1"],"M":[{}]}}]}}"#, mail.join(","));
        let twenty = format!(r#"{{"v":4,"name":"Inbox","seen":"2026-10","B":["Friend1"],"M":[{}]}}"#, mail[5..].join(","));
        let cases: Vec<(&str, Vec<&str>)> = vec![
            ("{not json", vec![]),
            ("", vec![]),
            (
                r#"{"v":2,"note":"NFSU2 online friends lists (persona names only)","personas":[{"name":"Alpha","seen":"2026-10","B":["Bravo","Charlie"]}]}"#,
                vec![r#"{"v":4,"name":"Alpha","seen":"2026-10","B":["Bravo","Charlie"]}"#],
            ),
            // a friend twice: the later spelling in the earlier one's place; friends that are no name; an owner twice:
            // the more recently seen list, in the other one's place
            (
                r#"{"personas":[{"name":"Alpha","seen":"2026-10","B":["Bravo","bravo","x y",5,null,"Delta"],"I":["Mallory"]},{"name":"alpha","seen":"2026-09","B":["Echo"]}]}"#,
                vec![r#"{"v":4,"name":"Alpha","seen":"2026-10","B":["bravo","Delta"],"I":["Mallory"]}"#],
            ),
            // owners that are no name not read; of the others the lists with anything in them, all of them
            (
                r#"{"personas":[{"name":"NoFriends","seen":"2026-10","B":[]},{"name":"Bad Name","B":["Alpha"]},{"name":"Old","B":["Alpha"]},{"name":"Mid","seen":"2026-05","B":["Alpha"]},{"name":"New","seen":"2026-12","B":"Alpha"},{"name":"Newer","seen":"2027-01","B":["Zed"]}]}"#,
                vec![
                    r#"{"v":4,"name":"Mid","seen":"2026-05","B":["Alpha"]}"#,
                    r#"{"v":4,"name":"Newer","seen":"2027-01","B":["Zed"]}"#,
                    r#"{"v":4,"name":"Old","seen":"1970-01","B":["Alpha"]}"#,
                ],
            ),
            // MAX_FRIENDS friends at most
            (many.as_str(), vec![most.as_str()]),
            // version 3: the blocked, the requests sent (ones that are no name or no time left out), each also on the
            // asked one's list (one made for Charlie), the messages waiting (text cleaned, ones from no name or
            // without a time left out); a list with only some of them
            (
                r#"{"v":3,"personas":[{"name":"Alpha","seen":"2026-10","B":["Bravo"],"I":["Mallory","x y"],"R":[["Charlie",1761200000000],["x y",1],["Delta"],["Echo",-5]],"M":[{"from":"Bravo","t":1761200000123.7,"body":"hi\u0007 there","subj":"","type":"C"},{"from":"x y","t":1,"body":"no"},{"from":"Bravo","body":"no time"}]},{"name":"Lonely","seen":"2026-10","B":[],"R":[["Alpha",5]]}]}"#,
                vec![
                    r#"{"v":4,"name":"Alpha","seen":"2026-10","B":["Bravo"],"I":["Mallory"],"R":[["Charlie",1761200000000]],"Q":[["Lonely",5]],"M":[{"from":"Bravo","t":1761200000123,"body":"hi there","subj":"","type":"C"}]}"#,
                    r#"{"v":4,"name":"Charlie","seen":"1970-01","B":[],"Q":[["Alpha",1761200000000]]}"#,
                    r#"{"v":4,"name":"Lonely","seen":"2026-10","B":[],"R":[["Alpha",5]]}"#,
                ],
            ),
            // the newest 20 messages
            (lots.as_str(), vec![twenty.as_str()]),
        ];
        for (text, kept) in cases {
            let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
            std::fs::write(dir.path().join(OLD_FILE), text).unwrap();
            let _ = Buddies::new(Some(dir.path().to_path_buf()), BuddyLimits::default());
            assert_eq!(shelf_texts(dir.path()), kept, "{text}");
            assert!(!dir.path().join(OLD_FILE).exists() && dir.path().join("buddies.json.moved").exists(), "{text}");
        }
    }

    // the shelf at scale (cargo test -p nfsu2-online --lib shelf_at_scale -- --ignored --nocapture): 200,000
    // players' lists of 5 friends each on disk, then players logging in (their lists read, one change each written)
    // with 20,000 lists in memory; what a save costs is the lists that changed, never the shelf's size
    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn shelf_at_scale() {
        use std::time::Instant;
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let n = 200_000;
        let name = |i: usize| format!("P{i:06}");
        let t = Instant::now();
        for i in 0..n {
            let mut l = FriendsList::new(&name(i), "2026-10".into());
            for f in 1..=5 {
                let x = name((i + f * 7919) % n);
                l.b.insert(lower(&x), x);
            }
            Shelf::write(dir.path(), &lower(&name(i)), &list_json(&l)).unwrap();
        }
        let wrote = t.elapsed();
        let mut s = Buddies::new(Some(dir.path().to_path_buf()), BuddyLimits { lists: 20_000.0, ..Default::default() });
        let none = |_: &str| false;
        let t = Instant::now();
        let logins = 50_000;
        for k in 0..logins {
            let key = lower(&name((k * 104_729) % n));
            assert!(s.fetch(&key, 0.0, &none));
            s.mark(&key);
            if k % 1000 == 999 {
                assert!(s.write_dirty().is_none());
            }
        }
        let fetched = t.elapsed();
        eprintln!(
            "{n} lists written in {:.1} s ({:.0} us each); {logins} logins (a list read, then written again a thousand at a time) in {:.1} s ({:.0} us each); {} lists in memory",
            wrote.as_secs_f64(),
            wrote.as_secs_f64() * 1e6 / n as f64,
            fetched.as_secs_f64(),
            fetched.as_secs_f64() * 1e6 / logins as f64,
            s.lists.len()
        );
        assert!(s.lists.len() <= 20_000);
    }

    // a list read from the shelf the next time it is needed, as it was written; lists past `lists` go from memory
    // (written first) and come back from the shelf; the sweep takes the lists of claims that ended
    #[test]
    fn lists_come_and_go_from_memory() {
        let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let claims = Arc::new(nfsu2_claims::Claims::in_memory());
        let (a, b) = (nfsu2_claims::owner_of_token(&"A".repeat(43)).unwrap(), nfsu2_claims::owner_of_token(&"B".repeat(43)).unwrap());
        claims.claim("Alpha", &a, 0).unwrap();
        claims.claim("Bravo", &b, 0).unwrap();
        let l = BuddyLimits { lists: 2.0, ..Default::default() };
        let mut s = Buddies::with_claims(Some(dir.path().to_path_buf()), l, Some(claims.clone()), 0);
        let none = |_: &str| false;
        for (n, o) in [("Alpha", &a), ("Bravo", &b)] {
            let mut x = FriendsList::new(n, "2026-10".into());
            x.owner = Some(o.clone());
            s.put_list(lower(n), x);
        }
        s.add_friend("alpha", "bravo".into(), "Bravo".into());
        s.add_friend("bravo", "alpha".into(), "Alpha".into());
        s.ask("alpha", "charlie".into(), "Charlie".into(), 7.0);
        assert!(s.write_dirty().is_none());
        // a third list pushes the least recently seen out of memory
        s.make_room(&none);
        s.lists.insert("charlie".into(), FriendsList::new("Charlie", "2026-10".into()));
        assert!(!s.lists.contains_key("alpha") && !s.fans.contains_key("bravo"), "Alpha's list out, and its fan entry");
        assert!(s.fetch("alpha", 0.0, &none), "back from the shelf");
        let x = s.list("Alpha").unwrap();
        assert_eq!((x.b.keys().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>(), x.r.len(), x.owner.as_deref()), (vec!["bravo"], 1, Some(&*a)));
        // (Bravo's went for it) a list the caller pins is never pushed out: Charlie's goes for Bravo's
        assert!(!s.lists.contains_key("bravo"));
        assert!(s.fetch("bravo", 0.0, &|k: &str| k == "alpha"));
        assert!(s.lists.contains_key("alpha") && !s.lists.contains_key("charlie"));
        // a claim that ended: its list goes from the shelf when it is read, or when the shelf is swept
        claims.release(&b);
        let gone = sweep(dir.path(), &claims, 0, &HashSet::new());
        assert_eq!(gone, 1);
        assert!(Shelf::read(dir.path(), "bravo").is_none() && Shelf::read(dir.path(), "alpha").is_some());
    }
}

//! The online host's state and its events: one struct for the virtual host, the lobby, EA Messenger, the results and
//! the timers, run on one thread with no locks.  The services call each other freely (a lobby send fails, the
//! connection goes, its session leaves, the others hear of it), so they are methods of one `Core` that name
//! sessions, games and connections by id: each call finds what is still there.
//!
//! An event is a frame from the switch, a browser that left, a timer, the lobby's tick: what it ended (a session, a
//! game, a Messenger connection) is let go once it is over (`purge`).

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::rc::Rc;
use std::sync::Arc;

use nfsu2_util::{Charge, FrameCtx, SwitchSend, Tap};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

use crate::buddy::{Buddies, BuddyLimits};
use crate::lobby::{Limits, Lobby};
use crate::stats::{Stats, StatsOptions};
use crate::timers::{Action, TimerId, Timers};
use crate::vhost::{Listener, VHost, VhostLimits};
use crate::{Clocks, LogFn, PORT_BUDDY, PORT_HTTP, PORT_LOBBY, PORT_REDIRECTOR};

/// what the core is given (`OnlineOptions`, and the limits: the defaults in the server, the tests' own)
pub struct CoreOptions {
    pub state_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub log: LogFn,
    pub tap: Option<Tap>,
    pub claims: Option<Arc<nfsu2_claims::Claims>>,
    pub deny: Option<Arc<nfsu2_names::Deny>>,
    pub clocks: Rc<Clocks>,
    pub limits: Limits,
    pub buddy_limits: BuddyLimits,
    pub vhost: VhostLimits,
}

pub struct Core {
    pub clocks: Rc<Clocks>,
    pub log: LogFn,
    pub tap: Option<Tap>,
    pub send: Option<SwitchSend>,
    /// the state folder (races.rs keeps the races going on there over a restart), and whether the races of before the
    /// start were read from it (the file goes at the first tick)
    pub state_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    pub races_read: bool,
    /// the budgets of the frame being handled (what the host sends for it is charged to its sender)
    pub cause: Option<Arc<dyn Charge>>,
    /// the claimed names (OnlineOptions::claims)
    pub claims: Option<Arc<nfsu2_claims::Claims>>,
    /// the names taken away (OnlineOptions::deny)
    pub deny: Option<Arc<nfsu2_names::Deny>>,
    /// the browsers that spoke to this host and are still on the switch
    here: HashSet<u32>,
    pub timers: Timers,
    tick_timer: Option<TimerId>,
    pub vh: VHost,
    pub lobby: Lobby,
    pub buddies: Buddies,
    /// the races' results (stats.rs): the lobby records them, EA Messenger's search reads their names
    pub stats: Stats,
    /// (tests) what a service probe was told
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub probe: Vec<String>,
    /// (tests) the error lines (`console_error`)
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub errors: Vec<String>,
}

impl Core {
    pub fn new(o: CoreOptions) -> Core {
        let mut vh = VHost::new(o.vhost);
        vh.listen(PORT_REDIRECTOR, Listener::Redirector);
        vh.listen(PORT_LOBBY, Listener::Lobby);
        vh.listen(PORT_BUDDY, Listener::Buddy);
        vh.listen(PORT_HTTP, Listener::Http);
        let stats = Stats::new(StatsOptions::new(o.state_dir.clone(), o.clocks.clone(), o.log.clone()));
        let started = (o.clocks.now)() as i64;
        let mut core = Core {
            clocks: o.clocks,
            log: o.log,
            tap: o.tap,
            send: None,
            state_dir: o.state_dir.clone(),
            races_read: false,
            cause: None,
            claims: o.claims.clone(),
            deny: o.deny,
            here: HashSet::new(),
            timers: Timers::default(),
            tick_timer: None,
            vh,
            lobby: Lobby::new(o.limits),
            buddies: Buddies::with_claims(o.state_dir, o.buddy_limits, o.claims.clone(), started),
            stats,
            #[cfg(test)]
            probe: Vec::new(),
            #[cfg(test)]
            errors: Vec::new(),
        };
        core.load_races();
        // the lobby's tick, every 5 s
        core.tick_timer = Some(core.set_timeout(5000.0, Action::LobbyTick));
        core
    }

    /// `a` once `ms` have passed on the timer clock
    pub fn set_timeout(&mut self, ms: f64, a: Action) -> TimerId {
        // a delay below 1 ms, or beyond 2^31 - 1 ms, is 1 ms (as the Node server's timers took it)
        let ms = if (1.0..=2_147_483_647.0).contains(&ms) { ms } else { 1.0 };
        let at = (self.clocks.timer)() + ms;
        self.timers.set(at, a)
    }

    /// a handler that failed, as an error line on the console (and kept for the tests)
    pub fn console_error(&mut self, line: &str) {
        nfsu2_util::log::error(line);
        #[cfg(test)]
        self.errors.push(line.to_string());
    }

    /// the switch's way to its browsers
    pub fn attach(&mut self, send: SwitchSend) {
        self.send = Some(send);
    }

    /// a frame from a browser (ctx: its client's group and site ids and its budgets, from the switch); what the host
    /// sent because of it is charged to that client, and when that was more than its share the stream it came on
    /// goes (vhost.rs `overrun`)
    pub fn frame(&mut self, from: u32, data: &[u8], ctx: &FrameCtx) {
        self.here.insert(from);
        self.lobby.seen(from);
        self.cause = ctx.cause.clone();
        self.vh_frame(from, data, ctx);
        self.cause = None;
        if ctx.cause.as_ref().is_some_and(|c| c.overspent()) {
            self.overrun(from, data);
        }
        self.purge();
    }

    pub fn peer_gone(&mut self, vip: u32) {
        self.here.remove(&vip);
        self.vh_peer_gone(vip);
        let now = (self.clocks.now)();
        self.lobby.peer_gone(vip, now);
        self.purge();
    }

    /// what left or ended during the event is let go
    pub fn purge(&mut self) {
        self.lobby.purge();
        self.buddies.purge();
    }

    /// when the next timer is due (the timer clock)
    pub fn next_due(&mut self) -> Option<f64> {
        let t = self.timers.next_due();
        match (t, self.stats.save_due()) {
            (Some(a), Some(b)) => Some(a.min(b)),
            (a, b) => a.or(b),
        }
    }

    /// every timer due by `now` (the timer clock), one event each
    pub fn run_due(&mut self, now: f64) {
        loop {
            if self.stats.save_due().is_some_and(|t| t <= now && self.timers.next_due().is_none_or(|n| t <= n)) {
                self.stats.save_timer();
                continue;
            }
            let Some((id, a)) = self.timers.pop_due(now) else { break };
            self.run(id, a);
            self.purge();
        }
    }

    fn run(&mut self, id: TimerId, a: Action) {
        match a {
            Action::LobbyTick => {
                self.tick_timer = Some(self.set_timeout(5000.0, Action::LobbyTick));
                self.lobby_tick();
                self.buddy_tick();
            }
            Action::Later(k) => self.later_timer(k, id),
            Action::RedirectorIdle(c) => self.redirector_idle(c),
            Action::HttpIdle(c) => self.http_idle(c),
            Action::BuddyLogin(b) => self.buddy_login_idle(b),
            Action::BuddyRetry(b, f) => self.buddy_retry(b, f),
            Action::Presence(b) => self.presence_timer(b),
            Action::BuddyMail(b) => self.buddy_mail_timer(b),
            Action::BuddySave => self.buddy_save_timer(),
        }
    }

    /// the lobby's tick as one event (the tests call it when they move their clock)
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub fn tick(&mut self) {
        self.lobby_tick();
        self.purge();
    }

    /// the virtual host's counts, then the lobby's, as one object.  Both have a `refused`, and the lobby two `games`
    /// (the games at once, and its stats' games made in all): the lobby's `refused` and its games made in all stand,
    /// each in the place of the first of its name (as the Node server's object spread put them).
    pub fn info(&self) -> Value {
        let v = &self.vh.stats;
        let l = &self.lobby.stats;
        let (sessions, personas, racing, _) = self.lobby.info(&self.here);
        json!({
            "conns": self.vh.conns.len(), "synIn": v.syn_in, "refused": l.refused, "limited": v.limited,
            "rstIn": v.rst_in, "framesIn": v.frames_in, "framesOut": v.frames_out, "echoes": v.echoes,
            "udpUnreach": v.udp_unreach, "bad": v.bad, "slow": v.slow, "overrun": v.overrun,
            "sessions": sessions, "personas": personas, "racing": racing, "games": l.games, "logins": l.logins,
            "chats": l.chats, "races": l.races, "dropped": l.dropped,
        })
    }

    /// the browsers in Online mode now (the ones info() counts)
    pub fn vips(&self) -> HashSet<u32> {
        self.lobby.vips(&self.here)
    }

    /// the server stops: the lobby's links go, the files are written, the timers end
    pub fn stop(&mut self) {
        if let Some(t) = self.tick_timer.take() {
            self.timers.clear(t);
        }
        self.lobby_stop();
        self.buddy_stop();
        self.purge();
    }
}

//! The files of the state folder (stats.json, buddies.json, races.json), written atomically (`nfsu2_util::atomic_file`):
//! the folder made 0700 when it is missing (the Online audit's ONL-13), a temporary file of 0600, then a rename; a
//! failure described in Node's words (its `e.message`: the console line quotes it, as the Node server's line did).
//! Not synced: the Online host's one thread writes them (the friends lists that changed every 10 s, the results every
//! 30 s), and waiting on the disk there holds up every player's lobby.

use std::io;
use std::path::Path;

use nfsu2_util::atomic_file::{Options, Step};

/// the folder (0700, with its parents), the temporary file (0600), then the rename over `file`
pub fn write_atomic(file: &Path, body: &[u8]) -> Result<(), String> {
    Options::new().make_folder().no_sync().write(file, body).map_err(|f| match f.step {
        Step::Folder => node_error(&f.error, "mkdir", Some(&f.path), None),
        Step::Open => node_error(&f.error, "open", Some(&f.tmp), None),
        Step::Write => node_error(&f.error, "write", None, None),
        Step::Sync => node_error(&f.error, "fsync", None, None),
        Step::Rename => node_error(&f.error, "rename", Some(&f.tmp), Some(file)),
    })
}

/// libuv's name and text of an errno (uv_err_name, uv_strerror)
fn uv(errno: i32) -> Option<(&'static str, &'static str)> {
    // Linux's numbers: the server runs there
    Some(match errno {
        1 => ("EPERM", "operation not permitted"),
        2 => ("ENOENT", "no such file or directory"),
        5 => ("EIO", "i/o error"),
        9 => ("EBADF", "bad file descriptor"),
        11 => ("EAGAIN", "resource temporarily unavailable"),
        12 => ("ENOMEM", "not enough memory"),
        13 => ("EACCES", "permission denied"),
        16 => ("EBUSY", "resource busy or locked"),
        17 => ("EEXIST", "file already exists"),
        18 => ("EXDEV", "cross-device link not permitted"),
        19 => ("ENODEV", "no such device"),
        20 => ("ENOTDIR", "not a directory"),
        21 => ("EISDIR", "illegal operation on a directory"),
        22 => ("EINVAL", "invalid argument"),
        23 => ("ENFILE", "file table overflow"),
        24 => ("EMFILE", "too many open files"),
        26 => ("ETXTBSY", "text file is busy"),
        27 => ("EFBIG", "file too large"),
        28 => ("ENOSPC", "no space left on device"),
        30 => ("EROFS", "read-only file system"),
        31 => ("EMLINK", "too many links"),
        36 => ("ENAMETOOLONG", "name too long"),
        39 => ("ENOTEMPTY", "directory not empty"),
        40 => ("ELOOP", "too many symbolic links encountered"),
        _ => return None,
    })
}

/// Node's message of a failed fs call: "EACCES: permission denied, open '/x'" ("rename 'a' -> 'b'")
pub fn node_error(e: &io::Error, syscall: &str, path: Option<&Path>, dest: Option<&Path>) -> String {
    let Some((code, text)) = e.raw_os_error().filter(|_| cfg!(target_os = "linux")).and_then(uv) else {
        return e.to_string();
    };
    let mut s = format!("{code}: {text}, {syscall}");
    if let Some(p) = path {
        s.push_str(&format!(" '{}'", p.display()));
    }
    if let Some(d) = dest {
        s.push_str(&format!(" -> '{}'", d.display()));
    }
    s
}

//! The online host's web pages (port 80 of 10.77.0.1): the two addresses the server config hands the game
//! (lobby.rs `config_fields`), NEWSURL and TOSURL.  The game fetches them with its own HTTP/1.0 client (ProtoHTTP)
//! and runs the answer through EA's "web offer" script engine: a %{ CMD=... %} header line with the command and its
//! fields, then the text.  Only the "news" command is ever served (a title, the text, one button that closes the
//! page); never "card" (a credit-card form) or "prom", nor anything that collects input.
//!
//! One GET per connection, at most 4 KB of request, answered and closed.  The pages hold nothing about any player.

use crate::core::Core;
use crate::jsx;
use crate::timers::{Action, TimerId};
use crate::vhost::{ConnId, Svc};

struct Page {
    title: &'static str,
    text: &'static str,
}

const NEWS: Page = Page {
    title: "NFSU2 Online",
    // the welcome, then only the important changes from the original game; CRLF breaks a line (the box scrolls),
    // latin1: plain quotes and hyphens only
    text: "Welcome to Online play on this server: open the Lobby, create a game or join one, ready up and race.\r\n\
           \r\n\
           Changes from the original game:\r\n\
           - Online works again, on this server instead of EA's. You play under your own name, with no EA account.\r\n\
           - Up to 6 players in every race type (the original had 4, and 6 only in Street X). Drag keeps one car per lane.\r\n\
           - Every track is open, whatever your career has unlocked, and a new game starts at 2 laps.\r\n\

           - Free roam with other players: their cars drive in your city, with their names over them.\r\n\
           - A horn: N, in races and in free roam, eight to pick from in Settings. The others hear it from your car.\r\n\
           - Widescreen, and up to 120 fps on a 120 Hz screen.",
};

const TOS: Page = Page {
    title: "Terms of Service",
    text: "This server is a stand-in for the online service of the original game, run by whoever runs this server. \
           Play fair and be kind in the chat.",
};

/// a web-offer page: the script header, then the text (CRLF line ends, as the game's own pages had)
fn offer_page(p: &Page) -> String {
    let q: String = p.title.chars().map(|c| if matches!(c, '"' | '%' | '{' | '}' | '\r' | '\n') { ' ' } else { c }).collect();
    format!("%{{ CMD=news TITLE=\"{q}\" BTN1=\"OK\" BTN1-GOTO=\"$quit\" %}}\r\n{}\r\n", p.text)
}

/// one connection's request so far
pub struct HttpConn {
    buf: Vec<u8>,
    pub done: bool,
    pub timer: Option<TimerId>,
}

/// `/^(GET|HEAD) (\/[^ ?#]*)[^ ]* HTTP\/1\.[01]$/` on the request line: the method and the path
fn request_line(line: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let (method, rest) = line.split_once(' ')?;
    if method != "GET" && method != "HEAD" {
        return None;
    }
    let target = rest.strip_suffix(" HTTP/1.0").or_else(|| rest.strip_suffix(" HTTP/1.1"))?;
    if !target.starts_with('/') || target.contains(' ') {
        return None;
    }
    let end = target.find(['?', '#']).unwrap_or(target.len());
    Some((method, &target[..end]))
}

impl Core {
    pub fn http_connect(&mut self, c: ConnId) {
        let t = self.set_timeout(15_000.0, Action::HttpIdle(c));
        self.vh.https.insert(c, HttpConn { buf: Vec::new(), done: false, timer: Some(t) });
        self.set_svc(c, Svc::Http);
    }

    /// the 15 s for a request are over
    pub fn http_idle(&mut self, c: ConnId) {
        if self.vh.https.contains_key(&c) {
            self.conn_destroy(c, "http: no request");
        }
    }

    pub fn http_data(&mut self, c: ConnId, chunk: &[u8]) {
        let Some(h) = self.vh.https.get_mut(&c) else { return };
        if h.done {
            return;
        }
        h.buf.extend_from_slice(chunk);
        if h.buf.len() > 4096 {
            h.done = true;
            return self.conn_destroy(c, "http: request too large");
        }
        let Some(_) = h.buf.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n") else { return };
        h.done = true;
        if let Some(t) = h.timer.take() {
            self.timers.clear(t);
        }
        let first = h.buf.windows(2).position(|w| w == b"\r\n").unwrap_or(0);
        let line = jsx::latin1_decode(&h.buf[..first]);
        let m = request_line(&line);
        let page = m.and_then(|(_, p)| match p.to_lowercase().as_str() {
            "/news" => Some(&NEWS),
            "/tos" => Some(&TOS),
            _ => None,
        });
        let mut body = Vec::new();
        jsx::latin1_encode(&page.map_or_else(|| "Not found\r\n".to_string(), offer_page), &mut body);
        let status = if page.is_some() {
            "200 OK"
        } else if m.is_some() {
            "404 Not Found"
        } else {
            "400 Bad Request"
        };
        let head = format!("HTTP/1.0 {status}\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n", body.len());
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        jsx::latin1_encode(&head, &mut out);
        if m.is_none_or(|(method, _)| method != "HEAD") {
            out.extend_from_slice(&body);
        }
        self.conn_write(c, &out);
        self.conn_end(c);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn request_lines() {
        assert_eq!(request_line("GET /news HTTP/1.0"), Some(("GET", "/news")));
        assert_eq!(request_line("HEAD /tos?x=1#y HTTP/1.1"), Some(("HEAD", "/tos")));
        assert_eq!(request_line("GET /a b HTTP/1.0"), None);
        assert_eq!(request_line("POST /news HTTP/1.0"), None);
        assert_eq!(request_line("GET news HTTP/1.0"), None);
        assert_eq!(request_line("GET / HTTP/1.2"), None);
        assert!(offer_page(&NEWS).starts_with("%{ CMD=news TITLE=\"NFSU2 Online\" BTN1=\"OK\" BTN1-GOTO=\"$quit\" %}\r\nWelcome"));
    }
}

{"id": "AT001604", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/online/src/jsonparse.rs", "originalBytes": 15571, "originalSha256": "2caa9fed99a2920e8ef6949fe28de319d36ba51e50db0954343f2eca9ba46f93", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 15571, "utf8TotalBytes": 15571}

//! `JSON.parse` for the two files the online host reads (stats.json, buddies.json), as lenient as V8 where
//! serde_json is stricter, and with V8's error messages (the console line of a file that does not parse quotes
//! one).  What serde_json would refuse and V8 takes:
//!
//! - a number beyond the doubles (1e400): V8 reads Infinity.  A `serde_json::Value` cannot hold one, so it is read as
//!   `true`: every rule of the two loaders treats Infinity and `true` alike (not a finite number, a truthy count
//!   block, no `name`, no `seen`, no list).
//! - an escaped lone surrogate ("\ud800"): read as U+FFFD (no string the loaders keep can hold one: names, months and
//!   track keys are checked against ASCII patterns).
//! - nesting deeper than serde_json's 128 levels: this parser keeps its own stack, and what it made is let go
//!   without recursion too ([`Parsed`]): a file nested deeper than a thread's stack (V8 reads one of millions of
//!   levels) would otherwise overflow it when dropped, and take the whole server down at its start.

use std::ops::Deref;

use serde_json::{Map, Number, Value};

const MAX_CONTEXT: usize = 10;

/// `JSON.parse(text)`: the value, or V8's message (`e.message`)
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Parsed, String> {
    let mut stack = Vec::new();
    let r = Parser { s: text.as_bytes(), text, i: 0 }.run(&mut stack);
    // (what a text that does not parse had made so far)
    for f in stack {
        match f {
            Frame::Array(a) => drop_flat(Value::Array(a)),
            Frame::Object(m, _) => drop_flat(Value::Object(m)),
        }
    }
    r.map(Parsed)
}

/// A parsed file's value: read through `Deref`; let go without recursion, however deep it is (a serde_json `Value`
/// drops each level from the one above it, a stack frame a level).  The loaders only borrow from it (a clone of a
/// part would recurse the same way).
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Parsed(Value);

impl Deref for Parsed {
    type Target = Value;
    fn deref(&self) -> &Value {
        &self.0
    }
}

impl Drop for Parsed {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        drop_flat(std::mem::take(&mut self.0));
    }
}

/// a value let go level by level: each array or object's members are moved out before it goes
fn drop_flat(v: Value) {
    let mut todo = vec![v];
    while let Some(v) = todo.pop() {
        match v {
            Value::Array(a) => todo.extend(a),
            Value::Object(m) => todo.extend(m.into_iter().map(|(_, v)| v)),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
}

enum Frame {
    Array(Vec<Value>),
    Object(Map<String, Value>, String),
}

struct Parser<'a> {
    s: &'a [u8],
    text: &'a str,
    i: usize,
}

impl Parser<'_> {
    fn peek(&self) -> Option<u8> {
        self.s.get(self.i).copied()
    }
    fn skip_ws(&mut self) {
        while let Some(b' ' | b'\t' | b'\n' | b'\r') = self.peek() {
            self.i += 1;
        }
    }

    /// the value (what a text that does not parse made is left on `stack`, for `parse` to let go)
    fn run(&mut self, stack: &mut Vec<Frame>) -> Result<Value, String> {
        'value: loop {
            self.skip_ws();
            let mut v = match self.peek() {
                Some(b'{') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                    self.skip_ws();
                    if self.peek() == Some(b'}') {
                        self.i += 1;
                        Value::Object(Map::new())
                    } else {
                        let key = self.key("Expected property name or '}'")?;
                        stack.push(Frame::Object(Map::new(), key));
                        continue 'value;
                    }
                }
                Some(b'[') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                    self.skip_ws();
                    if self.peek() == Some(b']') {
                        self.i += 1;
                        Value::Array(Vec::new())
                    } else {
                        stack.push(Frame::Array(Vec::new()));
                        continue 'value;
                    }
                }
                Some(b'"') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                    Value::String(self.string()?)
                }
                Some(b'-' | b'0'..=b'9') => self.number()?,
                Some(b't') => self.literal("true", Value::Bool(true))?,
                Some(b'f') => self.literal("false", Value::Bool(false))?,
                Some(b'n') => self.literal("null", Value::Null)?,
                _ => return Err(self.unexpected()),
            };
            loop {
                match stack.last_mut() {
                    None => {
                        self.skip_ws();
                        if self.i < self.s.len() {
                            let (pos, line, col) = self.location();
                            drop_flat(v);
                            return Err(format!(
                                "Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position {pos} (line {line} column {col})"
                            ));
                        }
                        return Ok(v);
                    }
                    Some(Frame::Array(a)) => {
                        a.push(v);
                        self.skip_ws();
                        match self.peek() {
                            Some(b',') => {
                                self.i += 1;
                                continue 'value;
                            }
                            Some(b']') => {
                                self.i += 1;
                                let Some(Frame::Array(a)) = stack.pop() else { unreachable!() };
                                v = Value::Array(a);
                            }
                            _ => return Err(self.at("Expected ',' or ']' after array element")),
                        }
                    }
                    Some(Frame::Object(m, k)) => {
                        // a repeated key: the last value, in the first one's place (as JSON.parse)
                        m.insert(std::mem::take(k), v);
                        self.skip_ws();
                        match self.peek() {
                            Some(b',') => {
                                self.i += 1;
                                self.skip_ws();
                                let key = self.key("Expected double-quoted property name")?;
                                if let Some(Frame::Object(_, k)) = stack.last_mut() {
                                    *k = key;
                                }
                                continue 'value;
                            }
                            Some(b'}') => {
                                self.i += 1;
                                let Some(Frame::Object(m, _)) = stack.pop() else { unreachable!() };
                                v = Value::Object(m);
                            }
                            _ => return Err(self.at("Expected ',' or '}' after property value")),
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// a property name and its colon (whitespace before it skipped)
    fn key(&mut self, missing: &str) -> Result<String, String> {
        if self.peek() != Some(b'"') {
            return Err(self.at(missing));
        }
        self.i += 1;
        let k = self.string()?;
        self.skip_ws();
        if self.peek() != Some(b':') {
            return Err(self.at("Expected ':' after property name"));
        }
        self.i += 1;
        Ok(k)
    }

    /// the rest of a string (the opening quote taken)
    fn string(&mut self) -> Result<String, String> {
        let mut out = String::new();
        let mut units: Vec<u16> = Vec::new();
        loop {
            let start = self.i;
            while let Some(c) = self.peek() {
                if c == b'"' || c == b'\\' || c < 0x20 {
                    break;
                }
                self.i += 1;
            }
            if self.i > start {
                flush_units(&mut units, &mut out);
                out.push_str(&self.text[start..self.i]);
            }
            match self.peek() {
                None => return Err(self.at("Unterminated string")),
                Some(b'"') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                    flush_units(&mut units, &mut out);
                    return Ok(out);
                }
                Some(b'\\') => {
                    self.i += 1;
                    let e = self.peek();
                    let simple = match e {
                        Some(b'"') => Some('"'),
                        Some(b'\\') => Some('\\'),
                        Some(b'/') => Some('/'),
                        Some(b'b') => Some('\u{8}'),
                        Some(b'f') => Some('\u{c}'),
                        Some(b'n') => Some('\n'),
                        Some(b'r') => Some('\r'),
                        Some(b't') => Some('\t'),
                        _ => None,
                    };
                    if let Some(c) = simple {
                        flush_units(&mut units, &mut out);
                        out.push(c);
                        self.i += 1;
                    } else if e == Some(b'u') {
                        let mut v = 0u32;
                        for _ in 0..4 {
                            self.i += 1;
                            match self.peek().and_then(|c| (c as char).to_digit(16)) {
                                Some(d) => v = v * 16 + d,
                                None => return Err(self.at("Bad Unicode escape")),
                            }
                        }
                        self.i += 1;
                        units.push(v as u16);
                    } else if e.is_none() {
                        return Err(self.at("Unterminated string"));
                    } else {
                        return Err(self.at("Bad escaped character"));
                    }
                }
                Some(_) => return Err(self.at("Bad control character in string literal")),
            }
        }
    }

    fn number(&mut self) -> Result<Value, String> {
        let start = self.i;
        if self.peek() == Some(b'-') {
            self.i += 1;
        }
        match self.peek() {
            Some(b'0') => {
                self.i += 1;
                if self.peek().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
                    return Err(self.at("Unexpected number"));
                }
            }
            Some(b'1'..=b'9') => self.digits(),
            _ => return Err(self.at("No number after minus sign")),
        }
        if self.peek() == Some(b'.') {
            self.i += 1;
            if !self.peek().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
                return Err(self.at("Unterminated fractional number"));
            }
            self.digits();
        }
        if let Some(b'e' | b'E') = self.peek() {
            self.i += 1;
            if let Some(b'+' | b'-') = self.peek() {
                self.i += 1;
            }
            if !self.peek().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
                return Err(self.at("Exponent part is missing a number"));
            }
            self.digits();
        }
        let x: f64 = self.text[start..self.i].parse().unwrap_or(f64::NAN);
        Ok(number(x))
    }

    fn digits(&mut self) {
        while self.peek().is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) {
            self.i += 1;
        }
    }

    fn literal(&mut self, word: &str, v: Value) -> Result<Value, String> {
        for &w in word.as_bytes() {
            match self.peek() {
                Some(c) if c == w => self.i += 1,
                _ => return Err(self.unexpected()),
            }
        }
        Ok(v)
    }

    /// the UTF-16 position of the cursor, and its line and column (\r, \n and \r\n end a line)
    fn location(&self) -> (usize, usize, usize) {
        let u: Vec<u16> = self.text[..self.i.min(self.text.len())].encode_utf16().collect();
        let n = u.len();
        let (mut line, mut last_break, mut k) = (1, 0, 0);
        while k < n {
            if u[k] == 13 && k + 1 < n && u[k + 1] == 10 {
                k += 1;
            }
            if u[k] == 13 || u[k] == 10 {
                line += 1;
                last_break = k + 1;
            }
            k += 1;
        }
        (n, line, 1 + n - last_break)
    }

    /// "<what> in JSON at position N (line L column C)"
    fn at(&self, what: &str) -> String {
        let (pos, line, col) = self.location();
        format!("{what} in JSON at position {pos} (line {line} column {col})")
    }

    /// V8's message for a token where none fits: the end, a number, a string, else the character with some context
    fn unexpected(&self) -> String {
        let Some(c) = self.text[self.i..].chars().next() else { return "Unexpected end of JSON input".into() };
        match c {
            '-' | '0'..='9' => return self.at("Unexpected number"),
            '"' => return self.at("Unexpected string"),
            _ => {}
        }
        if matches!(self.text, "NaN" | "Infinity" | "undefined" | "[object Object]") {
            return format!("\"{}\" is not valid JSON", self.text);
        }
        let all: Vec<u16> = self.text.encode_utf16().collect();
        let pos: usize = self.text[..self.i].encode_utf16().count();
        let tok = String::from_utf16_lossy(&all[pos..pos + 1]);
        let sub = |a: usize, b: usize| String::from_utf16_lossy(&all[a..b.min(all.len())]);
        if all.len() < 2 * MAX_CONTEXT + 1 {
            format!("Unexpected token '{tok}', \"{}\" is not valid JSON", self.text)
        } else if pos < MAX_CONTEXT {
            format!("Unexpected token '{tok}', \"{}\"... is not valid JSON", sub(0, pos + MAX_CONTEXT))
        } else if pos < all.len() - MAX_CONTEXT {
            format!("Unexpected token '{tok}', ...\"{}\"... is not valid JSON", sub(pos - MAX_CONTEXT, pos + MAX_CONTEXT))
        } else {
            format!("Unexpected token '{tok}', ...\"{}\" is not valid JSON", sub(pos - MAX_CONTEXT, all.len()))
        }
    }
}

/// escaped UTF-16 units into text: pairs joined, a lone surrogate as U+FFFD
fn flush_units(units: &mut Vec<u16>, out: &mut String) {
    if !units.is_empty() {
        out.extend(char::decode_utf16(units.drain(..)).map(|r| r.unwrap_or('\u{FFFD}')));
    }
}

/// a JSON number as JS holds it: whole numbers as integers, Infinity as `true` (see the module's text)
fn number(x: f64) -> Value {
    if x.is_infinite() {
        return Value::Bool(true);
    }
    if x.fract() == 0.0 && x.abs() < 9_007_199_254_740_992.0 {
        return Value::from(x as i64);
    }
    Number::from_f64(x).map_or(Value::Null, Value::Number)
}

        assert_eq!(*parse("1e400").unwrap(), Value::Bool(true));

//! The JavaScript rules the online host keeps from the Node server it replaced, beyond nfsu2_util::js, so that a
//! field the game sends reads as the same number and a text is cut in the same place: `Number(s)` and what `| 0`
//! and `>>> 0` make of it, latin1 buffers, slices in UTF-16 code units, `Math.round`, and the few patterns of names
//! and text written out by hand.  Every text the online host reads comes from latin1 bytes (aries.rs), so its
//! strings hold characters up to U+00FF only; the helpers still follow JS for any string.

use nfsu2_util::js;
use unicode_general_category::{GeneralCategory, get_general_category};
use unicode_normalization::UnicodeNormalization;

/// JS `Number(s)` of a string: JS white space trimmed, "" is 0, decimal (with "Infinity"), 0x/0o/0b, else NaN.
pub fn to_number(s: &str) -> f64 {
    let t = js::trim(s);
    if t.is_empty() {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let b = t.as_bytes();
    if b.len() > 2 && b[0] == b'0' {
        let radix = match b[1] {
            b'x' | b'X' => 16,
            b'o' | b'O' => 8,
            b'b' | b'B' => 2,
            _ => 0,
        };
        if radix != 0 {
            return radix_number(&t[2..], radix);
        }
    }
    let (sign, rest) = match b[0] {
        b'+' => (1.0, &t[1..]),
        b'-' => (-1.0, &t[1..]),
        _ => (1.0, t),
    };
    if rest == "Infinity" {
        return sign * f64::INFINITY;
    }
    if !is_decimal(rest) {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    // the grammar is checked: Rust's parser rounds as JS does (to the nearest double)
    sign * rest.parse::<f64>().unwrap_or(f64::NAN)
}

/// StrUnsignedDecimalLiteral without "Infinity": digits, an optional fraction, an optional exponent
fn is_decimal(s: &str) -> bool {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let mut i = 0;
    let digits = |i: &mut usize| {
        let s0 = *i;
        while *i < b.len() && b[*i].is_ascii_digit() {
            *i += 1;
        }
        *i - s0
    };
    let mut n = digits(&mut i);
    if i < b.len() && b[i] == b'.' {
        i += 1;
        n += digits(&mut i);
    }
    if n == 0 {
        return false;
    }
    if i < b.len() && (b[i] == b'e' || b[i] == b'E') {
        i += 1;
        if i < b.len() && (b[i] == b'+' || b[i] == b'-') {
            i += 1;
        }
        if digits(&mut i) == 0 {
            return false;
        }
    }
    i == b.len()
}

/// the digits of a 0x/0o/0b literal, rounded to the nearest double as JS rounds them
fn radix_number(s: &str, radix: u32) -> f64 {
    if s.is_empty() {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    let bits = radix.trailing_zeros();
    let (mut acc, mut shift, mut sticky) = (0u128, 0i32, false);
    for c in s.chars() {
        let Some(d) = c.to_digit(radix) else { return f64::NAN };
        if acc < (1u128 << (128 - bits)) {
            acc = (acc << bits) | d as u128;
        } else {
            shift += bits as i32;
            sticky |= d != 0;
        }
    }
    // more than 128 bits: the lowest kept bit stands for what was cut (it is far below the double's precision,
    // so it only breaks a tie the way the exact value would)
    if sticky {
        acc |= 1;
    }
    (acc as f64) * 2f64.powi(shift)
}

/// JS ToInt32 (`x | 0`)
pub fn to_int32(x: f64) -> i32 {
    to_uint32(x) as i32
}

/// JS ToUint32 (`x >>> 0`)
pub fn to_uint32(x: f64) -> u32 {
    if !x.is_finite() {
        return 0;
    }
    x.trunc().rem_euclid(4_294_967_296.0) as u32
}

/// JS `Math.round`: the nearest integer, a half up
pub fn round(x: f64) -> f64 {
    if !x.is_finite() {
        return x;
    }
    let r = x.floor();
    if x - r >= 0.5 { r + 1.0 } else { r }
}

/// Node's `Buffer.from(s, 'latin1')`: the low byte of each UTF-16 code unit
pub fn latin1_encode(s: &str, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
    for c in s.chars() {
        let u = c as u32;
        if u <= 0xFFFF {
            out.push(u as u8);
        } else {
            let v = u - 0x10000;
            out.push((0xD800 + (v >> 10)) as u8);
            out.push((0xDC00 + (v & 0x3FF)) as u8);
        }
    }
}

/// Node's `buf.toString('latin1')`: each byte a character
pub fn latin1_decode(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    b.iter().map(|&x| x as char).collect()
}

/// JS `s.slice(0, n)` in UTF-16 code units (a pair the cut would split is left out: the online host's strings are
/// latin1 and have none)
pub fn slice16(s: &str, n: usize) -> &str {
    let mut units = 0;
    for (i, c) in s.char_indices() {
        units += c.len_utf16();
        if units > n {
            return &s[..i];
        }
    }
    s
}

/// what the game lets one type for a persona or account (letters, digits, - and _), 3 to 15
/// characters
pub fn valid_name(s: &str) -> bool {
    (3..=15).contains(&s.len()) && s.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b == b'_' || b == b'-')
}

/// text another player will see (chat, game names): NFC, control and format
/// characters as spaces, white space collapsed and trimmed, at most max code points
pub fn clean_text(s: &str, max: usize) -> String {
    let nfc: String = s.nfc().collect();
    let spaced: String = nfc
        .chars()
        .map(|c| match get_general_category(c) {
            GeneralCategory::Control | GeneralCategory::Format => ' ',
            _ => c,
        })
        .collect();
    let collapsed = js::collapse_space(&spaced, " ");
    js::trim(&collapsed).chars().take(max).collect()
}

/// JS line terminators: where `.` stops
fn line_terminator(c: char) -> bool {
    matches!(c, '\n' | '\r' | '\u{2028}' | '\u{2029}')
}

/// the name before a "@domain" or "/resource" (EA Messenger's USER): the pattern `[@/].*$` cut off.  `.` does not
/// cross a line terminator and `$` is the end of the text, so the cut is at the first @ or / after the last line
/// terminator.
pub fn strip_at(s: &str) -> &str {
    let from = s.char_indices().rfind(|(_, c)| line_terminator(*c)).map_or(0, |(i, c)| i + c.len_utf8());
    match s[from..].find(['@', '/']) {
        Some(i) => &s[..from + i],
        None => s,
    }
}

/// JS `toLowerCase()`
pub fn lower(s: &str) -> String {
    s.to_lowercase()
}

/// a day as the lobby writes it, "2026.1.5" (UTC, no leading zeros), of a time in ms since 1970
pub fn day(t: f64) -> String {
    let (y, m, d, ..) = js::utc_parts(t.trunc() as i64);
    format!("{y}.{m}.{d}")
}

/// `YYYY-MM` (UTC) of a time in ms since 1970: the month the results and the friends lists keep
pub fn month_of(t: f64) -> String {
    let (y, m, ..) = js::utc_parts(t.trunc() as i64);
    format!("{y}-{m:02}")
}

/// a month as the files keep it: `YYYY-MM`, in digits
pub fn is_month(s: &str) -> bool {
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    b.len() == 7 && b[4] == b'-' && b.iter().enumerate().all(|(i, c)| i == 4 || c.is_ascii_digit())
}

/// lowercase hex
pub fn hex(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    const H: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(b.len() * 2);
    for &x in b {
        s.push(H[(x >> 4) as usize] as char);
        s.push(H[(x & 15) as usize] as char);
    }
    s
}

mod tests {

    #[test]
    fn numbers_as_js_reads_them() {
        for (s, v) in [
            ("0x1F", 31.0),
            (" 12 ", 12.0),
            ("1e3", 1000.0),
            ("", 0.0),
            ("Infinity", f64::INFINITY),
            (".5", 0.5),
            ("5.", 5.0),
            ("0b101", 5.0),
            ("0o17", 15.0),
            ("\u{a0}12", 12.0),
            ("-Infinity", f64::NEG_INFINITY),
            ("+7", 7.0),
            ("0x", f64::NAN),
            ("-0x1", f64::NAN),
            ("1_0", f64::NAN),
            ("inf", f64::NAN),
            ("nan", f64::NAN),
            ("1e", f64::NAN),
            (".", f64::NAN),
            ("0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF", 295147905179352830000.0),
            ("00012", 12.0),
        ] {
            let got = to_number(s);
            assert!(got == v || (got.is_nan() && v.is_nan()), "{s:?}: {got}");
        }
        assert_eq!(to_int32(to_number("4294967297")), 1);
        assert_eq!(to_int32(to_number("2147483648")), -2147483648);
        assert_eq!(to_uint32(to_number("-1")), 4294967295);
        assert_eq!(to_uint32(to_number("x")), 0);
        assert_eq!(round(2.5), 3.0);
        assert_eq!(round(-2.5), -2.0);
        assert_eq!(round(0.49999999999999994), 0.0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn text() {
        assert_eq!(strip_at("a@b"), "a");
        assert_eq!(strip_at("a@b\nc"), "a@b\nc");
        assert_eq!(strip_at("a@b\u{2028}c@d"), "a@b\u{2028}c");
        assert_eq!(strip_at("x/y"), "x");
        assert_eq!(clean_text("hello \u{9b} there\u{7}", 255), "hello there");
        assert_eq!(clean_text("  a\u{ad}b  ", 255), "a b");
        assert_eq!(clean_text("abcdef", 3), "abc");
        assert_eq!(slice16("a\u{1F600}b", 2), "a");
        assert!(valid_name("Speedy") && !valid_name("x y") && !valid_name("ab") && !valid_name("abcdefghijklmnop"));
        assert_eq!(day(1_000_000.0), "1970.1.1");
        assert_eq!(month_of(1_792_565_740_123.0), "2026-10");
        let mut b = Vec::new();
        latin1_encode("A\u{100}\u{1F600}", &mut b);
        assert_eq!(b, [0x41, 0x00, 0x3d, 0x00]);
    }
}

//! The server's stand-in for EA's online servers of NFS Underground 2, for the game's own Online mode (main menu,
//! Online) between browsers on this server.  It keeps the rules and the console lines of the Node server it
//! replaced, and its results in the state folder (online/stats.json) byte for byte as that one wrote them, so the
//! results kept before are read as they are; the friends lists, one buddies.json then, are one file a persona since
//! 2026-10-31 (online/friends/, buddy.rs), and free roam's pages befriend and message through them too
//! ([`OnlineHost::friends`]; a message for a page goes out through [`OnlineHost::page_mail`]).
//!
//! - browser: lifted DirtySock -> winsock.c (pcnfs05.ea.com = 10.77.0.1) -> runtime/web/net_lan.c -> page -> /lan
//!   WebSocket -> the switch (nfsu2-lan)
//! - switch: frames to 10.77.0.1 -> [`OnlineHost`] -> vhost.rs (TCP, ICMP) -> the services below, by port:
//!   20920 the redirector (@dir -> our lobby's address; no @tic: no RC4, no SSL), 20922 the lobby (login under any
//!   name but a slur, personas, rooms, chat, games: lobby.rs), 13505 EA Messenger (friends, presence, messages,
//!   invites: buddy.rs), 80 the news and terms pages the config names (http.rs)
//!
//! Race traffic never comes here: the players' browsers send it to each other through the switch (UDP 3658, a star
//! around the game's creator), as in LAN play.  Every address a player learns is a virtual one (10.77.x.x).
//!
//! What the server keeps: sessions, rooms, games and chat in memory only (of chat, each persona's last lines for a
//! complaint about it, which writes them to the log: lobby.rs `said`); on disk only the races' public results per
//! persona (stats.rs) and each persona's friends list (buddy.rs), names only, under the server's --state directory,
//! and from a stop to the next start the races going on (races.rs).
//! Nothing secret is ever read (aries.rs SECRET_KEYS: the password, the CD key and the file checksum are passed over
//! undecoded).  The log names players by persona and virtual address only, never their real address or what they
//! typed as a password.  The lines a client causes (logins, games, races, complaints, friends) go through
//! `log(line, key)` with that client's opaque group id as the key: the server shows at most a few a minute per
//! client (`nfsu2_util::log::limited`; the Online audit's ONL-8).
//!
//! The whole of it runs on one thread of its own, as it ran on Node's one thread: the switch posts it its frames in
//! order ([`OnlineHost`] is a `nfsu2_util::Host`), and its timers (the lobby's ticks, the services' time-outs, the
//! saves) run on that thread between them.  Its load is small (the .NET port: 120 lobby clients took 0.1-0.2
//! cores) and its state is one tangle of sessions, rooms, games and friends, so one thread and no locks is both the
//! simplest and the fastest.

/// What the Online host is given.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct OnlineOptions {
    /// where stats.json, buddies.json and races.json are kept (the server's --state/online); None: in memory only
    pub state_dir: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// a console line, and the opaque group id of the client that caused it (None: the server's own line); the
    /// server shows at most a few a minute per client (`nfsu2_util::log::limited`, the Online audit's ONL-8)
    pub log: Arc<dyn Fn(&str, Option<&str>) + Send + Sync>,
    /// the dev trace: sees every frame the host sends (the switch's own tap sees what the browsers send)
    pub tap: Option<Tap>,
    /// the claimed names (nfsu2-claims): who may play under a name, and whose EA Messenger lists are kept; None: every
    /// name is anyone's, and every list is kept (as before names could be claimed)
    pub claims: Option<Arc<nfsu2_claims::Claims>>,
    /// the names the operator took away (nfsu2-bans `rename`): no login or persona under one; None: none
