//! The free-roam hub.  Its links are the ones the Node server's hub made before it: the same pairs in the same order,
//! the grid and heap of a large room included.
//!
//! The hub is the server's host on the switch at 10.77.0.253 (runtime/web/net_proto.h NET_ROAM_HUB, an address the
//! switch never hands out) that tells each free-roam player which players are near it.  Without it every player
//! talks to every other one, in groups of at most 8 (the first to meet); with it a server takes many more players:
//! each player's peers are the hub's list of the players nearest to it (runtime/roam_core.c, hub mode), and the
//! snapshots still go straight from player to player through the switch.
//!
//! - player -> hub: a HELLO every second (its id, room, status, name, and its crews), a SNAP twice a second (where
//!   its car is), a BYE when it stops.
//! - hub -> player: twice a second (`tick_ms`) a PEERS message: the players linked to it, { virtual address, port, id }, at most
//!   its degree: what its HELLO asks for (roam_core version 10: the friends' cars its game shows, its "Players' cars shown"),
//!   `degree` (64: roam_core's group of 65 with itself) at most; 48 at most for a core of versions 10 to 13 and 32 for one
//!   before, which read no longer lists; an empty one says the hub is there.  To a player in a crew the list ends in
//!   crew marks: its own crews, then which of them each listed player is in.
//! - player -> hub -> player: when its world map opens, and a quarter second after each answer while it is open, a
//!   MAPREQ naming the answer it holds; the hub answers with MAPD datagrams (at most 16, 48 to a page that takes
//!   them): the other players of its room in free roam, past its links, map_max (4096) of them at most (the nearest,
//!   and as many as the answer's datagrams hold: 1664 in 16 with heights), or as many as the MAPREQ asks
//!   for, by the hub's slot of each, as what changed since that answer: each player come, or moved off where the
//!   page has it, placed (x, y in whole metres, heading a byte, velocity in m/s: the page moves its marker on at
//!   it), each one gone gone.  A player standing costs nothing, a car going straight little.
//! - player -> hub -> player: while it drives, four times a second (a quarter second after each answer), a NEARREQ for
//!   its minimap: the same, but of the players within the radius it asks for (its minimap's reach, 1000 m at most), at
//!   most the 128 nearest (it asks for 64), each where it is at the question, placed again 2 m off where the page has
//!   it, in one NEARD datagram laid out as a MAPD.  One answer a browser every `near_gap_ms` (150), every 500 ms while
//!   the hub's thread is 60 % busy and every second at 75 %: the links come first (bench.rs bench_near: 3000 players
//!   asking took 3 to 6 % of the thread).
//!
//! The links, in each room: the pairs of players with a position younger than `stale_ms` (60 s: one in a shop or a
//! race keeps its links for a while), nearest first, each player at most its degree of them.  "Nearest" looks ahead,
//! for the cars a player will see: a pair counts at the nearest of
//! - its distance once both cars went on `soon_ms` (1 s) at the speeds their last SNAPs gave (from where those SNAPs
//!   had them, moved on by their age), so a car a player drives away from gives way at once,
//! - its distance once both went on `look_ms` (4 s), so a car a player heads for is linked (and its car loaded) before
//!   it is near,
//! - and the distance from either one's view point, `view_m` (150 m) ahead of where its car points (from its place
//!   soon_ms on), to the other one soon_ms on: the camera looks that way, so a car in front, parked or driving, shows
//!   from farther away than one beside or behind it.
//!
//! Only a car in free roam moves on and has a view point; a player not in free roam (a shop, a race, the menus,
//! loading) counts `away_m` (100 m) up, so its links go to the cars shown first.  Parked players in free roam count by
//! distance and view point.  A simulation of 1400 players (tests/popin.rs, 2026-10-23) against the links of before
//! (now and 3 s ahead, a tick a second): of the cars within 250 m in front of a driver 84 % shown instead of 63 %,
//! a car showing within 100 m in front 0.30 times a minute instead of 0.63, a car left behind gone at 300 m instead of
//! 390; for 600 players in 800 m square, 20 such pop-ins a minute instead of 66.  Both ends of a link list each other
//! (roam_core takes a player only when both hear each other).  A link stays at least `hold_ms` (5 s), and
//! after that counts as `keep` (half) its distance: a new link costs a handshake, the car's record and maybe a car
//! swapped on the screen, so it has to be much nearer to take the place of one (62 simulated players circling within
//! 240 m changed links 28 times a second with 20 % instead).  The game shows a car for each of a player's links
//! (runtime/roam_game.c).
//!
//! A race lobby's links come before all of these (its messages go between linked players only, roam_game.c mp_*):
//! from its host's advert (to the hub every second, with its players), the host is linked with each of its players,
//! with each player asking to join it (a copy of its JOIN to the hub, for 6 s), and with the 24 nearest players in
//! free roam within 20 m of its start, while both ends have room.  By distance alone a host at a busy start had its
//! links full of nearer players, the ones who went into the career race there among them: the link to a player who
//! stopped there to join came and went, and its Enter went nowhere.
//!
//! Then the crews' (a word each, up to 4 a player, set on the start page; its HELLO names them by roam_core's room
//! hash): two players of one room who share a crew are linked before the rest, nearest first, while both ends have
//! room, at most 16 such links a player, so crew-mates always see each other and still see the cars around them.  By
//! distance alone a friend 300 m off in a crowd was never linked (32 nearer players were, 8 under the busy cap): his
//! car, name and map arrow never showed.  A crew of more than 64 players in one room gets no links first (its pairs
//! grow as the square of its players): they link by distance as everyone does.  /players counts each crew's players
//! for the start page (`in_crews()`).  A player learns which of its peers share a crew from the hub's marks on its
//! list, never from the peers: a crew's hash in a stranger's hands is all it takes to be linked with that player
//! anywhere on the map, and a short crew name is quickly found from its hash.
//!
//! A busy server gives every player fewer links: each link is two players' snapshots to each other, 20 a second each
//! way (fewer for far ones), so a crowd costs its players times their links, all through the switch; a switch that
//! cannot keep up delays every snapshot, and the cars stutter for everyone (nfsu2.xyz at 855 players, 2026-10-20:
//! 180-600 ms for a /players answer on Node's one thread).  While the server worked more than `busy_high` of the last
//! `BUSY_WINDOW` (10 s; of its workers' time, or of its CPU quota) the cap on the links goes down by a quarter, at
//! most every `cap_down_ms`, to `min_degree` at the least; once it has room again (under `busy_low`) the cap goes back
//! up by 2 every `cap_up_ms`.  The nearest links stay.  While
//! the cap is under `ask_cap` (24) free roam counts as busy (the server's /players roamBusy): until 2026-11-05 the start
//! page did not ask its question (Free roam with others?) at a Play then, so fewer new players joined a crowd that
//! already got fewer cars (free roam is on by default since).  /players also says how many drive in free roam, or are paused
//! there (`in_roam()`, counted at each tick).
//!
//! The hub also watches how each player's car moves (watch.rs): a teleport, a car faster than any of the game's, or a
//! game whose clock runs fast (a speed hack) is a `[cheat]` line with the player's address and name, and who was
//! next to where its car came to.  And it judges each race lobby's race by its racers' results (results.rs): a win
//! no car makes is a `[cheat]` line too (the races' clean wins it goes by are by two clients' games at least: a
//! frame's client is its site, an IPv6 /48, or else its address, `FrameCtx::site` and `group`).  Lines only: the
//! operator decides (`nfsu2-server ctl kick|ban`).
//!
//! A claimed name (nfsu2-claims) is its keyphrase's only: a player whose HELLO names one that another keyphrase
//! claimed (its page's hello to the switch named the keyphrase it plays with: `FrameCtx::owner`) gets no links, is on
//! nobody's map and counts nowhere, and the console says so once.  The page plays under the name with four digits
//! then (as the Online lobby gives it), so only a page that ignores that plays alone.  A player's own claim hears that
//! it plays (it holds two years from its last game).
//!
//! A page may block players by the name over their car (its hello to the switch: `Host::blocks`, `Hub::blocks`): the
//! hub links it with none of them, either way, nor with the host of a race lobby one of them is in, and leaves each
//! out of the other's world map and lobby list.  Names count as their Online form (any case), and a claimed name's
//! keyphrase stays blocked under its next name while the old one is still its own.  The console has a line for each
//! page that blocks (`[roam] <address> blocks "<name>", ...`), so the operator sees who many players block.
//!
//! What the hub keeps, in memory only: per player endpoint its virtual address, port, id, room hash, crews' hashes,
//! status, name and last position (and what its watch counted), and per browser the names it blocks; gone `gone_ms`
//! after its last message, when it says BYE, or when it leaves the switch.  Reading positions is what choosing by
//! distance costs: the switch itself never looks inside a frame.  At
//! most `max_per_vip` endpoints per virtual address (a browser has one, two in co-op), and `max_players` in all.
//!
//! Co-op free roam: a browser's second local player (player 2 beside player 1 on one screen) is a second endpoint of
//! its browser, on a port of its own (player 1's + 1), its HELLO flagged (wire::HF_SEAT2), its name the second form of
//! player 1's ("Alex 2": nfsu2-claims `second`, its claim's owner's).  Every other player sees it as one more player;
//! the hub never links two endpoints of one browser (nor shows one on the other's maps: the game shows its own cars),
//! answers the maps of the browser's first player only, marks the second as nobody's friend, tells it apart on the
//! console and lets its car come to the first one's side without a teleport (hub.rs `Player::seat2`).
//!
//! - [`Hub`]: the hub's logic, single-threaded, with the clock, the busy measure and the sending given to it (the
//!   tests drive it by its `frame()`, `tick()` and `info()`)
//! - [`RoamHub`]: the hub on a thread of its own, a `nfsu2_util::Host` for the switch: frames are posted to it in
//!   order, it ticks every `tick_ms`, and sends its lists through the switch.  Its "busy" is the share of their time
//!   the runtime's workers, which run the switch, spent working (nfsu2_util::cpu::WorkersBusy): Node read its one
//!   thread's event-loop use.  (The process's CPU time over every core, which it was, never passed `busy_high` once
//!   the workers were half the cores: all of them busy was 50 %.)  Or, where it is higher, the share of a CPU quota
//!   the server shares used (nfsu2_util::cpu::QuotaBusy), both over the last `BUSY_WINDOW` (a half second's share of a
//!   slice at 73 % went up to 88 %): the game's containers share nfsu2.slice's, and cloudflared pays for every
//!   snapshot too, so a slice near its limit gets fewer links before its players get them late.

mod hub;
// (made by tools/map_jumps.py: its rows as the tool writes them)
#[rustfmt::skip]
mod jumps;
mod links;
mod results;
mod watch;
mod wire;

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::panic::{AssertUnwindSafe, catch_unwind};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicUsize, Ordering};
use std::sync::mpsc;
use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};

pub use hub::{Hosted, Hub, Whereabouts};
pub use wire::{decode_roam, encode_peers, encode_peers_crews};

/// 10.77.0.253, runtime/web/net_proto.h NET_ROAM_HUB
pub const ROAM_HUB_VIP: u32 = 0x0A4D_00FD;

/// the most crews a player is in (roam_core.h RC_CREW_MAX), and so the most /players counts for one question
pub const CREWS: usize = wire::CREWS;

/// The race tracks' spots a game's free roam can go to (the page menu's Tracks, runtime/travel.c SPOTS), each by its
/// room's key: on one, a game plays in a room of its own, its world's room with the key mixed in (`track_room`), so
/// its players meet only the players at the same spot.  A world's count takes its spots' players too (`world_count`).
pub const TRACK_KEYS: [u32; 9] = [4711, 4701, 4311, 4301, 4201, 4211, 4221, 4601, 4605];

/// the room of the race track's spot of this key in the world of room `base` (runtime/roam_game.c room_at,
/// web/src/app/tracks.ts trackRoom): never 0, the main world's
pub fn track_room(base: u32, key: u32) -> u32 {
    match base ^ key.wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B1) {
        0 => 1,
        r => r,
    }
}

/// whether room `room` is in the main world (the room of everyone): its city's, 0, or one of its race tracks' spots'
/// (`track_room`).  A page names its other worlds' rooms (`Hub::room_name`); this one has no name.
pub fn main_world(room: u32) -> bool {
    room == 0 || TRACK_KEYS.iter().any(|&k| track_room(0, k) == room)
}

/// how many of free roam play in the world of room `room` (counts: `Hub::in_rooms`), its race tracks' spots too
pub fn world_count(counts: &HashMap<u32, usize>, room: u32) -> usize {
    let n = |r: u32| counts.get(&r).copied().unwrap_or(0);
    n(room) + TRACK_KEYS.iter().map(|&k| n(track_room(room, k))).sum::<usize>()
}

/// The hub's options.  exact_room: a room of at most this many players sorts every pair of them; a larger one takes
/// the pairs in the same order but only as far as it needs them: each player's nearest one after another (a grid)
/// until it has its links (every pair of 2000 players in one room took the Node hub 1.5-4.5 s a tick, 1000 players
/// 0.5 s).  A value that is not a positive number keeps its default.
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct RoamOptions {
    /// the most links a player has (what its HELLO asks for under it; 48 at most for a core of versions 10 to 13, 32 for
    /// one before)
    pub degree: usize,
    pub tick_ms: u64,
    pub stale_ms: f64,
    pub gone_ms: f64,
    pub keep: f64,
    pub hold_ms: f64,
    /// The endpoints of one browser (virtual address) at most, 3: co-op free roam's two local players (the second on a
    /// port of its own, its HELLO flagged: hub.rs `Player::seat2`), and one more for a game started again while its
    /// last start's endpoint lingers (until `gone_ms`).  A browser's endpoints are never linked with each other.
    pub max_per_vip: usize,
    /// The players (endpoints) on the hub at most, 24576: the switch's 24000 places (nfsu2-lan `ADDRS`, one browser
    /// each), of which nearly all can be in free roam (the hub keeps those in a race, a shop or the menus too: 10,401 of
    /// 11,571 on nfsu2.xyz, 2026-11-06), and 576 more for co-op's second players (desktop pages only) and a restart's
    /// lingering endpoints (a few seconds each).  At most hub.rs SLOTS_MAX (25600), and that far under it that a full
    /// hub's new player purges the slots of the ones gone at most once in 1024 (else an eighth of the players, as
    /// before).  What grows with it: a player's slot (some 1.5 KB with its links), the kept watches (one each at most),
    /// the tick (each link; a second player asks for few, its first one fewer: their page's two together, as many as
    /// one player's).  The world map's keys are a pool of their own (hub.rs MAP_KEYS), for the players it shows.
    pub max_players: usize,
    pub exact_room: usize,
    pub min_degree: usize,
    pub busy_high: f64,
    pub busy_low: f64,
    pub cap_down_ms: f64,
    pub cap_up_ms: f64,
    /// under this cap free roam is busy (`crowded()`)
    pub ask_cap: usize,
    /// how far ahead the links look (ms): a pair counts at the nearer of its distance once both cars went on soon_ms
    /// and once they went on look_ms at their speeds, so a car a player heads for is linked before it is near, and one
    /// it drives away from gives way at once
    pub soon_ms: f64,
    pub look_ms: f64,
    /// a player not in free roam (a shop, a race, the menus) counts this far up (m): its links go to the cars shown
    pub away_m: f64,
    /// a player's view point, this far ahead of where its car points (m): a car in front counts from there too, so it
    /// is linked from farther away than one beside or behind
    pub view_m: f64,
    /// one-way links (a core of version 15 and up: `wire::CORE_ONEWAY`): a player sends its car to this many players
    /// at most (its links if more), so that a player who shows more cars than the players round it gets theirs.  A
    /// game sends a car state once whatever the receivers (the page's bundles name them, web/src/net TxBundle): a
    /// phone's upload grows by 4 bytes a receiver, the server makes the copies.  Under the busy cap, its links.
    pub sends: usize,
    /// one-way links among players this near (m, where they are now): by that distance, before any farther (the
    /// distances on and from the view point move with every turn and donut of a car at a meet, and changed which of
    /// the cars round a player it got every few seconds), and one younger than near_hold_ms first, as one younger than
    /// hold_ms is: a car that comes near stays that long while it is
    pub near_m: f64,
    pub near_hold_ms: f64,
    /// ...for a player slower than this (m/s: parked, about to park, a donut, cruising round a meet): a driver at
    /// speed gets its cars as before, the ones it heads for first (with near ones first, a crowd's drivers had fewer
    /// of the cars ahead of them, tests/popin.rs "crowd")
    pub near_fast: f64,
    /// a gap in height between two players that no road explains (a highway over a street, a tunnel under a hill):
    /// up to level_slack_m (m) plus level_grade of the way across (a hill, a ramp, a jump) it counts as it is, and
    /// each metre past that counts level_k metres more.  Two cars on one road weigh as before, one on a road above or
    /// below as one far off (10 m under a highway: as a car 135 m away), so its link goes to a car on the player's
    /// own road when there are more players near than links (links.rs `Level`)
    pub level_slack_m: f64,
    pub level_grade: f64,
    pub level_k: f64,
    /// the world map (MAPREQ): at most this many players a answer, one answer a browser every map_gap_ms at most, of
    /// the players in free roam (or paused there) with a position younger than map_fresh_ms
    pub map_max: usize,
    pub map_gap_ms: f64,
    pub map_fresh_ms: f64,
    /// the minimap (NEARREQ): one answer a browser every near_gap_ms at most (the game asks again 200 ms after each)
    pub near_gap_ms: f64,
    /// the threads a tick reads a large room's walks ahead on (each player's nearest ones, `link_many`), its own
    /// thread among them: by default a quarter of the cores, 1 to 4; 1, on the hub's thread alone.  The links are the
    /// same either way.
    pub link_threads: usize,
    /// the names the operator took away (nfsu2-bans `rename`): a player under one plays alone, as under a name another
    /// keyphrase claimed; None: none
    pub deny: Option<std::sync::Arc<nfsu2_names::Deny>>,
    /// the cars the server race-bans a player for (hub.rs `server_bans`), and what it tells of each such race (the
    /// app's autoban.rs: the ban); None: none (the `[cheat]` lines only)
    pub car_bans: Option<CarBans>,
}

/// A lobby race a player raced with others in a car the server race-bans for (hub.rs `server_bans`), as its own game
/// reported it: who (its virtual address, its name on the hub), its car, the race, how it did
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct CarBan {
    pub vip: u32,
    pub name: String,
    /// the car type's name (printable ASCII, from the report), its type, engine power (kW), weight (kg), top speed
    /// (km/h), the game's rating
    pub car: String,
    pub car_type: u8,
    pub kw: f64,
    pub kg: f64,
    pub kmh: f64,
    pub rating: f64,
    /// the race: its kind ("sprint", "drag", ...), laps, how the player did ("1st of 4", "did not finish", "quit")
    pub kind: String,
    pub laps: u8,
    pub place: String,
    pub lobby: u32,
    pub race: u32,
}

/// The cars the server race-bans a player for: one of the player's car types at `kw` engine power or more, or rated
/// `rating` or more (None: that figure decides nothing).  The operator's numbers (the app reads them from its
/// environment: nothing of them in the code), past what any honest car of the lobby races' reports came near.  `call`
/// is told of each such race, on the hub's thread: it must not wait (the app's hands the race on).
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct CarBans {
    pub kw: Option<f64>,
    pub rating: Option<f64>,
    pub call: std::sync::Arc<dyn Fn(CarBan) + Send + Sync>,
}

// (no numbers in Debug either: they are the operator's)
impl std::fmt::Debug for CarBans {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        f.write_str("CarBans")
    }
}

    fn default() -> Self {
        RoamOptions {

            tick_ms: 500,
            stale_ms: 60_000.0,
            gone_ms: 6_000.0,
            keep: 0.5,
            hold_ms: 5_000.0,
            max_per_vip: 3,
            max_players: 24576,
            exact_room: 256,
            min_degree: 8,
            busy_high: 0.85,
            busy_low: 0.65,
            cap_down_ms: 5_000.0,
            cap_up_ms: 15_000.0,
            ask_cap: 24,
            soon_ms: 1_000.0,
            look_ms: 4_000.0,
            away_m: 100.0,
            view_m: 150.0,
            sends: 64,
            near_m: 60.0,
            near_hold_ms: 30_000.0,
            near_fast: 15.0,
            level_slack_m: 5.0,
            level_grade: 0.2,
            level_k: 25.0,
            map_max: 4096,
            map_gap_ms: 250.0,
            map_fresh_ms: 5_000.0,
            near_gap_ms: 150.0,
            link_threads: std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| (n.get() / 4).clamp(1, 4)),
            deny: None,
            car_bans: None,
        }
    }
}

/// The fields the hub reads of one free-roam datagram (`decode_roam`); a HELLO's crews are the ones it names (with the
/// crew flag), in its order
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub enum RoamMsg {
    Hello { sender: u32, core: u16, status: u8, room: u32, name: String, crews: Vec<u32> },
    Snap { sender: u32, status: u8, p: [f64; 3] },
    Bye { sender: u32 },
    Other { kind: u8, sender: u32 },
}

/// `Math.hypot(x, y, z)` as V8 computes it: the hub's distances (public for tests/hypot.rs, which checks it against
/// node's own)
pub fn hypot(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> f64 {
    links::hypot3(x, y, z)
}

/// one entry of a PEERS list
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct PeerEntry {
    pub vip: u32,
    pub port: u16,
    pub id: u32,
}

/// What the switch posts to the hub's thread, in order.
enum Cmd {
    /// a frame from a browser, the keyphrase its page plays with, and its client (`Hub::frame_of`)
    Frame(u32, Bytes, Option<Arc<str>>, Arc<str>),
    Gone(u32),
    Attach(SwitchSend),
    Info(oneshot::Sender<serde_json::Value>),
    Vips(oneshot::Sender<HashSet<u32>>),
    Blocks(u32, Vec<String>),
    PageName(u32, String),
    OtherNames(oneshot::Sender<HashMap<u32, Vec<String>>>),
    Pairs(oneshot::Sender<Vec<(u32, u32)>>),
    Friends(u32, Arc<str>, Vec<Arc<str>>),
    RoomName(u32, String),
    Flew(u32, f64),
    Linked(u32, String, oneshot::Sender<Option<(u32, Option<Arc<str>>)>>),
    Where(Vec<Arc<str>>, oneshot::Sender<Vec<Option<hub::Whereabouts>>>),
    Hosted(u32, oneshot::Sender<Option<hub::Hosted>>),
    Stop,
}

/// Frames waiting for the hub's thread at most: it handles one in well under a microsecond and 2048 players send
/// 6144 a second, so what waits is what came during a tick (15 ms with 2000 players in one room: 100 frames), and
/// this many (1.3 s of them) means the thread is stuck; the frames past it are left out as a busy network leaves out
/// datagrams, so that a stuck hub cannot take the server's memory (Node's hub could not fall behind: it ran inside
/// the switch's own calls).  A frame waiting is a slice of the 16 KiB block its connection's reader read it into,
/// and keeps that block: 128 MiB at most (65,536 of them were 1 GiB).
const MAX_PENDING: usize = 1 << 13;

/// how far back the busy cap reads the workers and the CPU quota (`WorkersBusy::sample_over`, `QuotaBusy::sample_over`):
/// long enough that one busy half second cuts no one's links, short enough for a server that fills up for good (the
/// cap goes down at most every 5 s anyway).  The workers were read a tick at a time until 2026-11-05: at 13,400
/// players on nfsu2.xyz, 65 % busy over minutes, a half second past 85 % every few minutes took every player from 54
/// links to 40, and back up 2 at a time.
const BUSY_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);

/// The hub on a thread of its own.
pub struct RoamHub {
    tx: mpsc::Sender<Cmd>,
    pending: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
    /// the hub's `crowded()`, `in_roam()`, `in_rooms()` and `crew_counts()` after its last tick, for /players (which
    /// must not wait for the hub's thread)
    crowded: Arc<AtomicBool>,
    in_roam: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
    in_rooms: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<u32, usize>>>,
    in_crews: Arc<Mutex<Vec<(u32, u32)>>>,
    /// the hub's `coop_seats()` after its last tick, for the server's `[players]` lines
    coop_seats: Arc<AtomicUsize>,
}

impl RoamHub {
    /// starts its thread; `log`: a console line (the cap's changes).  Called within the server's runtime, its busy
    /// measure is the runtime's workers' (the switch's) or a CPU quota's, the higher; outside one (tests), the
    /// process's over every core.
    pub fn spawn(o: RoamOptions, log: Arc<dyn Fn(&str) + Send + Sync>) -> Arc<RoamHub> {
        RoamHub::spawn_with(o, log, None)
    }

    /// `spawn`, with the claimed names (nfsu2-claims): a player under a name another keyphrase claimed plays alone
    pub fn spawn_with(o: RoamOptions, log: Arc<dyn Fn(&str) + Send + Sync>, claims: Option<Arc<nfsu2_claims::Claims>>) -> Arc<RoamHub> {
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
        let pending = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let busy: Box<dyn FnMut() -> f64 + Send> = match tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current() {
            Ok(rt) => {
                let mut b = WorkersBusy::new(&rt);
                let mut q = QuotaBusy::find();
                Box::new(move || b.sample_over(BUSY_WINDOW).max(q.as_mut().map_or(0.0, |q| q.sample_over(BUSY_WINDOW))))
            }
            Err(_) => {
                let mut b = Busy::new(std::thread::available_parallelism().map_or(1, |n| n.get()));
                Box::new(move || b.sample())
            }
        };
        let waiting = pending.clone();
        // random and never 0 (roam_core.c's decoder, as `wire::decode`, drops a datagram from sender 0)
        let id = nfsu2_util::rand::int(1, 0xFFFF_FFFF) as u32;
        let mut hub = Hub::new(o, Box::new(|| nfsu2_util::now_ms() as f64), busy, Box::new(move |l| log(l)), Box::new(|_, _| false), id);
        hub.set_claims(claims);
        // (made here, not on its thread: until its first tick crowded() is what the hub begins with)
        let crowded = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(hub.crowded()));
        let in_roam = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let in_rooms = Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new()));
        let in_crews = Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let coop_seats = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let (busy_now, roam_now, rooms_now, crews_now) = (crowded.clone(), in_roam.clone(), in_rooms.clone(), in_crews.clone());
        let coop_now = coop_seats.clone();
        std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("roam-hub".into())
            .spawn(move || run(hub, rx, &waiting, &busy_now, &roam_now, &rooms_now, &crews_now, &coop_now))
            .expect("a thread for the free-roam hub");
        Arc::new(RoamHub { tx, pending, crowded, in_roam, in_rooms, in_crews, coop_seats })
    }

    /// the hub's `crowded()`: free roam is busy, the cap is under `ask_cap` (as of the hub's last tick)
    pub fn crowded(&self) -> bool {
        self.crowded.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// the hub's `in_roam()`: how many browsers drive in free roam, or are paused there (as of the hub's last tick)
    pub fn in_roam(&self) -> usize {
        self.in_roam.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// the hub's `in_rooms()` of one room: how many browsers of the room (roam_core's rc_room_hash; 0 the main world;
    /// a race track's spot's: `track_room`) drive in free roam, or are paused there (as of the hub's last tick)
    pub fn in_room(&self, room: u32) -> usize {
        self.in_rooms.lock().map_or(0, |m| m.get(&room).copied().unwrap_or(0))
    }

    /// `in_room` of a world's room and of its race tracks' spots, together (`world_count`)
    pub fn in_world(&self, room: u32) -> usize {
        self.in_rooms.lock().map_or(0, |m| world_count(&m, room))
    }

    /// the hub's `in_crews()`: how many browsers drive in free roam, or are paused there, in each of these crews
    /// (roam_core's rc_room_hash of a crew's word; any room), in their order (as of the hub's last tick)
    pub fn in_crews(&self, crews: &[u32]) -> Vec<usize> {
        let counts = self.in_crews.lock();
        crews.iter().map(|&c| counts.as_ref().map_or(0, |t| hub::crew_count(t, c))).collect()
    }

    /// the hub's `coop_seats()`: how many second players of co-op free roam drive there, or are paused there (as of the
    /// hub's last tick)
    pub fn coop_seats(&self) -> usize {
        self.coop_seats.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
    }

    /// the switch's way to its browsers
    pub fn attach_switch(&self, send: SwitchSend) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Attach(send));
    }

    /// browser `vip`'s keyphrase `me` has these friends (their keyphrases): `Hub::friends`
    pub fn friends(&self, vip: u32, me: Arc<str>, owners: Vec<Arc<str>>) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Friends(vip, me, owners));
    }

    /// browser `vip`'s page plays in the room of this name: `Hub::room_name`
    pub fn room_name(&self, vip: u32, name: String) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::RoomName(vip, name));
    }

    /// browser `vip`'s game says its car was in the air in free roam for `secs`, and its page leaves the switch:
    /// `Hub::flew`
    pub fn flew(&self, vip: u32, secs: f64) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Flew(vip, secs));
    }

    /// the browser and keyphrase of the player under `name` that browser `vip`'s player is linked with now:
    /// `Hub::linked_with`
    pub fn linked_with(&self, vip: u32, name: String) -> oneshot::Receiver<Option<(u32, Option<Arc<str>>)>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Linked(vip, name, tx));
        rx
    }

    /// where each of these keyphrases plays in free roam: `Hub::whereabouts`
    pub fn whereabouts(&self, owners: Vec<Arc<str>>) -> oneshot::Receiver<Vec<Option<hub::Whereabouts>>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Where(owners, tx));
        rx
    }

    /// the race lobby browser `vip`'s player hosts, open now: `Hub::hosted`
    pub fn hosted(&self, vip: u32) -> oneshot::Receiver<Option<hub::Hosted>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Hosted(vip, tx));
        rx
    }
}

/// a panic in the hub (a bug) leaves the hub's thread running: the panic hook has printed it, the next frame or
/// tick goes on (Node would have died of the exception, and every player with it)
fn guard(f: impl FnOnce()) {
    let _ = catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(f));
}

/// The hub's thread: what the switch posts, in order, and a tick every tick_ms (the next one a tick_ms after this
/// one began).  It ends once the RoamHub is gone.
fn run(
    mut hub: Hub,
    rx: mpsc::Receiver<Cmd>,
    pending: &AtomicUsize,
    crowded: &AtomicBool,
    in_roam: &AtomicUsize,
    in_rooms: &Mutex<HashMap<u32, usize>>,
    in_crews: &Mutex<Vec<(u32, u32)>>,
    coop_seats: &AtomicUsize,
) {
    let every = Duration::from_millis(hub.options().tick_ms);
    let mut next = Some(Instant::now() + every);
    // the crews' counts made at a tick, then swapped with /players' (the two tables are kept: no allocation a tick)
    let mut crews = Vec::new();
    // how long the thread worked on ticks and frames since `since`: the hub hears how busy its thread was each second
    let (mut work, mut since) = (Duration::ZERO, Instant::now());
    loop {
        if since.elapsed() >= Duration::from_secs(1) {
            hub.set_thread_busy(work.as_secs_f64() / since.elapsed().as_secs_f64());
            (work, since) = (Duration::ZERO, Instant::now());
        }
        let cmd = match next {
            Some(at) => {
                let now = Instant::now();
                if now >= at {
                    guard(|| hub.tick());
                    work += now.elapsed();
                    crowded.store(hub.crowded(), Ordering::Relaxed);
                    in_roam.store(hub.in_roam(), Ordering::Relaxed);
                    coop_seats.store(hub.coop_seats(), Ordering::Relaxed);
                    let rooms = hub.in_rooms();
                    if let Ok(mut m) = in_rooms.lock() {
                        *m = rooms;
                    }
                    hub.crew_counts(&mut crews);
                    if let Ok(mut m) = in_crews.lock() {
                        std::mem::swap(&mut *m, &mut crews);
                    }
                    next = Some(now + every);
                    continue;
                }
                match rx.recv_timeout(at - now) {
                    Ok(c) => c,
                    Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => continue,
                    Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => return,
                }
            }
            None => match rx.recv() {
                Ok(c) => c,
                Err(_) => return,
            },
        };
        match cmd {
            Cmd::Frame(from, data, owner, client) => {
                pending.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                let t0 = Instant::now();
                guard(|| hub.frame_of(from, &data, owner.as_ref(), Some(&client)));
                work += t0.elapsed();
            }
            Cmd::Gone(vip) => guard(|| hub.peer_gone(vip)),
            Cmd::Attach(send) => hub.attach_switch(Box::new(move |vip, f| send(vip, f, None).sent())),
            Cmd::Info(tx) => guard(|| {
                let _ = tx.send(hub.info());
            }),
            Cmd::Vips(tx) => guard(|| {
                let _ = tx.send(hub.vips());
            }),
            Cmd::Blocks(vip, names) => guard(|| hub.blocks(vip, names)),
            Cmd::PageName(vip, name) => guard(|| hub.page_name(vip, name)),
            Cmd::OtherNames(tx) => guard(|| {
                let _ = tx.send(hub.other_names());
            }),
            Cmd::Pairs(tx) => guard(|| {
                let _ = tx.send(hub.link_pairs());
            }),
            Cmd::Friends(vip, me, owners) => guard(|| hub.friends(vip, me, owners)),
            Cmd::RoomName(vip, name) => guard(|| hub.room_name(vip, name)),
            Cmd::Flew(vip, secs) => guard(|| hub.flew(vip, secs)),
            Cmd::Linked(vip, name, tx) => guard(|| {
                let _ = tx.send(hub.linked_with(vip, &name));
            }),
            Cmd::Where(owners, tx) => guard(|| {
                let _ = tx.send(hub.whereabouts(&owners));
            }),
            Cmd::Hosted(vip, tx) => guard(|| {
                let _ = tx.send(hub.hosted(vip));
            }),
            Cmd::Stop => {
                // no more ticks, so no more lists: the switch's send goes too (it holds the switch, which holds
                // this hub)
                next = None;
                hub.attach_switch(Box::new(|_, _| false));
            }
        }
    }
}

impl Host for RoamHub {
    fn vip(&self) -> u32 {
        ROAM_HUB_VIP
    }
    fn name(&self) -> &str {
        "free-roam hub"
    }
    fn listed(&self) -> bool {
        false
    }
    fn frame(&self, from: u32, data: Bytes, ctx: FrameCtx) {
        // the hub's lists are charged to nobody; the owner is for the claimed names; the client, its site (an IPv6
        // /48) or else its address, for the races' clean wins (results.rs: one address's endpoints are one client)
        let (owner, client) = (ctx.owner, ctx.site.unwrap_or(ctx.group));
        if self.pending.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed) >= MAX_PENDING {
            self.pending.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
            return;
        }
        if self.tx.send(Cmd::Frame(from, data, owner, client)).is_err() {
            self.pending.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
    }
    fn peer_gone(&self, vip: u32) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Gone(vip));
    }
    fn info(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<serde_json::Value> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Info(tx));
        rx
    }
    fn vips(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<HashSet<u32>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Vips(tx));
        rx
    }
    fn blocks(&self, vip: u32, names: Vec<String>) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Blocks(vip, names));
    }
    fn page_name(&self, vip: u32, name: &str) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::PageName(vip, name.to_string()));
    }
    fn other_names(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<HashMap<u32, Vec<String>>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::OtherNames(tx));
        rx
    }
    fn link_pairs(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<Vec<(u32, u32)>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Pairs(tx));
        rx
    }
    fn stop(&self) {
        let _ = self.tx.send(Cmd::Stop);
    }
}

mod tests {

    // its spots' players: not another world's, not a spot of another world

        assert_eq!(track_room(0, 4605), 199_754_989);
        assert_eq!(track_room(0x1234_5678, 4301), 942_920_901);
        assert_eq!(track_room(0xFFFF_FFFF, 4201), 2_745_435_750);
        let w2 = 0xBEEF_0002;
        let counts = HashMap::from([(0, 5), (track_room(0, 4711), 2), (track_room(0, 4605), 1), (w2, 3), (track_room(w2, 4311), 4)]);
        assert_eq!(world_count(&counts, 0), 8);
        assert_eq!(world_count(&counts, w2), 7);
        assert_eq!(world_count(&counts, 0xBEEF_0003), 0);
        assert!(main_world(0) && main_world(track_room(0, 4711)) && main_world(track_room(0, 4605)));
        assert!(!main_world(w2) && !main_world(track_room(w2, 4311)));
    }

    // a hub whose thread is stuck holds MAX_PENDING frames and leaves out the rest; each may keep
    // its reader's block of 16 KiB alive, 128 MiB at most
    #[test]
    fn a_stuck_hub_holds_few_frames() {
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
        let hub = RoamHub {
            tx,
            pending: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
            crowded: Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)),
            in_roam: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
            in_rooms: Arc::new(Mutex::new(HashMap::new())),
            in_crews: Arc::new(Mutex::new(Vec::new())),
            coop_seats: Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)),
        };
        let ctx = FrameCtx { group: Arc::from("client"), site: None, cause: None, slot: None, owner: None, no_races: false };
        for _ in 0..100_000 {
            hub.frame(0x0A4D_0005, Bytes::from_static(b"a frame"), ctx.clone());
        }
        let held = rx.try_iter().filter(|c| matches!(c, Cmd::Frame(..))).count();
        assert_eq!(held, MAX_PENDING);
        assert!(held * (16 << 10) <= 128 << 20, "{held} frames, each a reader's block of 16 KiB");
    }

    // /players reads the hub's crowded() without its thread: as of the hub's last tick, and before the first one as
    // the hub begins (a hub of fewer links than `ask_cap` is busy from the start)
    #[test]
    fn what_players_reads_is_the_hubs_crowded() {
        let few = RoamHub::spawn(RoamOptions { degree: 16, ..RoamOptions::default() }, Arc::new(|_: &str| {}));
        assert!(few.crowded(), "16 links a player, under askCap 24: busy before any tick");
        let all = RoamHub::spawn(RoamOptions::default(), Arc::new(|_: &str| {}));
        assert!(!all.crowded(), "32 links a player");
        // a busy server: the cap down a quarter each tick (32, 24, 18), busy once it is under 24, and back once the
        // cap is (the thread's own loop, its ticks every 5 ms)
        let busy = Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(true));
        let b = busy.clone();
        let o = RoamOptions { tick_ms: 5, cap_down_ms: 1.0, cap_up_ms: 1.0, ..RoamOptions::default() };
        let hub = Hub::new(
            o,
            Box::new(|| nfsu2_util::now_ms() as f64),
            Box::new(move || if b.load(Ordering::Relaxed) { 0.95 } else { 0.1 }),
            Box::new(|_| {}),
            Box::new(|_, _| false),
            1,
        );
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
        let (pending, crowded) = (Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0)), Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false)));
        let c = crowded.clone();
        let t = std::thread::spawn(move || {
            run(hub, rx, &pending, &c, &AtomicUsize::new(0), &Mutex::new(HashMap::new()), &Mutex::new(Vec::new()), &AtomicUsize::new(0))
        });
        let until = |want: bool| {
            let t0 = Instant::now();
            while crowded.load(Ordering::Relaxed) != want {
                assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(5), "crowded {want}: not in 5 s");
                std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
            }
        };
        until(true);
        busy.store(false, Ordering::Relaxed);
        until(false);
        drop(tx);
        t.join().unwrap();
    }
}

//! The pieces the links are made of: the distance (Math.hypot as V8 computes it), the grid and its nearest-first walk
//! (Near), and the heap that merges the walks.  Together they give the pairs in the order a sort of every pair would,
//! bit for bit, ties included: the order decides between pairs at one distance, and so the links.

/// `Math.hypot(x, y, z)` as V8 computes it (scaled by the largest, Kahan's sum): the same distances as the Node hub,
/// so the same order of pairs.  (Rust never fuses the multiply and the subtraction into an FMA, nor does V8.)
pub(crate) fn hypot3(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> f64 {
    let abs = [x.abs(), y.abs(), z.abs()];
    let mut max = 0.0f64;
    let mut nan = false;
    for &v in &abs {
        if v.is_nan() {
            nan = true;
        } else if v > max {
            max = v;
        }
    }
    if max == f64::INFINITY {
        return f64::INFINITY;
    }
    if nan {
        return f64::NAN;
    }
    if max == 0.0 {
        return 0.0;
    }
    let (mut sum, mut compensation) = (0.0f64, 0.0f64);
    for &v in &abs {
        let n = v / max;
        let summand = n * n - compensation;
        let preliminary = sum + summand;
        compensation = (preliminary - sum) - summand;
        sum = preliminary;
    }
    sum.sqrt() * max
}

/// the distance of two positions: `hypot3` of their differences in x, y and z, in that order
#[inline]
pub(crate) fn distance(a: &[f64; 3], b: &[f64; 3]) -> f64 {
    hypot3(a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2])
}

/// A place as the links weigh it: x, y, the height, and how far up a player not in free roam counts (`prepare`:
/// RoamOptions::away_m, 0 in free roam).  The two stay apart: the height says whether two cars are on one road or on
/// two roads one above the other (`Level`), the "up" only puts a player in a shop farther off.
pub(crate) type Place = [f64; 4];

/// How the links weigh a gap in height that no road between two places explains.  A car on a highway and one on the
/// street under it are a few metres apart, and neither shows to the other; a link between them took a car's room from
/// one on the same road farther on.  A gap of up to `slack` metres, plus `grade` of the way across (a road up a hill,
/// a ramp, a car in the air over a bump), counts as it is, as it always did; each metre past that counts `k` metres
/// more.  So two cars on one road, however steep, weigh as before, and a car on a road above or below weighs as one
/// far off: linked when there is room, after the cars on its own road when there is not.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Level {
    pub(crate) slack: f64,
    pub(crate) grade: f64,
    pub(crate) k: f64,
    /// grade's square
    grade2: f64,
}

impl Default for Level {
    /// no gap weighs more than it is
    fn default() -> Level {
        Level::new(f64::INFINITY, 0.0, 0.0)
    }
}

impl Level {
    pub(crate) fn new(slack: f64, grade: f64, k: f64) -> Level {
        Level { slack, grade, k, grade2: grade * grade }
    }

    /// a gap in height `dz` as it counts, between two places `h2` apart across (the square of the distance in x and
    /// y); the same for (a, b) and (b, a), bit for bit.  Whether it is past what a road explains is found from the
    /// squares, both tests at once (one branch, nearly always the same way: a walk weighs every player of each cell it
    /// reads), and only a gap past it takes a root.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn gap(&self, h2: f64, dz: f64) -> f64 {
        let v = dz.abs();
        let over = v - self.slack;
        if (over <= 0.0) | (over * over <= self.grade2 * h2) {
            return v;
        }
        v + self.k * (over - self.grade * h2.sqrt()).max(0.0)
    }

    /// the third side of a pair's distance: the gap in height as it counts and the difference in "up"
    #[inline]
    fn up(&self, a: &Place, b: &Place, h2: f64) -> f64 {
        self.gap(h2, a[2] - b[2]) + (a[3] - b[3]).abs()
    }
}

/// How far apart two places count for the links: `hypot3` of their differences in x and y and of `Level::up`.  Never
/// less than the distance in x and y (the grid's walk needs that); for two places with no gap past the slack and one
/// "up", the distance of before, bit for bit.
#[inline]
pub(crate) fn weigh(a: &Place, b: &Place, l: &Level) -> f64 {
    let (dx, dy, dz) = (a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2]);
    if one_level(a, b, dz, l) {
        return hypot3(dx, dy, dz);
    }
    hypot3(dx, dy, l.up(a, b, dx * dx + dy * dy))
}

/// the square of `weigh`, rounded (within 1e-15 of it, as the square of a distance always was)
#[inline]
pub(crate) fn square(a: &Place, b: &Place, l: &Level) -> f64 {
    let (dx, dy, dz) = (a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2]);
    let h2 = dx * dx + dy * dy;
    if one_level(a, b, dz, l) {
        return h2 + dz * dz;
    }
    let u = l.up(a, b, h2);
    h2 + u * u
}

/// Two places within the slack of each other in height and alike "up": nearly every pair a walk weighs (a crowd on
/// one spot is on one road), which takes the sums of before and nothing more (`Level::up` gives the same: `dz` as it
/// is).  One test for both (one branch, nearly always the same way).
#[inline]
fn one_level(a: &Place, b: &Place, dz: f64, l: &Level) -> bool {
    (dz.abs() <= l.slack) & (a[3] == b[3])
}

/// A number's place in the order of numbers as a u64 (the sign flipped, a negative one's bits all flipped; -0 as 0,
/// which it equals).
#[inline]
pub(crate) fn order_key(d: f64) -> u64 {
    let b = (d + 0.0).to_bits();
    b ^ (((b as i64) >> 63) as u64 | 1 << 63)
}

/// Sorts (key, index) by key, and at one key by the order they were in: the stable sort of a room's pairs by
/// their place.  A stable radix sort (11 bits a pass, a pass that would move nothing skipped): every pair of 250
/// players is 31,000 of them, which a comparison sort took most of a tick over.  `tmp`: room to work in.
pub(crate) fn sort_stable(v: &mut Vec<(u64, u32)>, tmp: &mut Vec<(u64, u32)>) {
    const BITS: u32 = 11;
    const BUCKETS: usize = 1 << BITS;
    let n = v.len();
    if n < 64 {
        v.sort_by_key(|e| e.0);
        return;
    }
    tmp.clear();
    tmp.resize(n, (0, 0));
    let mut count = vec![0usize; BUCKETS];
    let mut shift = 0;
    while shift < 64 {
        count.iter_mut().for_each(|c| *c = 0);
        for e in v.iter() {
            count[(e.0 >> shift) as usize & (BUCKETS - 1)] += 1;
        }
        // every key has this digit: nothing would move
        if count.contains(&n) {
            shift += BITS;
            continue;
        }
        let mut at = 0;
        for c in count.iter_mut() {
            let k = *c;
            *c = at;
            at += k;
        }
        for e in v.iter() {
            let b = (e.0 >> shift) as usize & (BUCKETS - 1);
            tmp[count[b]] = *e;
            count[b] += 1;
        }
        std::mem::swap(v, tmp);
        shift += BITS;
    }
}

/// the grid: cells (x and y) for about 8 players each, 5 m at least
const PER_CELL: f64 = 8.0;
const MIN_CELL: f64 = 5.0;

/// The players of a room (indices into its list) by their cell in x and y, sized for PER_CELL players over the area
/// they span, and the cells they span.  The cells are an array over the span (positions are within 20 km and cells at
/// least 5 m, so the span is at most 8001 cells a side and the array at most n/8 + 32004 cells); a cell outside the
/// span is empty.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Grid {
    pub(crate) cell: f64,
    pub(crate) x1: i64,
    pub(crate) x2: i64,
    pub(crate) y1: i64,
    pub(crate) y2: i64,
    rows: i64,
    /// where each cell's players start in `members` (one more than the cells: the end)
    start: Vec<u32>,
    members: Vec<u32>,
    /// each member's position, in the order of `members`: a walk reads a cell's players one after another in memory
    /// (by the list they are anywhere, and the reads of their positions were most of a ring's time)
    mpos: Vec<Place>,
    /// where each cell's players end (`remove` takes players out: a cell's players in `start[c]..end[c]`); and by
    /// index in the list, each one's place in `members` and its cell
    end: Vec<u32>,
    at: Vec<u32>,
    cell_of: Vec<u32>,
    /// how its walks weigh a gap in height (`weigh`)
    level: Level,
}

impl Grid {
    /// the grid of every position in `pos`, its walks weighing gaps in height as `level` says
    pub(crate) fn build(&mut self, pos: &[Place], level: Level) {
        self.level = level;
        self.start.clear();
        self.members.clear();
        if pos.is_empty() {
            *self = Grid { cell: MIN_CELL, x2: -1, y2: -1, ..std::mem::take(self) };
            return;
        }
        let (mut w1, mut w2, mut h1, mut h2) = (f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::INFINITY, f64::NEG_INFINITY);
        for p in pos {
            w1 = w1.min(p[0]);
            w2 = w2.max(p[0]);
            h1 = h1.min(p[1]);
            h2 = h2.max(p[1]);
        }
        let cell = MIN_CELL.max((1f64.max(w2 - w1) * 1f64.max(h2 - h1) * PER_CELL / pos.len() as f64).sqrt());
        self.cell = cell;
        self.x1 = (w1 / cell).floor() as i64;
        self.x2 = (w2 / cell).floor() as i64;
        self.y1 = (h1 / cell).floor() as i64;
        self.y2 = (h2 / cell).floor() as i64;
        self.rows = self.y2 - self.y1 + 1;
        let cells = ((self.x2 - self.x1 + 1) * self.rows) as usize;
        // counted, then placed (a counting sort): each cell's players in the order of the list
        self.start.clear();
        self.start.resize(cells + 1, 0);
        for p in pos {
            let c = self.index(p);
            self.start[c + 1] += 1;
        }
        for c in 0..cells {
            self.start[c + 1] += self.start[c];
        }
        self.members.clear();
        self.members.resize(pos.len(), 0);
        self.at.clear();
        self.at.resize(pos.len(), 0);
        self.cell_of.clear();
        for (i, p) in pos.iter().enumerate() {
            let c = self.index(p);
            // `start[c]` moves on as the cell fills: afterwards each start is the next cell's
            self.members[self.start[c] as usize] = i as u32;
            self.at[i] = self.start[c];
            self.cell_of.push(c as u32);
            self.start[c] += 1;
        }
        self.end.clear();
        self.end.extend_from_slice(&self.start[..cells]);
        for c in (1..=cells).rev() {
            self.start[c] = self.start[c - 1];
        }
        self.start[0] = 0;
        self.mpos.clear();
        self.mpos.extend(self.members.iter().map(|&i| pos[i as usize]));
    }

    /// Takes list[i] out: the walks read from then on pass it by (a player whose links are full, which no pair can link
    /// any more: `link_many`).  Its cell's last one takes its place; the order a cell's players are read in makes no
    /// difference to a walk.  Once out, it stays out until the next `build`.
    pub(crate) fn remove(&mut self, i: u32) {
        let (Some(&c), Some(&p)) = (self.cell_of.get(i as usize), self.at.get(i as usize)) else { return };
        let (c, p) = (c as usize, p as usize);
        let last = self.end[c] as usize;
        if p >= last {
            return;
        }
        let last = last - 1;
        let j = self.members[last];
        self.members.swap(p, last);
        self.mpos.swap(p, last);
        self.at[j as usize] = p as u32;
        self.at[i as usize] = last as u32;
        self.end[c] -= 1;
    }

    fn index(&self, p: &Place) -> usize {
        let (x, y) = ((p[0] / self.cell).floor() as i64, (p[1] / self.cell).floor() as i64);
        ((x - self.x1) * self.rows + (y - self.y1)) as usize
    }

    /// the players of cell (x, y) and their positions: none outside the span
    fn cell(&self, x: i64, y: i64) -> (&[u32], &[Place]) {
        if x < self.x1 || x > self.x2 || y < self.y1 || y > self.y2 {
            return (&[], &[]);
        }
        let c = ((x - self.x1) * self.rows + (y - self.y1)) as usize;
        let (a, z) = (self.start[c] as usize, self.end[c] as usize);
        (&self.members[a..z], &self.mpos[a..z])
    }
}

/// list[i]'s others in the grid, nearest first (`next()` gives (distance, j), or None after the last; at one
/// distance the lowest j first): ring after ring of cells around its own; one found is the nearest left once the
/// next ring is farther (a cell r rings away is at least r - 1 cells off).
///
/// A plain walk sorts what it found after each ring and takes the nearest off the end.  Here what
/// is found waits in a pool, in no order; once the ones within reach of the rings read (r - 1 cells) are all given,
/// the next ring is read and those within its reach move to `ready`, still in no order, and of those only the
/// nearest `CHUNK` at a time are put in order (`next`): of the 100 to 200 a player finds it takes 30 or 40 (in a
/// crowd on one spot, of 2000 within reach), so most are never sorted.  The same order, step for step: the nearest
/// found is in `next` or `ready` whenever any is within reach (every j is found once, so the order by distance,
/// then j, is total), and a ring is read exactly when a plain walk reads it, when none found is within reach.
///
/// Nor is the distance (Math.hypot as V8 computes it, three divisions) worked out for most.  The pool and `ready`
/// keep the square of the distance (rounded, within 1e-15 of the true one).  Where the reach decides, only a square
/// within 1e-9 of the reach's (a margin far wider than either rounding) needs the distance itself; where the
/// nearest CHUNK are taken, the distance of those and of the ones about as near (by the same margin), and of those
/// only the ones clearly nearer than the rest go into `next`.  A distance is never negative, so its bits are in its
/// order.
pub(crate) struct Near {
    i: u32,
    /// where the walk is from: list[i]'s position, or a point of its own (`from`)
    at: Place,
    /// how it weighs a gap in height (its grid's)
    level: Level,
    x0: i64,
    y0: i64,
    last: i64,
    r: i64,
    found: Found,
}

/// The ready ones put in order at a time (a player's links at most, 32: most take no more)
const CHUNK: usize = 32;
/// How far one square may be from another, relatively, and still be taken for the same distance: squares are
/// rounded by 1e-15 at most, Math.hypot by less; a square farther than this is a distance farther, for sure.
const MARGIN: f64 = 1e-9;

/// What a Near found and has not given yet.  Its vectors are kept from tick to tick.
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Found {
    /// beyond the reach of the rings read so far, in no order: (the square of the distance, j)
    pool: Vec<(f64, u32)>,
    /// within it, in no order: (the square of the distance, j), each farther than every one in `next`
    ready: Vec<(f64, u32)>,
    /// the nearest of the ones within reach, in order, the nearest last: (the distance's bits, j)
    next: Vec<(u64, u32)>,
}

impl Near {
    /// `found`: empty vectors to keep them in (reused from tick to tick)
    pub(crate) fn new(g: &Grid, pos: &[Place], i: u32, found: Found) -> Near {
        Near::from(g, pos[i as usize], i, found)
    }

    /// the others of list[i] nearest first from point `at` (weigh(at, pos[j])), not from its own position
    pub(crate) fn from(g: &Grid, at: Place, i: u32, found: Found) -> Near {
        let (x0, y0) = ((at[0] / g.cell).floor() as i64, (at[1] / g.cell).floor() as i64);
        let last = (x0 - g.x1).max(g.x2 - x0).max(y0 - g.y1).max(g.y2 - y0);
        Near { i, at, level: g.level, x0, y0, last, r: 0, found }
    }

    /// its vectors back (emptied), for the next tick
    pub(crate) fn into_found(self) -> Found {
        let mut f = self.found;
        f.pool.clear();
        f.ready.clear();
        f.next.clear();
        f
    }

    pub(crate) fn next(&mut self, g: &Grid, pos: &[Place]) -> Option<(f64, u32)> {
        loop {
            if let Some((d, j)) = self.found.next.pop() {
                return Some((f64::from_bits(d), j));
            }
            if !self.found.ready.is_empty() {
                self.order(pos);
                continue;
            }
            // none found is within reach of the rings read (a plain walk's test of its nearest): the next ring, or
            // once every ring is read, all that is left
            let reach = if self.r <= self.last { self.r as f64 * g.cell } else { f64::INFINITY };
            if reach == f64::INFINITY && self.found.pool.is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
            let w = Within::new(reach);
            let (a, l) = (&self.at, &self.level);
            let Found { pool, ready, .. } = &mut self.found;
            pool.retain(|&(sq, j)| {
                if w.beyond(sq, || weigh(a, &pos[j as usize], l)) {
                    return true;
                }
                ready.push((sq, j));
                false
            });
            // the ring's own go where they belong as they are read
            if self.r <= self.last {
                self.ring(g, self.r, &w);
                self.r += 1;
            }
        }
    }

    /// The nearest CHUNK of the ready ones (or all, when they are few) into `next`, in order.  The CHUNK-th nearest
    /// by its square, s: every one whose square is under s (1 + MARGIN) has its distance worked out, and the ones
    /// within sqrt(s) (1 + MARGIN / 5) go: the CHUNK nearest by their squares are among them (their distances are at
    /// most sqrt(s) (1 + 2e-15)), and every one left is farther (a square over s (1 + MARGIN) is a distance over
    /// sqrt(s) (1 + MARGIN / 2.1)).
    fn order(&mut self, pos: &[Place]) {
        let (a, l) = (&self.at, &self.level);
        let Found { ready, next, .. } = &mut self.found;
        if ready.len() <= 2 * CHUNK {
            next.extend(ready.drain(..).map(|(_, j)| (weigh(a, &pos[j as usize], l).to_bits(), j)));
        } else {
            ready.select_nth_unstable_by(CHUNK - 1, |x, y| x.0.total_cmp(&y.0));
            let s = ready[CHUNK - 1].0;
            let (far, within) = (s * (1.0 + MARGIN), s.sqrt() * (1.0 + MARGIN / 5.0));
            ready.retain(|&(sq, j)| {
                if sq > far {
                    return true;
                }
                let d = weigh(a, &pos[j as usize], l);
                if d > within {
                    return true;
                }
                next.push((d.to_bits(), j));
                false
            });
        }
        next.sort_unstable_by(|x, y| y.cmp(x));
    }

    /// the cells r rings around its own (the order they are read in does not matter: what they give is ordered);
    /// the rows and columns outside the grid's span are skipped, as they hold nobody
    fn ring(&mut self, g: &Grid, r: i64, w: &Within) {
        let (x0, y0) = (self.x0, self.y0);
        if r == 0 {
            self.cell(g, x0, y0, w);
            return;
        }
        let (xa, xb) = ((x0 - r).max(g.x1), (x0 + r).min(g.x2));
        for y in [y0 - r, y0 + r] {
            if y >= g.y1 && y <= g.y2 {
                for x in xa..=xb {
                    self.cell(g, x, y, w);
                }
            }
        }
        let (ya, yb) = ((y0 - r + 1).max(g.y1), (y0 + r - 1).min(g.y2));
        for x in [x0 - r, x0 + r] {
            if x >= g.x1 && x <= g.x2 {
                for y in ya..=yb {
                    self.cell(g, x, y, w);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// a cell's players into the pool, or into `ready` when they are within reach of the ring being read
    fn cell(&mut self, g: &Grid, x: i64, y: i64, w: &Within) {
        let (a, l) = (&self.at, &self.level);
        let Found { pool, ready, .. } = &mut self.found;
        let (members, mpos) = g.cell(x, y);
        for (&j, b) in members.iter().zip(mpos) {
            if j != self.i {
                let sq = square(a, b, l);
                if w.beyond(sq, || weigh(a, b, l)) { pool.push((sq, j)) } else { ready.push((sq, j)) }
            }
        }
    }
}

/// Whether a square of a distance is a distance within `reach`: under `near` it is, over `far` it is not, between
/// the two the distance decides.
struct Within {
    reach: f64,
    near: f64,
    far: f64,
}

impl Within {
    fn new(reach: f64) -> Within {
        Within { reach, near: reach * reach * (1.0 - MARGIN), far: reach * reach * (1.0 + MARGIN) }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn beyond(&self, sq: f64, distance: impl FnOnce() -> f64) -> bool {
        sq > self.far || (sq >= self.near && distance() > self.reach)
    }
}

/// An entry of the order a large room's pairs are taken in: `(d, min(i, j), max(i, j), i, j, since, nearest)` in 16
/// bytes (a room of 2000 players has 34,000 of them).  `key` is `min << 34 | max << 4`, which walk found it (2 bits)
/// and two flags: whether this is i's nearest one (else a link of the last tick) and whether i is the higher one.
/// The order of `key >> 4` is the order of (min, max), and the walk and the flags take no part in it.  `since` is not
/// kept: it is the tick's time for a nearest one, and for a link of the last tick that link's (i's links do not change
/// in the tick).  Places in a room are below 2^30.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
pub(crate) struct Cand {
    pub(crate) d: f64,
    key: u64,
}

const I_HIGH: u64 = 1;
const NEAREST: u64 = 2;
const MASK: u64 = (1 << 30) - 1;

/// the walks a player's nearest ones come from (`link_many`): by the places soon, by the places ahead, and from its
/// view point to the others' places soon
pub(crate) const WALK_SOON: u8 = 0;
pub(crate) const WALK_AHEAD: u8 = 1;
pub(crate) const WALK_VIEW: u8 = 2;

impl Cand {
    pub(crate) fn new(d: f64, i: u32, j: u32, nearest: bool) -> Cand {
        let (lo, hi) = (i.min(j) as u64 & MASK, i.max(j) as u64 & MASK);
        Cand { d, key: lo << 34 | hi << 4 | if nearest { NEAREST } else { 0 } | if i > j { I_HIGH } else { 0 } }
    }
    /// i's nearest one of walk `walk`
    pub(crate) fn by(d: f64, i: u32, j: u32, walk: u8) -> Cand {
        let mut c = Cand::new(d, i, j, true);
        c.key |= (walk as u64 & 3) << 2;
        c
    }
    fn lo(&self) -> u32 {
        (self.key >> 34) as u32
    }
    fn hi(&self) -> u32 {
        ((self.key >> 4) & MASK) as u32
    }
    pub(crate) fn i(&self) -> u32 {
        if self.key & I_HIGH != 0 { self.hi() } else { self.lo() }
    }
    pub(crate) fn j(&self) -> u32 {
        if self.key & I_HIGH != 0 { self.lo() } else { self.hi() }
    }
    pub(crate) fn nearest(&self) -> bool {
        self.key & NEAREST != 0
    }
    /// the walk of a nearest one
    pub(crate) fn walk(&self) -> u8 {
        (self.key >> 2 & 3) as u8
    }
    /// (min(i, j), max(i, j)) in one number, in their order
    pub(crate) fn pair(&self) -> u64 {
        self.key >> 4
    }
}

/// the least by d, then min(i, j), then max(i, j)
#[inline]
pub(crate) fn before(x: &Cand, y: &Cand) -> bool {
    x.d < y.d || (x.d == y.d && x.key >> 4 < y.key >> 4)
}

/// A binary heap, the least on top: each player's nearest one not taken yet (`link_many`, which says
/// why entries equal in (d, lo, hi) may come out in any order).
#[derive(Default)]
pub(crate) struct Heap {
    a: Vec<Cand>,
}

impl Heap {
    pub(crate) fn clear(&mut self) {
        self.a.clear();
    }

    pub(crate) fn peek(&self) -> Option<&Cand> {
        self.a.first()
    }

    pub(crate) fn push(&mut self, e: Cand) {
        let a = &mut self.a;
        a.push(e);
        let mut k = a.len() - 1;
        while k > 0 {
            let up = (k - 1) >> 1;
            if !before(&e, &a[up]) {
                break;
            }
            a[k] = a[up];
            k = up;
        }
        a[k] = e;
    }

    pub(crate) fn pop(&mut self) -> Option<Cand> {
        let a = &mut self.a;
        let top = *a.first()?;
        let e = a.pop()?;
        if !a.is_empty() {
            let mut k = 0;
            loop {
                let mut c = 2 * k + 1;
                if c >= a.len() {
                    break;
                }
                if c + 1 < a.len() && before(&a[c + 1], &a[c]) {
                    c += 1;
                }
                if !before(&a[c], &e) {
                    break;
                }
                a[k] = a[c];
                k = c;
            }
            a[k] = e;
        }
        Some(top)
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn hypot_as_v8() {
        assert_eq!(hypot3(3.0, 4.0, 0.0), 5.0);
        assert_eq!(hypot3(0.0, -0.0, 0.0), 0.0);
        assert!(hypot3(f64::NAN, 1.0, 0.0).is_nan());
        assert_eq!(hypot3(f64::NAN, f64::NEG_INFINITY, 0.0), f64::INFINITY);
    }

    #[test]
    fn sorts_as_a_stable_sort_by_the_number() {
        let mut seed = 1u64;
        let mut rnd = || {
            seed = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);
            seed >> 33
        };
        for n in [0, 1, 5, 63, 64, 65, 1000, 31125] {
            let ds: Vec<f64> = (0..n)
                .map(|_| match rnd() % 6 {
                    0 => -1.0,
                    1 => 0.0,
                    2 => -0.0,
                    3 => (rnd() % 50) as f64 * 0.5,
                    4 => rnd() as f64 * 1e-3,
                    _ => rnd() as f64 * 1e6,
                })
                .collect();
            let mut v: Vec<(u64, u32)> = ds.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, &d)| (order_key(d), i as u32)).collect();
            sort_stable(&mut v, &mut Vec::new());
            let mut want: Vec<u32> = (0..n as u32).collect();
            // a stable comparison sort by the number
            want.sort_by(|&x, &y| ds[x as usize].partial_cmp(&ds[y as usize]).unwrap());
            assert_eq!(v.iter().map(|e| e.1).collect::<Vec<_>>(), want, "{n}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn heap_gives_the_least_first() {
        let mut h = Heap::default();
        for (d, i, j, nearest) in [(3.0, 1, 2, false), (1.0, 6, 5, true), (1.0, 2, 9, false), (-1.0, 7, 8, true), (1.0, 3, 2, false)] {
            h.push(Cand::new(d, i, j, nearest));
        }
        let order: Vec<(f64, u32, u32, bool)> = std::iter::from_fn(|| h.pop()).map(|e| (e.d, e.i(), e.j(), e.nearest())).collect();
        assert_eq!(order, [(-1.0, 7, 8, true), (1.0, 3, 2, false), (1.0, 2, 9, false), (1.0, 6, 5, true), (3.0, 1, 2, false)]);
        let big = Cand::new(0.5, (1 << 30) - 1, (1 << 30) - 2, true);
        assert_eq!((big.i(), big.j(), big.nearest(), big.walk()), ((1 << 30) - 1, (1 << 30) - 2, true, WALK_SOON));
        let a = Cand::by(0.5, 4, 9, WALK_AHEAD);
        assert_eq!((a.i(), a.j(), a.nearest(), a.walk(), a.pair()), (4, 9, true, WALK_AHEAD, Cand::new(0.5, 9, 4, false).pair()));
        let v = Cand::by(0.5, (1 << 30) - 1, 3, WALK_VIEW);
        assert_eq!((v.i(), v.j(), v.nearest(), v.walk()), ((1 << 30) - 1, 3, true, WALK_VIEW));
    }

    /// the hub's rule (RoamOptions level_*)
    const STEEP: Level = Level { slack: 5.0, grade: 0.2, k: 25.0, grade2: 0.2 * 0.2 };

    /// every other of list[i] (but i) from `from` by (weigh, j), as a sort of them all gives them
    fn sorted(pos: &[Place], i: u32, from: &Place, l: &Level) -> Vec<(f64, u32)> {
        let mut want: Vec<(f64, u32)> = (0..pos.len() as u32).filter(|&j| j != i).map(|j| (weigh(from, &pos[j as usize], l), j)).collect();
        want.sort_by(|x, y| x.0.total_cmp(&y.0).then(x.1.cmp(&y.1)));
        want
    }

    /// each one's walk gives the others as `sorted` does, bit for bit
    fn walks_as_sorted(pos: &[Place], l: Level) {
        let mut g = Grid::default();
        g.build(pos, l);
        for i in 0..pos.len() as u32 {
            let mut n = Near::new(&g, pos, i, Found::default());
            let got: Vec<(f64, u32)> = std::iter::from_fn(|| n.next(&g, pos)).collect();
            let want = sorted(pos, i, &pos[i as usize], &l);
            assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "{} players, player {i}, {l:?}", pos.len());
            assert!(
                got.iter().zip(&want).all(|(a, b)| a.0.to_bits() == b.0.to_bits() && a.1 == b.1),
                "{} players, player {i}, {l:?}",
                pos.len()
            );
        }
    }

    /// a place in free roam (nothing "up")
    fn at(x: f64, y: f64, z: f64) -> Place {
        [x, y, z, 0.0]
    }

    #[test]
    fn near_walks_nearest_first() {
        let pos: Vec<Place> = (0..50).map(|i| at((i * 7 % 50) as f64 * 3.0, (i * 11 % 50) as f64 * 2.0, 0.0)).collect();
        for l in [Level::default(), STEEP] {
            walks_as_sorted(&pos, l);
        }
    }

    // the walk on lattices whose points sit on the cells' edges (distances of exactly the reach, 5 m cells), on a few
    // spots (players at one place), and on scattered float32 positions near and far: all others by (distance, j); and
    // the same with roads over roads (a lattice at 0 m and one 6 to 30 m over it; a highway over streets with a hill
    // and players in a shop), where gaps in height weigh more than they are
    #[test]
    fn near_walks_nearest_first_at_the_edges() {
        let mut seed = 7u64;
        let mut rnd = || {
            seed = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);
            (seed >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64
        };
        let lattice = |n: usize, step: f64, z: f64| -> Vec<Place> {
            (0..n * n).map(|k| at((k % n) as f64 * step, (k / n) as f64 * step, z)).collect()
        };
        let mut layouts = vec![lattice(10, 1.0, 0.0), lattice(12, 5.0, 0.0), lattice(9, 2.5, 0.0)];
        layouts.push((0..120).map(|k| [at(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), at(5.0, 0.0, 0.0), at(0.0, 10.0, 1.0)][k % 3]).collect());
        layouts.push(
            (0..300)
                .map(|k| {
                    let r = if k % 10 == 0 { 15000.0 } else { 400.0 };
                    [(rnd() * 2.0 - 1.0) * r, (rnd() * 2.0 - 1.0) * r, rnd() * 20.0, 0.0].map(|x| x as f32 as f64)
                })
                .collect(),
        );
        for (n, step, up) in [(10, 5.0, 6.0), (12, 2.5, 10.0), (8, 5.0, 30.0)] {
            let mut two = lattice(n, step, 0.0);
            two.extend(lattice(n, step, up));
            layouts.push(two);
        }
        layouts.push(
            (0..400)
                .map(|k| {
                    let (x, y) = ((rnd() * 2.0 - 1.0) * 300.0, (rnd() * 2.0 - 1.0) * 300.0);
                    let z = match k % 4 {
                        0 => 12.0,
                        1 => 0.2 * x.abs(),
                        _ => rnd() * 2.0,
                    };
                    [x, y, z, if k % 9 == 0 { 100.0 } else { 0.0 }].map(|v| v as f32 as f64)
                })
                .collect(),
        );
        for pos in &layouts {
            for l in [Level::default(), STEEP] {
                walks_as_sorted(pos, l);
            }
        }
    }

    // from a point of its own (inside the players' span, on a cell's edge, far outside it, above them, in a shop): all
    // others but i by (weigh(from, pos[j]), j)
    #[test]
    fn near_walks_nearest_first_from_a_point() {
        let pos: Vec<Place> = (0..80).map(|i| at((i * 7 % 40) as f64 * 5.0, (i * 13 % 40) as f64 * 2.5, (i % 3) as f64 * 7.0)).collect();
        let froms = [
            (0u32, at(37.5, 20.0, 1.0)),
            (5, at(15.0, 10.0, 0.0)),
            (79, at(-400.0, 900.0, 100.0)),
            (12, at(190.0, -3.0, 0.0)),
            (3, [60.0, 40.0, 14.0, 100.0]),
        ];
        for l in [Level::default(), STEEP] {
            let mut g = Grid::default();
            g.build(&pos, l);
            for (i, from) in froms {
                let mut n = Near::from(&g, from, i, Found::default());
                let got: Vec<(f64, u32)> = std::iter::from_fn(|| n.next(&g, &pos)).collect();
                let want = sorted(&pos, i, &from, &l);
                assert_eq!(got.len(), want.len(), "from {from:?}");
                assert!(got.iter().zip(&want).all(|(a, b)| a.0.to_bits() == b.0.to_bits() && a.1 == b.1), "from {from:?}");
            }
        }
    }

    // two places with no gap past what a road explains, and the same "up", weigh what their distance always was, bit
    // for bit; any two weigh the same both ways, never less than their distance in x and y, and their square is the
    // weight's
    #[test]
    fn weighs_as_the_distance_on_one_road() {
        let mut seed = 3u64;
        let mut rnd = || {
            seed = seed.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);
            (seed >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64
        };
        for _ in 0..20000 {
            let up = |r: f64| if r < 0.2 { 100.0 } else { 0.0 };
            let a = [(rnd() - 0.5) * 6000.0, (rnd() - 0.5) * 6000.0, rnd() * 60.0, up(rnd())].map(|v| v as f32 as f64);
            let b = [a[0] + (rnd() - 0.5) * 400.0, a[1] + (rnd() - 0.5) * 400.0, a[2] + (rnd() - 0.5) * 40.0, up(rnd())]
                .map(|v| v as f32 as f64);
            for l in [Level::default(), STEEP] {
                let d = weigh(&a, &b, &l);
                let across = (a[0] - b[0]).hypot(a[1] - b[1]);
                assert_eq!(d.to_bits(), weigh(&b, &a, &l).to_bits(), "{a:?} {b:?}");
                assert_eq!(square(&a, &b, &l).to_bits(), square(&b, &a, &l).to_bits(), "{a:?} {b:?}");
                assert!(d >= across * (1.0 - 1e-15), "{a:?} {b:?}");
                assert!((square(&a, &b, &l) - d * d).abs() <= d * d * 1e-14, "{a:?} {b:?}");
                if (a[2] - b[2]).abs() <= l.slack + l.grade * across && a[3] == b[3] {
                    let (x, y) = ([a[0], a[1], a[2]], [b[0], b[1], b[2]]);
                    assert_eq!(d.to_bits(), distance(&x, &y).to_bits(), "{a:?} {b:?}");
                    let (dx, dy, dz) = (a[0] - b[0], a[1] - b[1], a[2] - b[2]);
                    assert_eq!(square(&a, &b, &l).to_bits(), (dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz).to_bits(), "{a:?} {b:?}");
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // what gaps weigh: a road up a hill as it is; the street under a highway (10 m below) as a car 135 m off, less
    // to the side, as it is once in sight; a car 4 m up over a bump beside ours as it is; a player in a shop 100 m up
    #[test]
    fn weighs_a_road_above_as_one_far_off() {
        let w = |a: Place, b: Place| (weigh(&a, &b, &STEEP) * 10.0).round() / 10.0;
        assert_eq!(w(at(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), at(100.0, 0.0, 20.0)), 102.0);
        assert_eq!(w(at(0.0, 0.0, 10.0), at(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)), 135.0);
        assert_eq!(w(at(0.0, 0.0, 10.0), at(8.0, 0.0, 0.0)), 95.3);
        assert_eq!(w(at(0.0, 0.0, 10.0), at(40.0, 0.0, 0.0)), 41.2);
        assert_eq!(w(at(0.0, 0.0, 4.0), at(3.0, 0.0, 0.0)), 5.0);
        assert_eq!(w([0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 100.0], at(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)), 100.0);
        assert_eq!(w([30.0, 0.0, 2.0, 100.0], [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 100.0]), 30.1);
    }
}
