//! How busy the server is, 0 to 1.  Node read its one thread's event-loop use.  Here the switch's work is spread over
//! the runtime's worker threads, which are only some of the cores (half of them, 2 to 8), so the measure that says
//! whether the switch keeps up is theirs: [`WorkersBusy`], the share of the workers' time they spent running tasks.
//! [`Busy`], the process's CPU time over a number of cores, is for a hub with no runtime (the tests).  [`QuotaBusy`]:
//! the share of a CPU quota the server shares with others (the game's containers in nfsu2.slice) they used together.

use std::collections::VecDeque;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// CPU seconds (user + system) the process has used.
pub fn process_cpu_seconds() -> f64 {
    // SAFETY: getrusage only writes the struct it is given
    unsafe {
        let mut u: libc::rusage = std::mem::zeroed();
        if libc::getrusage(libc::RUSAGE_SELF, &mut u) != 0 {
            return 0.0;
        }
        let tv = |t: libc::timeval| t.tv_sec as f64 + t.tv_usec as f64 / 1e6;
        tv(u.ru_utime) + tv(u.ru_stime)
    }
}

/// Resident memory in bytes (Linux: /proc/self/statm), 0 where it cannot be read.
pub fn resident_bytes() -> u64 {
    let Ok(s) = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/statm") else { return 0 };
    let pages: u64 = s.split_whitespace().nth(1).and_then(|x| x.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0);
    // SAFETY: sysconf has no preconditions
    let page = unsafe { libc::sysconf(libc::_SC_PAGESIZE) };
    pages * if page > 0 { page as u64 } else { 4096 }
}

/// The share of `threads` cores the process used between one `sample()` and the next.
pub struct Busy {
    threads: f64,
    cpu: f64,
    at: Instant,
}

impl Busy {
    pub fn new(threads: usize) -> Self {
        Busy { threads: threads.max(1) as f64, cpu: process_cpu_seconds(), at: Instant::now() }
    }
    /// 0 to 1 since the last call
    pub fn sample(&mut self) -> f64 {
        let cpu = process_cpu_seconds();
        let now = Instant::now();
        let wall = now.duration_since(self.at).as_secs_f64();
        let used = cpu - self.cpu;
        self.cpu = cpu;
        self.at = now;
        if wall <= 0.0 {
            return 0.0;
        }
        (used / (wall * self.threads)).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
    }
}

/// The share of a tokio runtime's worker threads' time they spent running tasks between one `sample()` and the next
/// (tokio's busy duration: a worker that waits for work, or looks for some to steal, is idle), the event-loop use of
/// the workers together.  Wall time, not CPU time: a worker the OS does not run while it has tasks is not keeping up
/// either.  The CPU time of the whole process over every core could not tell: workers that are all busy are half
/// of it at most, and the cap on the links never came down.
pub struct WorkersBusy {
    metrics: tokio::runtime::RuntimeMetrics,
    busy: Duration,
    at: Instant,
    /// `sample_over`'s samples
    recent: Recent,
}

impl WorkersBusy {
    pub fn new(rt: &tokio::runtime::Handle) -> Self {
        let metrics = rt.metrics();
        let busy = Self::total(&metrics);
        WorkersBusy { metrics, busy, at: Instant::now(), recent: Recent::default() }
    }

    fn total(m: &tokio::runtime::RuntimeMetrics) -> Duration {
        (0..m.num_workers()).map(|w| m.worker_total_busy_duration(w)).sum()
    }

    /// 0 to 1 since the last call
    pub fn sample(&mut self) -> f64 {
        self.sample_wall().1
    }

    /// 0 to 1 over about the last `window`: what `sample` says of each call since then, each by its share of the time.
    /// The workers' share is of wall time (a task's time on a worker counts while the kernel runs something else on
    /// its core), so a half second in which the box had more to run than it has cores went up past 90 % with 65 % for
    /// minutes around it (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-11-05, 13,400 players): over seconds, such a moment is one among many.
    pub fn sample_over(&mut self, window: Duration) -> f64 {
        let (wall, share) = self.sample_wall();
        self.recent.add(wall, share, window)
    }

    /// the seconds since the last call, and the share of them the workers were busy
    fn sample_wall(&mut self) -> (f64, f64) {
        let busy = Self::total(&self.metrics);
        let now = Instant::now();
        let secs = now.duration_since(self.at).as_secs_f64();
        let wall = secs * self.metrics.num_workers().max(1) as f64;
        let used = busy.saturating_sub(self.busy).as_secs_f64();
        self.busy = busy;
        self.at = now;
        if wall <= 0.0 {
            return (0.0, 0.0);
        }
        (secs, (used / wall).clamp(0.0, 1.0))
    }
}

/// Samples of a share (0 to 1), each with the seconds it covers, oldest first: their mean, each by its seconds, over
/// about the last window (at least the newest sample, however long)
#[derive(Default)]
struct Recent(VecDeque<(f64, f64)>);

impl Recent {
    fn add(&mut self, secs: f64, share: f64, window: Duration) -> f64 {
        if secs > 0.0 {
            self.0.push_back((secs, share));
        }
        let mut total: f64 = self.0.iter().map(|r| r.0).sum();
        while self.0.len() > 1 && total - self.0[0].0 >= window.as_secs_f64() {
            total -= self.0.pop_front().map_or(0.0, |r| r.0);
        }
        if total <= 0.0 {
            return 0.0;
        }
        self.0.iter().map(|&(t, s)| t * s).sum::<f64>() / total
    }
}

/// The CPU quotas of the process's cgroups (cgroup v2): its own group's and every parent's `cpu.max`, with the CPU
/// time each group used (`cpu.stat`'s usage_usec).  A quota is for a group's processes together: the game's containers
/// share nfsu2.slice's 14 cores (web/deploy/nfsu2.slice), and at 2,001 players cloudflared took three quarters of the
/// 4.5 they used while the switch's workers were 13 % busy (nfsu2.xyz, 2026-10-24): the workers' measure alone never
/// sees the slice fill up.  A container sees its parents only in the VPS's cgroup namespace (compose.yml's `cgroup:
/// host`); in one of its own it sees itself alone.  Each sample reads the quotas again: `systemctl set-property`
/// changes one while the server runs.
pub struct QuotaBusy {
    /// each group's folder, its path in the cgroup tree, and its usage_usec at the last sample
    groups: Vec<(PathBuf, String, u64)>,
    at: Instant,
    /// `sample_over`'s samples: each one's seconds and the fullest quota's share in them
    recent: Recent,
}

/// What the group with the fullest quota used between two samples.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct QuotaUse {
    /// its path in the cgroup tree ("/nfsu2.slice")
    pub group: String,
    /// its quota and the CPU it used, in cores
    pub cores: f64,
    pub used: f64,
}

impl QuotaUse {
    /// 0 to 1
    pub fn share(&self) -> f64 {
        (self.used / self.cores).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
    }
}

impl QuotaBusy {
    /// This process's groups and their parents (Linux, cgroup v2); None where there are none to read.
    pub fn find() -> Option<Self> {
        let own = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/self/cgroup").ok()?;
        Self::of(Path::new("/sys/fs/cgroup"), &own)
    }

    /// `root`: where the cgroup tree is mounted; `own`: /proc/self/cgroup (cgroup v2's line: "0::/its/path")
    fn of(root: &Path, own: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        let mut p = Path::new(own.lines().find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("0::"))?.trim());
        let mut groups = Vec::new();
        loop {
            let dir = root.join(p.strip_prefix("/").unwrap_or(p));
            if dir.join("cpu.stat").exists() {
                let used = usage_usec(&dir);
                groups.push((dir, p.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), used));
            }
            let Some(up) = p.parent() else { break };
            p = up;
        }
        (!groups.is_empty()).then(|| QuotaBusy { groups, at: Instant::now(), recent: Recent::default() })
    }

    /// the groups with a quota now, and its cores
    pub fn quotas(&self) -> Vec<(String, f64)> {
        self.groups.iter().filter_map(|(dir, name, _)| Some((name.clone(), quota_cores(dir)?))).collect()
    }

    /// the group with the fullest quota since the last call; None while no group has one
    pub fn sample_use(&mut self) -> Option<QuotaUse> {
        self.sample_use_at(Instant::now())
    }

    fn sample_use_at(&mut self, now: Instant) -> Option<QuotaUse> {
        let wall = now.duration_since(self.at).as_secs_f64();
        self.at = now;
        let mut fullest: Option<QuotaUse> = None;
        for (dir, name, was) in &mut self.groups {
            let used = usage_usec(dir);
            let since = used.saturating_sub(*was) as f64 / 1e6;
            *was = used;
            let Some(cores) = quota_cores(dir) else { continue };
            if wall <= 0.0 {
                continue;
            }
            let u = QuotaUse { group: name.clone(), cores, used: since / wall };
            if fullest.as_ref().is_none_or(|f| u.share() > f.share()) {
                fullest = Some(u);
            }
        }
        fullest
    }

    /// 0 to 1 since the last call: the fullest quota's share (0 while no group has one)
    pub fn sample(&mut self) -> f64 {
        self.sample_use().map_or(0.0, |u| u.share())
    }

    /// 0 to 1: the fullest quota's share over about the last `window`, from a sample at each call.  A share of half a
    /// second is no measure of a slice that is nearly full: nfsu2.xyz's slice used 73 % of its 14 cores over minutes
    /// while its half-second shares went from 62 to 88 % (2026-10-30), and free roam's busy cap, which read those, cut
    /// every player's links to 9-19 of 32 at each high one.
    pub fn sample_over(&mut self, window: Duration) -> f64 {
        self.sample_over_at(Instant::now(), window)
    }

    fn sample_over_at(&mut self, now: Instant, window: Duration) -> f64 {
        let wall = now.duration_since(self.at).as_secs_f64();
        let share = self.sample_use_at(now).map_or(0.0, |u| u.share());
        self.recent.add(wall, share, window)
    }
}

/// a group's CPU time in microseconds (0 where it cannot be read)
fn usage_usec(dir: &Path) -> u64 {
    let Ok(s) = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("cpu.stat")) else { return 0 };
    s.lines().find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("usage_usec ")?.trim().parse().ok()).unwrap_or(0)
}

/// a group's quota in cores ("1400000 100000": 14), None for none ("max 100000", or no cpu.max)
fn quota_cores(dir: &Path) -> Option<f64> {
    let s = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("cpu.max")).ok()?;
    let mut it = s.split_whitespace();
    let (quota, period): (f64, f64) = (it.next()?.parse().ok()?, it.next()?.parse().ok()?);
    (quota > 0.0 && period > 0.0).then_some(quota / period)
}

/// This thread runs at a lower priority (Linux: a nice value of its own, `by` above the one it had, 19 at most;
/// elsewhere nothing): background work that must never keep the switch's workers off a core, such as compressing the
/// game data's runs.  From where it is, not a fixed value: in a server started under `nice` a fixed 10 was refused
/// (going back down needs privileges) and left the thread as high as the workers, or with privileges put it above
/// them.  False when it could not.
pub fn lower_this_thread(by: i32) -> bool {
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    {
        // SAFETY: gettid, getpriority and setpriority take and return plain integers, and errno is this thread's own;
        // a thread may lower its own priority
        unsafe {
            let tid = libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as libc::id_t;
            // (-1 is a nice value too: an error is told by errno)
            *libc::__errno_location() = 0;
            let now = libc::getpriority(libc::PRIO_PROCESS, tid);
            if now == -1 && *libc::__errno_location() != 0 {
                return false;
            }
            libc::setpriority(libc::PRIO_PROCESS, tid, (now + by.max(0)).min(19)) == 0
        }
    }
    #[cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]
    {
        let _ = by;
        false
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    // all the workers busy is busy, however many cores the machine has; idle workers are idle
    #[test]
    fn workers_busy_is_the_workers_share() {
        let rt = tokio::runtime::Builder::new_multi_thread().worker_threads(2).enable_all().build().expect("a runtime");
        let mut b = WorkersBusy::new(rt.handle());
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200));
        let idle = b.sample();
        assert!(idle < 0.2, "idle workers: {idle}");
        let stop = std::sync::Arc::new(std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool::new(false));
        for _ in 0..2 {
            let stop = stop.clone();
            rt.spawn(async move {
                while !stop.load(std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed) {
                    let t = Instant::now();
                    while t.elapsed() < Duration::from_millis(1) {
                        std::hint::spin_loop();
                    }
                    tokio::task::yield_now().await;
                }
            });
        }
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300));
        b.sample();
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(300));
        let busy = b.sample();
        stop.store(true, std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Relaxed);
        assert!(busy > 0.85, "two busy workers: {busy}");
    }

    // the fullest quota of the process's group and its parents, read again at each sample; none without one
    #[test]
    fn quota_busy_is_the_fullest_quota_of_the_groups_and_their_parents() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("nfsu2-cgroup-{}", std::process::id()));
        let slice = root.join("nfsu2.slice");
        let own = slice.join("docker-1.scope");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&own).unwrap();
        let put = |dir: &Path, max: &str, usec: u64| {
            std::fs::write(dir.join("cpu.max"), max).unwrap();
            std::fs::write(dir.join("cpu.stat"), format!("usage_usec {usec}\nuser_usec 0\nsystem_usec 0\n")).unwrap();
        };
        // the tree's root has no cpu.max
        std::fs::write(root.join("cpu.stat"), "usage_usec 5\n").unwrap();
        put(&slice, "max 100000\n", 1_000_000);
        put(&own, "max 100000\n", 400_000);
        let mut q = QuotaBusy::of(&root, "0::/nfsu2.slice/docker-1.scope\n").expect("its groups");
        let t0 = q.at;
        put(&slice, "max 100000\n", 2_000_000);
        assert_eq!(q.sample_use_at(t0 + Duration::from_secs(1)), None, "no quota anywhere");
        assert!(q.quotas().is_empty());
        // systemctl set-property: the slice gets 14 cores, and uses 10.5 of them the next second
        put(&slice, "1400000 100000\n", 12_500_000);
        let u = q.sample_use_at(t0 + Duration::from_secs(2)).expect("a quota");
        assert_eq!(u, QuotaUse { group: "/nfsu2.slice".into(), cores: 14.0, used: 10.5 });
        assert_eq!(u.share(), 0.75);
        assert_eq!(q.quotas(), vec![("/nfsu2.slice".to_string(), 14.0)]);
        // a container of its own 1 core, 0.9 of it used in 2 s (1.8 s): fuller than the slice's 1 core of 14
        put(&own, "100000 100000\n", 2_200_000);
        put(&slice, "1400000 100000\n", 14_500_000);
        let u = q.sample_use_at(t0 + Duration::from_secs(4)).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((u.group.as_str(), u.cores), ("/nfsu2.slice/docker-1.scope", 1.0));
        assert!((u.share() - 0.9).abs() < 1e-9, "{u:?}");
        // a container in a cgroup namespace of its own: its own group alone, as the tree's root
        let mut alone = QuotaBusy::of(&own, "0::/\n").expect("its own group");
        assert_eq!(alone.quotas(), vec![("/".to_string(), 1.0)]);
        assert!(alone.sample_use_at(alone.at + Duration::from_secs(1)).is_some_and(|u| u.used == 0.0));
        // cgroup v1, or no tree: none
        assert!(QuotaBusy::of(&root, "12:cpu,cpuacct:/x\n").is_none());
        assert!(QuotaBusy::of(&root.join("none"), "0::/\n").is_none());
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
    }

    // the share over the last window: half-second shares of 62 and 88 % in turn are 75 % over it, a full one counts for
    // as long as it lasts, and the samples older than the window go
    // the window's mean weighs each sample by its seconds, keeps at least the newest, and lets go of the oldest once the
    // rest still cover the window: one busy half second among ten seconds of 65 % stays under 85 %
    #[test]
    fn recent_is_the_windows_mean_by_time() {
        let w = Duration::from_secs(10);
        let mut r = Recent::default();
        assert_eq!(r.add(0.0, 0.9, w), 0.0, "nothing yet");
        for _ in 0..19 {
            r.add(0.5, 0.65, w);
        }
        let m = r.add(0.5, 0.95, w);
        assert!((m - (19.0 * 0.65 + 0.95) / 20.0).abs() < 1e-9 && m < 0.85, "{m}");
        for _ in 0..20 {
            r.add(0.5, 0.95, w);
        }
        assert!((r.add(0.5, 0.95, w) - 0.95).abs() < 1e-9, "ten seconds busy: busy");
        assert!(r.0.len() <= 21, "{} samples kept", r.0.len());
        let mut one = Recent::default();
        assert_eq!(one.add(30.0, 0.4, w), 0.4, "a sample longer than the window is the window");
    }

    #[test]
    fn quota_busy_over_a_window_is_the_share_of_its_samples_together() {
        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("nfsu2-cgroup-window-{}", std::process::id()));
        let slice = root.join("nfsu2.slice");
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&slice).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(slice.join("cpu.max"), "1400000 100000\n").unwrap();
        let used = |usec: u64| std::fs::write(slice.join("cpu.stat"), format!("usage_usec {usec}\n")).unwrap();
        used(0);
        let mut q = QuotaBusy::of(&root, "0::/nfsu2.slice\n").expect("its group");
        let (t0, w, half) = (q.at, Duration::from_secs(10), Duration::from_millis(500));
        let (mut usec, mut t, mut highest) = (0u64, t0, 0.0f64);
        for i in 0..40 {
            // 14 cores for half a second: 7 s of CPU at 100 %; 62 % and 88 % of it in turn
            usec += if i % 2 == 0 { 4_340_000 } else { 6_160_000 };
            used(usec);
            t += half;
            let b = q.sample_over_at(t, w);
            if i >= 1 {
                highest = highest.max(b);
            }
        }
        assert!((highest - 0.75).abs() < 0.02, "every half-second share at most 88 %, the window's {highest}");
        assert!(q.recent.0.len() <= 21, "{} samples kept for 10 s", q.recent.0.len());
        // a full slice for 5 s: half of the window
        for _ in 0..10 {
            usec += 7_000_000;
            used(usec);
            t += half;
        }
        let b = q.sample_over_at(t, w);
        assert!((b - 0.75 * 0.5 - 1.0 * 0.5).abs() < 0.03, "half the window full: {b}");
        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
    }

    /// this thread's nice value
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    fn nice() -> i32 {
        // SAFETY: as in lower_this_thread
        unsafe {
            *libc::__errno_location() = 0;
            let n = libc::getpriority(libc::PRIO_PROCESS, libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as libc::id_t);
            assert!(n != -1 || *libc::__errno_location() == 0, "getpriority");
            n
        }
    }

    // (the port's own) A thread is lowered from where it is: below the threads it was made from, also in a server
    // started under `nice` (a nice value of 10 for it was refused without privileges there, the pool ran as high as
    // the switch's workers, and with them it was put above them)
    #[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
    #[test]
    fn a_thread_is_lowered_from_where_it_is() {
        std::thread::spawn(|| {
            let was = nice();
            assert!(lower_this_thread(4));
            assert_eq!(nice(), (was + 4).min(19), "4 lower than it was");
        })
        .join()
        .unwrap();
        std::thread::spawn(|| {
            // a process at nice 12, say
            let was = nice().max(12);
            // SAFETY: as in lower_this_thread (a higher nice value needs no privilege)
            assert_eq!(unsafe { libc::setpriority(libc::PRIO_PROCESS, libc::syscall(libc::SYS_gettid) as libc::id_t, was) }, 0);
            assert!(lower_this_thread(10));
            assert_eq!(nice(), 19, "lower than the process's {was}, as low as it goes");
        })
        .join()
        .unwrap();
    }
}

{"id": "AT001663", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/util/src/host.rs", "originalBytes": 9635, "originalSha256": "c926add124ff4320d4d7355b1690c111a1484a07999d865b5630140f261139df", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 9635, "utf8TotalBytes": 9635}

//! The switch's hosts: the server's own addresses on the virtual LAN, the Online host (10.77.0.1, nfsu2-online) and
//! the free-roam hub (10.77.0.253, nfsu2-roam).  Each host runs on a thread of its own and the switch (nfsu2-lan)
//! posts it its frames in order.  Both directions:
//!
//! - switch -> host: [`Host::frame`] for every frame a browser sends to the host's address (the switch has written
//!   the sender's true address into it), [`Host::peer_gone`] for every browser that left the switch.  Both only
//!   queue: they never wait for the host.
//! - host -> switch: the [`SwitchSend`] the host is given (`attach_switch`), `send(vip, frame, cause)`, from the
//!   host's own thread, which answers at once whether the frame went ([`SendResult`]).
//!
//! What the Online host sends while it handles a frame (its answer, and what it tells other players because of it)
//! is charged to the sender's budgets: the switch hands the host a [`Charge`] with each frame (`FrameCtx::cause`), the
//! host passes it to every `send` it makes for that frame, and the switch spends from the sender's buckets for each
//! frame that goes (after its checks that the receiver is there and not too far behind).  After the frame the host
//! asks [`Charge::overspent`]: the sender spent more than its budgets, and the host closes the stream the frame came
//! on (nfsu2-online's `overrun`).  The free-roam hub's frames are charged to nobody (`cause: None`).

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering::SeqCst};

use bytes::Bytes;
use tokio::sync::oneshot;

/// What became of a frame a host sent to one browser.
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SendResult {
    /// queued to the browser
    Sent,
    /// not sent: the browser is too far behind (more than the switch's `online_queue` queued, or its queue is over
    /// `send_buffer` and it was cut); the host closes the stream it was for
    Full,
    /// not sent: no such browser on the switch
    Gone,
}

impl SendResult {
    pub fn sent(self) -> bool {
        self == SendResult::Sent
    }
}

/// The sender's budgets while a host handles its frame (see the module's text).  Thread-safe: the switch's buckets
/// behind their own locks.
pub trait Charge: Send + Sync {
    /// one frame of `bytes` that the host sent for the sender's frame: spent from the sender's buckets (connection,
    /// client, site), into a debt of at most one burst
    fn spend(&self, frames: u32, bytes: usize);
    /// the sender's buckets ran dry while this frame was handled (any `spend` found one below zero).  The first call
    /// that answers true also counts it in the switch's `limited`.
    fn overspent(&self) -> bool;
}

/// What the switch knows of a frame's sender besides its virtual address: the opaque ids of its client (one client
/// address) and site (an IPv6 /48), for a host's own per-client limits (never the address itself), and its budgets.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct FrameCtx {
    pub group: Arc<str>,
    pub site: Option<Arc<str>>,
    pub cause: Option<Arc<dyn Charge>>,
    /// the frame's place in the host's backlog ([`Backlog`]): given back when the host has handled it (drops it)
    pub slot: Option<Arc<Slot>>,
    /// the keyphrase its page plays with, as the server knows it (nfsu2-claims: an owner of claimed names), from the
    /// hello's "claim"; None: none
    pub owner: Option<Arc<str>>,
    /// its player races nobody (the operator's race ban, nfsu2-bans): the Online lobby gives it no game
    pub no_races: bool,
}

/// The frames a host has been posted and not handled yet.  Node's hosts could never fall behind: they ran inside the
/// switch's own calls, on its one thread, and a thread that could not keep up stopped reading the sockets, so TCP
/// slowed the senders down.  Here a host has a thread of its own and the readers could post to it without end; so
/// past `high` frames waiting, a reader that posted to it waits until it is back under `low` before it reads more
/// from its client (the same TCP backpressure, only for the clients that talk to that host: free roam goes on).
pub struct Backlog {
    n: AtomicUsize,
    high: usize,
    low: usize,
    room: tokio::sync::Notify,
}

impl Backlog {
    pub fn new(high: usize, low: usize) -> Arc<Backlog> {
        Arc::new(Backlog { n: AtomicUsize::new(0), high, low: low.min(high), room: tokio::sync::Notify::new() })
    }
    /// one more frame for the host: its slot, held until the host has handled it
    pub fn enter(self: &Arc<Self>) -> Arc<Slot> {
        self.n.fetch_add(1, SeqCst);
        Arc::new(Slot(self.clone()))
    }
    /// frames waiting now
    pub fn waiting(&self) -> usize {
        self.n.load(SeqCst)
    }
    /// past `high`: whoever posted should wait for `room()`
    pub fn over(&self) -> bool {
        self.waiting() > self.high
    }
    /// once at most `low` are waiting
    pub async fn room(&self) {
        loop {
            let notified = self.room.notified();
            tokio::pin!(notified);
            // registered before the count is read: a slot given back in between still wakes it
            notified.as_mut().enable();
            if self.waiting() <= self.low {
                return;
            }
            notified.await;
        }
    }
}

/// A frame's place in its host's [`Backlog`].
pub struct Slot(Arc<Backlog>);

impl Drop for Slot {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        let was = self.0.n.fetch_sub(1, SeqCst);
        // the readers waiting go on when the backlog falls to `low` (once, as it passes there)
        if was == self.0.low + 1 {
            self.0.room.notify_waiters();
        }
    }
}

/// The switch's way to its browsers, given to a host: `send(vip, frame, cause)`.  `cause`: the `FrameCtx::cause` of
/// the frame being handled, when the host sends because of one (the Online host), else None.
pub type SwitchSend = Arc<dyn Fn(u32, Bytes, Option<&dyn Charge>) -> SendResult + Send + Sync>;

/// The dev trace (--online-trace): sees frames (any kind; it picks the lobby's TCP streams).
pub type Tap = Arc<dyn Fn(&[u8]) + Send + Sync>;

/// A host on the switch.  Every method returns at once (the work happens on the host's own thread); `info` and
/// `vips` answer through a channel once the host has handled everything posted before them.
pub trait Host: Send + Sync + 'static {
    /// its virtual address
    fn vip(&self) -> u32;
    /// its name on the peer list (the Online host; the hub is on no list)
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    /// whether the switch's peer lists show it (`{ vip, name, server: true }`): the Online host yes, the hub no
    fn listed(&self) -> bool;
    /// a frame from browser `from` to this host's address
    fn frame(&self, from: u32, data: Bytes, ctx: FrameCtx);
    /// browser `vip` left the switch
    fn peer_gone(&self, vip: u32);
    /// counts for the tests and the console, as JSON
    fn info(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<serde_json::Value>;
    /// the browsers this host counts as its players now
    fn vips(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<HashSet<u32>>;
    /// the names browser `vip`'s page blocks (its hello's "block"): the free-roam hub links none of those players with
    /// it, either way; the others take no notice
    fn blocks(&self, _vip: u32, _names: Vec<String>) {}
    /// browser `vip`'s page goes by `name` on the switch (its hello's): the free-roam hub says so on the console when
    /// that browser's game shows another name over its car; the others take no notice
    fn page_name(&self, _vip: u32, _name: &str) {}
    /// the names browsers' games show other players that are not their pages' on the switch (`page_name`), by
    /// browser, for the operator's `who`: the free-roam hub's; the others have none
    fn other_names(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<HashMap<u32, Vec<String>>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = tx.send(HashMap::new());
        rx
    }
    /// each pair of browsers whose players this host links now, once (the lower address first), for the server's
    /// counts of the players' paths (nfsu2-lan paths.rs): the free-roam hub's links; the others have none
    fn link_pairs(&self) -> oneshot::Receiver<Vec<(u32, u32)>> {
        let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
        let _ = tx.send(Vec::new());
        rx
    }
    /// the server stops: save what is kept, end the timers
    fn stop(&self);
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::time::Duration;

    // past `high` a poster waits; it goes on once the host has handled the frames down to `low`, not before
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_backlog_waits_from_high_down_to_low() {
        let b = Backlog::new(3, 1);
        let mut slots: Vec<Arc<Slot>> = (0..4).map(|_| b.enter()).collect();
        assert!(b.over());
        let waiter = {
            let b = b.clone();
            tokio::spawn(async move { b.room().await })
        };
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
        slots.pop();
        slots.pop();
        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
        assert!(!waiter.is_finished(), "2 still waiting: over low");
        slots.pop();
        tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), waiter).await.expect("room at low").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(b.waiting(), 1);
        // a clone of a frame's context shares its slot: one place in the backlog
        drop(slots);
        let s = b.enter();
        let again = s.clone();
        drop(s);
        assert_eq!(b.waiting(), 1);
        drop(again);
        assert_eq!(b.waiting(), 0);
    }
}

//! A hasher for maps keyed by the server's own small numbers (virtual addresses, slots, rooms, the game's player ids):
//! a multiplication and a shift where std's maps run SipHash.  The free-roam hub looks its players' blocks up twice for
//! every pair it weighs (hub.rs `blocked`), and SipHash of those keys took a tenth of its thread on nfsu2.xyz
//! (2026-11-05, 11,500 players).  None of these keys is one a client can pick by the thousand (a page holds one
//! address, its game one id), so a weaker hash leaves no flood of colliding keys to fear.

use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
use std::hash::{BuildHasherDefault, Hasher};

/// The hasher: each integer written mixed in by one multiplication (the golden ratio's, odd) and the product's high
/// half folded onto its low one, so that both the low bits (the table's slot) and the top ones (hashbrown's tag) vary.
#[derive(Default, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct IdHasher(u64);

impl Hasher for IdHasher {
    fn finish(&self) -> u64 {
        self.0
    }
    fn write(&mut self, b: &[u8]) {
        for &x in b {
            self.write_u64(x as u64);
        }
    }
    fn write_u8(&mut self, k: u8) {
        self.write_u64(k as u64);
    }
    fn write_u16(&mut self, k: u16) {
        self.write_u64(k as u64);
    }
    fn write_u32(&mut self, k: u32) {
        self.write_u64(k as u64);
    }
    fn write_usize(&mut self, k: usize) {
        self.write_u64(k as u64);
    }
    fn write_u64(&mut self, k: u64) {
        let x = (self.0 ^ k).wrapping_mul(0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15);
        self.0 = x ^ x >> 32;
    }
}

pub type IdBuild = BuildHasherDefault<IdHasher>;
/// a map by such a number
pub type IdMap<K, V> = HashMap<K, V, IdBuild>;
/// a set of them
pub type IdSet<K> = HashSet<K, IdBuild>;

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::hash::BuildHasher;

    #[test]
    fn neighbours_spread_over_slots_and_tags() {
        // a run of addresses (10.77.x.y one after the other) lands in as many slots of a 4096-slot table, and their top
        // 7 bits (hashbrown's tag) take most of their 128 values
        let b = IdBuild::default();
        let (mut slots, mut tags) = (std::collections::HashSet::new(), std::collections::HashSet::new());
        for v in 0x0A4D_0000u32..0x0A4D_1000 {
            let h = b.hash_one(v);
            slots.insert(h & 0xFFF);
            tags.insert(h >> 57);
        }
        assert!(slots.len() > 4096 * 6 / 10, "{} slots", slots.len());
        assert!(tags.len() > 120, "{} tags", tags.len());
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_map_by_it_works_as_any() {
        let mut m: IdMap<u32, u32> = IdMap::default();
        for k in 0..10_000u32 {
            m.insert(k.wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761), k);
        }
        assert_eq!(m.len(), 10_000);
        assert!((0..10_000u32).all(|k| m[&k.wrapping_mul(2_654_435_761)] == k));
        let s: IdSet<u32> = (0..100).collect();
        assert!(s.contains(&99) && !s.contains(&100));
    }
}

//! Text and numbers the way JavaScript makes them, so that what the server prints, stores and sends is byte for byte
//! what the Node server it replaced did (the state files it left, the pages and tools that read the answers).

/// JS `\s` and what `String#trim()` removes: WhiteSpace and LineTerminator (ECMA-262), which is not Rust's
/// `char::is_whitespace` (that has U+0085 and not U+FEFF).
#[inline]
pub fn is_space(c: char) -> bool {
    matches!(
        c,
        '\u{0009}' | '\u{000A}' | '\u{000B}' | '\u{000C}' | '\u{000D}' | '\u{0020}' | '\u{00A0}' | '\u{1680}' | '\u{2000}'
            ..='\u{200A}' | '\u{2028}' | '\u{2029}' | '\u{202F}' | '\u{205F}' | '\u{3000}' | '\u{FEFF}'
    )
}

/// JS `String#trim()`
pub fn trim(s: &str) -> &str {
    s.trim_matches(is_space)
}

/// JS `s.replace(/\s+/g, rep)`
pub fn collapse_space(s: &str, rep: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut in_space = false;
    for c in s.chars() {
        if is_space(c) {
            if !in_space {
                out.push_str(rep);
                in_space = true;
            }
        } else {
            out.push(c);
            in_space = false;
        }
    }
    out
}

/// Length in UTF-16 code units (JS `s.length`).
pub fn utf16_len(s: &str) -> usize {
    s.chars().map(char::len_utf16).sum()
}

/// Text for a console line: every character outside printable ASCII a '?', at most `n` of them (JS
/// `String(x).replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]/g, '?').slice(0, n)`, over UTF-16 code units: a character outside the BMP is two
/// code units, so two '?').
pub fn printable(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len().min(n));
    for c in s.chars() {
        if out.len() >= n {
            break;
        }
        if (' '..='~').contains(&c) {
            out.push(c);
        } else {
            for _ in 0..c.len_utf16() {
                out.push('?');
            }
        }
    }
    out.truncate(n);
    out
}

/// JS `Number.prototype.toString()` (radix 10): the shortest digits that read back as the same double, in JS's
/// layout (no exponent from 1e-6 up to 1e21; "1e+21", "1.5e-7" beyond).
pub fn number_to_string(x: f64) -> String {
    if x.is_nan() {
        return "NaN".into();
    }
    if x == 0.0 {
        return "0".into();
    }
    if x.is_infinite() {
        return if x > 0.0 { "Infinity".into() } else { "-Infinity".into() };
    }
    if x < 0.0 {
        return format!("-{}", number_to_string(-x));
    }
    // Rust's `{:e}` is the shortest round-trip digits in exponent form: "d.ddde<exp>"
    let e = format!("{x:e}");
    let (mant, exp) = e.split_once('e').expect("exponent form");
    let exp: i32 = exp.parse().expect("exponent");
    let mut digits: String = mant.chars().filter(|c| *c != '.').collect();
    let n = exp + 1; // value = 0.digits * 10^n
    if let Some(even) = even_of_a_tie(x, &digits, n) {
        digits = even;
    }
    let k = digits.len() as i32;
    if k <= n && n <= 21 {
        let mut s = digits;
        for _ in 0..(n - k) {
            s.push('0');
        }
        s
    } else if 0 < n && n <= 21 {
        format!("{}.{}", &digits[..n as usize], &digits[n as usize..])
    } else if -6 < n && n <= 0 {
        format!("0.{}{}", "0".repeat((-n) as usize), digits)
    } else {
        let sign = if n - 1 < 0 { '-' } else { '+' };
        if k == 1 {
            format!("{}e{}{}", digits, sign, (n - 1).abs())
        } else {
            format!("{}.{}e{}{}", &digits[..1], &digits[1..], sign, (n - 1).abs())
        }
    }
}

/// When x lies exactly halfway between two shortest forms (digits, and the one a unit of its last digit away), JS
/// takes the even one (Number::toString: "if there are two such possible values of s, choose the one that is
/// even"); Rust's formatter may take the other.  Only a double with few significant bits just past the point can be
/// such a tie (a float32's value, as the game's race times are): its exact value then has one digit more than the
/// shortest form, a 5.  Some(the even digits) where Rust took the odd ones.
fn even_of_a_tie(x: f64, digits: &str, n: i32) -> Option<String> {
    let exact = short_exact_digits(x)?;
    let k = digits.len();
    if exact.len() != k + 1 || !exact.ends_with('5') || digits.as_bytes()[k - 1] & 1 == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    // the two candidates: the exact digits cut after k, and one more (a carry past the first digit makes "10...0",
    // even already)
    let lower = &exact[..k];
    let mut upper = lower.as_bytes().to_vec();
    let mut i = k;
    loop {
        if i == 0 {
            return None;
        }
        i -= 1;
        if upper[i] == b'9' {
            upper[i] = b'0';
        } else {
            upper[i] += 1;
            break;
        }
    }
    let upper = String::from_utf8(upper).ok()?;
    let other = if digits == lower {
        upper
    } else if digits == upper {
        lower.to_string()
    } else {
        return None;
    };
    // the even one, if it reads back as x too (at a power of two the gap below is half the one above)
    let back = format!("0.{other}e{n}").parse::<f64>().ok()?;
    (back == x).then(|| other.trim_end_matches('0').to_string()).filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
}

/// The significant digits of x's exact value when there are at most 18 of them, else None.  x = m * 2^e with m odd:
/// for e >= 0 an integer (never a tie: its last nonzero digit cannot be a 5 the double's gap reaches), for e < 0 the
/// digits are those of m * 5^-e, which has more than 18 once -e > 25.
fn short_exact_digits(x: f64) -> Option<String> {
    let bits = x.abs().to_bits();
    let exp = ((bits >> 52) & 0x7ff) as i32;
    let frac = bits & ((1u64 << 52) - 1);
    let (mut m, mut e) = if exp == 0 { (frac, -1074) } else { (frac | (1u64 << 52), exp - 1075) };
    if m == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let tz = m.trailing_zeros();
    m >>= tz;
    e += tz as i32;
    if !(-25..0).contains(&e) {
        return None;
    }
    let p = (m as u128) * 5u128.pow((-e) as u32);
    let s = p.to_string();
    (s.len() <= 18).then_some(s)
}

/// JS `Number.prototype.toFixed(digits)` (0 to 100 digits): the exact value rounded half up at `digits` decimals
/// (Rust's `{:.N}` rounds a tie to even: 0.125 -> "0.12", where JS says "0.13").  1e21 and beyond as `toString()`.
/// More than 100 digits (a RangeError in JS) are 100.
pub fn to_fixed(x: f64, digits: usize) -> String {
    // (past the 1100 decimals worked out below, the digits ran out: a panic)
    let digits = digits.min(100);
    if x.is_nan() {
        return "NaN".into();
    }
    if x.abs() >= 1e21 || x.is_infinite() {
        return number_to_string(x);
    }
    // every double has at most 1074 decimals: this is its exact value
    let exact = format!("{:.1100}", x.abs());
    let (int, frac) = exact.split_once('.').unwrap_or((&exact, ""));
    let mut ds: Vec<u8> = int.bytes().chain(frac.bytes().take(digits)).map(|b| b - b'0').collect();
    let round_up = frac.as_bytes().get(digits).is_some_and(|d| *d >= b'5');
    if round_up {
        let mut i = ds.len();
        loop {
            if i == 0 {
                ds.insert(0, 1);
                break;
            }
            i -= 1;
            if ds[i] == 9 {
                ds[i] = 0;
            } else {
                ds[i] += 1;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    let int_len = ds.len() - digits;
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(ds.len() + 2);
    // JS keeps the sign of a negative number that rounds to zero: (-0.0001).toFixed(2) is "-0.00"
    let negative = x < 0.0;
    if negative {
        s.push('-');
    }
    for d in &ds[..int_len] {
        s.push((b'0' + d) as char);
    }
    if digits > 0 {
        s.push('.');
        for d in &ds[int_len..] {
            s.push((b'0' + d) as char);
        }
    }
    s
}

/// The parts of a UTC time (JS `new Date(ms).getUTC...()`): year, month 1-12, day 1-31, hours, minutes, seconds, ms.
pub fn utc_parts(ms: i64) -> (i64, u32, u32, u32, u32, u32, u32) {
    let days = ms.div_euclid(86_400_000);
    let rem = ms.rem_euclid(86_400_000);
    // Howard Hinnant's civil_from_days
    let z = days + 719_468;
    let era = z.div_euclid(146_097);
    let doe = z.rem_euclid(146_097);
    let yoe = (doe - doe / 1460 + doe / 36_524 - doe / 146_096) / 365;
    let doy = doe - (365 * yoe + yoe / 4 - yoe / 100);
    let mp = (5 * doy + 2) / 153;
    let d = (doy - (153 * mp + 2) / 5 + 1) as u32;
    let m = if mp < 10 { mp + 3 } else { mp - 9 } as u32;
    let y = yoe + era * 400 + if m <= 2 { 1 } else { 0 };
    let h = (rem / 3_600_000) as u32;
    let mi = (rem / 60_000 % 60) as u32;
    let s = (rem / 1000 % 60) as u32;
    let msec = (rem % 1000) as u32;
    (y, m, d, h, mi, s, msec)
}

/// JS `new Date(ms).toISOString()`: "2026-10-21T06:55:40.123Z"
pub fn iso_string(ms: i64) -> String {
    let (y, m, d, h, mi, s, msec) = utc_parts(ms);
    if (0..=9999).contains(&y) {
        format!("{y:04}-{m:02}-{d:02}T{h:02}:{mi:02}:{s:02}.{msec:03}Z")
    } else {
        let sign = if y < 0 { '-' } else { '+' };
        format!("{sign}{:06}-{m:02}-{d:02}T{h:02}:{mi:02}:{s:02}.{msec:03}Z", y.abs())
    }
}

/// Node's `Buffer#toString('base64url')` (no padding)
pub fn base64url(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    use base64::Engine;
    base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD.encode(b)
}

/// Node's `Buffer.from(s, 'base64url')`: lenient as Node is (padding and characters outside the alphabet are
/// skipped; '+' and '/' read as '-' and '_')
pub fn from_base64url(s: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
    use base64::Engine;
    let clean: String = s
        .chars()
        .filter_map(|c| match c {
            'A'..='Z' | 'a'..='z' | '0'..='9' | '-' | '_' => Some(c),
            '+' => Some('-'),
            '/' => Some('_'),
            _ => None,
        })
        .collect();
    // a last group of one character holds no byte (Node drops it)
    let usable = if clean.len() % 4 == 1 { &clean[..clean.len() - 1] } else { &clean[..] };
    base64::engine::general_purpose::URL_SAFE_NO_PAD
        .decode(usable)
        .or_else(|_| {
            base64::engine::GeneralPurpose::new(
                &base64::alphabet::URL_SAFE,
                base64::engine::GeneralPurposeConfig::new()
                    .with_decode_allow_trailing_bits(true)
                    .with_encode_padding(false)
                    .with_decode_padding_mode(base64::engine::DecodePaddingMode::Indifferent),
            )
            .decode(usable)
        })
        .unwrap_or_default()
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn numbers_as_js_writes_them() {
        for (x, s) in [
            (0.0, "0"),
            (-0.0, "0"),
            (1.0, "1"),
            (-1.5, "-1.5"),
            (0.1, "0.1"),
            (1e21, "1e+21"),
            (1e20, "100000000000000000000"),
            (123456789012345680000.0, "123456789012345680000"),
            (1.5e-7, "1.5e-7"),
            (1e-6, "0.000001"),
            (1e-7, "1e-7"),
            (1729512345123.4567, "1729512345123.4568"),
            (0.30000000000000004, "0.30000000000000004"),
            (5e-324, "5e-324"),
            (1.7976931348623157e308, "1.7976931348623157e+308"),
            (f64::NAN, "NaN"),
            (f64::INFINITY, "Infinity"),
            (2.5e25, "2.5e+25"),
            (100.0, "100"),
            (1234.5678, "1234.5678"),
            // -0.53125762939453125, halfway between two shortest forms: the even one, as JS
            (-69633.0 / 131072.0, "-0.5312576293945312"),
        ] {
            assert_eq!(number_to_string(x), s, "{x}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn to_fixed_rounds_half_up() {
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(0.125, 2), "0.13");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(1.005, 2), "1.00"); // 1.005 is 1.00499999999999989...
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(61.125, 2), "61.13");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(9.995, 2), "9.99");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(99.999, 2), "100.00");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(-0.0001, 2), "-0.00");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(-0.0, 2), "0.00");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(-0.5, 0), "-1");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(1e20, 2), "100000000000000000000.00");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(-1.5, 0), "-2");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(2.5, 0), "3");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(12.0, 3), "12.000");
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(1.234, 0), "1");
        // more digits than JS allows: 100, not a panic
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(0.5, 5000), to_fixed(0.5, 100));
        assert_eq!(to_fixed(0.5, 100).len(), 102);
    }

    #[test]
    fn printable_counts_utf16() {
        assert_eq!(printable("a\u{1F600}b", 160), "a??b");
        assert_eq!(printable("héllo\n", 4), "h?ll");
        assert_eq!(printable("abc", 2), "ab");
    }

    #[test]
    fn trim_and_space() {
        assert_eq!(trim("\u{FEFF} a b \u{3000}"), "a b");
        assert_eq!(trim("\u{0085}x"), "\u{0085}x");
        assert_eq!(collapse_space("a \t\n b", " "), "a b");
    }

    #[test]
    fn dates() {
        assert_eq!(iso_string(0), "1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z");
        assert_eq!(iso_string(1_792_565_740_123), "2026-10-21T06:55:40.123Z");
        assert_eq!(utc_parts(951_782_400_000).0, 2000);
        assert_eq!(utc_parts(951_782_400_000).1, 2);
        assert_eq!(utc_parts(951_782_400_000).2, 29);
    }

    #[test]
    fn base64url_both_ways() {
        assert_eq!(base64url(&[0xfb, 0xff]), "-_8");
        assert_eq!(from_base64url("-_8"), vec![0xfb, 0xff]);
        assert_eq!(from_base64url("-_8="), vec![0xfb, 0xff]);
    }
}

//! `JSON.stringify` of a `serde_json::Value`, byte for byte: keys in insertion order (serde_json's preserve_order),
//! strings escaped as JS escapes them (the same set serde_json escapes), numbers as JS writes them (serde_json
//! writes the double 5 as "5.0" and 1e21 as "1e21"; JS "5" and "1e+21").  Integers are integers already.

use serde_json::Value;

use crate::js::number_to_string;

/// `JSON.stringify(v)` (no spaces)
pub fn stringify(v: &Value) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(64);
    write_value(&mut out, v);
    out
}

fn write_value(out: &mut String, v: &Value) {
    match v {
        Value::Null => out.push_str("null"),
        Value::Bool(b) => out.push_str(if *b { "true" } else { "false" }),
        Value::Number(n) => {
            if let Some(i) = n.as_i64() {
                out.push_str(itoa_i64(i).as_str());
            } else if let Some(u) = n.as_u64() {
                out.push_str(&u.to_string());
            } else {
                let f = n.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN);
                // JSON.stringify writes NaN and the infinities as null
                if f.is_finite() { out.push_str(&number_to_string(f)) } else { out.push_str("null") }
            }
        }
        Value::String(s) => write_str(out, s),
        Value::Array(a) => {
            out.push('[');
            for (i, x) in a.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_value(out, x);
            }
            out.push(']');
        }
        Value::Object(m) => {
            out.push('{');
            for (i, (k, x)) in m.iter().enumerate() {
                if i > 0 {
                    out.push(',');
                }
                write_str(out, k);
                out.push(':');
                write_value(out, x);
            }
            out.push('}');
        }
    }
}

fn itoa_i64(i: i64) -> String {
    i.to_string()
}

/// a JSON string as `JSON.stringify` writes it: `"` and `\` escaped, \b \f \n \r \t, other controls as \u00XX
pub fn write_str(out: &mut String, s: &str) {
    out.push('"');
    for c in s.chars() {
        match c {
            '"' => out.push_str("\\\""),
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\u{08}' => out.push_str("\\b"),
            '\u{0C}' => out.push_str("\\f"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            '\t' => out.push_str("\\t"),
            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => {
                out.push_str(&format!("\\u{:04x}", c as u32));
            }
            c => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out.push('"');
}

/// A JSON number that JS would read from `x` (whole numbers as integers, so `stringify` writes "5", not "5.0").
pub fn num(x: f64) -> Value {
    if x.fract() == 0.0 && x.abs() < 9_007_199_254_740_992.0 {
        Value::from(x as i64)
    } else {
        serde_json::Number::from_f64(x).map(Value::Number).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
    }
}

/// JS `Number.isSafeInteger(v)` for a parsed JSON value (1.0 counts: JS reads it as 1)
pub fn safe_integer(v: &Value) -> Option<i64> {
    let f = v.as_f64()?;
    if f.fract() == 0.0 && f.abs() <= 9_007_199_254_740_991.0 { Some(f as i64) } else { None }
}

/// `v === n` in JS for a parsed JSON value and a small integer (1 and 1.0 are both 1)
pub fn is_num(v: Option<&Value>, n: f64) -> bool {
    v.and_then(Value::as_f64).is_some_and(|f| f == n)
}

    use serde_json::json;

    #[test]
    fn as_js_writes_it() {
        let v = json!({ "b": 5.0, "a": [1e21, 0.5, -0.0, "x\"\n\u{1}é"], "c": null, "d": true });
        assert_eq!(stringify(&v), r#"{"b":5.0,"a":[1e+21,0.5,0,"x\"\n\u0001é"],"c":null,"d":true}"#.replace("5.0", "5"));
        assert_eq!(stringify(&num(5.0)), "5");
        assert_eq!(safe_integer(&json!(3.0)), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(safe_integer(&json!(3.5)), None);
        assert!(is_num(Some(&json!(1.0)), 1.0));
    }
}

/// one line to stdout (console.log)
pub fn line(s: &str) {

/// a line to the console, then the log files (under the console's lock: both in the same order)
fn write_line(o: &mut impl Write, s: &str) {
    let _ = o.write_all(s.as_bytes());
    let _ = o.write_all(b"\n");
    let _ = o.flush();
    crate::logfile::write(s);
}

/// one line to stderr (console.error), then the log files (after stderr's lock: `logfile::write` may write to stderr)
pub fn error(s: &str) {
    {
        let out = std::io::stderr();
        let mut o = out.lock();
        let _ = o.write_all(s.as_bytes());
        let _ = o.write_all(b"\n");
        let _ = o.flush();

struct Quiet {
    t: i64,
    n: u32,
    left: u32,
    kind: String,
    topic: String,
}

/// The counts by topic and client, in the order they began (the lines that say how many were left out come in that
/// order).  A count leaves and comes back at the end each minute, among up to 10,000 of them: a place
/// number per count keeps the order with no shift of the others (an IndexMap's ordered removal moved them all, under
/// the lock every client's line takes).
#[derive(Default)]
struct Counts {
    place: HashMap<String, u64>,
    order: BTreeMap<u64, (String, Quiet)>,
    next: u64,
}

impl Counts {
    fn get(&self, k: &str) -> Option<&Quiet> {
        self.place.get(k).and_then(|p| self.order.get(p)).map(|(_, q)| q)
    }
    fn get_mut(&mut self, k: &str) -> Option<&mut Quiet> {
        let p = *self.place.get(k)?;
        self.order.get_mut(&p).map(|(_, q)| q)
    }
    fn contains_key(&self, k: &str) -> bool {
        self.place.contains_key(k)
    }
    fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.place.len()
    }
    /// at the end of the order
    fn insert(&mut self, k: String, q: Quiet) {
        let p = self.next;
        self.next += 1;
        if let Some(old) = self.place.insert(k.clone(), p) {
            self.order.remove(&old);
        }
        self.order.insert(p, (k, q));
    }
    fn remove(&mut self, k: &str) -> Option<Quiet> {
        let p = self.place.remove(k)?;
        self.order.remove(&p).map(|(_, q)| q)
    }
    /// every count, in order
    fn drain(&mut self) -> Vec<Quiet> {
        self.place.clear();
        std::mem::take(&mut self.order).into_values().map(|(_, q)| q).collect()
    }
    /// the counts `keep` says no to go, in order, each seen by `keep`
    fn retain(&mut self, mut keep: impl FnMut(&Quiet) -> bool) {
        let gone: Vec<u64> = self.order.iter().filter(|(_, (_, q))| !keep(q)).map(|(p, _)| *p).collect();
        for p in gone {
            if let Some((k, _)) = self.order.remove(&p) {
                self.place.remove(&k);
            }
        }
    }
}

fn quiet() -> &'static Mutex<Counts> {
    static Q: OnceLock<Mutex<Counts>> = OnceLock::new();
    Q.get_or_init(|| {
        // every 15 s: the counts of the minutes that are over
        std::thread::Builder::new()
            .name("log-quiet".into())
            .spawn(|| {
                loop {
                    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(15));
                    flush_all(false);
                }
            })
            .ok();
        Mutex::new(Counts::default())
    })
}

/// the line that says how many of a minute's lines were left out, if any were
fn left_out(b: &Quiet) -> Option<String> {
    (b.left > 0).then(|| format!("[{}] {} more {} from one client in that minute (not shown)", b.kind, b.left, b.topic))
}

fn flush_all(force: bool) {
    let now = now_ms();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut q = quiet().lock();
    q.retain(|b| {
        let over = force || now - b.t >= 60_000;
        if over {
            out.extend(left_out(b));
        }
        !over
    });
    if out.is_empty() {
        return;
    }
    // (the console taken before the counts are let go: see `limited`)
    let mut c = console();
    drop(q);
    for l in out {
        write_line(&mut c, &l);
    }
}

/// A line client `key` caused: shown while it is among the first `per` of its `kind` and `topic` in a minute, else
/// counted, and the count of those left out said once the minute is over ("[kind] N more topic from one client in
/// that minute (not shown)").  What goes out is decided under the counts' lock and written after it (with
/// --access-log every request comes here: none waits on another's write to the console).  A call that ends a minute
/// with lines left out takes the console before it lets the counts go, so that its "N more" line comes before every
/// line decided after it (a client over its share: once a minute at most).
pub fn limited(kind: &str, topic: &str, key: &str, text: &str, per: u32) {
    let now = now_ms();
    let k = format!("{kind} {topic} {key}");
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let (show, held) = {
        let mut q = quiet().lock();
        if q.get(&k).is_some_and(|b| now - b.t >= 60_000)
            && let Some(b) = q.remove(&k)
        {
            out.extend(left_out(&b));
        }
        if !q.contains_key(&k) {
            if q.len() >= 10_000 {
                // every count goes out at once: at most 10,000 are kept
                out.extend(q.drain().iter().filter_map(left_out));
            }
            q.insert(k.clone(), Quiet { t: now, n: 0, left: 0, kind: kind.to_string(), topic: topic.to_string() });
        }
        let b = q.get_mut(&k).expect("just made");
        b.n += 1;
        if b.n > per {
            b.left += 1;
        }
        (b.n <= per, (!out.is_empty()).then(console))
    };
    match held {
        Some(mut c) => {
            for l in &out {
                write_line(&mut c, l);
            }
            if show {
                write_line(&mut c, text);
            }
        }
        None if show => line(text),
        None => {}
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use parking_lot::{ReentrantMutex, ReentrantMutexGuard};
    use std::cell::RefCell;
    use std::time::Instant;

    /// the console of this crate's tests: what was written, for them to read back (reentrant, as stdout's lock is)
    static SINK: ReentrantMutex<RefCell<Vec<u8>>> = parking_lot::const_reentrant_mutex(RefCell::new(Vec::new()));

    pub(super) struct Console(ReentrantMutexGuard<'static, RefCell<Vec<u8>>>);

    impl Write for Console {
        fn write(&mut self, b: &[u8]) -> std::io::Result<usize> {
            self.0.borrow_mut().extend_from_slice(b);
            Ok(b.len())
        }
        fn flush(&mut self) -> std::io::Result<()> {
            Ok(())
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn console() -> Console {
        Console(SINK.lock())
    }

    fn written(prefix: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        let g = SINK.lock();
        let all = String::from_utf8_lossy(&g.borrow()).into_owned();
        all.lines().filter(|l| l.starts_with(prefix)).map(str::to_string).collect()
    }

    // the counts keep the order they began in, a count that comes back goes to the end
    #[test]
    fn counts_keep_the_maps_order() {
        let q = |t: i64| Quiet { t, n: 0, left: 0, kind: String::new(), topic: String::new() };
        let mut c = Counts::default();
        for (k, t) in [("a", 1), ("b", 2), ("c", 3)] {
            c.insert(k.into(), q(t));
        }
        assert_eq!(c.remove("a").map(|x| x.t), Some(1));
        c.insert("a".into(), q(4));
        c.retain(|x| x.t != 2);
        assert_eq!(c.len(), 2);
        assert!(c.get("b").is_none() && c.contains_key("c"));
        c.get_mut("c").unwrap().n = 7;
        assert_eq!(c.drain().iter().map(|x| (x.t, x.n)).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [(3, 7), (4, 0)]);
        assert_eq!(c.len(), 0);
    }

    // The line that says how many of a client's lines a minute left out comes before any line decided after it.  The
    // line is decided under the counts' lock and written after it, so another thread's line decided later could be
    // written first, while the console was busy: "[order] third" before "1 more".
    #[test]
    fn a_minutes_count_comes_before_the_lines_decided_after_it() {
        let (kind, topic, key) = ("order", "test lines", "client a");
        let k = format!("{kind} {topic} {key}");
        limited(kind, topic, key, "[order] first", 1);
        limited(kind, topic, key, "[order] left out", 1);
        // that minute is over
        quiet().lock().get_mut(&k).expect("its count").t -= 60_000;
        // the console busy (another line being written) while a call ends the minute: "1 more", then its own line
        let busy = console();
        let a = std::thread::spawn(move || limited(kind, topic, key, "[order] second", 2));
        // a call decided after that one: made here once that one has let the counts go (its line can be written at
        // once: this thread holds the console); not made while that one holds the counts until it has the console
        let t0 = Instant::now();
        let mut held_since: Option<Instant> = None;
        let mut third = false;
        while !third {
            assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(5), "the other call did not come");
            match quiet().try_lock() {
                Some(q) => {
                    held_since = None;
                    if q.get(&k).is_some_and(|b| b.n == 1) {
                        drop(q);
                        limited(kind, topic, key, "[order] third", 2);
                        third = true;
                    }
                }
                None if held_since.is_some_and(|t| t.elapsed() > Duration::from_millis(100)) => break,
                None => held_since = held_since.or(Some(Instant::now())),
            }
            std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(1));
        }
        drop(busy);
        a.join().unwrap();
        if !third {
            limited(kind, topic, key, "[order] third", 2);
        }
        assert_eq!(
            written("[order]"),
            ["[order] first", "[order] 1 more test lines from one client in that minute (not shown)", "[order] second", "[order] third"]
        );
    }
}

{"id": "AT001669", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/util/src/logfile.rs", "originalBytes": 9704, "originalSha256": "e0485215bcf38ee5014097933a2270c8cdd31167d5fcf8d1052467e5eb7b632d", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 9704, "utf8TotalBytes": 9704}

//! The log files ([`to_files`]): every console line (`log::line`, `log::error`, the lines `log::limited` shows) also
//! goes into the state folder's `logs/<day>.log` (UTC), each after its time ("2026-10-31T10:20:40.155Z "), so the log
//! outlasts a deploy and Docker's own (its `local` driver keeps 100 MB of the console: about 16 hours with 4,000
//! players, 2026-10-31).  A day that ended is gzipped (`<day>.log.gz`, a fifth of it) and kept until DAYS_KEPT days
//! are there; then it goes.  `web/deploy/nfsu2 logs [days]` sends them out.

use std::fs::{File, OpenOptions};
use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::os::unix::fs::{DirBuilderExt, OpenOptionsExt};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::OnceLock;

use flate2::Compression;
use flate2::write::GzEncoder;
use parking_lot::Mutex;

use crate::atomic_file;
use crate::clock::now_ms;
use crate::js::iso_string;

/// the days kept, today's included (a day's file gzipped: 20-30 MB with 4,000 players)
pub const DAYS_KEPT: i64 = 30;
const DAY_MS: i64 = 86_400_000;

struct Files {
    dir: PathBuf,
    day: i64,
    file: Option<File>,
    /// a write or an open failed, and that was said (once, until one works again)
    failed: bool,
}

static FILES: OnceLock<Mutex<Files>> = OnceLock::new();

/// one tidy at a time (the start's and a day's end's)
static TIDY: Mutex<()> = Mutex::new(());

/// "2026-10-31": a day (days since 1970) as its file is named
fn day_name(day: i64) -> String {
    iso_string(day * DAY_MS)[..10].to_string()
}

fn open(dir: &Path, day: i64) -> io::Result<File> {
    OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true).mode(0o600).open(dir.join(format!("{}.log", day_name(day))))
}

/// From now on the console's lines go into `dir` too (made, private to this server's user, if it is not there); the
/// days that ended are gzipped and the ones past DAYS_KEPT go, in a thread of its own.  Err: `dir` or today's file
/// cannot be made, or the files were set already.
pub fn to_files(dir: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700).create(dir)?;
    let day = now_ms().div_euclid(DAY_MS);
    let file = open(dir, day)?;
    FILES
        .set(Mutex::new(Files { dir: dir.to_path_buf(), day, file: Some(file), failed: false }))
        .map_err(|_| io::Error::other("the log files were set already"))?;
    tidy(dir.to_path_buf(), day);
    Ok(())
}

/// a console line (or lines: one after another, each after the time) into today's file; at a day's end into the
/// next day's, and the day that ended gzipped
pub(crate) fn write(text: &str) {
    let Some(files) = FILES.get() else { return };
    let now = now_ms();
    let mut b = String::with_capacity(text.len() + 32);
    let t = iso_string(now);
    for l in text.split('\n') {
        b.push_str(&t);
        b.push(' ');
        b.push_str(l);
        b.push('\n');
    }
    let say = {
        let mut f = files.lock();
        let day = now.div_euclid(DAY_MS);
        let mut err = None;
        if day != f.day || f.file.is_none() {
            let was = f.day;
            f.day = day;
            match open(&f.dir, day) {
                Ok(x) => f.file = Some(x),
                Err(e) => {
                    f.file = None;
                    err = Some(e);
                }
            }
            if day != was {
                tidy(f.dir.clone(), day);
            }
        }
        if let Some(file) = f.file.as_mut()
            && let Err(e) = file.write_all(b.as_bytes())
        {
            err = Some(e);
        }
        match err {
            Some(e) if !f.failed => {
                f.failed = true;
                Some(format!("{}/{}.log: {e} (the log files stop until a line can be written again)", f.dir.display(), day_name(day)))
            }
            Some(_) => None,
            None => {
                let back = f.failed;
                f.failed = false;
                back.then(|| format!("{}/{}.log: written again", f.dir.display(), day_name(day)))
            }
        }
    };
    // (to stderr itself, after the files' lock: `log::error` would come back here)
    if let Some(s) = say {
        let mut o = io::stderr().lock();
        let _ = o.write_all(s.as_bytes());
        let _ = o.write_all(b"\n");
    }
}

/// In a thread: each day's file before `today` gzipped (`<day>.log` into `<day>.log.gz`, through a temporary file, so
/// a stop on the way leaves the day's file as it was), and the days before the last DAYS_KEPT gone
fn tidy(dir: PathBuf, today: i64) {
    let shown = dir.display().to_string();
    let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new().name("log-tidy".into()).spawn(move || {
        let _one = TIDY.lock();
        if let Err(e) = tidy_now(&dir, today) {
            let _ = writeln!(io::stderr().lock(), "{}: {e} (the log files' tidy)", dir.display());
        }
    });
    if let Err(e) = spawned {
        let _ = writeln!(io::stderr().lock(), "{shown}: {e} (the log files' tidy)");
    }
}

/// a log file's day, "2026-10-31", and whether it is gzipped: `<day>.log` or `<day>.log.gz`
fn file_day(name: &str) -> Option<(&str, bool)> {
    let (day, rest) = name.split_at_checked(10)?;
    let b = day.as_bytes();
    let digits = b.iter().enumerate().all(|(i, c)| if i == 4 || i == 7 { *c == b'-' } else { c.is_ascii_digit() });
    match rest {
        ".log" if digits => Some((day, false)),
        ".log.gz" if digits => Some((day, true)),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn tidy_now(dir: &Path, today: i64) -> io::Result<()> {
    let (today, oldest) = (day_name(today), day_name(today - DAYS_KEPT + 1));
    let mut names: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(dir)?.filter_map(|e| e.ok()?.file_name().into_string().ok()).collect();
    names.sort();
    for name in &names {
        let path = dir.join(name);
        // a gzip a stop cut short: its temporary file (`.part` as older servers named it)
        if name.ends_with(".part") || name.contains(".tmp-") {
            let _ = std::fs::remove_file(&path);
            continue;
        }
        let Some((day, gz)) = file_day(name) else { continue };
        if day < oldest.as_str() {
            std::fs::remove_file(&path)?;
        } else if !gz && day < today.as_str() {
            gzip(dir, day)?;
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// `<day>.log` gzipped onto the end of `<day>.log.gz` (a gzip file of two members, when there was one already: a
/// day's file made again after it was gzipped), then gone
fn gzip(dir: &Path, day: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
    let (log, gz) = (dir.join(format!("{day}.log")), dir.join(format!("{day}.log.gz")));
    atomic_file::Options::new().write_with(&gz, |out| {
        match File::open(&gz) {
            Ok(mut was) => {
                io::copy(&mut was, out)?;
            }
            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        }
        let mut enc = GzEncoder::new(out, Compression::default());
        io::copy(&mut File::open(&log)?, &mut enc)?;
        enc.finish().map(drop)
    })?;
    std::fs::remove_file(&log)
}

        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(&d).unwrap();
        d
    }

    fn gunzip(p: &Path) -> String {
        let mut s = String::new();
        flate2::read::MultiGzDecoder::new(File::open(p).unwrap()).read_to_string(&mut s).unwrap();
        s
    }

        for no in ["2026-10-31.log.gz.part", "2026-10-31.txt", "2026_10_31.log", "26-10-31.log", "x", ""] {
            assert_eq!(file_day(no), None, "{no}");
        }
        assert_eq!(day_name(0), "1970-01-01");
        assert_eq!(day_name(20_392), "2025-10-31");
    }

    // the days before today gzipped (onto a day gzipped already: one file of two members), today's left as it is,
    // the ones before the last DAYS_KEPT gone, a .part of a stop on the way gone, other files left alone
    #[test]

        let d = temp("tidy");

        let w = |name: &str, s: &str| std::fs::write(d.join(name), s).unwrap();
        w("2025-10-31.log", "today\n");
        w("2025-10-30.log", "yesterday\n");
        w("2025-10-29.log", "again\n");
        let mut enc = GzEncoder::new(File::create(d.join("2025-10-29.log.gz")).unwrap(), Compression::default());
        enc.write_all(b"before\n").unwrap();
        enc.finish().unwrap();
        w("2025-10-02.log.gz", "the oldest kept");
        w("2025-10-01.log.gz", "gone");
        w("2025-09-30.log", "gone");
        w("2025-10-28.log.gz.part", "a stop on the way");
        w("2025-10-27.log.gz.tmp-1-0", "a stop on the way");
        w("notes.txt", "not ours");
        tidy_now(&d, today).unwrap();
        let mut names: Vec<String> = std::fs::read_dir(&d).unwrap().map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name().into_string().unwrap()).collect();
        names.sort();
        assert_eq!(names, ["2025-10-02.log.gz", "2025-10-29.log.gz", "2025-10-30.log.gz", "2025-10-31.log", "notes.txt"]);
        assert_eq!(gunzip(&d.join("2025-10-30.log.gz")), "yesterday\n");
        assert_eq!(gunzip(&d.join("2025-10-29.log.gz")), "before\nagain\n");
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read_to_string(d.join("2025-10-31.log")).unwrap(), "today\n");
        let _ = std::fs::remove_dir_all(&d);
    }
}

//! Randomness from the OS: Node's `crypto.randomBytes(n)` and `crypto.randomInt(min, max)`.

/// n random bytes
pub fn bytes(n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut b = vec![0u8; n];
    fill(&mut b);
    b
}

/// fills `b` with random bytes
pub fn fill(b: &mut [u8]) {
    getrandom::fill(b).expect("the OS's random numbers");
}

/// a random u32
pub fn u32() -> u32 {
    let mut b = [0u8; 4];
    fill(&mut b);
    u32::from_le_bytes(b)
}

/// a random u64
pub fn u64() -> u64 {
    let mut b = [0u8; 8];
    fill(&mut b);
    u64::from_le_bytes(b)
}

/// `crypto.randomInt(min, max)`: uniform in min..max (max exclusive), no modulo bias
pub fn int(min: i64, max: i64) -> i64 {
    assert!(max > min, "randomInt: max must be above min");
    let range = (max - min) as u64;
    let zone = u64::MAX - (u64::MAX % range);
    loop {
        let v = u64();
        if v < zone {
            return min + (v % range) as i64;
        }
    }
}

/// `Math.random()`: uniform in [0, 1)
pub fn unit() -> f64 {
    (u64() >> 11) as f64 / (1u64 << 53) as f64
}

/// lowercase hex of n random bytes (`crypto.randomBytes(n).toString('hex')`)
pub fn hex(n: usize) -> String {
    bytes(n).iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

//! `js::number_to_string` against node's `String(x)` (skipped with a message without node): every kind of double,
//! and many with few significant bits (float32 values, dyadic fractions), where two shortest forms can tie.

use nfsu2_util::js::number_to_string;

fn numbers() -> Vec<f64> {
    let mut x: u64 = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15;
    let mut next = move || {
        x ^= x << 13;
        x ^= x >> 7;
        x ^= x << 17;
        x
    };
    let mut out = vec![0.0, -0.0, 1.0, 0.1, 0.5, 1e21, 1e-7, 5e-324, f64::MAX, f64::MIN_POSITIVE, -69633.0 / 131072.0];
    for _ in 0..200_000 {
        // a float32's value (the game's times and positions)
        let f = f32::from_bits(next() as u32);
        if f.is_finite() {
            out.push(f as f64);
        }
    }
    for _ in 0..100_000 {
        // m / 2^q with few bits in m: the ties' home
        let m = next() >> (64 - 1 - (next() % 40)) as u32;
        let q = (next() % 30) as i32;
        out.push(m as f64 / 2f64.powi(q));
        out.push(-(m as f64) * 2f64.powi(q));
    }
    for _ in 0..100_000 {
        // any double
        let d = f64::from_bits(next());
        if d.is_finite() {
            out.push(d);
        }
    }
    out
}

#[test]
fn numbers_as_node_writes_them() {
    if std::process::Command::new("node").arg("--version").output().is_err() {
        println!("skipped: no node");
        return;
    }
    let xs = numbers();
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("nfsu2-util-numbers-{}", std::process::id()));
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    // as bits, so nothing is lost on the way
    let input = dir.join("bits.txt");
    std::fs::write(&input, xs.iter().map(|x| format!("{:016x}\n", x.to_bits())).collect::<String>()).unwrap();
    let script = "const fs = require('fs'); const b = Buffer.alloc(8); const out = [];\n\
        for (const l of fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], 'utf8').split('\\n')) { if (!l) continue; b.writeBigUInt64BE(BigInt('0x' + l)); out.push(String(b.readDoubleBE(0))); }\n\
        process.stdout.write(out.join('\\n'));";
    let out = std::process::Command::new("node").args(["-e", script, input.to_str().unwrap()]).output().expect("node");
    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&dir).ok();
    assert!(out.status.success(), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stderr));
    let js = String::from_utf8(out.stdout).unwrap();
    let js: Vec<&str> = js.split('\n').collect();
    assert_eq!(js.len(), xs.len());
    let bad: Vec<String> = xs
        .iter()
        .zip(&js)
        .filter(|(x, s)| number_to_string(**x) != **s)
        .map(|(x, s)| format!("{:e}: rust {}, js {s}", x, number_to_string(*x)))
        .collect();
    println!("number_to_string: {} numbers, {} differ", xs.len(), bad.len());
    assert!(bad.is_empty(), "{} differ, e.g.\n{}", bad.len(), bad[..bad.len().min(20)].join("\n"));
}
