//! Keyphrase saves (`/vault`): a player's saves, kept on the server under a keyphrase only the player has.
//!
//! The page does everything that knows what a save is (web/src/app/vault.ts): it makes the keyphrase, derives a key
//! and a token from it, packs the save folder (but the screenshots), encrypts that with the key and sends the result
//! with the token.  The server sees neither the keyphrase, nor the key, nor a save: it keeps the bytes it was sent
//! under the SHA-256 of the token, and hands them back to whoever shows that token.  A copy of the folder (a backup,
//! a disk) names no player and opens no save.
//!
//! # On disk
//!
//! `<dir>/<3 hex>/<64 hex>`: one file per keyphrase, named by its id's hex (the first 3 digits are a folder: 4096 of
//! them, a few thousand files each at millions of keyphrases).  A file is a 64-byte head, the current version, then
//! the copy of an earlier day (the undo of a bad day: a browser that synced a lost career):
//!
//! | at | size | |
//! |---|---|---|
//! | 0 | 4 | "NFV1" |
//! | 4 | u32 | flags ([`KEPT`]) |
//! | 8 | u64 | the current version's rev (random: its ETag) |
//! | 16 | i64 | when it was saved (ms since 1970) |
//! | 24 | u32 | its length |
//! | 28 | u32 | the earlier copy's length |
//! | 32 | u64 | its rev |
//! | 40 | i64 | when it was saved (0: there is none) |
//! | 48 | i64 | when the keyphrase was first saved |
//! | 56 | 8 | 0 |
//!
//! All little-endian.  The earlier copy is the last version saved on an earlier day (UTC) than the current one: the
//! first save of a day moves the current version there.  A file is written whole: a temporary file beside it
//! (`<id>.tmp-<pid>-<n>`, 0600), synced, then renamed over it, so a crash leaves the old file or the new one, never
//! half of one.  Its mtime is when the keyphrase was last used (saved, or read: touched at most once a day).
//!
//! # Limits
//!
//! - one version at most [`VaultOptions::max_body`] bytes (256 KB: a save folder without screenshots and covers packs
//!   into 6-14 KB, so that is dozens of profiles);
//! - new keyphrases stop once all of them take [`VaultOptions::new_until`] bytes, every write that grows a file at
//!   [`VaultOptions::max_bytes`] (counted in 4 KB blocks, as the disk takes them); what is kept stays readable;
//! - what the saves add to the disk comes at most [`VaultOptions::per_day`] bytes a day from all clients together, a
//!   quarter of that at once: what fills the room for new keyphrases in [`FILL_DAYS`], 2000 new keyphrases' worth at
//!   least.  A new keyphrase counts as [`VaultOptions::base`] at least (32 KB: two versions of a 14 KB save folder)
//!   and may grow to that without counting again; a save that grows its file past it counts what it adds.  So no
//!   byte on the disk goes uncounted, also of small keyphrases grown later, and a save that keeps its size, or stays
//!   within `base`, never waits for it.  The per-client limits alone let anyone with enough addresses fill the room
//!   within days, and whatever fills it stays two years (the third security audit, 2026-10-23); so a flood now takes
//!   a month, and leaves a line a minute in the log.  (The first cap counted keyphrases, each as the most it can hold,
//!   528 KB: 50 GB took 2838 a day, and turned players away at 4,300 at once, 2026-10-23.);
//! - every write that grows a file stops while the disk under the folder has less than [`VaultOptions::min_free`]
//!   bytes free, or fewer than [`VaultOptions::min_free_files`] files (inodes): the caps count bytes, the room given
//!   may be more than the disk has, and many small files run a disk out of inodes before its bytes;
//! - a keyphrase unused for [`VaultOptions::unused_ms`] (two years) goes at the next sweep, unless its flags say
//!   [`KEPT`] (an operator's choice for one keyphrase: kept however long it goes unused).
//!
//! The totals behind the caps are counted by [`Vault::sweep`] (at the start, then daily) and kept up to date by each
//! write; until the first count ends only the day's bytes and the free disk limit them.  A write during a
//! sweep may be missed by its count: the next one sets it right; a file that goes while the sweep looks at it (a
//! save's rename, a delete) is passed over.
//!
//! Every call blocks (file I/O): the server makes them on its blocking threads.  Calls for one keyphrase take turns
//! (a lock per id, of 256 stripes); the others run side by side.

use std::fs;
use std::io::{self, Read};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicI64, Ordering};
use std::time::{Duration, SystemTime, UNIX_EPOCH};

use parking_lot::{Mutex, MutexGuard};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use nfsu2_util::atomic_file::Options;

pub const MAGIC: &[u8; 4] = b"NFV1";
pub const HEAD: usize = 64;
/// a flag: the keyphrase is kept without end (the sweep leaves it however long it goes unused)
pub const KEPT: u32 = 1;
pub const DAY_MS: i64 = 86_400_000;
/// the disk's block: what a file takes is its length rounded up to it
pub const BLOCK: u64 = 4096;
/// a temporary file that was never renamed (the server stopped mid-write) goes at the first sweep an hour after
const STALE_TMP_MS: i64 = 3_600_000;
/// the days the saves take at the least to fill the room for new keyphrases (`sized`)
pub const FILL_DAYS: u64 = 30;

pub struct VaultOptions {
    /// the folder (made 0700)
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    /// one version's bytes at most
    pub max_body: usize,
    /// every write that grows a file stops at this many bytes in all
    pub max_bytes: u64,
    /// new keyphrases stop at this many bytes in all
    pub new_until: u64,
    /// the bytes the saves may add to the disk a day, all clients together (a quarter of it at once)
    pub per_day: u64,
    /// what a new keyphrase counts as at the least: its file grows to it without counting again
    pub base: u64,
    /// every write that grows a file stops while the disk has fewer bytes free than this...
    pub min_free: u64,
    /// ...or fewer files (inodes)
    pub min_free_files: u64,
    /// a keyphrase unused this long goes (but a [`KEPT`] one)
    pub unused_ms: i64,
}

impl VaultOptions {
    /// `gb` gigabytes in all, new keyphrases until 90 % of it, the saves adding at most what fills that in
    /// [`FILL_DAYS`], 256 KB a version, a new keyphrase 32 KB at the least, 2 GB and 100,000 files kept free on the
    /// disk, two years unused
    pub fn sized(dir: PathBuf, gb: f64) -> VaultOptions {
        let max_bytes = (gb * 1e9) as u64;
        let (max_body, new_until, base) = (256 << 10, max_bytes / 10 * 9, 32 << 10);
        VaultOptions {
            dir,
            max_body: max_body as usize,
            max_bytes,
            new_until,
            per_day: (new_until / FILL_DAYS).max(2000 * base),
            base,
            min_free: 2_000_000_000,
            min_free_files: 100_000,
            unused_ms: 730 * DAY_MS,
        }
    }
}

/// What a keyphrase is kept under: the SHA-256 of the token the page derives from it.
pub type Id = [u8; 32];

pub fn id_of(token: &[u8]) -> Id {
    Sha256::digest(token).into()
}

fn hex(id: &Id) -> String {
    id.iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
}

/// a file name that is an id's hex (64 lowercase hex digits)
fn parse_hex(name: &str) -> Option<Id> {
    let b = name.as_bytes();
    if b.len() != 64 || !b.iter().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit() || (b'a'..=b'f').contains(c)) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut id = [0u8; 32];
    for (i, o) in id.iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *o = u8::from_str_radix(&name[i * 2..i * 2 + 2], 16).ok()?;
    }
    Some(id)
}

/// what a file of `len` bytes takes on the disk
pub fn disk(len: u64) -> u64 {
    len.div_ceil(BLOCK) * BLOCK
}

/// A version: its rev (the ETag) and when it was saved.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Version {
    pub rev: u64,
    pub saved: i64,
}

/// What is known of a keyphrase's file: its current version, the copy of an earlier day, its flags, its first save.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Meta {
    pub cur: Version,
    pub prev: Option<Version>,
    pub flags: u32,
    pub created: i64,
}

/// Which version a read wants.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Want {
    Current,
    Earlier,
}

/// What a write expects to find: no keyphrase yet (If-None-Match: *), or this rev as the current version (If-Match).
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Cond {
    New,
    Rev(u64),
}

/// What a write did.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Put {
    Saved {
        meta: Meta,
        created: bool,
    },
    /// the condition did not hold: what is there (None: no keyphrase)
    Conflict(Option<Meta>),
    TooLarge,
    /// the caps: no new keyphrase, or no more bytes
    Full,
    /// the disk is nearly full (`min_free`, `min_free_files`): nothing that grows a file
    DiskLow,
    /// the day's bytes are taken (`per_day`): a new keyphrase, or a save that grows one, later
    Busy,
}

/// What a sweep found, and did.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Sweep {
    pub keyphrases: u64,
    pub bytes: u64,
    /// keyphrases removed after going unused
    pub removed: u64,
    /// temporary files of unfinished writes removed
    pub temps: u64,
}

pub struct Vault {
    o: VaultOptions,
    locks: Vec<Mutex<()>>,
    bytes: AtomicI64,
    count: AtomicI64,
    counted: AtomicBool,
    /// the bytes the saves may add now (`per_day`'s bucket) and when it was last filled up (ms)
    room: Mutex<(f64, i64)>,
}

fn u32_at(b: &[u8], i: usize) -> u32 {
    u32::from_le_bytes(b[i..i + 4].try_into().expect("4 bytes"))
}
fn u64_at(b: &[u8], i: usize) -> u64 {
    u64::from_le_bytes(b[i..i + 8].try_into().expect("8 bytes"))
}

/// the head of a file: its Meta and the two lengths, or None when it is not one of ours (`size`: the whole file's)
fn parse_head(b: &[u8], size: u64) -> Option<(Meta, usize, usize)> {
    if b.len() < HEAD || &b[..4] != MAGIC {
        return None;
    }
    let (len, plen) = (u32_at(b, 24) as usize, u32_at(b, 28) as usize);
    if (HEAD + len + plen) as u64 != size {
        return None;
    }
    let prev_saved = u64_at(b, 40) as i64;
    let meta = Meta {
        cur: Version { rev: u64_at(b, 8), saved: u64_at(b, 16) as i64 },
        prev: (prev_saved != 0).then(|| Version { rev: u64_at(b, 32), saved: prev_saved }),
        flags: u32_at(b, 4),
        created: u64_at(b, 48) as i64,
    };
    Some((meta, len, plen))
}

/// a whole file: the head, the current version, the earlier copy
fn file_bytes(meta: &Meta, cur: &[u8], prev: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut b = Vec::with_capacity(HEAD + cur.len() + prev.len());
    b.extend_from_slice(MAGIC);
    b.extend_from_slice(&meta.flags.to_le_bytes());
    b.extend_from_slice(&meta.cur.rev.to_le_bytes());
    b.extend_from_slice(&(meta.cur.saved as u64).to_le_bytes());
    b.extend_from_slice(&(cur.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    b.extend_from_slice(&(prev.len() as u32).to_le_bytes());
    let p = meta.prev.unwrap_or(Version { rev: 0, saved: 0 });
    b.extend_from_slice(&p.rev.to_le_bytes());
    b.extend_from_slice(&(p.saved as u64).to_le_bytes());
    b.extend_from_slice(&(meta.created as u64).to_le_bytes());
    b.extend_from_slice(&[0u8; 8]);
    b.extend_from_slice(cur);
    b.extend_from_slice(prev);
    b
}

/// (no path in it: the console never names a keyphrase's file, nor its id)
fn corrupt() -> io::Error {
    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, "a keyphrase's file is damaged")
}

fn mtime_ms(m: &fs::Metadata) -> i64 {
    m.modified().ok().and_then(|t| t.duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).ok()).map_or(0, |d| d.as_millis() as i64)
}

fn system_time(ms: i64) -> SystemTime {
    UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_millis(ms.max(0) as u64)
}

fn mkdir(p: &Path) -> io::Result<()> {
    use std::os::unix::fs::DirBuilderExt;
    fs::DirBuilder::new().recursive(true).mode(0o700).create(p)
}

impl Vault {
    /// The vault in `o.dir` (made 0700 when missing).  Nothing is counted yet: [`Vault::sweep`] does that.
    pub fn open(o: VaultOptions) -> io::Result<Vault> {
        mkdir(&o.dir)?;
        Ok(Vault {
            locks: (0..256).map(|_| Mutex::new(())).collect(),
            bytes: AtomicI64::new(0),
            count: AtomicI64::new(0),
            counted: AtomicBool::new(false),
            room: Mutex::new((Self::room_burst(&o), 0)),
            o,
        })
    }

    /// the bytes the saves may add at once: a quarter of a day's
    fn room_burst(o: &VaultOptions) -> f64 {
        o.per_day as f64 / 4.0
    }

    /// `n` bytes out of the day's, if they are left (the bucket refills at per_day a day)
    fn take_room(&self, n: u64, now: i64) -> bool {
        let mut q = self.room.lock();
        let (v, t) = *q;
        let refill = if t == 0 { 0.0 } else { (now - t).max(0) as f64 * self.o.per_day as f64 / DAY_MS as f64 };
        let v = (v + refill).min(Self::room_burst(&self.o));
        let ok = v >= n as f64;
        *q = (if ok { v - n as f64 } else { v }, now.max(t));
        ok
    }

    /// the disk under the folder has `min_free` bytes and `min_free_files` files free (what an unprivileged writer
    /// may take); true when statvfs cannot tell, or the filesystem counts no files
    fn disk_ok(&self) -> bool {
        use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
        let Ok(path) = std::ffi::CString::new(self.o.dir.as_os_str().as_bytes()) else { return true };
        // SAFETY: statvfs writes the struct it is given, and only that; the path is NUL-terminated
        let mut s: libc::statvfs = unsafe { std::mem::zeroed() };
        if unsafe { libc::statvfs(path.as_ptr(), &mut s) } != 0 {
            return true;
        }
        let free = s.f_bavail as u64 * s.f_frsize as u64;
        free >= self.o.min_free && (s.f_files == 0 || s.f_favail as u64 >= self.o.min_free_files)
    }

    pub fn options(&self) -> &VaultOptions {
        &self.o
    }

    /// keyphrases kept, the bytes they take on the disk, and whether that was counted yet
    pub fn usage(&self) -> (u64, u64, bool) {
        (
            self.count.load(Ordering::Relaxed).max(0) as u64,
            self.bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed).max(0) as u64,
            self.counted.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
        )
    }

    fn lock(&self, id: &Id) -> MutexGuard<'_, ()> {
        self.locks[id[0] as usize].lock()
    }

    fn path(&self, id: &Id) -> PathBuf {
        let h = hex(id);
        self.o.dir.join(&h[..3]).join(h)
    }

    /// the file's bytes, or None when there is none
    fn read(p: &Path) -> io::Result<Option<Vec<u8>>> {
        match fs::read(p) {
            Ok(b) => Ok(Some(b)),
            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
            Err(e) => Err(e),
        }
    }

    /// the keyphrase was used: its file's mtime moves to now when it is a day old or more
    fn touch(p: &Path, now: i64) {
        if let Ok(m) = fs::metadata(p)
            && mtime_ms(&m) <= now - DAY_MS
            && let Ok(f) = fs::File::options().write(true).open(p)
        {
            let _ = f.set_modified(system_time(now));
        }
    }

    /// the whole file in place of the old one: a temporary file beside it (0600), synced, renamed over it
    fn write(&self, p: &Path, bytes: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
        Options::new().make_folder().write(p, bytes)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// What is known of a keyphrase (its file's head), or None; a read: the keyphrase counts as used.
    pub fn meta(&self, id: &Id, now: i64) -> io::Result<Option<Meta>> {
        let p = self.path(id);
        let _g = self.lock(id);
        let mut f = match fs::File::open(&p) {
            Ok(f) => f,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(None),
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        let size = f.metadata()?.len();
        let mut head = [0u8; HEAD];
        f.read_exact(&mut head).map_err(|_| corrupt())?;
        let (meta, ..) = parse_head(&head, size).ok_or_else(corrupt)?;
        Self::touch(&p, now);
        Ok(Some(meta))
    }

    /// A keyphrase's version (the current one, or the copy of an earlier day: empty when there is none) with what is
    /// known of it, or None when there is no keyphrase; a read: the keyphrase counts as used.
    pub fn get(&self, id: &Id, want: Want, now: i64) -> io::Result<Option<(Meta, Vec<u8>)>> {
        let p = self.path(id);
        let _g = self.lock(id);
        let Some(b) = Self::read(&p)? else { return Ok(None) };
        let (meta, len, _) = parse_head(&b, b.len() as u64).ok_or_else(corrupt)?;
        Self::touch(&p, now);
        let body = match want {
            Want::Current => b[HEAD..HEAD + len].to_vec(),
            Want::Earlier => b[HEAD + len..].to_vec(),
        };
        Ok(Some((meta, body)))
    }

    /// Saves `body` as the keyphrase's current version, if `cond` holds and the caps allow.  The first save of a day
    /// keeps the version it replaces as the earlier copy.
    pub fn put(&self, id: &Id, cond: Cond, body: &[u8], now: i64) -> io::Result<Put> {
        if body.len() > self.o.max_body {
            return Ok(Put::TooLarge);
        }
        let p = self.path(id);
        let _g = self.lock(id);
        let old = Self::read(&p)?;
        let parsed = match &old {
            Some(b) => Some(parse_head(b, b.len() as u64).ok_or_else(corrupt)?),
            None => None,
        };
        match (cond, &parsed) {
            (Cond::New, Some((m, ..))) => return Ok(Put::Conflict(Some(*m))),
            (Cond::Rev(_), None) => return Ok(Put::Conflict(None)),
            (Cond::Rev(r), Some((m, ..))) if m.cur.rev != r => return Ok(Put::Conflict(Some(*m))),
            _ => {}
        }
        let (meta, prev_body): (Meta, &[u8]) = match (&old, &parsed) {
            (Some(b), Some((m, len, _))) => {
                let new_day = m.cur.saved.div_euclid(DAY_MS) != now.div_euclid(DAY_MS);
                let (prev, prev_body) = if new_day { (Some(m.cur), &b[HEAD..HEAD + len]) } else { (m.prev, &b[HEAD + len..]) };
                let rev = Self::new_rev(&[m.cur.rev, prev.map_or(0, |v| v.rev)]);
                (Meta { cur: Version { rev, saved: now }, prev, flags: m.flags, created: m.created }, prev_body)
            }
            _ => (Meta { cur: Version { rev: Self::new_rev(&[]), saved: now }, prev: None, flags: 0, created: now }, &[]),
        };
        let bytes = file_bytes(&meta, body, prev_body);
        let (was, will) = (old.as_ref().map(|b| disk(b.len() as u64)), disk(bytes.len() as u64));
        let grows = will as i64 - was.unwrap_or(0) as i64;
        // what counts against the day's bytes: a new keyphrase at least `base`, a save what it grows the file past
        // both its blocks and `base`
        let counts = match was {
            None => will.max(self.o.base),
            Some(was) => will.saturating_sub(was.max(self.o.base)),
        };
        if self.counted.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
            let total = self.bytes.load(Ordering::Relaxed);
            let over = |cap: u64| total + grows > cap as i64;
            if (old.is_none() && over(self.o.new_until)) || (grows > 0 && over(self.o.max_bytes)) {
                return Ok(Put::Full);
            }
        }
        if grows > 0 && !self.disk_ok() {
            return Ok(Put::DiskLow);
        }
        if counts > 0 && !self.take_room(counts, now) {
            return Ok(Put::Busy);
        }
        self.write(&p, &bytes)?;
        self.bytes.fetch_add(grows, Ordering::Relaxed);
        if old.is_none() {
            self.count.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        }
        Ok(Put::Saved { meta, created: old.is_none() })
    }

    /// a rev that is none of `not` (nor 0)
    fn new_rev(not: &[u64]) -> u64 {
        loop {
            let r = nfsu2_util::rand::u64();
            if r != 0 && !not.contains(&r) {
                return r;
            }
        }
    }

    /// Removes a keyphrase, both versions: false when there was none.
    pub fn delete(&self, id: &Id) -> io::Result<bool> {
        let p = self.path(id);
        let _g = self.lock(id);
        let size = match fs::metadata(&p) {
            Ok(m) => m.len(),
            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => return Ok(false),
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        fs::remove_file(&p)?;
        self.bytes.fetch_sub(disk(size) as i64, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.count.fetch_sub(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Sets a keyphrase's flags (an operator's: [`KEPT`]); its versions and its last use stay as they were.  False
    /// when there is no such keyphrase.
    pub fn set_flags(&self, id: &Id, flags: u32) -> io::Result<bool> {
        let p = self.path(id);
        let _g = self.lock(id);
        let Some(b) = Self::read(&p)? else { return Ok(false) };
        let (mut meta, len, _) = parse_head(&b, b.len() as u64).ok_or_else(corrupt)?;
        let used = fs::metadata(&p)?.modified()?;
        meta.flags = flags;
        self.write(&p, &file_bytes(&meta, &b[HEAD..HEAD + len], &b[HEAD + len..]))?;
        fs::File::options().write(true).open(&p)?.set_modified(used)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    /// Goes through every file: removes the keyphrases unused for `unused_ms` (but the [`KEPT`] ones) and the
    /// temporary files of writes that never finished, and counts the rest, which the caps go by from then on.  Files
    /// that are not a keyphrase's are left alone and not counted.
    pub fn sweep(&self, now: i64) -> io::Result<Sweep> {
        let mut s = Sweep::default();
        let shards = match fs::read_dir(&self.o.dir) {
            Ok(r) => r,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
                self.set_totals(&s);
                return Ok(s);
            }
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        };
        for shard in shards {
            let shard = shard?;
            let name = shard.file_name();
            let name = name.to_string_lossy();
            if name.len() != 3 || !shard.file_type()?.is_dir() {
                continue;
            }
            let files = match fs::read_dir(shard.path()) {
                Ok(r) => r,
                Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => continue,
                Err(e) => return Err(e),
            };
            for f in files {
                let f = f?;
                // a file that went since it was listed (a save's temporary file renamed, a delete): passed over, not
                // the end of the count (which left the caps off until the next day's)
                let m = match f.metadata() {
                    Ok(m) => m,
                    Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => continue,
                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
                };
                let name = f.file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned();
                if !m.is_file() {
                    continue;
                }
                if name.contains(".tmp-") && parse_hex(&name[..name.find(".tmp-").unwrap_or(0)]).is_some() {
                    if mtime_ms(&m) < now - STALE_TMP_MS && fs::remove_file(f.path()).is_ok() {
                        s.temps += 1;
                    } else {
                        s.bytes += disk(m.len());
                    }
                    continue;
                }
                let Some(id) = parse_hex(&name) else { continue };
                if mtime_ms(&m) < now - self.o.unused_ms && self.remove_unused(&id, now)? {
                    s.removed += 1;
                    continue;
                }
                s.keyphrases += 1;
                s.bytes += disk(m.len());
            }
        }
        self.set_totals(&s);
        Ok(s)
    }

    /// removes a keyphrase that is still unused once its lock is held (a save may have come since it was seen), and
    /// not [`KEPT`]
    fn remove_unused(&self, id: &Id, now: i64) -> io::Result<bool> {
        let p = self.path(id);
        let _g = self.lock(id);
        let Ok(m) = fs::metadata(&p) else { return Ok(false) };
        if mtime_ms(&m) >= now - self.o.unused_ms {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        let mut head = [0u8; HEAD];
        let kept = fs::File::open(&p).and_then(|mut f| f.read_exact(&mut head)).is_ok()
            && parse_head(&head, m.len()).is_some_and(|(meta, ..)| meta.flags & KEPT != 0);
        if kept {
            return Ok(false);
        }
        fs::remove_file(&p)?;
        Ok(true)
    }

    fn set_totals(&self, s: &Sweep) {
        self.bytes.store(s.bytes as i64, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.count.store(s.keyphrases as i64, Ordering::Relaxed);
        self.counted.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }
}

fn vault(o: impl FnOnce(&mut VaultOptions)) -> (tempfile::TempDir, Vault) {

#[test]
fn a_new_keyphrase_then_its_versions() {
    let (_d, v) = vault(|_| {});
    let id = id_of(b"a");
    assert_eq!(v.get(&id, Want::Current, T0).unwrap(), None);
    assert_eq!(v.meta(&id, T0).unwrap(), None);
    let p = v.put(&id, Cond::New, b"one", T0).unwrap();
    let Put::Saved { meta: m1, created: true } = p else { panic!("{p:?}") };
    assert_eq!((m1.cur.saved, m1.prev, m1.flags, m1.created), (T0, None, 0, T0));
    assert_eq!(v.get(&id, Want::Current, T0).unwrap(), Some((m1, b"one".to_vec())));
    assert_eq!(v.meta(&id, T0).unwrap(), Some(m1));
    // New again: there is one
    assert_eq!(v.put(&id, Cond::New, b"two", T0).unwrap(), Put::Conflict(Some(m1)));
    // the wrong rev, or a rev where there is nothing
    assert_eq!(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m1.cur.rev ^ 1), b"two", T0).unwrap(), Put::Conflict(Some(m1)));
    assert_eq!(v.put(&id_of(b"b"), Cond::Rev(m1.cur.rev), b"two", T0).unwrap(), Put::Conflict(None));
    // the same day: the current version is replaced, no earlier copy
    let m2 = saved(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m1.cur.rev), b"two", T0 + HOUR).unwrap());
    assert_ne!(m2.cur.rev, m1.cur.rev);
    assert_eq!((m2.cur.saved, m2.prev, m2.created), (T0 + HOUR, None, T0));
    assert_eq!(v.get(&id, Want::Earlier, T0).unwrap(), Some((m2, vec![])));
    // the next day: the version of the day before is the earlier copy
    let m3 = saved(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m2.cur.rev), b"three", T0 + DAY_MS).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(m3.prev, Some(m2.cur));
    assert_eq!(v.get(&id, Want::Earlier, T0).unwrap(), Some((m3, b"two".to_vec())));
    // more saves that day keep it
    let m4 = saved(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m3.cur.rev), b"four", T0 + DAY_MS + HOUR).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(m4.prev, Some(m2.cur));
    assert_eq!(v.get(&id, Want::Earlier, T0).unwrap().unwrap().1, b"two");
    assert_eq!(v.get(&id, Want::Current, T0).unwrap().unwrap().1, b"four");
    // two days on: the day before's last version
    let m5 = saved(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m4.cur.rev), b"five", T0 + 3 * DAY_MS).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(m5.prev, Some(m4.cur));
    assert_eq!(v.get(&id, Want::Earlier, T0).unwrap().unwrap().1, b"four");
    assert_eq!(fs::metadata(file(&v, &id)).unwrap().len(), (HEAD + 4 + 4) as u64);
}

#[test]
fn the_caps_count_disk_blocks_once_counted() {
    // three blocks for new keyphrases, four in all
    let (_d, v) = vault(|o| {
        o.new_until = 3 * BLOCK;
        o.max_bytes = 4 * BLOCK;
    });
    let ids: Vec<Id> = (0..5u8).map(|i| id_of(&[i])).collect();
    // not counted yet: no cap
    assert_eq!(v.usage(), (0, 0, false));
    let m0 = saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(v.sweep(T0).unwrap(), Sweep { keyphrases: 1, bytes: BLOCK, removed: 0, temps: 0 });
    assert_eq!(v.usage(), (1, BLOCK, true));
    saved(v.put(&ids[1], Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap());
    saved(v.put(&ids[2], Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(v.usage(), (3, 3 * BLOCK, true));
    // a fourth keyphrase would pass the new ones' cap
    assert_eq!(v.put(&ids[3], Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap(), Put::Full);
    // a keyphrase there may grow to the cap of all
    let big = vec![7u8; BLOCK as usize];
    let m0b = saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0.cur.rev), &big, T0).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(v.usage(), (3, 4 * BLOCK, true));
    // not past it
    assert_eq!(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0b.cur.rev), &vec![7u8; 2 * BLOCK as usize], T0).unwrap(), Put::Full);
    // shrinking is always fine, and gives room again
    let m0c = saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0b.cur.rev), b"y", T0).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(v.usage(), (3, 3 * BLOCK, true));
    // and so does a deletion
    assert!(v.delete(&ids[1]).unwrap());
    assert!(!v.delete(&ids[1]).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(v.usage(), (2, 2 * BLOCK, true));
    assert!(matches!(v.put(&ids[3], Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap(), Put::Saved { created: true, .. }));
    assert_eq!(v.get(&ids[0], Want::Current, T0).unwrap().unwrap().0, m0c);
    assert_eq!(v.get(&ids[1], Want::Current, T0).unwrap(), None);
}

#[test]
fn the_saves_add_at_most_per_day() {
    // 32 blocks a day: 8 at once, then one every 45 minutes; a new keyphrase counts as 2 blocks at least
    let (_d, v) = vault(|o| {
        o.per_day = 32 * BLOCK;
        o.base = 2 * BLOCK;
    });
    let ids: Vec<Id> = (0..10u8).map(|i| id_of(&[i])).collect();
    // a version whose file takes n blocks (no earlier copy: all of it on one day)
    let blocks = |n: u64| vec![7u8; (n * BLOCK) as usize - HEAD];
    let m0 = saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap());
    for id in &ids[1..4] {
        saved(v.put(id, Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap());
    }
    assert_eq!(v.put(&ids[4], Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap(), Put::Busy);
    assert!(!file(&v, &ids[4]).exists());
    // a keyphrase there grows to `base` without counting, and saves at its size never wait
    let m0 = saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0.cur.rev), &blocks(2), T0).unwrap());
    let m0 = saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0.cur.rev), &blocks(2), T0).unwrap());
    // past it, what it adds counts: so small keyphrases grown later fill nothing faster
    assert_eq!(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0.cur.rev), &blocks(3), T0).unwrap(), Put::Busy);
    let m0 = saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0.cur.rev), b"y", T0).unwrap());
    // two hours on, 2.7 blocks: a new keyphrase, then not a block more
    saved(v.put(&ids[4], Cond::New, b"x", T0 + 2 * HOUR).unwrap());
    assert_eq!(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0.cur.rev), &blocks(3), T0 + 2 * HOUR).unwrap(), Put::Busy);
    // an hour more: the block it grows past `base`
    saved(v.put(&ids[0], Cond::Rev(m0.cur.rev), &blocks(3), T0 + 3 * HOUR).unwrap());
    // a day later: 8 blocks at once again, not 32
    for id in &ids[5..9] {
        saved(v.put(id, Cond::New, b"x", T0 + 30 * HOUR).unwrap());
    }
    assert_eq!(v.put(&ids[9], Cond::New, b"x", T0 + 30 * HOUR).unwrap(), Put::Busy);
    // what `sized` gives: what fills the room for new keyphrases in FILL_DAYS, 2000 new keyphrases' worth at least
    let o = VaultOptions::sized(PathBuf::from("/x"), 50.0);
    assert_eq!((o.per_day, o.base), (1_500_000_000, 32 << 10));
    assert_eq!(VaultOptions::sized(PathBuf::from("/x"), 140.0).per_day, 126_000_000_000 / FILL_DAYS);
    assert_eq!(VaultOptions::sized(PathBuf::from("/x"), 1.0).per_day, 2000 * (32 << 10));
}

#[test]
fn a_nearly_full_disk_takes_nothing_that_grows() {
    let (d, v) = vault(|_| {});
    let id = id_of(b"a");
    let mut m = saved(v.put(&id, Cond::New, b"four", T0).unwrap());

        assert_eq!(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m.cur.rev), &vec![1u8; 2 * BLOCK as usize], T0).unwrap(), Put::DiskLow);
        // the same blocks, or fewer: a save goes on, and so do reads and deletes

    }

#[test]
fn the_count_passes_over_files_that_go_while_it_runs() {
    // saves (a temporary file renamed over the old) and deletes next to sweeps: every sweep ends with a count
    let (_d, v) = vault(|_| {});
    let v = std::sync::Arc::new(v);
    for i in 0..400u32 {
        v.put(&id_of(&i.to_le_bytes()), Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap();
    }
    let stop = std::sync::Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
    let churn = {
        let (v, stop) = (v.clone(), stop.clone());
        std::thread::spawn(move || {
            let mut n = 0u32;
            while !stop.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
                let id = id_of(&(1000 + n % 64).to_le_bytes());
                match v.meta(&id, T0).unwrap() {
                    Some(_) if n.is_multiple_of(3) => assert!(v.delete(&id).unwrap()),
                    Some(m) => drop(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m.cur.rev), &n.to_le_bytes(), T0).unwrap()),
                    None => drop(v.put(&id, Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap()),
                }
                n += 1;
            }
        })
    };
    for _ in 0..200 {
        let s = v.sweep(T0).expect("a count");
        assert!(s.keyphrases >= 400);
    }
    stop.store(true, Ordering::Relaxed);
    churn.join().unwrap();
}

#[test]
fn the_sweep_removes_the_unused_but_the_kept() {
    let (_d, v) = vault(|_| {});
    let now = T0 + 800 * DAY_MS;
    let (old, kept, recent, read) = (id_of(b"old"), id_of(b"kept"), id_of(b"recent"), id_of(b"read"));
    for id in [&old, &kept, &recent, &read] {
        v.put(id, Cond::New, b"x", T0).unwrap();
    }
    for id in [&old, &kept, &read] {
        set_mtime(&file(&v, id), now - 731 * DAY_MS);
    }
    set_mtime(&file(&v, &recent), now - 729 * DAY_MS);
    assert!(v.set_flags(&kept, KEPT).unwrap());
    assert!(!v.set_flags(&id_of(b"none"), KEPT).unwrap());
    // the flags stay out of the way of its last use
    assert_eq!(mtime_ms(&fs::metadata(file(&v, &kept)).unwrap()), now - 731 * DAY_MS);
    assert_eq!(v.meta(&kept, now - 731 * DAY_MS).unwrap().unwrap().flags, KEPT);
    // a read is a use
    assert!(v.meta(&read, now).unwrap().is_some());
    // what is not ours stays, uncounted
    fs::create_dir_all(v.o.dir.join("abc")).unwrap();
    fs::write(v.o.dir.join("abc").join("notes.txt"), b"mine").unwrap();
    fs::write(v.o.dir.join("readme"), b"mine").unwrap();
    // a write that never finished: gone after an hour
    let (stale, fresh) = (format!("{}.tmp-1-0", hex(&recent)), format!("{}.tmp-1-1", hex(&recent)));
    let shard = file(&v, &recent).parent().unwrap().to_path_buf();
    fs::write(shard.join(&stale), b"half").unwrap();
    set_mtime(&shard.join(&stale), now - 2 * HOUR);
    fs::write(shard.join(&fresh), b"half").unwrap();
    set_mtime(&shard.join(&fresh), now - HOUR / 2);
    let s = v.sweep(now).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(s, Sweep { keyphrases: 3, bytes: 4 * BLOCK, removed: 1, temps: 1 });
    assert!(!file(&v, &old).exists());
    assert!(file(&v, &kept).exists() && file(&v, &recent).exists() && file(&v, &read).exists());
    assert!(!shard.join(&stale).exists() && shard.join(&fresh).exists());
    assert!(v.o.dir.join("abc").join("notes.txt").exists());
    assert_eq!(v.usage(), (3, 4 * BLOCK, true));
}

#[test]
fn many_writers_one_keyphrase_take_turns() {

    let id = id_of(b"a");
    let m = saved(v.put(&id, Cond::New, b"0", T0).unwrap());
    // eight writers that all expect the same rev: exactly one wins
    let wins: usize = std::thread::scope(|s| {
        let hs: Vec<_> = (0..8)
            .map(|i| {
                let v = v.clone();
                s.spawn(move || matches!(v.put(&id, Cond::Rev(m.cur.rev), &[i], T0).unwrap(), Put::Saved { .. }) as usize)
            })
            .collect();
        hs.into_iter().map(|h| h.join().unwrap()).sum()
    });
    assert_eq!(wins, 1);
}

{"id": "AT001676", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/ws/src/lib.rs", "originalBytes": 8084, "originalSha256": "4efb630131bb40c74e8ca1f62bbb843db13daa46f042fa03e7c09670d1c2f9fa", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 8084, "utf8TotalBytes": 8084}

//! The WebSocket protocol (RFC 6455) as the server speaks it on /lan, the way the `ws` library (8.x) that the Node
//! server used spoke it (`perMessageDeflate: false`, `autoPong: false`, `maxPayload` 64 KiB, `skipUTF8Validation`
//! false): the parts the switch (nfsu2-lan) builds its connections from.
//!
//! - the handshake: [`accept_key`], [`pick_protocol`] (ws's reading of Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: a malformed one is
//!   refused with 400), [`handshake_response`] (the 101 ws wrote)
//! - [`WsReader`]: messages from a client (masked frames; fragments joined; a message over `max_payload` is a
//!   1009, broken frames a 1002, a text message that is not UTF-8 a 1007, as ws closed them)
//! - [`frame`]: frames to a client (unmasked), into a buffer, so that a writer puts many into one write
//!
//! Every rule, code and reason is ws's (receiver.js, subprotocol.js, validation.js, websocket-server.js); the tests
//! compare the reader and the handshake with ws itself (tests/node.rs).

use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::fmt;

use base64::Engine;
use bytes::Bytes;
use sha1::{Digest, Sha1};

mod reader;

pub use reader::WsReader;

/// RFC 6455's GUID
pub const GUID: &str = "258EAFA5-E914-47DA-95CA-C5AB0DC85B11";

/// Sec-WebSocket-Accept for a Sec-WebSocket-Key
pub fn accept_key(key: &str) -> String {
    let mut h = Sha1::new();
    h.update(key.as_bytes());
    h.update(GUID.as_bytes());
    base64::engine::general_purpose::STANDARD.encode(h.finalize())
}

/// ws's reading of a Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header: Ok(None) when there is none, Ok(Some(first)) for the protocol
/// ws picks (the first: the server has no handleProtocols), Err(()) when it is malformed (ws: 400 "Invalid
/// Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header"; the server answers its own 400)
///
/// subprotocol.js's parse(), step for step: tokens separated by commas, spaces and tabs around them but not first
/// (nor last: Node trims a header's value, so a trailing one never came), no empty item, no token twice.  An empty
/// header is malformed too.
// (the unit error is the fixed API: there is one way to be malformed, and it is answered with a 400)
#[allow(clippy::result_unit_err)]
pub fn pick_protocol(header: Option<&str>) -> Result<Option<String>, ()> {
    let Some(h) = header else { return Ok(None) };
    // a set, not a list: a header of thousands of short tokens must not cost their square
    let mut seen: HashSet<&str> = HashSet::new();
    let mut first: Option<&str> = None;
    let (mut start, mut end): (Option<usize>, Option<usize>) = (None, None);
    for (i, &c) in h.as_bytes().iter().enumerate() {
        if end.is_none() && is_token(c) {
            start.get_or_insert(i);
        } else if i != 0 && (c == b' ' || c == b'\t') {
            if end.is_none() && start.is_some() {
                end = Some(i);
            }
        } else if c == b',' {
            let Some(s) = start else { return Err(()) };
            // start and end sit on ASCII bytes: always character boundaries
            let p = h.get(s..end.unwrap_or(i)).ok_or(())?;
            if !seen.insert(p) {
                return Err(());
            }
            first.get_or_insert(p);
            (start, end) = (None, None);
        } else {
            return Err(());
        }
    }
    let (Some(s), None) = (start, end) else { return Err(()) };
    let p = h.get(s..).ok_or(())?;
    if seen.contains(p) {
        return Err(());
    }
    Ok(Some(first.unwrap_or(p).to_string()))
}

/// validation.js's tokenChars: the characters of an HTTP token (RFC 7230)
fn is_token(c: u8) -> bool {
    matches!(c, b'!' | b'#'..=b'\'' | b'*' | b'+' | b'-' | b'.' | b'0'..=b'9' | b'A'..=b'Z' | b'^'..=b'z' | b'|' | b'~')
}

/// The 101 answer ws wrote: `HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols`, Upgrade, Connection, Sec-WebSocket-Accept, and
/// Sec-WebSocket-Protocol when one was picked; nothing else
///
/// completeUpgrade's lines, in its order and spelling (the server had no 'headers' listener and no extensions).
pub fn handshake_response(key: &str, protocol: Option<&str>) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut s = String::with_capacity(160);
    s.push_str("HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nSec-WebSocket-Accept: ");
    s.push_str(&accept_key(key));
    s.push_str("\r\n");
    // ws: `if (protocol)`, so an empty one writes no header
    if let Some(p) = protocol.filter(|p| !p.is_empty()) {
        s.push_str("Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: ");
        s.push_str(p);
        s.push_str("\r\n");
    }
    s.push_str("\r\n");
    s.into_bytes()
}

/// A message from the client.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Message {
    /// UTF-8 (checked)
    Text(Bytes),
    Binary(Bytes),
    Ping(Bytes),
    Pong(Bytes),
    /// its close frame: the code (1005 when it had none) and reason (UTF-8, checked).  ws answered it with a close
    /// frame of the same code and reason (`frame::close_payload(code, reason)`, empty for 1005).
    Close(u16, Bytes),
}

/// Why no more messages come.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ReadError {
    /// the connection ended (or failed) without a close frame (ws's 'close' then says 1006)
    Closed,
    /// the client broke the protocol: the close frame to send it (ws's codes: 1002 a broken frame, 1007 a text
    /// message or close reason that is not UTF-8, 1009 a message over `max_payload`), then the connection goes.
    /// ws's close frame carried the code alone (`frame::close_payload(code, "")`); `reason` is the message of the
    /// error ws emitted (its 'error' event, which the server ignored), e.g. "Invalid WebSocket frame: MASK must be
    /// set" (the one for a bad close code is without the code: ws put it in, a static text cannot).
    Protocol { code: u16, reason: &'static str },
}

impl fmt::Display for ReadError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            ReadError::Closed => f.write_str("the connection ended"),
            ReadError::Protocol { code, reason } => write!(f, "{reason} ({code})"),
        }
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for ReadError {}

/// Frames to a client (unmasked, FIN set, one frame a message).
pub mod frame {
    pub const CONTINUATION: u8 = 0x0;
    pub const TEXT: u8 = 0x1;
    pub const BINARY: u8 = 0x2;
    pub const CLOSE: u8 = 0x8;
    pub const PING: u8 = 0x9;
    pub const PONG: u8 = 0xA;

    /// the bytes of a frame's header for a payload of `len` (2, 4 or 10 bytes)
    ///
    /// As ws's Sender framed it: the shortest length form (7 bits up to 125, 16 up to 65535, 64 beyond), no mask (a
    /// server's frames are never masked).
    pub fn header(opcode: u8, len: usize, out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
        let b0 = 0x80 | opcode;
        if len < 126 {
            out.extend_from_slice(&[b0, len as u8]);
        } else if len < 65536 {
            let [hi, lo] = (len as u16).to_be_bytes();
            out.extend_from_slice(&[b0, 126, hi, lo]);
        } else {
            out.extend_from_slice(&[b0, 127]);
            out.extend_from_slice(&(len as u64).to_be_bytes());
        }
    }
    /// header and payload
    pub fn encode(opcode: u8, payload: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
        header(opcode, payload.len(), out);
        out.extend_from_slice(payload);
    }
    /// a close frame's payload: the code and the reason (at most 123 bytes)
    ///
    /// A longer reason is cut at a character (ws threw a RangeError: a close frame's payload is 125 bytes at most).
    /// 1005 is "no code": the empty payload ws sent for a close() without one (its answer to a client's close frame
    /// that had no code; 1005 itself may never be sent).
    pub fn close_payload(code: u16, reason: &str) -> Vec<u8> {
        if code == 1005 {
            return Vec::new();
        }
        let mut n = reason.len().min(123);
        while !reason.is_char_boundary(n) {
            n -= 1;
        }
        let mut p = Vec::with_capacity(2 + n);
        p.extend_from_slice(&code.to_be_bytes());
        p.extend_from_slice(&reason.as_bytes()[..n]);
        p
    }
}

{"id": "AT001677", "source": "archive:A028!/nfsu2-web-public/web/server-rs/crates/ws/src/reader.rs", "originalBytes": 15416, "originalSha256": "b19d632277d91a4f0bb9f6c10dcdfbc41b9972f8a0b4c9e9ce430fa7dd0f1aae", "originalEncoding": "utf-8", "utf8RangeStart": 0, "utf8RangeEnd": 15416, "utf8TotalBytes": 15416}

//! Reading a client's frames: ws's Receiver (receiver.js) as an incremental parser over one read buffer.

use bytes::{Buf, Bytes, BytesMut};
use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncReadExt};

use crate::{Message, ReadError};

/// A read block: what one read takes at most when no larger frame is announced.
const BLOCK: usize = 16 << 10;
/// A read with less room than this left in the block starts another (or reclaims the old one once its payloads are
/// all dropped): reads of a few bytes would cost a system call each.
const MIN_READ: usize = 1 << 10;
/// Without a max_payload (0) a frame's buffer grows by this much a read at most (or by what it holds, past it), so
/// that what a client only announces is never reserved before it comes.
const STEP: usize = 1 << 20;

// ws's error messages (receiver.js createError: "Invalid WebSocket frame: " before the ones made with a prefix)
macro_rules! invalid {
    ($s:expr) => {
        concat!("Invalid WebSocket frame: ", $s)
    };
}
const RSV_2_3: &str = invalid!("RSV2 and RSV3 must be clear");
const RSV_1: &str = invalid!("RSV1 must be clear");
const EXPECTED_FIN: &str = invalid!("FIN must be set");
const EXPECTED_MASK: &str = invalid!("MASK must be set");
const INVALID_UTF8: &str = invalid!("invalid UTF-8 sequence");
const INVALID_CLOSE_CODE: &str = invalid!("invalid status code");
const MAX_PAYLOAD: &str = "Max payload size exceeded";
const OVER_2_53: &str = "Unsupported WebSocket frame: payload length > 2^53 - 1";
/// "invalid opcode N" by opcode (8, 9 and 10 are never refused for their opcode)
const INVALID_OPCODE: [&str; 16] = [
    invalid!("invalid opcode 0"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 1"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 2"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 3"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 4"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 5"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 6"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 7"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 8"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 9"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 10"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 11"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 12"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 13"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 14"),
    invalid!("invalid opcode 15"),
];

fn protocol(code: u16, reason: &'static str) -> ReadError {
    ReadError::Protocol { code, reason }
}

/// "invalid payload length N" for a control frame's 7-bit length: 1 (a close frame's), 126 or 127
fn invalid_control_length(len7: u8) -> ReadError {
    protocol(
        1002,
        match len7 {
            1 => invalid!("invalid payload length 1"),
            126 => invalid!("invalid payload length 126"),
            _ => invalid!("invalid payload length 127"),
        },
    )
}

/// validation.js isValidStatusCode: the codes a close frame may carry
fn valid_close_code(code: u16) -> bool {
    ((1000..=1014).contains(&code) && !(1004..=1006).contains(&code)) || (3000..=4999).contains(&code)
}

/// Messages from a client, read from the connection's read half; `pre`: what the HTTP server read past the
/// handshake's head (already this connection's bytes).
///
/// Reads go into blocks of 16 KiB, or one as large as a frame when a larger frame is announced (so never more than
/// `max_payload` + 14 bytes for one), and a single-frame message is its frame's own bytes in the block, unmasked in
/// place: no copy.  A payload keeps its block alive until it is dropped: copy what is kept for long.  A message in
/// fragments is joined (copied once, as ws's concat() did).
///
/// `next()` is cancel safe: a `select!` with a timer may drop it, nothing read is lost.  After a close frame or a
/// protocol error nothing the client sends counts (ws's receiver stopped): `next()` reads and drops it until the
/// connection ends, then says Closed.
pub struct WsReader<R> {
    r: R,
    buf: BytesMut,
    /// 0: no limit (ws's maxPayload 0)
    max_payload: u64,
    /// the opcode of the message whose fragments are coming (ws's `_fragmented`), 0 when none
    fragmented: u8,
    /// that message's payload bytes so far (ws's `_totalPayloadLength`): what max_payload counts
    total: u64,
    parts: Parts,
    /// a close frame came, the client broke the protocol, or the connection ended: no more messages
    done: bool,
    /// the connection ended
    ended: bool,
}

/// A frame's header, read and checked.
struct Header {
    fin: bool,
    /// the message's opcode for a continuation frame
    opcode: u8,
    /// the header's length (2 to 14 bytes)
    head: usize,
    len: usize,
    mask: [u8; 4],
}

enum Step {
    /// the buffer must hold this many bytes before the frame can be read further
    Need(usize),
    Frame(Header),
}

impl<R: AsyncRead + Unpin + Send> WsReader<R> {
    pub fn new(r: R, pre: Bytes, max_payload: usize) -> Self {
        let mut buf = BytesMut::with_capacity(BLOCK.max(pre.len()));
        buf.extend_from_slice(&pre);
        WsReader { r, buf, max_payload: max_payload as u64, fragmented: 0, total: 0, parts: Parts::None, done: false, ended: false }
    }

    /// the next message (a payload is the frame's own bytes, unmasked in place: no copy)
    pub async fn next(&mut self) -> Result<Message, ReadError> {
        if self.done {
            return self.drain().await;
        }
        loop {
            let want = match self.header() {
                Err(e) => return Err(self.stop(e)),
                Ok(Step::Need(n)) => n,
                Ok(Step::Frame(h)) if self.buf.len() >= h.head + h.len => match self.take(h) {
                    Ok(Some(m)) => return Ok(m),
                    Ok(None) => continue,
                    Err(e) => return Err(self.stop(e)),
                },
                Ok(Step::Frame(h)) => h.head + h.len,
            };
            self.fill(want).await?;
        }
    }

    /// The frame at the front of the buffer, as far as it is there: receiver.js getInfo, getPayloadLength16/64,
    /// haveLength and getMask, in their order (so that a frame broken twice is refused for what ws saw first, and
    /// as soon as ws would: a message over max_payload before its payload comes).
    fn header(&self) -> Result<Step, ReadError> {
        let b = &self.buf[..];
        let &[b0, b1, ..] = b else { return Ok(Step::Need(2)) };
        if b0 & 0x30 != 0 {
            return Err(protocol(1002, RSV_2_3));
        }
        // RSV1 is permessage-deflate's, which the server never accepts
        if b0 & 0x40 != 0 {
            return Err(protocol(1002, RSV_1));
        }
        let fin = b0 & 0x80 != 0;
        let mut opcode = b0 & 0x0f;
        let len7 = b1 & 0x7f;
        match opcode {
            0 => {
                if self.fragmented == 0 {
                    return Err(protocol(1002, INVALID_OPCODE[0]));
                }
                opcode = self.fragmented;
            }
            1 | 2 => {
                if self.fragmented != 0 {
                    return Err(protocol(1002, INVALID_OPCODE[opcode as usize]));
                }
            }
            8..=10 => {
                if !fin {
                    return Err(protocol(1002, EXPECTED_FIN));
                }
                if len7 > 125 || (opcode == 8 && len7 == 1) {
                    return Err(invalid_control_length(len7));
                }
            }
            _ => return Err(protocol(1002, INVALID_OPCODE[opcode as usize])),
        }
        // a client's frames are masked (RFC 6455 5.1)
        if b1 & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Err(protocol(1002, EXPECTED_MASK));
        }
        let (len, at) = match len7 {
            126 => {
                let Some(&[hi, lo]) = b.get(2..4) else { return Ok(Step::Need(4)) };
                (u16::from_be_bytes([hi, lo]) as u64, 4)
            }
            127 => {
                let Some(x) = b.get(2..10).and_then(|x| <[u8; 8]>::try_from(x).ok()) else { return Ok(Step::Need(10)) };
                let v = u64::from_be_bytes(x);
                // ws counted in JS numbers: more than 2^53 - 1 it could not
                if v >> 32 > (1 << 21) - 1 {
                    return Err(protocol(1009, OVER_2_53));
                }
                (v, 10)
            }
            n => (n as u64, 2),
        };
        if len > 0 && opcode < 8 && self.max_payload > 0 && self.total.saturating_add(len) > self.max_payload {
            return Err(protocol(1009, MAX_PAYLOAD));
        }
        let Some(&[m0, m1, m2, m3]) = b.get(at..at + 4) else { return Ok(Step::Need(at + 4)) };
        // within max_payload, a usize; only a 32-bit build without a limit could see more
        let len = usize::try_from(len).map_err(|_| protocol(1009, OVER_2_53))?;
        Ok(Step::Frame(Header { fin, opcode, head: at + 4, len, mask: [m0, m1, m2, m3] }))
    }

    /// The frame (all in the buffer) taken off it: a message, or None for a fragment that is not the last
    /// (receiver.js getData, controlMessage, dataMessage).
    fn take(&mut self, h: Header) -> Result<Option<Message>, ReadError> {
        self.buf.advance(h.head);
        let data = if h.len == 0 {
            Bytes::new()
        } else {
            let mut p = self.buf.split_to(h.len);
            unmask(&mut p, h.mask);
            p.freeze()
        };
        match h.opcode {
            8 => {
                self.end();
                close(data).map(Some)
            }
            9 => Ok(Some(Message::Ping(data))),
            10 => Ok(Some(Message::Pong(data))),
            op => {
                self.total = self.total.saturating_add(h.len as u64);
                self.parts.push(data);
                if !h.fin {
                    self.fragmented = op;
                    return Ok(None);
                }
                self.fragmented = 0;
                self.total = 0;
                let data = self.parts.take();
                if op == 2 {
                    return Ok(Some(Message::Binary(data)));
                }
                // the whole message is checked, as ws did: a character may be split across fragments
                if std::str::from_utf8(&data).is_err() {
                    return Err(protocol(1007, INVALID_UTF8));
                }
                Ok(Some(Message::Text(data)))
            }
        }
    }

    /// No more messages: what was put together is let go.
    fn end(&mut self) {
        self.done = true;
        self.parts = Parts::None;
    }

    fn stop(&mut self, e: ReadError) -> ReadError {
        self.end();
        e
    }

    /// More bytes for a step that needs `want` in the buffer.
    async fn fill(&mut self, want: usize) -> Result<(), ReadError> {
        // past STEP the buffer at most doubles a read: what is reserved follows what came
        let room = want.saturating_sub(self.buf.len()).clamp(MIN_READ, STEP.max(self.buf.len()));
        self.make_room(room);
        match self.r.read_buf(&mut self.buf).await {
            Ok(n) if n > 0 => Ok(()),
            _ => {
                self.ended = true;
                Err(self.stop(ReadError::Closed))
            }
        }
    }

    /// Room for `room` more bytes: the block's own, the block reclaimed once no payload holds it, or a new block
    /// with the bytes not yet read (at most a frame).
    fn make_room(&mut self, room: usize) {
        if self.buf.try_reclaim(room) {
            return;
        }
        let mut b = BytesMut::with_capacity((self.buf.len() + room).max(BLOCK));
        b.extend_from_slice(&self.buf);
        self.buf = b;
    }

    /// What comes after the end is dropped until the connection ends (ws resumed the socket and ignored it).
    async fn drain(&mut self) -> Result<Message, ReadError> {
        while !self.ended {
            self.buf.clear();
            self.make_room(MIN_READ);
            match self.r.read_buf(&mut self.buf).await {
                Ok(n) if n > 0 => {}
                _ => self.ended = true,
            }
        }
        self.buf = BytesMut::new();
        Err(ReadError::Closed)
    }
}

/// A close frame's payload: Close(code, reason), or what ws refused in it.
fn close(data: Bytes) -> Result<Message, ReadError> {
    if data.is_empty() {
        return Ok(Message::Close(1005, Bytes::new()));
    }
    // a payload of 1 byte was refused with the header
    let &[hi, lo, ..] = &data[..] else { return Err(invalid_control_length(1)) };
    let code = u16::from_be_bytes([hi, lo]);
    if !valid_close_code(code) {
        return Err(protocol(1002, INVALID_CLOSE_CODE));
    }
    let reason = data.slice(2..);
    if std::str::from_utf8(&reason).is_err() {
        return Err(protocol(1007, INVALID_UTF8));
    }
    Ok(Message::Close(code, reason))
}

/// The fragments of a message so far: the first one as it is (a message of one non-empty fragment is not copied),
/// the others joined to it.  Empty fragments are skipped, as ws did.
enum Parts {
    None,
    One(Bytes),
    Many(BytesMut),
}

impl Parts {
    fn push(&mut self, data: Bytes) {
        if data.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        *self = match std::mem::replace(self, Parts::None) {
            Parts::None => Parts::One(data),
            Parts::One(first) => {
                let mut m = BytesMut::with_capacity(first.len() + data.len());
                m.extend_from_slice(&first);
                m.extend_from_slice(&data);
                Parts::Many(m)
            }
            Parts::Many(mut m) => {
                m.extend_from_slice(&data);
                Parts::Many(m)
            }
        };
    }

    fn take(&mut self) -> Bytes {
        match std::mem::replace(self, Parts::None) {
            Parts::None => Bytes::new(),
            Parts::One(b) => b,
            Parts::Many(m) => m.freeze(),
        }
    }
}

/// XOR with the mask, eight bytes at a time (a mask of zeros changes nothing: ws skipped it too).
fn unmask(data: &mut [u8], mask: [u8; 4]) {
    if mask == [0; 4] {
        return;
    }
    let [a, b, c, d] = mask;
    let m = u64::from_ne_bytes([a, b, c, d, a, b, c, d]);
    // chunks_exact is what makes it vectorize (twice as fast as chunks); not as_chunks_mut, which the workspace's
    // Rust 1.85 does not have
    #[allow(unknown_lints, clippy::chunks_exact_to_as_chunks)]
    let mut words = data.chunks_exact_mut(8);
    for w in &mut words {
        if let Ok(x) = <[u8; 8]>::try_from(&*w) {
            w.copy_from_slice(&(u64::from_ne_bytes(x) ^ m).to_ne_bytes());
        }
    }
    // the rest starts at a multiple of 8: the mask's first byte again
    for (i, x) in words.into_remainder().iter_mut().enumerate() {
        *x ^= mask[i & 3];
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn unmask_matches_bytewise() {
        let mask = [0x37, 0xfa, 0x21, 0x3d];
        for n in 0..40 {
            let orig: Vec<u8> = (0..n as u8).map(|i| i.wrapping_mul(31)).collect();
            let mut fast = orig.clone();
            unmask(&mut fast, mask);
            let slow: Vec<u8> = orig.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, b)| b ^ mask[i % 4]).collect();
            assert_eq!(fast, slow, "length {n}");
        }
    }

        // validation.js isValidStatusCode, as it is written there
        for code in 0..=u16::MAX {
            let ws = (code >= 1000 && code <= 1014 && code != 1004 && code != 1005 && code != 1006) || (code >= 3000 && code <= 4999);
            assert_eq!(valid_close_code(code), ws, "{code}");
        }
    }
}

//! How fast WsReader reads (ignored by default; in release:
//! `cargo.sh ws test -p nfsu2-ws --release --test bench -- --ignored --nocapture`).

mod common;

use std::time::Instant;

use bytes::Bytes;
use common::*;
use nfsu2_ws::{Message, WsReader};

/// `keep`: payloads held at once (as queues to slow receivers hold them), so that blocks stay pinned and new ones
/// are made
async fn measure(what: &str, payload: usize, frames: usize, keep: usize) {
    let p: Vec<u8> = (0..payload).map(|i| i as u8).collect();
    let one = binary(&p);
    let data = one.repeat(frames);
    let mut held = std::collections::VecDeque::with_capacity(keep + 1);
    let t = Instant::now();
    // from memory through the AsyncRead path, as from a socket (reads of what the block has room for)
    let mut r = WsReader::new(&data[..], Bytes::new(), 65536);
    let (mut n, mut bytes) = (0usize, 0usize);
    while let Ok(m) = r.next().await {
        let Message::Binary(b) = m else { panic!() };
        bytes += b.len();
        n += 1;
        if keep > 0 {
            held.push_back(b);
            if held.len() > keep {
                held.pop_front();
            }
        }
    }
    let s = t.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
    assert_eq!((n, bytes), (frames, frames * payload));
    eprintln!(
        "{what}: {frames} frames of {payload} bytes in {:.1} ms: {:.1} M frames/s, {:.0} MB/s of payload",
        s * 1e3,
        frames as f64 / s / 1e6,
        bytes as f64 / s / 1e6
    );
}

#[tokio::test]
#[ignore]
async fn read_a_million_small_frames() {
    measure("small", 32, 1_000_000, 0).await;
    measure("small, 4096 held", 32, 1_000_000, 4096).await;
    measure("roam-sized", 200, 1_000_000, 0).await;
    measure("roam-sized, 4096 held", 200, 1_000_000, 4096).await;
    measure("large", 8192, 100_000, 0).await;
}

//! What the tests share: clients' frames built by hand, readers that hand their bytes out in pieces.
#![allow(dead_code)]

use std::pin::Pin;
use std::task::{Context, Poll};

use bytes::Bytes;
use nfsu2_ws::{Message, ReadError, WsReader};
use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, ReadBuf};

/// RFC 6455's example mask (5.7)
pub const MASK: [u8; 4] = [0x37, 0xfa, 0x21, 0x3d];

/// How a frame says its length.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub enum Len {
    /// the shortest form
    Short,
    /// 126 and 16 bits
    L16,
    /// 127 and 64 bits
    L64,
}

/// A client's frame: the first byte as given (FIN, RSV, opcode), masked with MASK, its length in the shortest form.
pub fn raw(b0: u8, payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    raw_with(b0, payload, Some(MASK), Len::Short)
}

pub fn raw_with(b0: u8, payload: &[u8], mask: Option<[u8; 4]>, len: Len) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut v = vec![b0];
    v.extend(length(payload.len() as u64, mask.is_some(), len));
    match mask {
        Some(k) => {
            v.extend(k);
            v.extend(payload.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, b)| b ^ k[i % 4]));
        }
        None => v.extend(payload),
    }
    v
}

/// The second byte and the extended length for a payload of n bytes.
pub fn length(n: u64, masked: bool, len: Len) -> Vec<u8> {
    let m = if masked { 0x80 } else { 0 };
    match len {
        Len::Short if n < 126 => vec![m | n as u8],
        Len::Short | Len::L16 if n < 65536 => {
            let mut v = vec![m | 126];
            v.extend((n as u16).to_be_bytes());
            v
        }
        _ => {
            let mut v = vec![m | 127];
            v.extend(n.to_be_bytes());
            v
        }
    }
}

pub fn text(p: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    raw(0x81, p)
}
pub fn binary(p: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    raw(0x82, p)
}
pub fn ping(p: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    raw(0x89, p)
}
pub fn pong(p: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    raw(0x8a, p)
}
/// a continuation frame
pub fn cont(fin: bool, p: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    raw(if fin { 0x80 } else { 0x00 }, p)
}
/// a close frame with a code and a reason
pub fn close(code: u16, reason: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut p = code.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
    p.extend(reason);
    raw(0x88, &p)
}

pub fn cat(frames: &[Vec<u8>]) -> Vec<u8> {
    frames.concat()
}

pub fn t(s: &str) -> Message {
    Message::Text(Bytes::copy_from_slice(s.as_bytes()))
}
pub fn b(p: &[u8]) -> Message {
    Message::Binary(Bytes::copy_from_slice(p))
}
pub fn closed(code: u16, reason: &str) -> Message {
    Message::Close(code, Bytes::copy_from_slice(reason.as_bytes()))
}
pub fn err(code: u16, reason: &'static str) -> ReadError {
    ReadError::Protocol { code, reason }
}

/// A reader that hands out its bytes `chunk` at a time (or in the sizes `sizes` gives, round and round).
pub struct Drip {
    data: Vec<u8>,
    at: usize,
    sizes: Vec<usize>,
    turn: usize,
}

impl Drip {
    pub fn new(data: &[u8], chunk: usize) -> Self {
        Drip { data: data.to_vec(), at: 0, sizes: vec![chunk.max(1)], turn: 0 }
    }
    pub fn sizes(data: &[u8], sizes: Vec<usize>) -> Self {
        Drip { data: data.to_vec(), at: 0, sizes, turn: 0 }
    }
}

impl AsyncRead for Drip {
    fn poll_read(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, _: &mut Context<'_>, buf: &mut ReadBuf<'_>) -> Poll<std::io::Result<()>> {
        let size = self.sizes[self.turn % self.sizes.len()].max(1);
        self.turn += 1;
        let n = size.min(self.data.len() - self.at).min(buf.remaining());
        let at = self.at;
        buf.put_slice(&self.data[at..at + n]);
        self.at += n;
        Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
    }
}

/// A reader that fails after its bytes (a connection reset).
pub struct Failing(pub Vec<u8>);

impl AsyncRead for Failing {
    fn poll_read(mut self: Pin<&mut Self>, _: &mut Context<'_>, buf: &mut ReadBuf<'_>) -> Poll<std::io::Result<()>> {
        if self.0.is_empty() {
            return Poll::Ready(Err(std::io::Error::from(std::io::ErrorKind::ConnectionReset)));
        }
        let n = self.0.len().min(buf.remaining());
        buf.put_slice(&self.0[..n]);
        self.0.drain(..n);
        Poll::Ready(Ok(()))
    }
}

/// Every message a reader gives, and the error that ends them.
pub async fn read_all<R: AsyncRead + Unpin + Send>(mut r: WsReader<R>) -> (Vec<Message>, ReadError) {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    loop {
        match r.next().await {
            Ok(m) => out.push(m),
            Err(e) => return (out, e),
        }
    }
}

/// The same bytes read four ways (all in `pre`, in one read, a byte a read, in pieces of 1 to 13 bytes), which must
/// agree.
pub async fn read_bytes(data: &[u8], max_payload: usize) -> (Vec<Message>, ReadError) {
    let whole = read_all(WsReader::new(tokio::io::empty(), Bytes::copy_from_slice(data), max_payload)).await;
    let one = read_all(WsReader::new(Drip::new(data, usize::MAX), Bytes::new(), max_payload)).await;
    assert_eq!(whole, one, "in pre vs in one read");
    let bytewise = read_all(WsReader::new(Drip::new(data, 1), Bytes::new(), max_payload)).await;
    assert_eq!(whole, bytewise, "in pre vs a byte a read");
    let pieces = read_all(WsReader::new(Drip::sizes(data, (1..=13).collect()), Bytes::new(), max_payload)).await;
    assert_eq!(whole, pieces, "in pre vs in pieces");
    whole
}

/// A small PRNG with a fixed seed (xorshift64*), so that random cases are the same every run.
pub struct Rng(pub u64);

impl Rng {
    pub fn next(&mut self) -> u64 {
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 12;
        self.0 ^= self.0 << 25;
        self.0 ^= self.0 >> 27;
        self.0.wrapping_mul(0x2545_f491_4f6c_dd1d)
    }
    /// 0..n
    pub fn below(&mut self, n: u64) -> u64 {
        self.next() % n.max(1)
    }
    /// true in pct out of 100
    pub fn chance(&mut self, pct: u64) -> bool {
        self.below(100) < pct
    }
    pub fn pick<'a, T>(&mut self, of: &'a [T]) -> &'a T {
        &of[self.below(of.len() as u64) as usize]
    }
    pub fn bytes(&mut self, n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
        (0..n).map(|_| self.next() as u8).collect()
    }
}

pub fn hex(b: &[u8]) -> String {
    b.iter().map(|x| format!("{x:02x}")).collect()
}

//! The handshake (accept key, subprotocol, the 101) and the server's own frames.

use nfsu2_ws::{accept_key, frame, handshake_response, pick_protocol};

#[test]
fn accept_key_of_rfc_6455() {
    // RFC 6455 1.3's example
    assert_eq!(accept_key("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ=="), "s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=");
}

#[test]
fn the_101() {
    let want = "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\n\
                Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=\r\n\r\n";
    assert_eq!(String::from_utf8(handshake_response("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==", None)).unwrap(), want);
    let want = "HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\n\
                Sec-WebSocket-Accept: s3pPLMBiTxaQ9kYGzzhZRbK+xOo=\r\nSec-WebSocket-Protocol: chat\r\n\r\n";
    assert_eq!(String::from_utf8(handshake_response("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==", Some("chat"))).unwrap(), want);
    // ws: `if (protocol)`: an empty one is no header
    assert_eq!(handshake_response("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==", Some("")), handshake_response("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==", None));
}

fn pick(h: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, ()> {
    pick_protocol(Some(h))
}
fn ok(p: &str) -> Result<Option<String>, ()> {
    Ok(Some(p.to_string()))
}

#[test]
fn subprotocols_as_ws_reads_them() {
    // none: none picked
    assert_eq!(pick_protocol(None), Ok(None));
    // subprotocol.js's own cases (ws's test/subprotocol.test.js), and the first is the one picked
    assert_eq!(pick("foo"), ok("foo"));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo,bar,baz"), ok("foo"));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo , bar,baz"), ok("foo"));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo\t,\tbar , baz"), ok("foo"));
    assert_eq!(pick("bar, foo"), ok("bar"));
    // spaces and tabs between tokens, never first, never last
    assert_eq!(pick("a, \t b"), ok("a"));
    assert_eq!(pick(" foo"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("\tfoo"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo "), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo\t"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo bar"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo\tbar"), Err(()));
    // empty: the header, an item, the end after a comma
    assert_eq!(pick(""), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick(","), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick(",foo"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo,"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo,,bar"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo, ,bar"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo, "), Err(()));
    // duplicates, wherever they are
    assert_eq!(pick("foo,foo"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo, bar, foo"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("bar,foo , foo"), Err(()));
    assert_eq!(pick("foo,Foo"), ok("foo"));
    // characters that are no token's
    for c in ['"', '(', ')', '/', ':', ';', '<', '=', '>', '?', '@', '[', '\\', ']', '{', '}', '\0', '\r', '\n', '\x7f', 'é', '😀'] {
        assert_eq!(pick(&format!("fo{c}o")), Err(()), "{c:?}");
    }
    // every token character
    assert_eq!(pick("!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~09AZaz"), ok("!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~09AZaz"));
}

#[test]
fn many_subprotocols() {
    // a header of thousands of tokens is read in one pass
    let h: Vec<String> = (0..20000).map(|i| format!("p{i}")).collect();
    assert_eq!(pick(&h.join(", ")), ok("p0"));
    let mut d = h.clone();
    d.push("p0".into());
    assert_eq!(pick(&d.join(",")), Err(()));
}

#[test]
fn frame_headers() {
    let header = |op, len| {
        let mut v = Vec::new();
        frame::header(op, len, &mut v);
        v
    };
    assert_eq!(header(frame::TEXT, 0), [0x81, 0]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::BINARY, 125), [0x82, 125]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::BINARY, 126), [0x82, 126, 0, 126]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::BINARY, 65535), [0x82, 126, 0xff, 0xff]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::BINARY, 65536), [0x82, 127, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::BINARY, 0x0012_3456_789a), [0x82, 127, 0, 0, 0, 0x12, 0x34, 0x56, 0x78, 0x9a]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::CLOSE, 2), [0x88, 2]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::PING, 1), [0x89, 1]);
    assert_eq!(header(frame::PONG, 125), [0x8a, 125]);
    // encode appends: many frames in one buffer
    let mut v = vec![0xee];
    frame::encode(frame::TEXT, b"Hello", &mut v);
    frame::encode(frame::PONG, b"", &mut v);
    assert_eq!(v, [0xee, 0x81, 5, b'H', b'e', b'l', b'l', b'o', 0x8a, 0]);
    let mut v = Vec::new();
    frame::encode(frame::BINARY, &[7; 300], &mut v);
    assert_eq!((v.len(), &v[..4]), (304, &[0x82, 126, 1, 44][..]));
}

#[test]
fn close_payloads() {
    assert_eq!(frame::close_payload(1000, ""), [0x03, 0xe8]);
    assert_eq!(frame::close_payload(1013, "LAN full"), b"\x03\xf5LAN full");
    assert_eq!(frame::close_payload(4999, "é"), [0x13, 0x87, 0xc3, 0xa9]);
    // 1005 is no code: the empty payload of ws's close() without one
    assert_eq!(frame::close_payload(1005, "ignored"), Vec::<u8>::new());
    // 123 bytes of reason at most, cut at a character
    let p = frame::close_payload(1000, &"x".repeat(200));
    assert_eq!(p.len(), 125);
    let p = frame::close_payload(1000, &format!("{}é", "x".repeat(122)));
    assert_eq!(p.len(), 124);
    assert!(std::str::from_utf8(&p[2..]).is_ok());
}
