//! Cross-checks against the ws library itself (web/node_modules/ws, run by node): its Receiver over random byte
//! streams of client frames, and its WebSocketServer's handshake over random Sec-WebSocket-Protocol headers.
//! Skipped (with a message) where node or ws is missing.

mod common;

use std::io::Write;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};

use bytes::Bytes;
use common::*;
use nfsu2_ws::{Message, ReadError, WsReader, handshake_response, pick_protocol};

fn ws_dir() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let d = PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../../node_modules/ws");
    if !d.join("lib/receiver.js").exists() {
        eprintln!("skipped: no ws library at {}", d.display());
        return None;
    }
    if Command::new("node").arg("--version").output().is_err() {
        eprintln!("skipped: no node");
        return None;
    }
    Some(d)
}

/// node running `script` (CommonJS, the ws folder as argv[2]) over these lines on stdin; its stdout's lines
fn node(ws: &PathBuf, script: &str, input: String) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut child = Command::new("node")
        .args(["-e", script, "--"])
        .arg(ws)
        .stdin(Stdio::piped())
        .stdout(Stdio::piped())
        .stderr(Stdio::inherit())
        .spawn()
        .expect("node");
    let mut stdin = child.stdin.take().unwrap();
    let feeder = std::thread::spawn(move || stdin.write_all(input.as_bytes()).unwrap());
    let out = child.wait_with_output().unwrap();
    feeder.join().unwrap();
    assert!(out.status.success(), "node failed");
    String::from_utf8(out.stdout).unwrap().lines().map(str::to_string).collect()
}

// Each line: maxPayload, a space, the stream's bytes in hex.  Out: the events, '|' between them.  The error for a
// bad close code loses its code, as ours has none.
const RECEIVER: &str = r#"
const ws = process.argv[process.argv.length - 1];
const Receiver = require(ws + '/lib/receiver.js');
const { kStatusCode } = require(ws + '/lib/constants.js');
const rl = require('readline').createInterface({ input: process.stdin });
const out = [];
(async () => {
  for await (const line of rl) {
    const [max, hex] = line.split(' ');
    const r = new Receiver({ isServer: true, maxPayload: +max });
    const ev = [];
    const h = d => Buffer.from(d).toString('hex');
    r.on('message', (d, binary) => ev.push((binary ? 'B ' : 'T ') + h(d)));
    r.on('ping', d => ev.push('P ' + h(d)));
    r.on('pong', d => ev.push('O ' + h(d)));
    r.on('conclude', (code, reason) => ev.push('C ' + code + ' ' + h(reason)));
    r.on('error', e => ev.push('E ' + e[kStatusCode] + ' ' + e.message.replace(/^(Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid status code) \d+$/, '$1')));
    r.write(Buffer.from(hex || '', 'hex'));
    // the error comes on the next tick
    await new Promise(res => setImmediate(res));
    out.push(ev.join('|'));
  }
  process.stdout.write(out.map(s => s + '\n').join(''));
})();
"#;

fn events(got: &(Vec<Message>, ReadError)) -> String {
    let mut ev: Vec<String> = got
        .0
        .iter()
        .map(|m| match m {
            Message::Text(d) => format!("T {}", hex(d)),
            Message::Binary(d) => format!("B {}", hex(d)),
            Message::Ping(d) => format!("P {}", hex(d)),
            Message::Pong(d) => format!("O {}", hex(d)),
            Message::Close(code, d) => format!("C {code} {}", hex(d)),
        })
        .collect();
    if let ReadError::Protocol { code, reason } = &got.1 {
        ev.push(format!("E {code} {reason}"));
    }
    ev.join("|")
}

/// a payload of UTF-8 pieces: whole characters mostly, sometimes a byte of one, or one no UTF-8 has
fn utf8ish(r: &mut Rng, n: usize) -> Vec<u8> {
    let atoms: [&[u8]; 12] = [
        b"a",
        b"Z",
        b" ",
        "é".as_bytes(),
        "€".as_bytes(),
        "😀".as_bytes(),
        b"\xc3",
        b"\xa9",
        b"\xe2\x82",
        b"\xf0\x9f\x98",
        b"\xff",
        b"\xed\xa0\x80",
    ];
    let mut p = Vec::new();
    while p.len() < n {
        let a = if r.chance(95) { *r.pick(&atoms[..6]) } else { *r.pick(&atoms) };
        p.extend_from_slice(a);
    }
    p
}

/// A random stream of client frames: mostly well formed, with every way of breaking one ws knew sprinkled in.
fn random_stream(r: &mut Rng) -> (usize, Vec<u8>) {
    let max = *r.pick(&[65536, 300, 100, 0]);
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    // a message in fragments is open (as the frames are meant: the reader decides what they are)
    let mut open = false;
    for _ in 0..1 + r.below(6) {
        let kind = r.below(100);
        let (mut op, fin) = match kind {
            0..=19 => (1, true),
            20..=34 => (2, true),
            35..=59 if open || r.chance(10) => (0, r.chance(60)),
            35..=59 => (*r.pick(&[1, 2]), false),
            60..=71 => (9, true),
            72..=77 => (10, true),
            78..=94 => (8, true),
            _ => (r.below(16) as u8, r.chance(70)),
        };
        if r.chance(2) {
            op = r.below(16) as u8;
        }
        let fin = if r.chance(2) { !fin } else { fin };
        if op < 3 {
            open = !fin;
        }
        let control = (8..=10).contains(&op);
        let n = match (control, r.chance(85)) {
            (_, true) => r.below(24) as usize,
            (true, false) => 120 + r.below(10) as usize,
            (false, false) => 90 + r.below(320) as usize,
        };
        let payload = match op {
            8 => match r.below(10) {
                0 => vec![],
                1 => vec![r.next() as u8],
                _ => {
                    let code: u16 = match r.below(4) {
                        0 => r.next() as u16,
                        _ => *r.pick(&[0, 999, 1000, 1001, 1004, 1005, 1006, 1011, 1014, 1015, 2999, 3000, 4999, 5000]),
                    };
                    let mut p = code.to_be_bytes().to_vec();
                    let n = r.below(12) as usize;
                    p.extend(utf8ish(r, n));
                    p
                }
            },
            1 | 0 => utf8ish(r, n),
            _ => r.bytes(n),
        };
        let mut b0 = (op & 0x0f) | if fin { 0x80 } else { 0 };
        if r.chance(2) {
            b0 |= ((1 + r.below(7)) as u8) << 4;
        }
        let mask = if r.chance(2) {
            None
        } else if r.chance(10) {
            Some([0; 4])
        } else {
            let k = r.next().to_le_bytes();
            Some([k[0], k[1], k[2], k[3]])
        };
        if r.chance(2) {
            // a length no payload follows: over 2^53, or past every limit
            out.push(b0);
            let n = if r.chance(50) { r.next() | 1 << 60 } else { (1 << 53) - 1 - r.below(1000) };
            out.extend(length(n, mask.is_some(), Len::L64));
            out.extend(mask.unwrap_or([1, 2, 3, 4]));
            continue;
        }
        // a control frame in a long form is refused: rarely
        let len = if control && r.chance(90) { Len::Short } else { *r.pick(&[Len::Short, Len::Short, Len::Short, Len::L16, Len::L64]) };
        out.extend(raw_with(b0, &payload, mask, len));
    }
    if r.chance(8) {
        let cut = r.below(out.len() as u64 + 1) as usize;
        out.truncate(cut);
    }
    (max, out)
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn reader_against_ws_receiver() {
    let Some(ws) = ws_dir() else { return };
    let mut rng = Rng(0x6455_0001);
    let cases: Vec<(usize, Vec<u8>)> = (0..50000).map(|_| random_stream(&mut rng)).collect();
    let input: String = cases.iter().map(|(max, s)| format!("{max} {}\n", hex(s))).collect();
    let want = node(&ws, RECEIVER, input);
    assert_eq!(want.len(), cases.len());
    let (mut errors, mut messages) = (std::collections::BTreeMap::new(), 0);
    for (i, ((max, s), want)) in cases.iter().zip(&want).enumerate() {
        let whole = read_all(WsReader::new(tokio::io::empty(), Bytes::copy_from_slice(s), *max)).await;
        assert_eq!(events(&whole), *want, "case {i}: max {max}, stream {}", hex(s));
        // and in pieces of random sizes
        let sizes: Vec<usize> = (0..7).map(|_| 1 + rng.below(40) as usize).collect();
        let pieces = read_all(WsReader::new(Drip::sizes(s, sizes), Bytes::new(), *max)).await;
        assert_eq!(pieces, whole, "case {i} in pieces");
        if let ReadError::Protocol { code, reason } = whole.1 {
            *errors.entry((code, reason)).or_insert(0) += 1;
        }
        messages += whole.0.len();
    }
    eprintln!("{} streams, {messages} messages, the same as ws's; its errors:", cases.len());
    for ((code, reason), n) in &errors {
        eprintln!("  {n:5} {code} {reason}");
    }
    // the corpus reaches every rule
    assert!(messages > 30000, "{messages} messages");
    assert!(errors.len() >= 24, "{} kinds of errors", errors.len());
}

// Each line: a Sec-WebSocket-Key, a tab, the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header in hex ("N": none).  Out: the 101 ws
// wrote, in hex, or "ERR" when it refused the handshake.
const HANDSHAKE: &str = r#"
const ws = process.argv[process.argv.length - 1];
const WebSocketServer = require(ws + '/lib/websocket-server.js');
const { Duplex } = require('stream');
const wss = new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true, perMessageDeflate: false, clientTracking: false, maxPayload: 65536, autoPong: false });
let refused = false;
wss.on('wsClientError', () => { refused = true; });
const rl = require('readline').createInterface({ input: process.stdin });
const out = [];
rl.on('line', line => {
  const [key, proto] = line.split('\t');
  const chunks = [];
  const sock = new Duplex({ read() {}, write(c, e, cb) { chunks.push(Buffer.from(c)); cb(); } });
  const headers = { upgrade: 'websocket', 'sec-websocket-key': key, 'sec-websocket-version': '13' };
  if (proto !== 'N') headers['sec-websocket-protocol'] = Buffer.from(proto, 'hex').toString('latin1');
  refused = false;
  wss.handleUpgrade({ method: 'GET', headers, url: '/lan' }, sock, Buffer.alloc(0), () => {});
  out.push(refused ? 'ERR' : Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('hex'));
  sock.destroy();
});
rl.on('close', () => process.stdout.write(out.map(s => s + '\n').join('')));
"#;

#[test]
fn handshake_against_ws_server() {
    let Some(ws) = ws_dir() else { return };
    let mut rng = Rng(0x6455_0002);
    const B64: &[u8] = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/";
    let pieces = ["a", "b", "chat", "x-1", "!", "~", " ", "\t", ",", ", ", ";", "\"", "é", "=", "/", "A", "a,b", "\u{1}"];
    let mut cases = Vec::new();
    for i in 0..20000 {
        let key: String = (0..22).map(|_| *rng.pick(B64) as char).chain("==".chars()).collect();
        let proto = if i % 10 == 0 {
            None
        } else {
            let n = rng.below(7);
            Some((0..n).map(|_| *rng.pick(&pieces)).collect::<String>())
        };
        cases.push((key, proto));
    }
    // headers as Node gives them: latin1 strings, so only ASCII ones are the same text on both sides (any other
    // character is refused on both)
    let input: String = cases
        .iter()
        .map(|(k, p)| {
            let h = match p {
                None => "N".to_string(),
                Some(p) if p.is_ascii() => hex(p.as_bytes()),
                // é as latin1 (one byte): no token character either way
                Some(p) => hex(&p.chars().map(|c| if c.is_ascii() { c as u8 } else { 0xe9 }).collect::<Vec<u8>>()),
            };
            format!("{k}\t{h}\n")
        })
        .collect();
    let want = node(&ws, HANDSHAKE, input);
    assert_eq!(want.len(), cases.len());
    let (mut picked, mut refused) = (0, 0);
    for ((key, proto), want) in cases.iter().zip(&want) {
        let got = match pick_protocol(proto.as_deref()) {
            Err(()) => {
                refused += 1;
                "ERR".to_string()
            }
            Ok(p) => {
                picked += p.is_some() as usize;
                hex(&handshake_response(key, p.as_deref()))
            }
        };
        assert_eq!(got, *want, "key {key}, Sec-WebSocket-Protocol {proto:?}");
    }
    eprintln!("{} handshakes: {picked} with a protocol, {refused} refused, the same as ws's", cases.len());
    assert!(picked > 2000 && refused > 2000);
}

//! WsReader against hand-built frames: every rule of ws's receiver.js, each read whole and in pieces.

mod common;

use std::time::Duration;

use bytes::Bytes;
use common::*;
use nfsu2_ws::{Message, ReadError, WsReader};
use tokio::io::AsyncWriteExt;

const MAX: usize = 65536;

const MASK_SET: &str = "Invalid WebSocket frame: MASK must be set";
const RSV1: &str = "Invalid WebSocket frame: RSV1 must be clear";
const RSV23: &str = "Invalid WebSocket frame: RSV2 and RSV3 must be clear";
const FIN: &str = "Invalid WebSocket frame: FIN must be set";
const UTF8: &str = "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid UTF-8 sequence";
const MAX_PAYLOAD: &str = "Max payload size exceeded";
const OVER_2_53: &str = "Unsupported WebSocket frame: payload length > 2^53 - 1";
const STATUS: &str = "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid status code";

#[tokio::test]
async fn rfc_6455_examples() {
    // 5.7: a single-frame masked text message, and a masked ping, both "Hello"
    let hello = [0x81, 0x85, 0x37, 0xfa, 0x21, 0x3d, 0x7f, 0x9f, 0x4d, 0x51, 0x58];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&hello, MAX).await, (vec![t("Hello")], ReadError::Closed));
    let ping = [0x89, 0x85, 0x37, 0xfa, 0x21, 0x3d, 0x7f, 0x9f, 0x4d, 0x51, 0x58];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&ping, MAX).await, (vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::from_static(b"Hello"))], ReadError::Closed));
    // its unmasked examples are a server's frames: from a client they break the protocol
    let unmasked = [0x81, 0x05, 0x48, 0x65, 0x6c, 0x6c, 0x6f];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&unmasked, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, MASK_SET)));
    let fragmented = [0x01, 0x03, 0x48, 0x65, 0x6c, 0x80, 0x02, 0x6c, 0x6f];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&fragmented, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, MASK_SET)));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn single_frames() {
    let data = cat(&[text(b"Hello"), binary(&[0, 1, 2, 255]), text(b""), binary(b""), pong(b"x"), ping(b"")]);
    let want = vec![t("Hello"), b(&[0, 1, 2, 255]), t(""), b(b""), Message::Pong(Bytes::from_static(b"x")), Message::Ping(Bytes::new())];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&data, MAX).await, (want, ReadError::Closed));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_mask_of_zeros() {
    let f = raw_with(0x81, b"plain", Some([0; 4]), Len::Short);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![t("plain")], ReadError::Closed));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn lengths_in_every_form() {
    for n in [0, 1, 125, 126, 127, 1000, 65535, 65536] {
        let p: Vec<u8> = (0..n).map(|i| (i * 7) as u8).collect();
        let (m, e) = read_bytes(&binary(&p), MAX).await;
        assert_eq!((m, e), (vec![b(&p)], ReadError::Closed), "length {n}");
    }
    // a length in a longer form than it needs: ws took it
    for len in [Len::L16, Len::L64] {
        let f = raw_with(0x81, b"short", Some(MASK), len);
        assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![t("short")], ReadError::Closed));
    }
    let f = raw_with(0x82, &[9; 300], Some(MASK), Len::L64);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![b(&[9; 300])], ReadError::Closed));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn max_payload_over_a_frame() {
    // exactly max_payload is fine, one byte more a 1009, refused on its header before the payload comes
    let p = vec![1u8; MAX + 1];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&binary(&p[..MAX]), MAX).await.0, vec![b(&p[..MAX])]);
    let f = binary(&p);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1009, MAX_PAYLOAD)));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f[..14], MAX).await, (vec![], err(1009, MAX_PAYLOAD)));
    // text the same, and a small limit
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&text(&[b'a'; 11]), 10).await, (vec![], err(1009, MAX_PAYLOAD)));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&text(&[b'a'; 10]), 10).await.0, vec![t("aaaaaaaaaa")]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn max_payload_over_a_message() {
    // counted over all of a message's fragments
    let a = vec![2u8; 40000];
    let ok = cat(&[raw(0x02, &a), cont(true, &[3; MAX - 40000])]);
    let mut whole = a.clone();
    whole.extend([3; MAX - 40000]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&ok, MAX).await, (vec![b(&whole)], ReadError::Closed));
    let over = cat(&[raw(0x02, &a), cont(true, &[3; MAX - 40000 + 1])]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&over, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1009, MAX_PAYLOAD)));
    // the second fragment's header alone is enough
    let header_only = &over[..6 + 40000 + 8];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(header_only, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1009, MAX_PAYLOAD)));
    // control frames between the fragments do not count; the next message starts from 0
    let pings = cat(&[raw(0x01, &[b'a'; 6]), ping(&[0; 125]), cont(true, &[b'b'; 4]), text(&[b'c'; 10])]);
    let (m, e) = read_bytes(&pings, 10).await;
    assert_eq!(e, ReadError::Closed);
    assert_eq!(m, vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::from(vec![0; 125])), t("aaaaaabbbb"), t("cccccccccc")]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn no_max_payload() {
    // ws: maxPayload 0 is no limit
    let p = vec![5u8; 200_000];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&binary(&p), 0).await, (vec![b(&p)], ReadError::Closed));
    // a length announced and never sent reserves nothing: the reader waits for it (here: the end)
    let mut f = vec![0x82];
    f.extend(length((1u64 << 53) - 1, true, Len::L64));
    f.extend(MASK);
    f.extend([0; 100]);
    assert_eq!(read_all(WsReader::new(Drip::new(&f, 16), Bytes::new(), 0)).await, (vec![], ReadError::Closed));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn lengths_over_2_53() {
    // ws counted in JS numbers: a length over 2^53 - 1 is a 1009 of its own, before max_payload
    let mut f = vec![0x82];
    f.extend(length(1u64 << 53, true, Len::L64));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1009, OVER_2_53)));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, 0).await, (vec![], err(1009, OVER_2_53)));
    let mut f = vec![0x82];
    f.extend(length(u64::MAX, true, Len::L64));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, 0).await, (vec![], err(1009, OVER_2_53)));
    let mut f = vec![0x82];
    f.extend(length((1u64 << 53) - 1, true, Len::L64));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1009, MAX_PAYLOAD)));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn rsv_bits() {
    // no extension was ever accepted (perMessageDeflate: false): RSV1 is a 1002 too; RSV2/3 are checked first
    for (b0, why) in [(0xc1, RSV1), (0xa1, RSV23), (0x91, RSV23), (0xb1, RSV23), (0xe1, RSV23), (0xf1, RSV23)] {
        assert_eq!(read_bytes(&raw(b0, b"x"), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, why)), "{b0:#x}");
    }
    // on a continuation and on a control frame
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"a"), raw(0xc0, b"b")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, RSV1)));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&raw(0xc9, b""), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, RSV1)));
    // an unmasked frame with RSV1: the RSV is seen first
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&raw_with(0xc1, b"x", None, Len::Short), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, RSV1)));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn every_opcode() {
    const NAMES: [&str; 16] = [
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 0",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 1",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 2",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 3",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 4",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 5",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 6",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 7",
        "",
        "",
        "",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 11",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 12",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 13",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 14",
        "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 15",
    ];
    for op in 0u8..16 {
        for fin in [true, false] {
            let b0 = op | if fin { 0x80 } else { 0 };
            let got = read_bytes(&raw(b0, b"ab"), MAX).await;
            let want = match (op, fin) {
                (1, true) => (vec![t("ab")], ReadError::Closed),
                (2, true) => (vec![b(b"ab")], ReadError::Closed),
                // the first fragment of a message that never ends
                (1 | 2, false) => (vec![], ReadError::Closed),
                // "ab" as a close code is 0x6162: not one a close frame may carry
                (8, true) => (vec![], err(1002, STATUS)),
                (9, true) => (vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::from_static(b"ab"))], ReadError::Closed),
                (10, true) => (vec![Message::Pong(Bytes::from_static(b"ab"))], ReadError::Closed),
                (8..=10, false) => (vec![], err(1002, FIN)),
                // 0: a continuation with no message to continue
                _ => (vec![], err(1002, NAMES[op as usize])),
            };
            assert_eq!(got, want, "opcode {op} fin {fin}");
        }
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn continuation_rules() {
    // a continuation with nothing to continue
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&cont(true, b"x"), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 0")));
    // after a whole message there is nothing to continue either
    let f = cat(&[text(b"a"), cont(true, b"b")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![t("a")], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 0")));
    // a new text or binary message while one is in fragments
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"a"), text(b"b")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 1")));
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"a"), raw(0x02, b"b")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 2")));
}

#[tokio::test]

#[tokio::test]
async fn control_frame_lengths() {
    let p125 = vec![7u8; 125];
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&ping(&p125), MAX).await.0, vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::from(p125.clone()))]);
    // over 125 bytes: refused on the 7-bit length (126 and 127 are what it can say)
    let f = raw_with(0x89, &[7; 126], Some(MASK), Len::Short);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid payload length 126")));
    let f = raw_with(0x8a, &[7; 5], Some(MASK), Len::L64);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid payload length 127")));
    let f = raw_with(0x88, &[7; 5], Some(MASK), Len::L16);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid payload length 126")));
    // a close frame of 1 byte (half a code)
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&raw(0x88, &[3]), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid payload length 1")));
    // FIN is checked before the length; the length before the mask
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&raw_with(0x09, &[0; 126], Some(MASK), Len::Short), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, FIN)));
    let f = raw_with(0x89, &[0; 126], None, Len::Short);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid payload length 126")));
}

#[tokio::test]

#[tokio::test]
async fn text_must_be_utf8() {
    for bad in [
        &[0xff][..],
        &[0x80],
        &[0xc3],                   // cut short
        &[0xc0, 0x80],             // overlong
        &[0xc1, 0xbf],             // overlong
        &[0xe0, 0x80, 0x80],       // overlong
        &[0xed, 0xa0, 0x80],       // a surrogate
        &[0xf0, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80], // overlong
        &[0xf4, 0x90, 0x80, 0x80], // over U+10FFFF
        &[0xf5, 0x80, 0x80, 0x80],
        &[0xe2, 0x82],
        b"ok then \xe2\x82",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(read_bytes(&text(bad), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1007, UTF8)), "{bad:x?}");
        // binary is anything
        assert_eq!(read_bytes(&binary(bad), MAX).await.0, vec![b(bad)]);
    }
    let good = "a\u{7f}\u{80}\u{7ff}\u{800}\u{d7ff}\u{e000}\u{fffd}\u{10000}\u{10ffff} é € 😀";
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&text(good.as_bytes()), MAX).await.0, vec![t(good)]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn utf8_across_fragments() {
    // a character split across fragments is fine: the whole message is checked
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"caf\xc3"), cont(true, b"\xa9")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await.0, vec![t("café")]);
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"\xe2"), ping(b""), cont(false, b"\x82"), cont(true, b"\xac!")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await.0, vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::new()), t("€!")]);
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"\xf0\x9f"), cont(false, b"\x98"), cont(true, b"\x80")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await.0, vec![t("😀")]);
    // a sequence broken across fragments
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"\xc3"), cont(true, b"(")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![], err(1007, UTF8)));
    // a bad first fragment is refused when the message ends, not before (ws checked the whole message)
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"\xff"), ping(b"still")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::from_static(b"still"))], ReadError::Closed));
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"\xff"), ping(b"still"), cont(true, b"end")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::from_static(b"still"))], err(1007, UTF8)));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn close_frames() {
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&raw(0x88, b""), MAX).await, (vec![closed(1005, "")], ReadError::Closed));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&close(1000, b"bye"), MAX).await, (vec![closed(1000, "bye")], ReadError::Closed));
    let reason = "x".repeat(123);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&close(4999, reason.as_bytes()), MAX).await.0, vec![closed(4999, &reason)]);
    for code in [1000, 1001, 1002, 1003, 1007, 1008, 1009, 1010, 1011, 1012, 1013, 1014, 3000, 3999, 4000, 4999] {
        assert_eq!(read_bytes(&close(code, b"r"), MAX).await, (vec![closed(code, "r")], ReadError::Closed), "{code}");
    }
    for code in [0, 999, 1004, 1005, 1006, 1015, 1016, 2000, 2999, 5000, 65535] {
        assert_eq!(read_bytes(&close(code, b""), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1002, STATUS)), "{code}");
    }
    // the reason must be UTF-8
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&close(1000, b"\xc3"), MAX).await, (vec![], err(1007, UTF8)));
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&close(1000, "é".as_bytes()), MAX).await.0, vec![closed(1000, "é")]);
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn nothing_counts_after_a_close() {
    // ws stopped reading at a close frame: what follows, good or broken, is never seen
    let f = cat(&[text(b"a"), close(1001, b""), text(b"b"), raw_with(0x81, b"c", None, Len::Short), ping(b"d")]);
    assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f, MAX).await, (vec![t("a"), closed(1001, "")], ReadError::Closed));
    // and next() goes on saying Closed
    let mut r = WsReader::new(tokio::io::empty(), Bytes::from(close(1000, b"")), MAX);
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Ok(closed(1000, "")));
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn nothing_counts_after_a_protocol_error() {
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x83, b""), text(b"later")]);
    let mut r = WsReader::new(Drip::new(&f, 3), Bytes::new(), MAX);
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(err(1002, "Invalid WebSocket frame: invalid opcode 3")));
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn the_end_of_the_connection() {
    let f = text(b"Hello");
    for cut in 0..f.len() {
        assert_eq!(read_bytes(&f[..cut], MAX).await, (vec![], ReadError::Closed), "cut at {cut}");
    }
    // an I/O error is the same as the end
    let mut r = WsReader::new(Failing(cat(&[text(b"a"), text(b"b")])), Bytes::new(), MAX);
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Ok(t("a")));
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Ok(t("b")));
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
    let mut r = WsReader::new(Failing(text(b"a")[..4].to_vec()), Bytes::new(), MAX);
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn pre_and_the_connection_together() {

    for split in 0..=f.len() {
        let r = WsReader::new(Drip::new(&f[split..], 5), Bytes::copy_from_slice(&f[..split]), MAX);
        assert_eq!(read_all(r).await, (vec![t("first"), t("second"), t("third")], ReadError::Closed), "split {split}");
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn a_single_frame_message_is_not_copied() {
    // payloads are views of the read block: two frames read together sit side by side in it, 6 header bytes apart
    let f = cat(&[binary(&[1; 100]), binary(&[2; 50]), raw(0x02, &[3; 10]), cont(true, &[4; 10])]);
    let n = f.len();
    let mut r = WsReader::new(tokio::io::empty(), Bytes::from(f), MAX);
    let (Ok(Message::Binary(a)), Ok(Message::Binary(b))) = (r.next().await, r.next().await) else { panic!() };
    assert_eq!(a.as_ptr() as usize + a.len() + 6, b.as_ptr() as usize);
    // a message in fragments is joined into a buffer of its own
    let Ok(Message::Binary(c)) = r.next().await else { panic!() };
    assert_eq!(&c[..], &[[3; 10], [4; 10]].concat()[..]);
    let block = a.as_ptr() as usize - 6..a.as_ptr() as usize + n;
    assert!(!block.contains(&(c.as_ptr() as usize)));
}

#[tokio::test]

    let (m, e) = read_bytes(&frames.concat(), MAX).await;
    assert_eq!(e, ReadError::Closed);

}

#[tokio::test]
async fn large_frames_in_random_pieces() {
    let mut rng = Rng(0x5eed);
    let mut frames = Vec::new();
    let mut want = Vec::new();
    for _ in 0..40 {
        let n = *rng.pick(&[0, 1, 125, 126, 4000, 16 << 10, (16 << 10) + 1, 40000, MAX]);
        let p = rng.bytes(n);
        frames.push(binary(&p));
        want.push(b(&p));
    }
    let data = frames.concat();
    for seed in 1..6 {
        let mut rng = Rng(seed);
        let sizes: Vec<usize> = (0..97).map(|_| 1 + rng.below(20000) as usize).collect();
        let got = read_all(WsReader::new(Drip::sizes(&data, sizes), Bytes::new(), MAX)).await;
        assert_eq!(got, (want.clone(), ReadError::Closed), "seed {seed}");
    }
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn cancel_safe() {
    // next() dropped by a timeout while a frame is half there (a select! with a timer): nothing is lost
    let f = cat(&[raw(0x01, b"frag"), ping(b"p"), cont(true, b"ment"), binary(&[9; 300])]);
    let (mut client, server) = tokio::io::duplex(1 << 16);
    let mut r = WsReader::new(server, Bytes::new(), MAX);
    let writer = tokio::spawn(async move {
        for piece in f.chunks(7) {
            client.write_all(piece).await.unwrap();
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(2)).await;
        }
        client
    });
    let (mut got, mut timeouts) = (Vec::new(), 0);
    while got.len() < 3 {
        match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_micros(500), r.next()).await {
            Ok(m) => got.push(m.unwrap()),
            Err(_) => timeouts += 1,
        }
    }
    drop(writer.await.unwrap());
    assert_eq!(got, vec![Message::Ping(Bytes::from_static(b"p")), t("fragment"), b(&[9; 300])]);
    assert!(timeouts > 0, "the timeout never fired");
    assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
}

//! A round trip with another implementation: tokio-tungstenite as the client, an echo server made of this crate's
//! parts (the handshake, WsReader, frame) on a real TCP connection.

use bytes::Bytes;
use futures_util::{SinkExt, StreamExt};
use nfsu2_ws::{Message, ReadError, WsReader, frame, handshake_response, pick_protocol};
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
use tokio::net::TcpListener;
use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::client::IntoClientRequest;
use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::http::HeaderValue;
use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::protocol::CloseFrame;
use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::protocol::frame::Frame;
use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::protocol::frame::coding::{Data, OpCode};
use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::{self as tung, Message as TMessage};

/// a header of the request's head
fn header(head: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    head.split("\r\n").skip(1).find_map(|l| {
        let (n, v) = l.split_once(':')?;
        n.trim().eq_ignore_ascii_case(name).then(|| v.trim().to_string())
    })
}

/// One connection's server: the handshake, then every message echoed, a ping answered with its pong, a close frame
/// with ws's answer (the same code and reason), a protocol error with its close frame.  What it saw comes back.
async fn echo_server() -> (String, tokio::task::JoinHandle<Vec<String>>) {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
    let url = format!("ws://{}/lan", listener.local_addr().unwrap());
    let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
        let (sock, _) = listener.accept().await.unwrap();
        sock.set_nodelay(true).unwrap();
        let (mut rd, mut wr) = sock.into_split();
        let mut head = Vec::new();
        let end = loop {
            let mut tmp = [0u8; 1024];
            let n = rd.read(&mut tmp).await.unwrap();
            assert!(n > 0, "no handshake");
            head.extend_from_slice(&tmp[..n]);
            if let Some(i) = head.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n") {
                break i + 4;
            }
        };
        let pre = Bytes::copy_from_slice(&head[end..]);
        let head = String::from_utf8(head[..end].to_vec()).unwrap();
        let key = header(&head, "sec-websocket-key").unwrap();
        let protocol = pick_protocol(header(&head, "sec-websocket-protocol").as_deref()).unwrap();
        wr.write_all(&handshake_response(&key, protocol.as_deref())).await.unwrap();
        let mut r = WsReader::new(rd, pre, 65536);
        let mut seen = Vec::new();
        loop {
            let mut out = Vec::new();
            let last = match r.next().await {
                Ok(Message::Text(t)) => {
                    seen.push(format!("text {}", t.len()));
                    frame::encode(frame::TEXT, &t, &mut out);
                    false
                }
                Ok(Message::Binary(b)) => {
                    seen.push(format!("binary {}", b.len()));
                    frame::encode(frame::BINARY, &b, &mut out);
                    false
                }
                Ok(Message::Ping(p)) => {
                    seen.push(format!("ping {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&p)));
                    frame::encode(frame::PONG, &p, &mut out);
                    false
                }
                Ok(Message::Pong(p)) => {
                    seen.push(format!("pong {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&p)));
                    false
                }
                Ok(Message::Close(code, reason)) => {
                    let reason = std::str::from_utf8(&reason).unwrap();
                    seen.push(format!("close {code} {reason}"));
                    frame::encode(frame::CLOSE, &frame::close_payload(code, reason), &mut out);
                    true
                }
                Err(ReadError::Protocol { code, reason }) => {
                    seen.push(format!("error {code} {reason}"));
                    frame::encode(frame::CLOSE, &frame::close_payload(code, ""), &mut out);
                    true
                }
                Err(ReadError::Closed) => {
                    seen.push("closed".into());
                    break;
                }
            };
            wr.write_all(&out).await.unwrap();
            if last {
                wr.shutdown().await.unwrap();
                // the client's end of the connection, whatever it sends before it
                assert_eq!(r.next().await, Err(ReadError::Closed));
                seen.push("closed".into());
                break;
            }
        }
        seen
    });
    (url, task)
}

fn text(s: &str) -> TMessage {
    TMessage::Text(s.into())
}

#[tokio::test]
async fn round_trip() {
    let (url, server) = echo_server().await;
    let mut req = url.into_client_request().unwrap();
    req.headers_mut().insert("Sec-WebSocket-Protocol", HeaderValue::from_static("chat, superchat"));
    let (mut ws, resp) = tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(req).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(resp.status(), 101);
    assert_eq!(resp.headers()["sec-websocket-protocol"], "chat");

    ws.send(text("hello")).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ws.next().await.unwrap().unwrap(), text("hello"));
    for n in [0, 125, 126, 200, 65535, 65536] {
        let p = Bytes::from((0..n).map(|i| (i % 251) as u8).collect::<Vec<u8>>());
        ws.send(TMessage::Binary(p.clone())).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(ws.next().await.unwrap().unwrap(), TMessage::Binary(p), "{n} bytes");
    }
    // a message in fragments, a ping between them
    ws.send(TMessage::Frame(Frame::message(Bytes::from_static(b"Hel"), OpCode::Data(Data::Text), false))).await.unwrap();
    ws.send(TMessage::Ping(Bytes::from_static(b"p"))).await.unwrap();
    ws.send(TMessage::Frame(Frame::message(Bytes::from_static("lo é".as_bytes()), OpCode::Data(Data::Continue), true))).await.unwrap();
    assert_eq!(ws.next().await.unwrap().unwrap(), TMessage::Pong(Bytes::from_static(b"p")));
    assert_eq!(ws.next().await.unwrap().unwrap(), text("Hello é"));
    ws.send(TMessage::Pong(Bytes::from_static(b"unasked"))).await.unwrap();
    // the close handshake: ws answered with the same code and reason
    ws.send(TMessage::Close(Some(CloseFrame { code: 1000.into(), reason: "bye".into() }))).await.unwrap();
    match ws.next().await.unwrap().unwrap() {
        TMessage::Close(Some(f)) => assert_eq!((u16::from(f.code), f.reason.as_str()), (1000, "bye")),
        m => panic!("{m:?}"),
    }
    assert!(ws.next().await.is_none());
    // the server waits for the client's end of the connection
    drop(ws);
    let seen = server.await.unwrap();
    let want = [
        "text 5",
        "binary 0",
        "binary 125",
        "binary 126",
        "binary 200",
        "binary 65535",
        "binary 65536",
        "ping p",
        "text 8",
        "pong unasked",
        "close 1000 bye",
        "closed",
    ];
    assert_eq!(seen, want);
}

/// the close code (and reason) the client got from the server after sending `m`
async fn refused(m: TMessage) -> ((u16, String), Vec<String>) {
    let (url, server) = echo_server().await;
    let (mut ws, resp) = tokio_tungstenite::connect_async(url).await.unwrap();
    assert!(resp.headers().get("sec-websocket-protocol").is_none());
    ws.send(m).await.unwrap();
    let got = match ws.next().await {
        Some(Ok(TMessage::Close(Some(f)))) => (u16::from(f.code), f.reason.to_string()),
        Some(Ok(m)) => panic!("{m:?}"),
        Some(Err(e)) => panic!("{e}"),
        None => panic!("no close frame"),
    };
    // tungstenite answers the close frame; the server waits for the end of the connection
    while let Some(r) = ws.next().await {
        if let Err(tung::Error::ConnectionClosed | tung::Error::AlreadyClosed) = r {
            break;
        }
    }
    drop(ws);
    (got, server.await.unwrap())
}

//! The server's own race bans: a player who raced others in a lobby race in a car past the operator's numbers (engine
//! power, rating: nfsu2-roam `CarBans`, hub.rs `server_bans`) is race-banned for AUTO_FOR by its `[cheat]` line's
//! handle, as the operator's `raceban <handle> 2w` would (control.rs `App::ban_by`), and the ban is posted to Discord.
//! A player banned so asks on Discord with its ban's number; `unban #N` lifts it, `change #N` makes it longer.
//!
//!   NFSU2_CAR_BANS=kw=<kW>,rating=<rating>  the numbers (either alone too); none: no such bans, the `[cheat]` lines
//!                                           only.  The operator's, in the server's environment (.env): never in the
//!                                           code, where a cheater would read how far to go.
//!   NFSU2_BAN_WEBHOOK=<url>                 a Discord channel's webhook (the channel's Edit Channel, Integrations,
//!                                           Webhooks): each such ban posted there; none: its `[ban]` line only.  The
//!                                           address is a secret too (whoever has it posts there): no line names it.
//!
//! The post is a Components V2 message (Discord's flag IS_COMPONENTS_V2; a webhook not of an application sends
//! components only with `with_components=true`): a container with the ban and the car, a line under it with the race
//! and the ban's length, no mentions.

use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::Duration;

use nfsu2_bans::Kind;
use nfsu2_roam::{CarBan, CarBans};
use nfsu2_util::{log, now_ms, vip_str};
use serde_json::{Value, json};
use tokio::sync::mpsc;

use super::App;
use super::control::{Made, Marker};
use super::outbound::Https;

/// how long the server's race ban lasts (the operator's choice, 2026-11-07: two weeks)
const AUTO_FOR: &str = "2w";
/// what the player's page says of it (the operator's own bans' words)
const AUTO_MSG: &str = "Cheating in multiplayer races";
/// Discord's answer, at most
const POST_WITHIN: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
/// the container's accent: red
const ACCENT: u32 = 0xE5_48_4D;
/// Discord's message flag IS_COMPONENTS_V2: the message is its components only (no content, no embeds)
const COMPONENTS_V2: u32 = 1 << 15;

/// NFSU2_CAR_BANS's numbers, engine power (kW) and rating: None when it is not set (or empty), Err when it says
/// something else than `kw=<n>` and `rating=<n>` (either, or both: by commas or spaces)
fn parse_numbers(v: &str) -> Result<Option<(Option<f64>, Option<f64>)>, String> {
    let (mut kw, mut rating) = (None, None);
    for part in v.split([',', ' ']).filter(|p| !p.trim().is_empty()) {
        let (k, n) = part.split_once('=').ok_or_else(|| format!("\"{part}\" is no kw=<n> or rating=<n>"))?;
        let n = n.trim().parse::<f64>().ok().filter(|n| n.is_finite() && *n > 0.0);
        let n = n.ok_or_else(|| format!("\"{part}\": not a number above 0"))?;
        match k.trim() {
            "kw" => kw = Some(n),
            "rating" => rating = Some(n),
            _ => return Err(format!("\"{part}\": kw or rating")),
        }
    }
    Ok((kw.is_some() || rating.is_some()).then_some((kw, rating)))
}

/// The cars the server race-bans for (free roam's hub takes them: `RoamOptions::car_bans`), from NFSU2_CAR_BANS, and
/// the races it tells of (`start` takes them once the app is made); none without it
pub fn from_env() -> Option<(CarBans, mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<CarBan>)> {
    let v = std::env::var("NFSU2_CAR_BANS").unwrap_or_default();
    match parse_numbers(&v) {
        Ok(Some((kw, rating))) => {
            // (the hub tells of a player's race once, and of one report a player in 20 s at most: few)
            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::unbounded_channel();
            let call = Arc::new(move |c: CarBan| {
                let _ = tx.send(c);
            });
            Some((CarBans { kw, rating, call }, rx))
        }
        Ok(None) => None,
        Err(e) => {
            log::error(&format!("NFSU2_CAR_BANS: {e}: no race bans by the server"));
            None
        }
    }
}

/// NFSU2_BAN_WEBHOOK with the query Discord needs: its answer (`wait`: the message made, or why not) and components
/// from a webhook of no application (`with_components`)
fn webhook_from_env() -> Option<String> {
    let v = std::env::var("NFSU2_BAN_WEBHOOK").unwrap_or_default().trim().to_string();
    if v.is_empty() {
        return None;
    }
    if !(v.starts_with("https://") || v.starts_with("http://")) {
        log::error("NFSU2_BAN_WEBHOOK: not an http(s) address: the server's bans are not posted");
        return None;
    }
    Some(format!("{v}{}wait=true&with_components=true", if v.contains('?') { '&' } else { '?' }))
}

/// The server's race bans from now on: each race the hub tells of, one after another
pub fn start(app: Arc<App>, marker: Marker, cars: &CarBans, mut races: mpsc::UnboundedReceiver<CarBan>) {
    let hook = webhook_from_env();
    log::line(&format!(
        "[ban] race bans by the server, for {AUTO_FOR}: a car of {}; {}",
        numbers(cars),
        if hook.is_some() { "posted to Discord" } else { "not posted (no NFSU2_BAN_WEBHOOK)" }
    ));
    let cars = cars.clone();
    let https = Https::new();
    tokio::spawn(async move {
        while let Some(c) = races.recv().await {
            ban_one(&app, &marker, &cars, hook.as_deref().map(|u| (&https, u)), c).await;
        }
    });
}

/// the operator's numbers as the start's line says them
fn numbers(cars: &CarBans) -> String {
    let mut t = Vec::new();
    if let Some(kw) = cars.kw {
        t.push(format!("{kw:.0} kW or more"));
    }
    if let Some(r) = cars.rating {
        t.push(format!("a rating of {r:.0} or more"));
    }
    t.join(" or ")
}

/// One race's ban: by the player's mark (its `[cheat]` line's handle, the keys the operator's ban would take); none
/// when it is in a race ban or a ban already (one it was let race in meanwhile is no reason for another)
async fn ban_one(app: &App, marker: &Marker, cars: &CarBans, post: Option<(&Https, &str)>, c: CarBan) {
    let who = format!("{} \"{}\"", vip_str(c.vip), c.name);
    let Some(m) = marker.mark_of(c.vip, &c.name) else {
        log::line(&format!("[ban] no race ban by the server for {who}: nothing to name it by; {}", car_text(&c)));
        return;
    };
    if let Some(&(id, _, kind)) = m.bans.iter().find(|&&(_, live, kind)| live && kind != Kind::Name) {
        log::line(&format!("[ban] {who} ({}) is in {} #{id} already; {}", m.handle, kind.word(), car_text(&c)));
        return;
    }
    let now = now_ms();
    let by = format!("; by the server: {}", car_text(&c));
    match app.ban_by(Kind::Races, &m.handle, AUTO_FOR, AUTO_MSG, now, &by).await {
        Ok(made) => {
            if let Some((https, url)) = post {
                send(https, url, &message(&c, cars, &made, &m.handle, &m.before), made.ban.id).await;
            }
        }
        Err(e) => log::error(&format!("[ban] the server's race ban of {who} ({}): {e}", m.handle)),
    }
}

/// the race as the `[ban]` line says it: "its SKYLINE (type 27): 2829 kW, 1338 kg, 381 km/h, rated 1451, in a lobby
/// sprint, 1st of 4 (lobby 000000c1, race 0badf00d)"
fn car_text(c: &CarBan) -> String {
    format!(
        "its {} (type {}): {:.0} kW, {:.0} kg, {:.0} km/h, rated {:.0}, in a lobby {}{}, {} (lobby {:08x}, race {:08x})",
        c.car,
        c.car_type,
        c.kw,
        c.kg,
        c.kmh,
        c.rating,
        c.kind,
        laps(c.laps),
        c.place,
        c.lobby,
        c.race
    )
}

fn laps(n: u8) -> String {
    if n > 1 { format!(" of {n} laps") } else { String::new() }
}

/// Discord's markdown off for a player's text: every ASCII punctuation mark escaped (a name like _-EVL-_GTR would be
/// italics, one with `|` or `#` would be something else again)
fn md(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut t = String::with_capacity(s.len() * 2);
    for ch in s.chars() {
        if ch.is_ascii_punctuation() {
            t.push('\\');
        }
        t.push(ch);
    }
    t
}

/// The post: a container, the ban's number and name over the car (the figure past the operator's number in bold, the
/// number itself not said), a line, then the race, the ban's length and end, the handle, and what else: out of races
/// at once (it was on), the names its earlier `[cheat]` lines had
fn message(c: &CarBan, cars: &CarBans, made: &Made, handle: &str, before: &[String]) -> Value {
    let past = |x: f64, at: Option<f64>, s: String| if at.is_some_and(|a| x >= a) { format!("**{s}**") } else { s };
    let head = format!(
        "### Race ban #{} · {}\nRaced a car no tuning makes: **{}**, {}, {}, {:.0} kg, {:.0} km/h",
        made.ban.id,
        md(&made.ban.name),
        md(&c.car),
        past(c.kw, cars.kw, format!("{:.0} kW", c.kw)),
        past(c.rating, cars.rating, format!("rated {:.0}", c.rating)),
        c.kg,
        c.kmh
    );
    let mut foot = vec!["Automatic".to_string(), format!("lobby {}{}, {}", md(&c.kind), laps(c.laps), md(&c.place))];
    foot.push(match made.ban.until {
        Some(t) => format!("2 weeks, until <t:{}:D>", t / 1000),
        None => "for good".to_string(),
    });
    foot.push(handle.to_string());
    if made.reached > 0 {
        foot.push("out of races now".to_string());
    }
    if !before.is_empty() {
        foot.push(format!("before as {}", before.iter().map(|n| md(n)).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ")));
    }
    json!({
        "flags": COMPONENTS_V2,
        "allowed_mentions": { "parse": [] },
        "components": [{
            "type": 17,
            "accent_color": ACCENT,
            "components": [
                { "type": 10, "content": head },
                { "type": 14, "divider": true, "spacing": 1 },
                { "type": 10, "content": format!("-# {}", foot.join(" · ")) },
            ],
        }],
    })
}

/// The post sent: a failure is a line (never the webhook's address: it is a secret), and a 429 (too many at once)
/// tried once more after a second
async fn send(https: &Https, url: &str, msg: &Value, id: u64) {
    let body = msg.to_string();
    for attempt in 0..2 {
        let what = match tokio::time::timeout(POST_WITHIN, https.post_json(url, &body)).await {
            Ok(Ok((s, _))) if (200..300).contains(&s) => return,
            Ok(Ok((429, _))) if attempt == 0 => {
                tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(1)).await;
                continue;
            }
            Ok(Ok((s, b))) => format!("its answer {s}: {}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..b.len().min(300)])),
            Ok(Err(e)) => e,
            Err(_) => format!("no answer in {} s", POST_WITHIN.as_secs()),
        };
        log::error(&format!("[ban] race ban #{id} not posted to Discord: {what}"));
        return;
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn the_operators_numbers_are_read_or_refused() {
        assert_eq!(parse_numbers(""), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(parse_numbers("  "), Ok(None));
        assert_eq!(parse_numbers("kw=1500,rating=3000"), Ok(Some((Some(1500.0), Some(3000.0)))));
        assert_eq!(parse_numbers("rating=3000 kw=1500"), Ok(Some((Some(1500.0), Some(3000.0)))));
        assert_eq!(parse_numbers("kw=1500"), Ok(Some((Some(1500.0), None))));
        assert_eq!(parse_numbers("rating=2500.5"), Ok(Some((None, Some(2500.5)))));
        for bad in ["1500", "kw=", "kw=fast", "kw=0", "kw=-5", "kw=inf", "speed=400", "kw=NaN"] {
            assert!(parse_numbers(bad).is_err(), "{bad}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_players_text_is_no_markdown() {
        assert_eq!(md("_-EVL-_GTR"), "\\_\\-EVL\\-\\_GTR");
        assert_eq!(md("a*b`c|d#e@f"), "a\\*b\\`c\\|d\\#e\\@f");
        assert_eq!(md("Plain 9"), "Plain 9");
    }

    fn car() -> CarBan {
        CarBan {
            vip: 0x0A4D_0005,
            name: "_-EVL-_GTR".into(),
            car: "SKYLINE".into(),
            car_type: 27,
            kw: 2829.0,
            kg: 1338.0,
            kmh: 381.0,
            rating: 1451.0,
            kind: "sprint".into(),
            laps: 1,
            place: "1st of 4".into(),
            lobby: 0xC1,
            race: 0x0BAD_F00D,
        }
    }

    fn made(until: Option<i64>, reached: usize) -> Made {
        let ban = serde_json::from_value(json!({ "id": 57, "kind": "races", "name": "_-EVL-_GTR", "at": 0, "until": until })).unwrap();
        Made { ban, reached, text: String::new() }
    }

    // the post: components only (the V2 flag, no content, no embeds), no mentions; a container of the head, a line and
    // the small print; the figure past the number in bold, the number never in it
    #[test]
    fn the_post_is_a_components_v2_container() {
        let cars = CarBans { kw: Some(1500.0), rating: Some(3000.0), call: Arc::new(|_| {}) };
        let m = message(&car(), &cars, &made(Some(1_794_000_000_000), 1), "c3058", &["PURE_EVL".to_string()]);
        assert_eq!(m["flags"], 32768);
        assert_eq!(m["allowed_mentions"], json!({ "parse": [] }));
        assert!(m.get("content").is_none() && m.get("embeds").is_none());
        let c = &m["components"][0];
        assert_eq!((c["type"].clone(), c["accent_color"].clone()), (json!(17), json!(0xE5484D)));
        let parts = c["components"].as_array().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(parts.iter().map(|p| p["type"].as_u64().unwrap()).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [10, 14, 10]);
        assert_eq!(
            parts[0]["content"],
            "### Race ban #57 · \\_\\-EVL\\-\\_GTR\nRaced a car no tuning makes: **SKYLINE**, **2829 kW**, rated 1451, 1338 kg, 381 km/h"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            parts[2]["content"],
            "-# Automatic · lobby sprint, 1st of 4 · 2 weeks, until <t:1794000000:D> · c3058 · out of races now · before as PURE\\_EVL"
        );
        let all = m.to_string();
        assert!(!all.contains("1500") && !all.contains("3000"), "the operator's numbers stay unsaid: {all}");
        // past the rating: that in bold; a circuit's laps; nobody on, no earlier names
        let mut r = car();
        (r.kw, r.rating, r.kind, r.laps, r.place) = (900.0, 3100.0, "circuit".into(), 3, "did not finish".into());
        let m = message(&r, &cars, &made(Some(1_794_000_000_000), 0), "c9", &[]);
        let parts = m["components"][0]["components"].as_array().unwrap().clone();
        assert!(parts[0]["content"].as_str().unwrap().ends_with("**SKYLINE**, 900 kW, **rated 3100**, 1338 kg, 381 km/h"), "{parts:?}");
        assert_eq!(parts[2]["content"], "-# Automatic · lobby circuit of 3 laps, did not finish · 2 weeks, until <t:1794000000:D> · c9");
    }
}

//! The game's files in blocks, compressed: /data-blocks/<path>?b=<first>&n=<count> is blocks first .. first+count-1
//! of a game file (BLOCK bytes each, the last one shorter; BLOCKS_MAX at most) as one 200 answer, compressed with what
//! the client takes (zstd, br or gzip as Content-Encoding, which the browser undoes by itself).  The game data then
//! crosses the network in about 70 % of its size, the tracks in about 40 %.  The page's I/O and predownload workers ask
//! for these when the manifest names them (its "blocks"), and for byte ranges of /data/ otherwise.
//!
//! The compressor streams, so a client that stops reading holds no more than its buffers.  Sent as they are, never
//! queued or refused: a run whose first PROBE bytes do not compress (the movies' VP6 video, most car textures; judged
//! per run, not per file: the music's first megabyte does not compress, the rest does), and an answer while the
//! compressors are taken (per client, per site, in all).  An answer holds its compressor until the client has its
//! last byte, so most of them wait on the network: about 100 players draw some 70 MB/s of game data, dozens of answers
//! under way at once.  The CPU follows the bytes, not the answers (br 3 does 200 MB/s on one core of an M4 Pro), so
//! the total bounds memory: 128 compressors take about 200 MB at most (zstd 1.5 MB each, br 0.9, gzip 0.4).  The
//! compressing itself, chunk by chunk, is on the pool's threads (pool.rs), never on the runtime's workers.
//!
//! A shared cache (Cloudflare's, with a Cache Rule for /data-blocks/*) may keep a run for good (EDGE_KEEP), as the
//! game data is the same for every player: only when its address names this version of the file (m and s, the
//! manifest's mtime and size, so a changed file is a new address) and it is as small as it gets (compressed, or a run
//! that does not compress; not one sent as it is because the compressors were taken).  The movies too.  At about 110
//! players the 1 Gbit uplink was full without it.
//!
//! One block (n=1, all the page asks for) to a client that takes br is better still: the block as kept.rs keeps it,
//! compressed once at brotli's best (or as it is, kept.rs having found it does not compress), with its length.  A
//! block not kept yet is answered as above and queued to be kept; a shared cache may keep that answer EDGE_WHILE
//! only, then asks again and keeps the kept one for good.  The addresses are /data-blocks/v2/ (v2 since blocks are
//! kept, so that no shared cache's copy of an answer from before is ever asked for again).
//!
//! With o and l in place of b and n, the answer is bytes o .. o+l-1 of the file as they are, a 200 with exactly them:
//! the page's HQ vinyls (gpu/hqskin.ts) read a car's pictures that way, ~30 KB each where a block is 1 MiB.  Kept for
//! good by a shared cache on the same terms (the address names this version), so every player after the first gets
//! them from the CDN, under the same Cache Rule.

use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::os::unix::fs::{FileExt, MetadataExt};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicU64, Ordering};

use nfsu2_headers::{Cache, EDGE_KEEP, pick_encoding};
use nfsu2_http::{Request, Response};

use super::files::{self, stream_range};
use super::kept::{self, Kept};
use super::manifest::{BLOCK, BLOCKS_MAX};
use super::url::Url;
use super::{App, Fail, Res, Share, etag, finish, send};

/// the bytes a run is judged by
pub const PROBE: usize = 64 << 10;
pub const COMPRESSORS_PER_CLIENT: usize = 8;
pub const COMPRESSORS_PER_SITE: usize = 16;
pub const COMPRESSORS_TOTAL: usize = 128;
/// the encoders, in the server's order of preference
pub const ENCODERS: [&str; 3] = ["zstd", "br", "gzip"];
/// what one job reads and compresses
const CHUNK: usize = 128 << 10;
/// a block answered before it is kept (compressed as it is sent, or as it is): a shared cache keeps it 10 minutes
pub const EDGE_WHILE: &str = "public, max-age=600";
/// the addresses' own folder since blocks are kept (the manifest's "blocks")
pub const V2: &str = "/v2";

/// The answers of /data-blocks/ since the last look: kept blocks, runs compressed as they are sent (by encoding:
/// zstd, br, gzip), as they are.  The 5-minute line (run.rs) shows whether a CDN in front asks for br (Cloudflare
/// does, from servers that give it): without it no kept block goes out.
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct Sent {
    kept: AtomicU64,
    compressed: [AtomicU64; 3],
    as_is: AtomicU64,
}

impl Sent {
    fn count(c: &AtomicU64) {
        c.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
    }

    /// the counts since the last look ("" when there were none), set back to 0
    pub fn take(&self) -> String {
        let t = |c: &AtomicU64| c.swap(0, Ordering::Relaxed);
        let (kept, z, as_is) = (t(&self.kept), self.compressed.each_ref().map(t), t(&self.as_is));
        if kept + z.iter().sum::<u64>() + as_is == 0 {
            return String::new();
        }
        format!("{kept} kept, compressed as sent {} zstd {} br {} gzip, {as_is} as they are", z[0], z[1], z[2])
    }
}

/// A compressor's state, which moves with its run's jobs from chunk to chunk.  Fast settings, at a fraction of the
/// CPU of the best (zstd 3: about 260 MB/s on one core; br 3, window 2^21; gzip 4): brotli's best is about 8 %
/// smaller for the game data, a fifth for the tracks, which is why kept.rs keeps the blocks that way.
pub enum Encoder {
    Zstd(zstd::stream::write::Encoder<'static, Vec<u8>>),
    Br(Box<brotli::CompressorWriter<Vec<u8>>>),
    Gzip(flate2::write::GzEncoder<Vec<u8>>),
}

impl Encoder {
    pub fn new(name: &str) -> io::Result<Encoder> {
        Ok(match name {
            "zstd" => Encoder::Zstd(zstd::stream::write::Encoder::new(Vec::new(), 3)?),
            "br" => Encoder::Br(Box::new(brotli::CompressorWriter::new(Vec::new(), 64 << 10, 3, 21))),
            // (the header as zlib writes it on a Unix: OS 3)
            _ => Encoder::Gzip(flate2::GzBuilder::new().operating_system(3).write(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::new(4))),
        })
    }
    /// data compressed: what has come out so far
    pub fn push(&mut self, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        match self {
            Encoder::Zstd(e) => {
                e.write_all(data)?;
                Ok(std::mem::take(e.get_mut()))
            }
            Encoder::Br(e) => {
                e.write_all(data)?;
                Ok(std::mem::take(e.get_mut()))
            }
            Encoder::Gzip(e) => {
                e.write_all(data)?;
                Ok(std::mem::take(e.get_mut()))
            }
        }
    }
    /// the end of the stream: the rest
    pub fn finish(self) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>> {
        match self {
            Encoder::Zstd(e) => e.finish(),
            Encoder::Br(e) => Ok(e.into_inner()),
            Encoder::Gzip(e) => e.finish(),
        }
    }
}

/// a query value of 1 to max digits
fn digits(x: &str, max: usize) -> bool {
    !x.is_empty() && x.len() <= max && x.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit())
}

/// whether the address names this version of the file: m and s, the manifest's mtime and size
fn names_version(u: &Url, md: &std::fs::Metadata) -> bool {
    u.param("m").as_deref() == Some(etag::num(etag::mtime_s(md)).as_str())
        && u.param("s").as_deref() == Some(etag::num(md.size() as f64).as_str())
}

/// buf filled from the file at off, as far as the file goes
pub fn read_full_at(f: &std::fs::File, buf: &mut [u8], off: u64) -> io::Result<usize> {
    let mut got = 0;
    while got < buf.len() {
        match f.read_at(&mut buf[got..], off + got as u64) {
            Ok(0) => break,
            Ok(n) => got += n,
            Err(e) if e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => {}
            Err(e) => return Err(e),
        }
    }
    Ok(got)
}

/// whether the bytes from start compress, judged from the first PROBE of them (raw deflate 1: about 0.3 ms)
pub fn compresses(f: &std::fs::File, start: u64, end: u64) -> io::Result<bool> {
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; PROBE.min((end - start) as usize)];
    let got = read_full_at(f, &mut buf, start)?;
    // zlib-rs's level 2 is zlib's level 1 (deflate_fast, 4/4/8/4, Huffman trees made for the data); its own level 1
    // is zlib-ng's "quick" (fixed trees only), which judged 1124 of the game folder's 4067 runs (car textures, vinyls)
    // as not compressing where Node's zlib compresses them.  Level 2 judges one of them otherwise (14 bytes from the
    // threshold).
    let mut z = flate2::write::DeflateEncoder::new(Vec::with_capacity(got + 64), flate2::Compression::new(2));
    z.write_all(&buf[..got])?;
    let z = z.finish()?;
    Ok((z.len() as f64) < got as f64 * 0.97)
}

/// one job's work: the run's next chunk read and compressed
struct Step {
    /// None: the stream is finished
    enc: Option<Encoder>,
    out: Vec<u8>,
    off: u64,
}

fn step(file: &std::fs::File, mut enc: Encoder, off: u64, end: u64) -> io::Result<Step> {
    let want = CHUNK.min((end - off) as usize);
    let mut buf = vec![0u8; want];
    let got = read_full_at(file, &mut buf, off)?;
    let mut out = enc.push(&buf[..got])?;
    let off = off + got as u64;
    // the end of the run (or of a file that came up short)
    if off >= end || got < want {
        out.extend(enc.finish()?);
        return Ok(Step { enc: None, out, off });
    }
    Ok(Step { enc: Some(enc), out, off })
}

impl App {
    /// /data-blocks/: the run of the game file `file` that b and n name (None: 404), compressed or as it is
    pub async fn send_blocks(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, file: Option<String>, u: &Url) -> Res {
        // one open file for the whole answer, its size and version, the probe and the bytes: a file put in place
        // meanwhile is another one, and a run kept for good is the version its address names (opened where it is
        // looked for: one trip to a blocking thread)
        let opened = match file {
            Some(file) => {
                let (roots, state, root) = (self.real_roots.clone(), self.real_state.clone(), self.o.data.clone());
                tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
                    let f = files::locate_sync(&roots, &state, &root, &file)?;
                    let (file, md) = files::open_found(&f.real).ok()?;
                    Some((file, md, f.real))
                })
                .await
                .ok()
                .flatten()
            }
            None => None,
        };
        let Some((file, md, real)) = opened else { return self.not_found(q, s).await };
        if u.param("o").is_some() {
            return self.send_exact(q, s, file, &md, u).await;
        }
        let (b, n) = (u.param("b").unwrap_or_default(), u.param("n").unwrap_or_default());
        if !digits(&b, 7) || !digits(&n, 2) {
            return self.bad_request(q, s).await;
        }
        let (b, n): (u64, u64) = (b.parse().unwrap_or(0), n.parse().unwrap_or(0));
        if !(1..=BLOCKS_MAX).contains(&n) {
            return self.bad_request(q, s).await;
        }
        let file = Arc::new(file);
        let size = md.size();
        let (start, end) = (b * BLOCK, size.min((b + n) * BLOCK));
        if start >= size {
            return self.plain(q, s, 416, "Range not satisfiable", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        let named = names_version(u, &md);
        let accept = q.headers.get("accept-encoding");
        // one block to a client that takes br: as kept.rs keeps it, if it does yet
        let kept = match &self.kept {
            Some(k) if n == 1 && pick_encoding(accept, &["br"]).is_some() => Some(k.clone()),
            _ => None,
        };
        let found = match &kept {
            Some(k) => {
                let (k, key) = (k.clone(), kept::key(&real, &md, b));
                tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || k.lookup(&key)).await.unwrap_or(Kept::No)
            }
            None => Kept::No,
        };
        let found = match found {
            Kept::Br(f, len) => return self.send_kept(q, s, f, len, named).await,
            other => other,
        };
        let (_, key, site) = self.client(q);
        let enc = pick_encoding(accept, &ENCODERS);
        let mut held = match enc {
            Some(_) if q.method != "HEAD" && !matches!(found, Kept::AsIs) => Share::take(&self.compressors, &key, &site),
            _ => None,
        };
        // a run whose probe failed is compressed: never kept as it is
        let as_is = matches!(found, Kept::AsIs)
            || held.is_some() && {
                let f = file.clone();
                !self.pool.submit(move || compresses(&f, start, end).unwrap_or(true)).await.unwrap_or(true)
            };
        if as_is {
            held = None;
        }
        let z = held.is_some();
        // a block that is not kept yet: queued, and its answer now (compressed as it is sent, or as it is where the
        // probe says so) kept by a shared cache for a while only
        let mut kept_soon = false;
        if let Some(k) = &kept
            && matches!(found, Kept::No)
            && k.keeping()
        {
            kept_soon = true;
            if q.method != "HEAD" {
                k.queue(&real, &md, b);
            }
        }
        let keep = (z || as_is) && named;
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/octet-stream");
        h.set("vary", "accept-encoding");
        if keep {
            let v = if kept_soon { EDGE_WHILE } else { EDGE_KEEP };
            h.set("cdn-cache-control", v);
            h.set("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control", v);
        }
        match enc {
            Some(e) if z => {
                h.set("content-encoding", e);
                Sent::count(&self.sent.compressed[ENCODERS.iter().position(|x| *x == e).unwrap_or(0)]);
            }
            _ => {
                h.set("content-length", (end - start).to_string());
                Sent::count(&self.sent.as_is);
            }
        }
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method == "HEAD" {
            return finish(s).await;
        }
        match enc {
            Some(e) if z => self.stream_compressed(s, file, e, start, end).await?,
            _ => stream_range(s, file, start, end).await?,
        }
        // the compressor is given back once the client has the last byte
        let r = finish(s).await;
        drop(held);
        r
    }

    /// `?o=&l=`: the file's bytes o .. o+l-1 (as far as it goes) as they are, at most a run's; kept for good by a
    /// shared cache when the address names this version
    async fn send_exact(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, file: std::fs::File, md: &std::fs::Metadata, u: &Url) -> Res {
        let (o, l) = (u.param("o").unwrap_or_default(), u.param("l").unwrap_or_default());
        if !digits(&o, 12) || !digits(&l, 8) {
            return self.bad_request(q, s).await;
        }
        let (o, l): (u64, u64) = (o.parse().unwrap_or(0), l.parse().unwrap_or(0));
        if !(1..=BLOCK * BLOCKS_MAX).contains(&l) {
            return self.bad_request(q, s).await;
        }
        let size = md.size();
        if o >= size {
            return self.plain(q, s, 416, "Range not satisfiable", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        let end = size.min(o + l);
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/octet-stream");
        if names_version(u, md) {
            h.set("cdn-cache-control", EDGE_KEEP);
            h.set("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control", EDGE_KEEP);
        }
        h.set("content-length", (end - o).to_string());
        Sent::count(&self.sent.as_is);
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            stream_range(s, Arc::new(file), o, end).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }

    /// a kept block: its brotli stream as it is on the disk, with its length (kept for good by a shared cache when
    /// the address names this version)
    async fn send_kept(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, f: std::fs::File, len: u64, named: bool) -> Res {
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/octet-stream");
        h.set("vary", "accept-encoding");
        if named {
            h.set("cdn-cache-control", EDGE_KEEP);
            h.set("cloudflare-cdn-cache-control", EDGE_KEEP);
        }
        h.set("content-encoding", "br");
        h.set("content-length", len.to_string());
        Sent::count(&self.sent.kept);
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            stream_range(s, Arc::new(f), 0, len).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }

    /// the run compressed chunk by chunk on the pool (the encoder made there too), the next chunk compressing while
    /// this one goes out
    async fn stream_compressed(&self, s: &mut Response, file: Arc<std::fs::File>, name: &'static str, start: u64, end: u64) -> Res {
        let job = |enc: Option<Encoder>, off: u64| {
            let f = file.clone();
            self.pool.submit(move || {
                let enc = match enc {
                    Some(e) => e,
                    None => Encoder::new(name)?,
                };
                step(&f, enc, off, end)
            })
        };
        let mut next = Some(job(None, start));
        while let Some(j) = next.take() {
            let Some(Ok(st)) = j.await else {
                // a read or compression error: the answer cannot be finished
                s.destroy();
                return Err(Fail::Gone);
            };
            if let Some(enc) = st.enc {
                next = Some(job(Some(enc), st.off));
            }
            if !st.out.is_empty() {
                send(s, &st.out).await?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Read;

    fn data(n: usize, compressible: bool) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut x = 0x1234_5678_9abc_def0u64;
        (0..n)
            .map(|_| {
                x ^= x << 13;
                x ^= x >> 7;
                x ^= x << 17;
                if compressible { ((x & 3) as u8) * 0x41 } else { x as u8 }
            })
            .collect()
    }

    fn decode(name: &str, z: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        match name {
            "zstd" => out = zstd::stream::decode_all(z).unwrap(),
            "br" => {
                brotli::Decompressor::new(z, 4096).read_to_end(&mut out).unwrap();
            }
            _ => {
                flate2::read::GzDecoder::new(z).read_to_end(&mut out).unwrap();
            }
        }
        out
    }

    // the encoders: the exact bytes back, chunk by chunk, and their parameters
    #[test]
    fn every_encoder_gives_the_bytes_back() {
        let raw = data(3 * CHUNK + 17, true);
        for name in ENCODERS {
            let mut e = Encoder::new(name).unwrap();
            let mut z = Vec::new();
            for c in raw.chunks(CHUNK) {
                z.extend(e.push(c).unwrap());
            }
            z.extend(e.finish().unwrap());
            assert_eq!(decode(name, &z), raw, "{name}");
            assert!(z.len() < raw.len() / 2, "{name}: {} for {}", z.len(), raw.len());
            match name {
                "zstd" => assert_eq!(&z[..4], &[0x28, 0xb5, 0x2f, 0xfd]),
                // WBITS 21: the stream header's first bits 1, then 21 - 17 = 4
                "br" => assert_eq!(z[0] & 0x0f, 1 | (4 << 1)),
                // gzip: deflate, no flags, mtime 0, XFL 0 (level 4), OS 3
                _ => assert_eq!(&z[..10], &[0x1f, 0x8b, 8, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 3]),
            }
        }
    }

    /// a measurement, not a check: each encoder over the first 32 MiB of $NFSU2_BENCH_FILE, chunk by chunk as an
    /// answer compresses it (cargo test --release -- --ignored bench_encoders --nocapture)
    #[test]
    #[ignore]
    fn bench_encoders() {
        let Ok(path) = std::env::var("NFSU2_BENCH_FILE") else { return };
        let mut raw = std::fs::read(&path).unwrap();
        raw.truncate(32 << 20);
        for name in ENCODERS {
            let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
            let mut e = Encoder::new(name).unwrap();
            let mut n = 0;
            for c in raw.chunks(CHUNK) {
                n += e.push(c).unwrap().len();
            }
            n += e.finish().unwrap().len();
            let s = t0.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
            println!(
                "{name}: {:.1} MB -> {:.1} MB ({:.0} %) in {:.0} ms, {:.0} MB/s",
                raw.len() as f64 / 1e6,
                n as f64 / 1e6,
                100.0 * n as f64 / raw.len() as f64,
                s * 1e3,
                raw.len() as f64 / 1e6 / s
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_probe_judges_a_run_by_its_start() {
        let d = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = d.path().join("f");
        let mut b = data(1 << 20, false);
        b.extend(data(1 << 20, true));
        std::fs::write(&p, &b).unwrap();
        let f = std::fs::File::open(&p).unwrap();
        assert!(!compresses(&f, 0, 1 << 20).unwrap(), "random bytes");
        assert!(compresses(&f, 1 << 20, 2 << 20).unwrap(), "bytes of 2 bits");
        assert!(!compresses(&f, 4 << 20, 5 << 20).unwrap(), "past the end: nothing read");
    }

    #[test]
    fn steps_finish_the_stream() {
        let d = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = d.path().join("f");
        let raw = data(CHUNK * 2 + 5, true);
        std::fs::write(&p, &raw).unwrap();
        let f = std::fs::File::open(&p).unwrap();
        let mut z = Vec::new();
        let mut st = step(&f, Encoder::new("gzip").unwrap(), 0, raw.len() as u64).unwrap();
        z.extend(std::mem::take(&mut st.out));
        while let Some(enc) = st.enc.take() {
            st = step(&f, enc, st.off, raw.len() as u64).unwrap();
            z.extend(std::mem::take(&mut st.out));
        }
        assert_eq!(st.off, raw.len() as u64);
        assert_eq!(decode("gzip", &z), raw);
        // a file shorter than the run: the stream ends where the file does
        let mut st = step(&f, Encoder::new("zstd").unwrap(), CHUNK as u64 * 2, CHUNK as u64 * 3).unwrap();
        assert!(st.enc.is_none());
        assert_eq!(decode("zstd", &std::mem::take(&mut st.out)), raw[CHUNK * 2..]);
    }
}

//! The operator's control socket: `control.sock` in the state folder (0600: this server's user, and root), which
//! `nfsu2-server ctl` talks to (src/ctl.rs).  Nothing on the network reaches it.  One request a connection: a line
//! of JSON, the command's words; the answer, {"ok":true|false,"text":...}; then the connection ends.
//!
//!   who [name]                    the players on the switch (address, name, what they do, for how long, and the name
//!                                 over their car when it is another), then the ones who left in the last hour; with
//!                                 a name, only those with a name that has it
//!   kick <player> [message]       the player's page shows the message, and the game goes on without the others
//!                                 (a reload brings it back)
//!   ban <player> <for> [message]  the same, and it is turned away until the ban ends: <for> is 30m, 12h, 3d, 2w or perm
//!   raceban <player> <for> [msg]  it plays on with the others, but races none of them until the ban ends (Online's
//!                                 games, LAN races, free roam's lobby races and outruns): its page says why
//!   rename <player> [message]     its name taken away from everyone (and names that read the same): its page asks for
//!                                 another, and no one plays under it again; of its other names (its page's, the ones
//!                                 over its car) one another keyphrase holds only when named (`App::rename`)
//!   unban <name | #ban>           the bans of that name, or with that number, lifted
//!   change #ban <races|full|for>  a ban made a race ban or a full one, or to last <for> from now on (or both)
//!   bans                          the bans in force: number, name, kind, until when, the message
//!   history <player | #ban>       the player's bans and renames, in force and ended in the last year (nfsu2-bans)

//!                                 setting's name shows only it, with every value
//!
//! A player is a virtual address (10.77.x.y, as `who` and the log show it) or a name (any case): its page's on the
//! switch, or the one its game shows over its car in free roam when that is another (`Who::game`: an edited page
