//! /lan: the WebSocket upgrade to the virtual LAN switch, every check in its order, and every refusal the same raw
//! answer with this server's headers.  A malformed Sec-WebSocket-Protocol is our 400 too (the Node server's ws library
//! refused it with an answer of its own, which had none of the security headers and named the library).

use std::pin::Pin;
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::task::{Context, Poll};
use std::time::Duration;

use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncWrite, AsyncWriteExt, ReadBuf};

use nfsu2_headers::Cache;
use nfsu2_http::{Hold, Request, Response, Upgraded};
use nfsu2_lan::AttachOpts;
use nfsu2_util::{js, log, vip_str};

use super::{App, Res, Share, finish, send, url};

/// One half of a /lan connection, holding the client's share of the /lan budget and the connection's own shares (the
/// per-client connection budget, the listener's count: nfsu2_http::Hold): given back once both halves are gone (the
/// connection closed).
pub struct Held<T> {
    inner: T,
    _share: Arc<(Share, Hold)>,
}

impl<T: AsyncRead + Unpin> AsyncRead for Held<T> {
    fn poll_read(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>, buf: &mut ReadBuf<'_>) -> Poll<std::io::Result<()>> {
        Pin::new(&mut self.get_mut().inner).poll_read(cx, buf)
    }
}

impl<T: AsyncWrite + Unpin> AsyncWrite for Held<T> {
    fn poll_write(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>, buf: &[u8]) -> Poll<std::io::Result<usize>> {
        Pin::new(&mut self.get_mut().inner).poll_write(cx, buf)
    }
    fn poll_write_vectored(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>, bufs: &[std::io::IoSlice<'_>]) -> Poll<std::io::Result<usize>> {
        Pin::new(&mut self.get_mut().inner).poll_write_vectored(cx, bufs)
    }
    fn is_write_vectored(&self) -> bool {
        self.inner.is_write_vectored()
    }
    fn poll_flush(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<std::io::Result<()>> {
        Pin::new(&mut self.get_mut().inner).poll_flush(cx)
    }
    fn poll_shutdown(self: Pin<&mut Self>, cx: &mut Context<'_>) -> Poll<std::io::Result<()>> {
        Pin::new(&mut self.get_mut().inner).poll_shutdown(cx)
    }
}

/// how long the 101 may take to go out: the time any answer has to move (the progress rule's 20 s)
const HANDSHAKE_MOVES: Duration = Duration::from_secs(20);

/// The 101 written, within `within`.  The connection is neither the engine's (its timers stopped at the upgrade) nor
/// the switch's yet (its rules for a client that does not read start once it is attached), so a client that takes
/// nothing (its connection's buffers full of answers it never read) held its /lan share, its connection and the
/// socket here for good.  Node's ws queued the 101 without waiting, and the switch's keepalive cut such a client.
async fn handshake<S: AsyncWrite + Unpin>(stream: &mut S, answer: &[u8], within: Duration) -> bool {
    let write = async {
        stream.write_all(answer).await?;
        stream.flush().await
    };
    matches!(tokio::time::timeout(within, write).await, Ok(Ok(())))
}

/// `/^[+/0-9A-Za-z]{22}==$/`
fn ws_key(k: &str) -> bool {
    let b = k.as_bytes();
    b.len() == 24 && b[..22].iter().all(|&c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'+' || c == b'/') && &b[22..] == b"=="
}

impl App {
    /// GET /lan, no upgrade: what the upgrade's checks of this client would say now, taking nothing, as
    /// {"lan":"ok" | "busy" | "fast" | "page"} (busy: its address holds its share of /lan connections already; fast:
    /// it opens them too fast; page: another site's page).  A browser tells a page nothing of why its WebSocket failed
    /// before it opened (a 429 here and a network that blocks it are the same 1006), so a page whose connection keeps
    /// failing asks (web/src/net/index.ts `check`), says why to the player and writes it in its log.
    pub(crate) async fn send_lan_check(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        let (_, key, site) = self.client(q);
        let v = if !self.own_page(q) {
            "page"
        } else if !self.lan_conns.room(&key, &site) {
            "busy"
        } else if !self.lan_opens.check(&key, &site) {
            "fast"
        } else {
            "ok"
        };
        let body = format!(r#"{{"lan":"{v}"}}"#);
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/json");
        h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            send(s, body.as_bytes()).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }

    /// the raw answer for code, then the connection goes (nfsu2_http::raw_refusal)
    async fn refuse(&self, up: Upgraded, code: u16) {
        nfsu2_http::raw_refusal(up.stream, self.raw_response(code)).await;
    }

    /// An upgrade: the target, the Host, the path, the handshake, the Origin, the client's /lan connections and how
    /// fast it opens them, the subprotocols, in that order; then the 101, and the connection to the switch.
    pub async fn on_upgrade(&self, q: Request, up: Upgraded) {
        let Some(u) = url::parse_target(&q.url) else { return self.refuse(up, 400).await };
        if !self.own_host(&q) {
            return self.refuse(up, 421).await;
        }
        if u.pathname != "/lan" {
            return self.refuse(up, 404).await;
        }
        // a WebSocket handshake, checked here so that every refusal looks the same
        let key = q.headers.get("sec-websocket-key").unwrap_or("");
        let upgrade = q.headers.get("upgrade").is_some_and(|v| v.to_lowercase() == "websocket");
        if q.method != "GET" || !upgrade || q.headers.get("sec-websocket-version") != Some("13") || !ws_key(key) {
            return self.refuse(up, 400).await;
        }
        // only this server's own pages (a page of another site must not join the LAN through a player's browser);
        // clients without an Origin header (tools) may
        if !self.own_page(&q) {
            return self.refuse(up, 403).await;
        }
        // the console names players by their virtual address and nickname, never by their real address (a VPS's
        // journal keeps it); --access-log is the one opt-in that records addresses
        let (_, key_, site) = self.client(&q);
        let Some(share) = Share::take(&self.lan_conns, &key_, &site) else {
            let line = format!("[lan] refused a connection: {} already open from that address", self.lan_conns.held(&key_));
            log::limited("lan", "refused connections", &key_, &line, 2);
            return self.refuse(up, 429).await;
        };
        if !self.lan_opens.take(&key_, &site) {
            log::limited("lan", "refused connections", &key_, "[lan] refused a connection: that address opens them too fast", 2);
            self.refuse(up, 429).await;
            drop(share);
            return;
        }
        // the subprotocols (a malformed list: 400), last, where the Node server's ws library checked them
        let Ok(protocol) = nfsu2_ws::pick_protocol(q.headers.get("sec-websocket-protocol")) else {
            self.refuse(up, 400).await;
            drop(share);
            return;
        };
        let answer = nfsu2_ws::handshake_response(key, protocol.as_deref());
        let Upgraded { mut stream, pre, hold } = up;
        if !handshake(&mut stream, &answer, HANDSHAKE_MOVES).await {
            return;
        }
        if self.lan_sndbuf > 0 {
            let _ = stream.set_send_buffer(self.lan_sndbuf);
        }
        let (r, w) = stream.split();
        let share = Arc::new((share, hold));
        // the operator's bans (control.rs), at its hello: by its page's ids and its keyphrase, and by the address's
        // keyed hash (alone, that keeps it out of races only: a VPN's server is many players')
        let ident = (!key_.is_empty()).then(|| self.bans.addr(&key_));
        let (bans, a, k0, days) = (self.bans.clone(), ident.clone(), key_.clone(), self.days.clone());
        let deny = self.bans.deny();
        let on_hello: nfsu2_lan::OnHello = Box::new(move |h| {
            let now = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
            // a game on the switch: it played today (days.rs), by its page's own id
            if let Some(id) = h.ids.first() {
                days.seen(id, super::days::Seen::Play, now);
            }
            let mut answer = nfsu2_lan::HelloAnswer::default();
            let seen = nfsu2_bans::Seen { pages: &h.ids, owner: h.owner, addr: a.as_deref() };
            let v = bans.by_hello(&seen, now);
            // a full ban: turned away
            if let Some(b) = v.full {
                let by = if b.pages.is_empty() && b.owners.is_empty() { "its address" } else { "its page or keyphrase" };
                let line = format!("[ban] turned away a client of ban #{} \"{}\" ({by})", b.id, b.name);
                log::limited("ban", "turned away", &k0, &line, 2);
                answer.refuse = Some((bytes::Bytes::from(b.message(nfsu2_bans::Match::Own)), nfsu2_lan::CLOSE_BANNED));
                return answer;
            }
            // a name taken away (`rename`): its page asks for another, with the rename's message
            if deny.has(h.name)
                && let Some(d) = bans.denied_as(h.name)
            {
                let msg = bans.record(d.by, now).map(|r| r.ban.msg).unwrap_or_default();
                let line = format!(
                    "[ban] asked a client under \"{}\" for another name (\"{}\": rename #{})",
                    js::printable(h.name, 32),
                    d.name,
                    d.by
                );
                log::limited("ban", "turned away", &k0, &line, 2);
                answer.refuse = Some((bytes::Bytes::from(nfsu2_bans::rename_message(h.name, &msg)), nfsu2_lan::CLOSE_RENAME));
                return answer;
            }
            // a race ban, or someone's ban by the address only: it plays on, out of races
            if let Some((b, m)) = v.races {
                let line = match m {
                    nfsu2_bans::Match::Own => format!("[ban] a client of race ban #{} \"{}\" plays on, out of races", b.id, b.name),
                    nfsu2_bans::Match::Addr => format!(
                        "[ban] a client at an address of {} #{} \"{}\" plays on, out of races (its address only)",
                        b.kind.word(),
                        b.id,
                        b.name
                    ),
                };
                log::limited("ban", "turned away", &k0, &line, 2);
                answer.no_races = Some(bytes::Bytes::from(b.message(m)));
            }
            answer
        });
        // a reconnecting page says ?resume and sends its old address with the token in its first message (nfsu2-lan);
        // the group and site ids stand for the client's address without naming it (the shared limits)
        let (k1, k2) = (key_.clone(), key_.clone());
        let opts = AttachOpts {
            resume: u.has_param("resume"),
            // a page that can wait in line when every place is taken (nfsu2-lan queue.rs)
            queue: u.has_param("queue"),
            group: Some(self.group_id(&key_)),
            site: (!site.is_empty()).then(|| self.group_id(&format!("site {site}"))),
            on_join: Some(Box::new(move |vip, resumed, n| {
                let line = format!("[lan] {} {} ({n} on the switch)", vip_str(vip), if resumed { "is back" } else { "joined" });
                log::limited("lan", "joins and leaves", &k1, &line, 20);
            })),
            on_leave: Some(Box::new(move |vip, name, n| {
                let line = format!("[lan] {} \"{}\" left ({n} on the switch)", vip_str(vip), js::printable(name, 32));
                log::limited("lan", "joins and leaves", &k2, &line, 20);
            })),
            ident,
            refuse: None,
            // the client's country as Cloudflare names it (a trusted proxy's CF-IPCountry): the 5-minute counts of the
            // paths' round trips by country (nfsu2-lan paths.rs), nothing else
            country: nfsu2_headers::client_country(&q, &self.o.trust),
            on_hello: Some(on_hello),
            // the keyphrase the page plays with, for the claimed names (names.rs): its owner, never the token
            on_claim: self.names.as_ref().map(|_| Box::new(nfsu2_claims::owner_of_token) as nfsu2_lan::OnClaim),
        };
        self.lan.attach(Held { inner: r, _share: share.clone() }, Held { inner: w, _share: share }, pre, opts);
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// a /lan upgrade from the address a trusted proxy (this machine) names: the connection and the status it got
    async fn upgrade(kit: &super::super::testkit::Kit, ip: &str) -> (tokio::net::TcpStream, u16) {
        use tokio::io::AsyncReadExt;
        let mut s = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(kit.addr).await.unwrap();
        let req = format!(
            "GET /lan HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nUpgrade: websocket\r\nConnection: Upgrade\r\nX-Forwarded-For: {ip}\r\n\
             Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13\r\nSec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==\r\n\r\n"
        );
        s.write_all(req.as_bytes()).await.unwrap();
        let mut b = [0u8; 64];
        let n = s.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
        let status = std::str::from_utf8(&b[9..12.min(n)]).unwrap_or("0").parse().unwrap_or(0);
        (s, status)
    }

    // GET /lan without an upgrade: what an upgrade from that client would meet now, taking nothing.  Its address
    // holding its 8 connections: "busy" (where its WebSocket gets a 429 that the browser shows its page only as a
    // failed connection), another address "ok", and "ok" again once one of the 8 goes; opening them too fast: "fast";
    // another site's page: "page"
    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
    async fn a_page_can_ask_why_its_connection_fails() {
        let kit = super::super::testkit::Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
        let ask = async |ip: &str, origin: Option<&str>| {
            let mut h = vec![("X-Forwarded-For", ip)];
            h.extend(origin.map(|o| ("Origin", o)));
            let r = kit.get("/lan?check", &h).await;
            assert_eq!((r.status, r.header("content-type")), (200, Some("application/json")));
            assert!(r.header("cache-control").is_some_and(|c| c.contains("no-store")));
            String::from_utf8(r.body).unwrap()
        };
        let (a, b) = ("203.0.113.7", "203.0.113.8");
        assert_eq!(ask(a, None).await, r#"{"lan":"ok"}"#);
        let mut held = Vec::new();
        for _ in 0..super::super::limits::WS_PER_ADDRESS {
            let (s, status) = upgrade(&kit, a).await;
            assert_eq!(status, 101);
            held.push(s);
        }
        let (_, refused) = upgrade(&kit, a).await;
        assert_eq!(refused, 429, "the 9th from that address");
        assert_eq!(ask(a, None).await, r#"{"lan":"busy"}"#);
        assert_eq!(ask(b, None).await, r#"{"lan":"ok"}"#);
        assert_eq!(kit.app.lan_conns.count(), held.len(), "asking took no share");
        drop(held.pop());
        super::super::testkit::eventually("a share back", || kit.app.lan_conns.count() == held.len()).await;
        assert_eq!(ask(a, Some("http://localhost")).await, r#"{"lan":"ok"}"#);
        assert_eq!(ask(a, Some("https://elsewhere.example")).await, r#"{"lan":"page"}"#);
        // more opens than the burst, each closed at once: "fast" until the bucket fills again
        let c = "203.0.113.9";
        for _ in 0..super::super::limits::LAN_OPEN_BURST as usize {
            let (s, status) = upgrade(&kit, c).await;
            assert_eq!(status, 101);
            drop(s);
            super::super::testkit::eventually("its share back", || kit.app.lan_conns.held(c) == 0).await;
        }
        assert_eq!(ask(c, None).await, r#"{"lan":"fast"}"#);
        assert_eq!(upgrade(&kit, c).await.1, 429, "as its upgrade meets it");
    }

    // A client whose connection takes nothing more (its buffers full of answers it never read) when its 101 is due:
    // let go once the time is up, not waited on for good.  One that reads gets it at once.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_handshake_nobody_takes_is_given_up() {
        let l = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
        let client = tokio::net::TcpSocket::new_v4().unwrap();
        client.set_recv_buffer_size(4096).unwrap();
        let client = client.connect(l.local_addr().unwrap()).await.unwrap();
        let (mut server, _) = l.accept().await.unwrap();
        // the send buffer filled while the client reads nothing
        let chunk = vec![0u8; 64 << 10];
        loop {
            match server.try_write(&chunk) {
                Ok(_) => {}
                Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {
                    // (once more after a moment: the kernel moves what it can into the client's window)
                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
                    if server.try_write(&chunk).is_err() {
                        break;
                    }
                }
                Err(e) => panic!("{e}"),
            }
        }
        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
        assert!(!handshake(&mut server, b"HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n\r\n", Duration::from_millis(300)).await);
        assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(2));
        drop(client);
        // and one that reads
        let client = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(l.local_addr().unwrap()).await.unwrap();
        let (mut server, _) = l.accept().await.unwrap();
        assert!(handshake(&mut server, b"HTTP/1.1 101 Switching Protocols\r\n\r\n", Duration::from_millis(300)).await);
        drop(client);
    }

    // Pages through a proxy on this machine (trusted) that names each one's country (Cloudflare's CF-IPCountry): their
    // round trips count under it in the 5-minute lines (nfsu2-lan paths.rs), one named "XX" (no country known) as unknown
    #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)]
    async fn a_page_counts_under_its_country() {
        use futures_util::StreamExt;
        use tokio_tungstenite::tungstenite::client::IntoClientRequest;
        let kit = super::super::testkit::Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
        let mut pages = Vec::new();
        for cc in ["DE", "XX"] {
            let s = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect(kit.addr).await.unwrap();
            let mut q = "ws://localhost/lan".into_client_request().unwrap();
            q.headers_mut().insert("cf-ipcountry", cc.parse().unwrap());
            let (mut ws, _) = tokio_tungstenite::client_async(q, s).await.expect("the handshake");
            // read on: a ping is answered as it is read
            pages.push(tokio::spawn(async move { while let Some(Ok(_)) = ws.next().await {} }));
        }
        // the switch's pings (a page not in free roam is timed every tenth probe)
        let t0 = std::time::Instant::now();
        loop {
            kit.app.lan.probe();
            let l = kit.app.lan.paths().await;
            if l.first().is_some_and(|l| l.contains("all 2 ") && l.contains("; DE 1 ") && l.contains("; unknown 1 ")) {
                assert!(l[1].starts_with("round trips to the server by region: Western Europe 1 "), "{l:?}");
                assert!(l[1].ends_with(&format!("; unknown {}", l[0].rsplit("; unknown ").next().unwrap())), "{l:?}");
                break;
            }
            assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(10), "{l:?}");
            tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20)).await;
        }
        pages.iter().for_each(|p| p.abort());
    }

    #[test]
    fn websocket_keys() {
        assert!(ws_key("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ=="));
        assert!(ws_key("+/+/+/+/+/+/+/+/+/+/+/=="));
        assert!(!ws_key("nope"));
        assert!(!ws_key("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ="));
        assert!(!ws_key("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==x"));
        assert!(!ws_key("dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZ-=="));
    }
}

//! /lastfm: the page scrobbles the songs a player hears in the game (EA Trax's and the Radio's) to their Last.fm
//! profile (web/src/app/lastfm.ts).  Last.fm signs every call with the API account's shared secret, which the repo is
//! public for: it lives in the server's environment and the server signs and forwards the page's calls.  Off unless
//! the server has both: NFSU2_LASTFM_KEY and NFSU2_LASTFM_SECRET (from last.fm/api/account/create); then 404 and
//! the page shows no Last.fm row.  NFSU2_LASTFM_API points the calls elsewhere (the tests' own server, over http://).
//!
//! - `GET /lastfm`: `{"key":<the API key>}`, for the page's link to Last.fm's "allow access" page.
//! - `POST /lastfm` `{"op":"session","token":<what that page gave back>}`: `{"name":<user>,"sk":<session key>}`.
//!   The page keeps the session key (this device only); the server keeps nothing.
//! - `POST /lastfm` `{"op":"playing"|"scrobble","sk":...,"artist":...,"track":...,"album":...,"duration":<s>,
//!   "timestamp":<unix s, scrobble only>}`: `{"ok":true}` (a scrobble Last.fm ignored, a duplicate say: also
//!   "ignored":true).
//!
//! Refusals: 400 `{"error":"invalid"}` (the body), 400 "token" (Last.fm refused the token: old or used), 401 "session"
//! (the session key no longer works: the player took the access back), 429 "rate" (this server's limit, or
//! Last.fm's), 503 "down" (Last.fm did not answer, or said it is offline), 502 "lastfm" with its "code".
//!
//! For this server's own pages only.  Per client (and twice that per site): 30 calls, then one every 10 s.  The
//! console names no player, token or session key.

use std::time::Duration;

use md5::{Digest, Md5};
use nfsu2_headers::Cache;
use nfsu2_http::{Request, Response};
use nfsu2_util::{Rate, log};
use serde_json::{Value, json};

use super::outbound::{Https, form};
use super::{App, Fail, Res, url};

pub const API: &str = "https://ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0/";
const TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);
const BURST: f64 = 30.0;
const PER_SEC: f64 = 0.1;
/// the most of a call's body (three lines of tags and a key)
const MAX_BODY: usize = 4096;
/// the most of one tag, in characters (Last.fm cuts longer ones anyway)
const MAX_TAG: usize = 256;
/// how old a scrobble may be: Last.fm takes two weeks
const MAX_AGE_S: i64 = 14 * 86_400;

pub struct Lastfm {
    /// the API key (public: it is in the link to Last.fm's page)
    pub key: String,
    secret: String,
    api: String,
    https: Https,
    calls: Rate,
}

impl Lastfm {
    /// the API account from the environment (both, or none)
    pub fn from_env() -> Option<Lastfm> {
        let get = |k: &str| std::env::var(k).ok().map(|v| v.trim().to_string()).filter(|v| !v.is_empty());
        let (key, secret) = (get("NFSU2_LASTFM_KEY")?, get("NFSU2_LASTFM_SECRET")?);
        Some(Lastfm::new(key, secret, get("NFSU2_LASTFM_API").unwrap_or_else(|| API.to_string())))
    }

    pub fn new(key: String, secret: String, api: String) -> Lastfm {
        Lastfm { key, secret, api, https: Https::new(), calls: Rate::new(BURST, PER_SEC) }
    }

    pub fn prune(&self) {
        self.calls.prune();
    }

    /// Last.fm's api_sig: every parameter but format, sorted by name, as name then value, the secret after them, MD5
    fn sign(&self, params: &[(&str, String)]) -> String {
        let mut p: Vec<&(&str, String)> = params.iter().filter(|(k, _)| *k != "format" && *k != "callback").collect();
        p.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(b.0));
        let mut h = Md5::new();
        for (k, v) in p {
            h.update(k.as_bytes());
            h.update(v.as_bytes());
        }
        h.update(self.secret.as_bytes());
        h.finalize().iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect()
    }

    /// a signed call (the API key goes in): Last.fm's answer, or Err(an error of ours) when it could not be asked
    async fn call(&self, method: &str, mut params: Vec<(&str, String)>) -> Result<Value, Refused> {
        params.push(("method", method.to_string()));
        params.push(("api_key", self.key.clone()));
        let sig = self.sign(&params);
        params.push(("api_sig", sig));
        params.push(("format", "json".into()));
        let body = params.iter().map(|(k, v)| format!("{k}={}", form(v))).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("&");
        let answer = match tokio::time::timeout(TIMEOUT, self.https.post_form(&self.api, &body)).await {
            Ok(Ok((_, b))) => b,
            Ok(Err(e)) => {
                log::error(&format!("[lastfm] {method}: {e}"));
                return Err(Refused::Down);
            }
            Err(_) => {
                log::error(&format!("[lastfm] {method}: no answer in 10 s"));
                return Err(Refused::Down);
            }
        };
        let v: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&answer).map_err(|_| {
            log::error(&format!("[lastfm] {method}: an answer that is not JSON"));
            Refused::Down
        })?;
        match v.get("error").and_then(Value::as_i64) {
            None => Ok(v),
            Some(code) => {
                let r = Refused::of(code);
                if matches!(r, Refused::Other(_) | Refused::Down) {
                    log::error(&format!("[lastfm] {method}: error {code}"));
                }
                Err(r)
            }
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq)]
enum Refused {
    Token,
    Session,
    Rate,
    Down,
    Other(i64),
}

impl Refused {
    /// Last.fm's error codes (last.fm/api/errorcodes)
    fn of(code: i64) -> Refused {
        match code {
            4 | 14 | 15 => Refused::Token,
            9 => Refused::Session,
            29 => Refused::Rate,
            11 | 16 => Refused::Down,
            c => Refused::Other(c),
        }
    }
    fn answer(&self) -> (u16, Value) {
        match self {
            Refused::Token => (400, json!({ "error": "token" })),
            Refused::Session => (401, json!({ "error": "session" })),
            Refused::Rate => (429, json!({ "error": "rate" })),
            Refused::Down => (503, json!({ "error": "down" })),
            Refused::Other(c) => (502, json!({ "error": "lastfm", "code": c })),
        }
    }
}

/// a key or token as Last.fm makes them: letters, digits, - and _ (a token has them now and then)
fn key_like(v: Option<&Value>) -> Option<String> {
    let s = v?.as_str()?;
    let ok = |c: u8| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'-' || c == b'_';
    (!s.is_empty() && s.len() <= 128 && s.bytes().all(ok)).then(|| s.to_string())
}

/// a tag: trimmed, without control characters, at most MAX_TAG characters; None when it is empty and must not be
fn tag(v: Option<&Value>, needed: bool) -> Option<Option<String>> {
    let s: String = v.and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").chars().filter(|c| !c.is_control()).collect();
    let s = s.trim();
    if s.chars().count() > MAX_TAG || (needed && s.is_empty()) {
        return None;
    }
    Some((!s.is_empty()).then(|| s.to_string()))
}

/// the call a page's body asks for: Last.fm's method and its parameters (but the API key's), or None: not valid
fn call_of(b: &Value, now_s: i64) -> Option<(&'static str, Vec<(&'static str, String)>)> {
    let op = b.get("op")?.as_str()?;
    if op == "session" {
        return Some(("auth.getSession", vec![("token", key_like(b.get("token"))?)]));
    }
    let method = match op {
        "playing" => "track.updateNowPlaying",
        "scrobble" => "track.scrobble",
        _ => return None,
    };
    let mut p = vec![("sk", key_like(b.get("sk"))?), ("artist", tag(b.get("artist"), true)??), ("track", tag(b.get("track"), true)??)];
    if let Some(album) = tag(b.get("album"), false)? {
        p.push(("album", album));
    }
    if let Some(d) = b.get("duration").filter(|d| !d.is_null()) {
        let d = d.as_i64().filter(|d| (1..=3600).contains(d))?;
        p.push(("duration", d.to_string()));
    }
    if method == "track.scrobble" {
        let t = b.get("timestamp")?.as_i64().filter(|t| *t > now_s - MAX_AGE_S && *t <= now_s + 60)?;
        p.push(("timestamp", t.to_string()));
    }
    Some((method, p))
}

impl App {
    pub(super) async fn lastfm(&self, q: &mut Request, s: &mut Response, _u: &url::Url) -> Res {
        let Some(l) = &self.lastfm else { return self.not_found(q, s).await };
        // only this server's own pages: another site must not scrobble through a player's browser
        let site_ok = q.headers.get("sec-fetch-site").is_none_or(|f| f == "same-origin");
        if !self.own_page(q) || !site_ok {
            return self.plain(q, s, 403, "Forbidden", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        match q.method.as_str() {
            "GET" | "HEAD" => self.json(q, s, 200, &json!({ "key": l.key })).await,
            "POST" => {
                let (_, key, site) = self.client(q);
                if !l.calls.take(&key, &site) {
                    return self.json(q, s, 429, &json!({ "error": "rate" })).await;
                }
                let body = match q.read_body(MAX_BODY).await {
                    Ok(b) => b,
                    Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::TooLarge) => return self.json(q, s, 413, &json!({ "error": "large" })).await,
                    Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::Broken) => {
                        s.destroy();
                        return Err(Fail::Gone);
                    }
                };
                let now_s = nfsu2_util::now_ms() as i64 / 1000;
                let Some((method, params)) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&body).ok().and_then(|b| call_of(&b, now_s)) else {
                    return self.json(q, s, 400, &json!({ "error": "invalid" })).await;
                };
                let (code, v) = match l.call(method, params).await {
                    Err(r) => r.answer(),
                    Ok(a) if method == "auth.getSession" => {
                        let session = a.get("session");
                        let (name, sk) = (session.and_then(|x| x.get("name")), session.and_then(|x| x.get("key")));
                        match (name.and_then(Value::as_str), key_like(sk)) {
                            (Some(n), Some(k)) => (200, json!({ "name": n, "sk": k })),
                            _ => Refused::Down.answer(),
                        }
                    }
                    Ok(a) => {
                        let ignored = a.pointer("/scrobbles/@attr/ignored").and_then(|i| i.as_i64().or_else(|| i.as_str()?.parse().ok()));
                        if ignored.is_some_and(|i| i > 0) {
                            (200, json!({ "ok": true, "ignored": true }))
                        } else {
                            (200, json!({ "ok": true }))
                        }
                    }
                };
                self.json(q, s, code, &v).await
            }
            _ => {
                self.plain(q, s, 405, "Method not allowed", &[("allow", "GET, HEAD, POST"), ("connection", "close")], Cache::Store, true)
                    .await
            }
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};

    /// a server that answers one request with `answer`, and what it was asked
    async fn fake(answer: &'static str) -> (String, tokio::task::JoinHandle<String>) {
        let l = tokio::net::TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:0").await.unwrap();
        let url = format!("http://{}/2.0/", l.local_addr().unwrap());
        let h = tokio::spawn(async move {
            let (mut s, _) = l.accept().await.unwrap();
            let mut got = Vec::new();
            let mut b = [0u8; 4096];
            while !String::from_utf8_lossy(&got).contains("format=json") {
                let n = s.read(&mut b).await.unwrap();
                got.extend_from_slice(&b[..n]);
            }
            s.write_all(answer.as_bytes()).await.unwrap();
            String::from_utf8_lossy(&got).into_owned()
        });
        (url, h)
    }

    #[test]
    fn signs_as_lastfm_does() {
        let l = Lastfm::new("k".into(), "secret".into(), API.into());
        // md5("api_keykmethodauth.getSessiontokentsecret"), the parameters sorted, format left out
        let p = vec![("token", "t".to_string()), ("method", "auth.getSession".into()), ("api_key", "k".into()), ("format", "json".into())];
        let want: String = Md5::digest(b"api_keykmethodauth.getSessiontokentsecret").iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
        assert_eq!(l.sign(&p), want);
    }

    #[test]
    fn checks_what_the_page_asks() {
        let now = 1_800_000_000;
        let ok = json!({ "op": "scrobble", "sk": "abc123", "artist": " Snoop Dogg ", "track": "Riders on the Storm", "album": "", "duration": 230, "timestamp": now - 100 });
        let (m, p) = call_of(&ok, now).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(m, "track.scrobble");
        assert_eq!(p.iter().find(|(k, _)| *k == "artist").unwrap().1, "Snoop Dogg");
        assert!(p.iter().all(|(k, _)| *k != "album"), "an empty album is left out");
        assert_eq!(call_of(&json!({ "op": "session", "token": "abc" }), now).unwrap().0, "auth.getSession");
        // a token as Last.fm gives them, with - and _
        assert_eq!(call_of(&json!({ "op": "session", "token": "Ab-3_x9Kq" }), now).unwrap().1, vec![("token", "Ab-3_x9Kq".to_string())]);
        for bad in [
            json!({ "op": "scrobble", "sk": "abc", "artist": "a", "track": "t" }), // no timestamp
            json!({ "op": "scrobble", "sk": "abc", "artist": "a", "track": "t", "timestamp": now - MAX_AGE_S - 1 }),
            json!({ "op": "playing", "sk": "a&b", "artist": "a", "track": "t" }),
            json!({ "op": "playing", "sk": "abc", "artist": "", "track": "t" }),
            json!({ "op": "playing", "sk": "abc", "artist": "a", "track": "t".repeat(MAX_TAG + 1) }),
            json!({ "op": "playing", "sk": "abc", "artist": "a", "track": "t", "duration": 0 }),
            json!({ "op": "love", "sk": "abc" }),
            json!({ "op": "session", "token": "" }),
        ] {
            assert!(call_of(&bad, now).is_none(), "{bad}");
        }
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn asks_lastfm_and_reads_its_answers() {
        let (url, h) = fake("HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n{\"session\":{\"name\":\"someone\",\"key\":\"SK1\",\"subscriber\":0}}").await;
        let l = Lastfm::new("KEY".into(), "s".into(), url);
        let a = l.call("auth.getSession", vec![("token", "TOK".into())]).await.unwrap();
        assert_eq!(a.pointer("/session/key").and_then(Value::as_str), Some("SK1"));
        let asked = h.await.unwrap();
        assert!(asked.starts_with("POST /2.0/ HTTP/1.1\r\n"), "{asked}");
        assert!(asked.contains("token=TOK&method=auth.getSession&api_key=KEY&api_sig="), "{asked}");
        assert!(!asked.contains("secret"), "{asked}");
        // Last.fm's errors come with 4xx statuses and a JSON body
        let (url, _) =
            fake("HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n{\"error\":9,\"message\":\"Invalid session key\"}").await;
        let l = Lastfm::new("KEY".into(), "s".into(), url);
        assert_eq!(l.call("track.scrobble", vec![]).await.unwrap_err(), Refused::Session);
        let (url, _) = fake("HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\r\n\r\n<html>").await;
        let l = Lastfm::new("KEY".into(), "s".into(), url);
        assert_eq!(l.call("track.scrobble", vec![]).await.unwrap_err(), Refused::Down);
    }
}

//! The install folder's manifest (/data-manifest): the files the game reads, with size and time, walked once and
//! again when a page asks (?refresh), at most every 10 s.
//!
//! Only what the game reads: its program, the LAN server module and its settings, and its data folders, compared
//! case-insensitively.  The rest of an install folder never leaves this machine: an installer's uninstall log
//! (unins000.dat names the PC, the Windows account and when it was installed), a SAVE folder that a widescreen fix
//! writes the player's profiles into, mod plugins and their settings, backups, notes (the audit's PRIV-1).  Dot files
//! are never served either, symbolic links are left out (nothing outside the folder is ever served), and the state
//! folder (keys) is skipped wherever it is (a second guard: the start refuses one inside the folder).

use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
use std::sync::Arc;

use bytes::Bytes;
use futures_util::FutureExt;
use futures_util::future::{BoxFuture, Shared};
use parking_lot::Mutex;
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

use nfsu2_util::json::write_str;

use super::blocks::V2;
use super::etag;
use crate::options::within;

/// what /data/ and /data-blocks/ serve: the top-level entries of the install folder that are the game's
pub const GAME_ENTRIES: [&str; 21] = [
    "speed2.exe",
    "server.dll",
    "server.cfg",
    "cars",
    "credits",
    "frontend",
    "global",
    "hqvinyls",  // the HQ vinyls' pictures (tools/hqvinyls.py), if the folder has them
    "langpacks", // the language packs (tools/langpacks.py), if the folder has them
    "languages",
    "memcard",
    "modpacks", // what community mods add, for everyone (tools/modpacks.py), if the folder has it
    "movies",
    "nis",
    "pfdata",
    "sound",
    "speech",
    "subtitles",
    "texpacks", // the texture packs (tools/texpacks.py), if the folder has them
    "tracks",
    "vinylpacks", // the Japanese release's vinyls (tools/vinylpacks.py), if the folder has them
];

/// the blocks of /data-blocks/: 1 MiB each, at most 8 in one answer
pub const BLOCK: u64 = 1 << 20;
pub const BLOCKS_MAX: u64 = 8;

/// a top-level name of the game's, compared in lower case (Unicode's, as JS's toLowerCase: the Kelvin sign is "k")
pub fn game_entry(name: &str) -> bool {
    let n = name.to_lowercase();
    GAME_ENTRIES.contains(&n.as_str())
}

pub struct Manifest {
    pub body: Bytes,
    pub gz: Bytes,
    pub etag: String,
    /// entries (folders and files)
    pub count: usize,
    /// when it was made (ms since the epoch)
    pub at: i64,
    /// the files' paths in the folder (kept.rs keeps their blocks)
    pub files: Vec<String>,
}

/// one entry of the walk, in the order Node's readdir gives them (libuv's scandir: sorted by byte)
fn entries(dir: &str) -> io::Result<Vec<(String, std::fs::FileType)>> {
    let mut v: Vec<(Vec<u8>, String, std::fs::FileType)> = Vec::new();
    for e in std::fs::read_dir(dir)? {
        let e = e?;
        let name = e.file_name();
        let t = e.file_type()?;
        v.push((name.as_bytes().to_vec(), name.to_string_lossy().into_owned(), t));
    }
    v.sort_by(|a, b| a.0.cmp(&b.0));
    Ok(v.into_iter().map(|(_, n, t)| (n, t)).collect())
}

fn walk(dir: &str, rel: &str, real_state: &str, out: &mut String, count: &mut usize, files: &mut Vec<String>) -> io::Result<()> {
    for (name, t) in entries(dir)? {
        if name.starts_with('.') || (rel.is_empty() && !game_entry(&name)) {
            continue;
        }
        let abs = format!("{dir}/{name}");
        let r = if rel.is_empty() { name.clone() } else { format!("{rel}/{name}") };
        if t.is_dir() {
            let real = std::fs::canonicalize(&abs).map(|p| p.to_string_lossy().into_owned()).unwrap_or_else(|_| abs.clone());
            if within(&real, real_state) {
                continue;
            }
            if *count > 0 {
                out.push(',');
            }
            out.push_str("{\"p\":");
            write_str(out, &r);
            out.push_str(",\"d\":1}");
            *count += 1;
            walk(&abs, &r, real_state, out, count, files)?;
        } else if t.is_file() {
            let md = std::fs::metadata(&abs)?;
            if *count > 0 {
                out.push(',');
            }
            out.push_str("{\"p\":");
            write_str(out, &r);
            out.push_str(",\"s\":");
            out.push_str(&etag::num(md.size() as f64));
            out.push_str(",\"m\":");
            out.push_str(&etag::num(etag::mtime_s(&md)));
            out.push('}');
            *count += 1;
            files.push(r);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

type Walk = Shared<BoxFuture<'static, Result<Arc<Manifest>, String>>>;

/// The manifest made last, and the walk under way: one walk at a time for everyone who asks meanwhile, on a task of
/// its own, so that its manifest is kept whoever is still there to take it.
/// (A walk that was the request's own went with a request that reset: the next ?refresh walked again, and a client
/// that asked and reset at once kept as many walks going as it liked.)
#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ManifestCell {
    cur: Mutex<Option<Arc<Manifest>>>,
    walk: Mutex<Option<Walk>>,
    /// told of each manifest a walk makes (the kept blocks' sweep)
    on_new: Mutex<Option<OnNew>>,
}

type OnNew = Arc<dyn Fn(&Manifest) + Send + Sync>;

impl ManifestCell {
    /// f told of each manifest a walk makes from now on
    pub fn on_new(&self, f: OnNew) {
        *self.on_new.lock() = Some(f);
    }

    pub fn current(&self) -> Option<Arc<Manifest>> {
        self.cur.lock().clone()
    }

    /// the walk under way, or a new one (on the runtime: the walk is a task of its own)
    pub fn refresh(self: &Arc<Self>, data: &str, real_state: &str, key: &[u8]) -> Walk {
        let mut walk = self.walk.lock();
        if let Some(w) = walk.as_ref() {
            return w.clone();
        }
        let (cell, data, state, key) = (self.clone(), data.to_string(), real_state.to_string(), key.to_vec());
        let task = tokio::spawn(async move {
            let r = match tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || build(&data, &state, &key)).await {
                Ok(Ok(m)) => Ok(Arc::new(m)),
                Ok(Err(e)) => Err(e.to_string()),
                Err(e) => Err(e.to_string()),
            };
            if let Ok(m) = &r {
                *cell.cur.lock() = Some(m.clone());
                let f = cell.on_new.lock().clone();
                if let Some(f) = f {
                    f(m);
                }
            }
            // (after the manifest is in place: a request that comes between finds the new one, or joins this walk)
            *cell.walk.lock() = None;
            r
        });
        let w = async move { task.await.unwrap_or_else(|e| Err(e.to_string())) }.boxed().shared();
        *walk = Some(w.clone());
        w
    }
}

/// the manifest of the install folder (blocking: on a blocking thread)
pub fn build(data: &str, real_state: &str, key: &[u8]) -> io::Result<Manifest> {
    let mut body = String::from("{\"v\":1,\"files\":[");
    let (mut count, mut files) = (0, Vec::new());
    walk(data, "", real_state, &mut body, &mut count, &mut files)?;
    body.push_str(&format!("],\"blocks\":{{\"url\":\"/data-blocks{V2}/\",\"size\":{BLOCK},\"max\":{BLOCKS_MAX}}}}}"));
    let mut gz = flate2::GzBuilder::new().operating_system(3).write(Vec::new(), flate2::Compression::default());
    gz.write_all(body.as_bytes())?;
    let gz = gz.finish()?;
    let hex: String = Sha256::digest(body.as_bytes()).iter().map(|b| format!("{b:02x}")).collect();
    Ok(Manifest {
        etag: etag::etag_of(key, &["manifest", &hex]),
        body: Bytes::from(body),
        gz: Bytes::from(gz),
        count,
        at: nfsu2_util::now_ms(),
        files,
    })
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::app::etag::tests::set_mtime;

    /// whether the file system of `dir` takes "a" and "A" for one name
    fn case_blind(dir: &std::path::Path) -> bool {
        let probe = dir.join("case-probe");
        std::fs::write(&probe, "").unwrap();
        let blind = dir.join("CASE-PROBE").exists();
        std::fs::remove_file(probe).unwrap();
        blind
    }

    /// a made-up install folder: the game's entries, and what is never listed
    fn folder() -> tempfile::TempDir {
        let d = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
        let p = |r: &str| d.path().join(r);
        std::fs::write(p("SPEED2.EXE"), "MZ fake").unwrap();
        for dir in ["GLOBAL", "TRACKS/sub", "SAVE", "scripts", "Movies"] {
            std::fs::create_dir_all(p(dir)).unwrap();
        }
        std::fs::write(p("GLOBAL/Game.txt"), "inside").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(p("GLOBAL/b.bin"), [0u8; 1000]).unwrap();
        // (a name that differs in case alone: not on a file system that ignores case, as macOS's does by default,
        // where it would be b.bin written again)
        if !case_blind(d.path()) {
            std::fs::write(p("GLOBAL/B.bin"), [0u8; 10]).unwrap();
        }
        std::fs::write(p("GLOBAL/_x"), "x").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(p("GLOBAL/\u{e9}t\u{e9}"), "\u{e9}").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(p("GLOBAL/a\"q.txt"), "q").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(p("GLOBAL/.hidden"), "SECRET").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(p(".hidden"), "SECRET").unwrap();
        std::fs::write(p("TRACKS/sub/L4RA.BUN"), [1u8; 3000]).unwrap();
        std::fs::write(p("Movies/INTRO.VP6"), [2u8; 50]).unwrap();

    }

    #[test]
    fn only_the_games_entries_in_byte_order() {

            "TRACKS",

import fsp from 'node:fs/promises'; import path from 'node:path';
const GAME_ENTRIES = ['speed2.exe', 'server.dll', 'server.cfg',
  'cars', 'credits', 'frontend', 'global', 'langpacks', 'languages', 'memcard', 'movies', 'nis', 'pfdata', 'sound', 'speech', 'subtitles', 'tracks'];
const GAME_TOP = new Set(GAME_ENTRIES);
const gameEntry = name => GAME_TOP.has(name.toLowerCase());
const within = (a, b) => { const x = a.toLowerCase(), y = b.toLowerCase(); return x === y || x.startsWith(y.endsWith(path.sep) ? y : y + path.sep); };

async function walk(dir, rel) {

    if (e.name.startsWith('.') || (!rel && !gameEntry(e.name))) continue;
    const abs = path.join(dir, e.name), r = rel ? rel + '/' + e.name : e.name;
    if (e.isDirectory() && within(await fsp.realpath(abs).catch(() => abs), REAL_STATE)) continue;
    if (e.isDirectory()) { files.push({ p: r, d: 1 }); await walk(abs, r); }
    else if (e.isFile()) { const st = await fsp.stat(abs); files.push({ p: r, s: st.size, m: Math.floor(st.mtimeMs / 1000) }); }
  }
}
await walk(DATA, '');
process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({ v: 1, files, blocks: { url: '/data-blocks/v2/', size: BLOCK, max: BLOCKS_MAX } }));
"#;
        let out = std::process::Command::new("node").args(["--input-type=module", "-e", script]).env("NFSU2_TEST_DATA", &root).output();
        match out {
            Ok(o) if o.status.success() => assert_eq!(String::from_utf8_lossy(&o.stdout), String::from_utf8_lossy(&m.body)),
            _ => eprintln!("no node: the cross-check of the manifest is skipped"),
        }
    }
}

//! The routes and rules: the files, the game data in blocks, the module, /players, /lan's handshake, the per-client
//! budgets, and the answers every response carries.
//!
//! There is no access control: whoever can reach the server may play, and the firewall in front of it decides who
//! that is.  What the server does instead is say nothing about the machine (no host name, addresses, paths, versions
//! or stack traces in any response; plain 4xx/5xx), keep every peer's real address to itself (nfsu2-lan), send
//! security headers on every response, keep shared caches (a CDN such as Cloudflare) from storing anything, and limit
//! what one client can make it do.  It answers only for its own names (the Host check): a page of another site that
//! points its own name at this machine (DNS rebinding) gets nothing, and neither does a scanner that connects to the
//! bare address.  The console is the operator's own: it may name paths, but it names players only by their virtual
//! address and nickname, never by their real address (--access-log is the one opt-in that records client addresses).
