/// What one client may hold and do (one connection's limits: nfsu2_http::Limits).  "Per client" is per client
/// address: an IPv4 address or an IPv6 /56 (nfsu2_headers::address_key); "per site" is per IPv6 /48 (site_key: one
/// site, or one free tunnel-broker allocation, which holds 256 /56s and would otherwise be 256 budgets for one client:
/// the review of the audit's F3).
pub mod limits {
    /// connections at once per client and per site, TCP peers that are not trusted proxies only: Chrome opens at
    /// most 6 per server and a WebSocket, so this leaves room for a household of players behind one address, and
    /// one client cannot take them all
    pub const CONNS_PER_ADDRESS: usize = 64;
    pub const CONNS_PER_SITE: usize = 128;
    /// requests in progress at once per client and per site, counted by the client's own address also when a proxy
    /// carries it (a proxy opens one connection here per request in progress, so without this one client behind
    /// Caddy or a tunnel could hold all of them: the audit's F3).  The page's I/O worker keeps at most 8 block
    /// requests in flight.  More gets 429.
    pub const REQUESTS_PER_CLIENT: usize = 64;
    pub const REQUESTS_PER_SITE: usize = 128;
    /// the last part of the connections (and of the requests in progress) is only for a client that holds none yet:
    /// clients that already hold some can never lock a newcomer out
    pub const FREE_SHARE: f64 = 0.25;
    /// idle keep-alive connections: longer for Cloudflare's own connections when its proxy connects here
    /// (--trusted-proxies cloudflare: it reuses an origin connection for up to 900 s and fails a request on one the
    /// origin has just closed)
    pub const KEEP_ALIVE_S: u64 = 65;
    pub const KEEP_ALIVE_CLOUDFLARE_S: u64 = 905;
    /// /lan connections at once per client, and per site
    pub const WS_PER_ADDRESS: usize = 8;
    pub const WS_PER_SITE: usize = 16;
    /// opening /lan: a burst, then this many a second, per client (twice that per site).  A page reconnects at most
    /// every 250 ms, backing off to every 5 s; a client that opens and closes connections as fast as it can gets 429
    /// (the review of the audit's F1: churning connections)
    pub const LAN_OPEN_BURST: f64 = 20.0;
    pub const LAN_OPEN_RATE: f64 = 1.0;
    /// one WebSocket message (the switch drops frames over 8 KB)
    pub const WS_MAX_PAYLOAD: usize = 64 << 10;
    pub const ARTIFACT_BYTES: usize = 64 << 20;
    /// each player holds at most 6 HTTP connections and a WebSocket, so with many players (a VPS with --max-peers
    /// 6000) the port takes 8 per player
    pub fn max_connections(max_peers: usize) -> usize {
        1024.max(max_peers * 8)
    }
}

/// What a route ended with: the answer was written to its end, the connection went first (nothing to log), or a
/// server error (the details go to this console, the client gets a plain 500).
pub enum Fail {
    Gone,
    Error(String),
}
pub type Res = Result<(), Fail>;

pub(crate) async fn send(s: &mut Response, b: &[u8]) -> Res {
    s.write(b).await.map_err(|_| Fail::Gone)
}
pub(crate) async fn finish(s: &mut Response) -> Res {
    s.end().await.map_err(|_| Fail::Gone)
}

/// A response's headers in the order they were first given (the security headers, the cache headers, then the
/// route's own): a name that is there already keeps its place and takes the new value.
pub struct Hdrs(pub Vec<(String, String)>);

impl Hdrs {
    pub fn set(&mut self, k: &str, v: impl Into<String>) {
        match self.0.iter_mut().find(|(n, _)| n == k) {
            Some(e) => e.1 = v.into(),
            None => self.0.push((k.to_string(), v.into())),
        }
    }
}

/// A share of a budget, given back when it is dropped (the answer is finished, the connection closed).
pub struct Share {
    b: Arc<Budget>,
    key: String,
    site: String,
}

impl Share {
    pub fn take(b: &Arc<Budget>, key: &str, site: &str) -> Option<Share> {
        b.take(key, site).then(|| Share { b: b.clone(), key: key.to_string(), site: site.to_string() })
    }
}

impl Drop for Share {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.b.give(&self.key, &self.site);
    }
}

/// a status line's text, for the answers written on the raw connection
const STATUS: [(u16, &str); 8] = [
    (400, "Bad Request"),
    (403, "Forbidden"),
    (404, "Not Found"),
    (408, "Request Timeout"),
    (421, "Misdirected Request"),
    (429, "Too Many Requests"),
    (431, "Request Header Fields Too Large"),
    (503, "Service Unavailable"),
];

/// /players' `rooms`: at most this many asked at once (the main world, World 1 to 4, a world of the player's own, and
/// room to spare)
const ROOMS_ASKED: usize = 8;
/// /players' `spots`: at most this many (a world's race tracks' spots, nfsu2_roam::TRACK_KEYS, and room to spare)
const SPOTS_ASKED: usize = 16;
pub const ROBOTS_TXT: &str = "User-agent: *\nAllow: /\nDisallow: /data/\nDisallow: /data-manifest\nDisallow: /game.wasm\nDisallow: /game.json\nDisallow: /players\nDisallow: /seen\nDisallow: /lan\nDisallow: /vault\nDisallow: /names\nDisallow: /friends";

/// what a client may ask a file to be sent as
const TYPES: [(&str, &str); 11] = [
    (".html", "text/html; charset=utf-8"),
    (".js", "text/javascript; charset=utf-8"),
    (".mjs", "text/javascript; charset=utf-8"),
    (".css", "text/css; charset=utf-8"),
    (".wasm", "application/wasm"),
    (".json", "application/json"),
    (".svg", "image/svg+xml"),
    (".png", "image/png"),
    (".ico", "image/x-icon"),
    (".txt", "text/plain; charset=utf-8"),
    (".map", "application/json"),
];

pub fn type_of(ext: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    TYPES.iter().find(|(e, _)| *e == ext).map(|(_, t)| *t)
}

/// `/\bword\b/.test(s)`: word as a whole word (JS \w: ASCII letters, digits and "_")
pub fn has_word(s: &str, word: &str) -> bool {
    let w = |c: u8| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'_';
    let b = s.as_bytes();
    let mut from = 0;
    while let Some(i) = s[from..].find(word) {
        let at = from + i;
        let end = at + word.len();
        if (at == 0 || !w(b[at - 1])) && (end == b.len() || !w(b[end])) {
            return true;
        }
        from = at + 1;
    }
    false
}

/// a header that is there and not empty (an empty one counts as none)
fn present(q: &Request, name: &str) -> bool {
    q.headers.get(name).is_some_and(|v| !v.is_empty())
}

pub struct App {
    pub o: Options,
    pub host_check: HostCheck,
    /// the state folder's real path (never served: locate() and the manifest skip it)
    pub real_state: String,
    pub etag_key: Vec<u8>,
    /// the key of the /lan group ids (random each start: they stand for a client address without naming it)
    group_key: Vec<u8>,
    /// the security and cache headers, made once: [hsts][noindex][cache]
    base: Vec<Vec<(String, String)>>,
    /// the raw answers (refused upgrades, requests the engine cannot read), made once
    raw: HashMap<u16, Vec<u8>>,
    /// requests in progress per client and site (REQUESTS_PER_CLIENT, REQUESTS_PER_SITE), of max_connections in all
    pub requests: Arc<Budget>,
    pub conns: Arc<Budget>,
    pub lan_conns: Arc<Budget>,
    pub lan_opens: Rate,
    pub compressors: Arc<Budget>,
    manifest: Arc<manifest::ManifestCell>,
    wasm: wasm::WasmCell,
    real_roots: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, String>>>,
    pool: Arc<pool::CpuPool>,
    /// the game data's blocks at brotli's best (kept.rs), none with NFSU2_COMPRESS_THREADS=0
    kept: Option<Arc<kept::KeptBlocks>>,
    /// the /data-blocks/ answers since the 5-minute line
    sent: blocks::Sent,
    pub lan: Arc<LanSwitch>,
    pub online: Option<Arc<OnlineHost>>,
    /// free roam's hub (its `crowded()` and `in_roam()` for /players), none with --roam-hub off
    pub roam: Option<Arc<nfsu2_roam::RoamHub>>,
    /// keyphrase saves (/vault), none with --vault-gb 0
    pub vault: Option<vault::VaultRoute>,
    /// claimed names (/names), none without keyphrase saves
    pub names: Option<names::NamesRoute>,
    /// Last.fm scrobbles (/lastfm), none without the API account's key and secret
    pub lastfm: Option<lastfm::Lastfm>,
    /// free roam's friends (/friends and the pages' friend messages), none without the Online host, the hub or names
    pub friends: Option<Arc<friends::Friends>>,
    /// the operator's bans (the control socket: control.rs), checked at /lan
    pub bans: Arc<nfsu2_bans::Bans>,
    /// how many come each day (days.rs: /seen, the hellos, the sweep)
    pub days: Arc<days::Days>,
    /// SO_SNDBUF for /lan connections (NFSU2_LAN_SNDBUF, a measurement knob; 0: the kernel's own, which Linux grows
    /// to megabytes, ahead of the switch's own queue rules)
    lan_sndbuf: usize,
}

fn cache_index(c: Cache) -> usize {
    match c {
        Cache::Store => 0,
        Cache::Revalidate => 1,
        Cache::Immutable => 2,
    }
}

impl App {
    pub fn new(
        o: Options,
        real_state: String,
        etag_key: Vec<u8>,
        lan: Arc<LanSwitch>,
        online: Option<Arc<OnlineHost>>,
        roam: Option<Arc<nfsu2_roam::RoamHub>>,
        vault: Option<Arc<nfsu2_vault::Vault>>,
        names: Option<names::NamesRoute>,
        bans: Arc<nfsu2_bans::Bans>,
        days: Arc<days::Days>,
        pool_threads: usize,
        lan_sndbuf: usize,
        compress_threads: usize,
    ) -> App {
        let host_check = HostCheck::new(&o.hosts);
        let real_roots: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, String>>> = Arc::default();
        let manifest: Arc<manifest::ManifestCell> = Arc::default();
        // the kept blocks: in the state folder, swept again for each new manifest
        let kept = (compress_threads > 0)
            .then(|| match kept::KeptBlocks::open(std::path::Path::new(&real_state).join("blocks"), compress_threads) {
                Ok(k) => Some(k),
                Err(e) => {
                    log::error(&format!("kept blocks: none ({e})"));
                    None
                }
            })
            .flatten();
        if let Some(k) = &kept {
            let (k, data, roots, state) = (k.clone(), o.data.clone(), real_roots.clone(), real_state.clone());
            manifest.on_new(Arc::new(move |m: &manifest::Manifest| {
                let (data, roots, state) = (data.clone(), roots.clone(), state.clone());
                k.sweep(&m.etag, m.files.clone(), move |rel| {
                    let file = files::resolve_game(&data, &format!("/{rel}"))?;
                    let f = files::locate_sync(&roots, &state, &data, &file)?;
                    Some((f.real, f.md))
                });
            }));
        }
        let mut base = Vec::new();
        for hsts in [false, true] {
            for noindex in [false, true] {
                for cache in [Cache::Store, Cache::Revalidate, Cache::Immutable] {
                    let mut h: Vec<(String, String)> =
                        security_headers(hsts, noindex).into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v)).collect();
                    // Cloudflare's check where names are claimed (turnstile.rs): its script and frame
                    if names.as_ref().is_some_and(|n| n.turnstile.is_some()) {
                        for (k, v) in h.iter_mut().filter(|(k, _)| k == "content-security-policy") {
                            let _ = k;
                            *v = nfsu2_headers::CSP_TURNSTILE.to_string();
                        }
                    }
                    for (k, v) in cache_headers(cache) {
                        h.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));
                    }
                    base.push(h);
                }
            }
        }
        let mut raw = HashMap::new();
        for (code, text) in STATUS {
            // the same headers as every answer, nothing else
            let mut s = format!("HTTP/1.1 {code} {text}\r\n");
            let mut h: Vec<(String, String)> = security_headers(false, true).into_iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.to_string(), v)).collect();
            for (k, v) in cache_headers(Cache::Store) {
                h.push((k.to_string(), v.to_string()));
            }
            h.push(("content-length".into(), "0".into()));
            h.push(("connection".into(), "close".into()));
            s.push_str(&h.iter().map(|(k, v)| format!("{k}: {v}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join("\r\n"));
            s.push_str("\r\n\r\n");
            raw.insert(code, s.into_bytes());
        }
        let max_conns = limits::max_connections(o.max_peers);
        let friends = match (&online, &roam, &names) {
            (Some(on), Some(r), Some(n)) => Some(friends::Friends::new(on.clone(), r.clone(), lan.clone(), n.claims.clone())),
            _ => None,
        };
        App {
            host_check,
            real_state,
            etag_key,
            group_key: nfsu2_util::rand::bytes(32),
            base,
            raw,
            requests: Arc::new(Budget::new(limits::REQUESTS_PER_CLIENT, limits::REQUESTS_PER_SITE, max_conns, limits::FREE_SHARE)),
            conns: Arc::new(Budget::new(limits::CONNS_PER_ADDRESS, limits::CONNS_PER_SITE, max_conns, limits::FREE_SHARE)),
            lan_conns: Arc::new(Budget::new(limits::WS_PER_ADDRESS, limits::WS_PER_SITE, usize::MAX, 0.0)),
            lan_opens: Rate::new(limits::LAN_OPEN_BURST, limits::LAN_OPEN_RATE),
            compressors: Arc::new(Budget::new(
                blocks::COMPRESSORS_PER_CLIENT,
                blocks::COMPRESSORS_PER_SITE,
                blocks::COMPRESSORS_TOTAL,
                0.0,
            )),
            manifest,
            wasm: wasm::WasmCell::default(),
            real_roots,
            pool: Arc::new(pool::CpuPool::new(pool_threads, "nfsu2-blocks")),
            kept,
            sent: blocks::Sent::default(),
            lan,
            online,
            roam,
            vault: vault.map(vault::VaultRoute::new),
            names,
            lastfm: lastfm::Lastfm::from_env(),
            friends,
            bans,
            days,
            lan_sndbuf,
            o,
        }
    }

    /// HSTS only over a certificate browsers check (this server's own or a proxy's that says https), never for
    /// localhost or an IP literal
    fn hsts_for(&self, q: &Request) -> bool {
        self.o.hsts_ok && via_https(q, &self.o.trust) && {
            let fwd = forwarded_host(q, &self.o.trust);
            !is_local_or_ip(fwd.as_deref().or(q.headers.get("host")))
        }
    }

    /// `headers(q, {}, cache, noindex)`: the security headers, then the cache headers; the caller sets the rest
    pub fn headers(&self, q: &Request, cache: Cache, noindex: bool) -> Hdrs {
        let i = (self.hsts_for(q) as usize) * 6 + (noindex as usize) * 3 + cache_index(cache);
        Hdrs(self.base[i].clone())
    }

    /// a short text answer: the code, the text (a newline after it), headers besides the usual ones, the cache rule,
    /// and whether search engines are told to keep out
    pub async fn plain(
        &self,
        q: &Request,
        s: &mut Response,
        code: u16,
        text: &str,
        extra: &[(&str, &str)],
        cache: Cache,
        noindex: bool,
    ) -> Res {
        let body = format!("{text}\n");
        let mut h = self.headers(q, cache, noindex);
        h.set("content-type", "text/plain; charset=utf-8");
        h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
        for (k, v) in extra {
            h.set(k, *v);
        }
        s.head(code, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            send(s, body.as_bytes()).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }

    pub async fn not_found(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        self.plain(q, s, 404, "Not found", &[], Cache::Store, true).await
    }

    async fn bad_request(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        self.plain(q, s, 400, "Bad request", &[], Cache::Store, true).await
    }

    /// the answer for code written on the raw connection (refused upgrades, requests the engine cannot read): the
    /// same headers as every answer, nothing else (a code it has none for: the 400)
    pub fn raw_response(&self, code: u16) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.raw.get(&code).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| self.raw[&400].clone())
    }

    /// the request's Host (and an absolute-form URL's host) is one of this server's names
    fn own_host(&self, q: &Request) -> bool {
        if !self.host_check.check(q.headers.get("host")) {
            return false;
        }
        if !q.url.starts_with('/') {
            match url::parse_absolute(&q.url) {
                Some(u) if self.host_check.check(Some(&u.host)) => {}
                _ => return false,
            }
        }
        true
    }

    /// A request from one of this server's own pages, or from no page at all (tools send no Origin): its Origin, when
    /// it has one, is the host it asked for (or the one a trusted proxy says it asked for) and one of this server's
    /// names.  A page of another site must not reach the LAN, or a player's saves, through a player's browser.
    fn own_page(&self, q: &Request) -> bool {
        let Some(o) = q.headers.get("origin").filter(|o| !o.is_empty()) else { return true };
        let Some(origin) = url::parse_absolute(o).map(|x| x.host.to_lowercase()) else { return false };
        let host = q.headers.get("host").unwrap_or("").to_lowercase();
        let fwd = forwarded_host(q, &self.o.trust);
        let ours = (!host.is_empty() && host == origin) || fwd.as_deref().is_some_and(|f| !f.is_empty() && f == origin);
        ours && self.host_check.check(Some(&origin))
    }

    /// the client's address, and the keys its budgets count by
    fn client(&self, q: &Request) -> (String, String, String) {
        let ip = client_ip(q, &self.o.trust, &self.o.real_ip);
        let key = address_key(&ip);
        let site = site_key(&ip);
        (ip, key, site)
    }

    /// a group id: the client's (or site's) budget key under a keyed hash, so the switch can count by it without
    /// ever holding the address
    fn group_id(&self, key: &str) -> String {
        use hmac::{Hmac, Mac};
        let mut mac = <Hmac<sha2::Sha256> as Mac>::new_from_slice(&self.group_key).expect("HMAC takes any key");
        mac.update(key.as_bytes());
        js::base64url(&mac.finalize().into_bytes())[..22].to_string()
    }

    /// One request: the requests budget, the Cloudflare keep-alive rule, the access log, and the handler with its 500
    async fn on_req(&self, mut q: Request, s: &mut Response) {
        // with Cloudflare's proxy in front, the long keep-alive is for the proxies' connections: any other peer gets
        // the usual one, and is told so (keep_alive() gives the engine the time itself)
        if self.o.trust.cloudflare && !self.o.trust.trusts(&q.conn.peer) {
            s.set_header("Keep-Alive", &format!("timeout={}", limits::KEEP_ALIVE_S));
        }
        let (ip, key, site) = self.client(&q);
        let Some(_counted) = Share::take(&self.requests, &key, &site) else {
            log::limited(
                "http",
                "refused requests",
                &key,
                &format!("[http] refused a request: {} in progress already from that client", self.requests.held(&key)),
                2,
            );
            let _ = self.plain(&q, s, 429, "Too many requests", &[("connection", "close"), ("retry-after", "1")], Cache::Store, true).await;
            return;
        };
        let t0 = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
        let r = AssertUnwindSafe(self.handler(&mut q, s)).catch_unwind().await;
        let error = match r {
            Ok(Ok(())) => None,
            Ok(Err(Fail::Gone)) => return,
            Ok(Err(Fail::Error(e))) => Some(e),
            Err(p) => Some(
                p.downcast_ref::<&str>()
                    .map(|s| s.to_string())
                    .or_else(|| p.downcast_ref::<String>().cloned())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "a panic".into()),
            ),
        };
        if let Some(e) = error {
            // the details stay on this console; the client gets a plain 500
            log::error(&format!("[error] {} {}: {e}", js::printable(&q.method, 8), js::printable(&q.url, 96)));
            if s.head_sent() {
                s.destroy();
                return;
            }
            if self.plain(&q, s, 500, "Server error", &[], Cache::Store, true).await.is_err() {
                return;
            }
        }
        if self.o.access_log {
            // the opt-in that names client addresses; a page loads its game data in thousands of requests: plenty
            // for one client, not a flood.  (The method and the URL as every console line has them: one line,
            // printable, short; a client chooses what is in a URL.)
            let line = format!(
                "[http] {} {} {} {} {} ms",
                if ip.is_empty() { "?" } else { &ip },
                js::printable(&q.method, 8),
                js::printable(&q.url, 160),
                s.status(),
                nfsu2_util::now_ms() - t0
            );
            log::limited("http", "requests", &key, &line, 3000);
        }
    }

    /// the router
    async fn handler(&self, q: &mut Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        const CLOSE: &[(&str, &str)] = &[("connection", "close")];
        // HTTP/1.1 needs a Host (checked here, not by the engine, so the answer has our headers)
        if !present(q, "host") && q.version != Version::Http10 {
            return self.plain(q, s, 400, "Bad request", CLOSE, Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        // only this server's own names (DNS rebinding, scanners on the bare address): before anything else
        if !self.own_host(q) {
            return self.plain(q, s, 421, "Misdirected request", CLOSE, Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        // a path ("/x", origin form) is read as a path, never as "//host/path"; an absolute URL as itself.  No encoded
        // separator and, once decoded, no empty segment: every route compares the path it sees, and a later
        // normalisation that merged "//" or turned %2f into "/" would hand a file a different path than the one
        // checked (the phase-2 deploy review's /%2ftest/... finding)
        let Some(u) = url::parse_target(&q.url) else { return self.bad_request(q, s).await };
        let lower = u.pathname.to_ascii_lowercase();
        if lower.contains("%2f") || lower.contains("%5c") {
            return self.bad_request(q, s).await;
        }
        let Some(p) = url::decode_uri_component(&u.pathname) else { return self.bad_request(q, s).await };
        if p.chars().any(|c| c <= '\u{1f}' || c == '\u{7f}' || c == '\\') || p.contains("//") {
            return self.bad_request(q, s).await;
        }
        if q.method == "PUT" && self.o.dev && !self.o.artifacts.is_empty() && p.starts_with("/artifacts/") {
            return self.put_artifact(q, s, &p[11..]).await;
        }
        // keyphrase saves, claimed names and friends: their own methods and bodies (vault.rs, names.rs, friends.rs)
        if p == "/vault" {
            return self.vault(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        if p == "/names" {
            return self.names(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        if p == "/friends" {
            return self.friends_route(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        if p == "/lastfm" {
            return self.lastfm(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        if q.method != "GET" && q.method != "HEAD" {
            return self
                .plain(q, s, 405, "Method not allowed", &[("allow", "GET, HEAD"), ("connection", "close")], Cache::Store, true)
                .await;
        }
        // nothing here takes a request body
        if js_to_number(q.headers.get("content-length").unwrap_or("0")) > 0.0 || present(q, "transfer-encoding") {
            return self.plain(q, s, 413, "Too large", CLOSE, Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        if p == "/data-manifest" {
            return self.send_manifest(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        // the game's files are bytes for the game, whatever their names say
        if let Some(rest) = p.strip_prefix("/data")
            && rest.starts_with('/')
        {
            let file = files::resolve_game(&self.o.data, rest);
            return self
                .send_file(q, s, &self.o.data, file, files::FileOpts { type_: Some("application/octet-stream"), ..Default::default() })
                .await;
        }
        if let Some(rest) = p.strip_prefix("/data-blocks")
            && rest.starts_with('/')
        {
            // (the manifest's addresses since blocks are kept; the ones from before, without /v2, are no more)
            let Some(rest) = rest.strip_prefix(blocks::V2).filter(|r| r.starts_with('/')) else {
                return self.not_found(q, s).await;
            };
            let file = files::resolve_game(&self.o.data, rest);
            return self.send_blocks(q, s, file, &u).await;
        }
        if p == "/game.wasm" {
            return self.send_wasm(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        if p == "/game.json" {
            return self.send_game_json(q, s).await;
        }
        if p == "/players" {
            return self.send_players(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        if p == "/seen" {
            return self.send_seen(q, s, &u).await;
        }
        if p == "/country" {
            return self.send_country(q, s).await;
        }
        if p == "/lan" {
            return self.send_lan_check(q, s).await;
        }
        if p == "/robots.txt" {
            return self.plain(q, s, 200, ROBOTS_TXT, &[], Cache::Revalidate, false).await;
        }
        // test aids (--dev only): the repo's test scripts, and the test pages and source maps from their own folder
        // (web/dist-dev), which the server never looks in without --dev
        if self.o.dev && p.starts_with("/tests/") {
            let tests = self.o.tests.clone();
            let file = files::resolve_inside(&tests, &p[6..]);
            return self.send_file(q, s, &tests, file, files::FileOpts::default()).await;
        }
        // a second guard, for a web/dist that an older build left test pages or maps in: their names, compared the
        // way a case-insensitive disk does (NFKC folds "ſ" to "s", "K" to "k")
        if !self.o.dev && files::dev_only(&p) {
            return self.not_found(q, s).await;
        }
        let rel = if p.ends_with('/') { format!("{p}index.html") } else { p.clone() };
        let mut root = self.o.dist.clone();
        let mut found = self.locate(&root, files::resolve_inside(&root, &rel)).await;
        if found.is_none() && self.o.dev {
            root = self.o.dev_dist.clone();
            found = self.locate(&root, files::resolve_inside(&root, &rel)).await;
        }
        let indexable = root == self.o.dist && rel == "/index.html";
        let cache = if rel.ends_with(".html") { Cache::Store } else { Cache::Revalidate };
        self.send_file(q, s, &root, None, files::FileOpts { found, cache, noindex: !indexable, ..Default::default() }).await
    }

    /// /data-manifest: built at the start, again on ?refresh at most every 10 s
    async fn send_manifest(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, u: &url::Url) -> Res {
        let m = match self.current_manifest() {
            Some(m) if !(u.has_param("refresh") && nfsu2_util::now_ms() - m.at > 10_000) => m,
            _ => self.refresh_manifest().await.map_err(|e| Fail::Error(format!("the manifest: {e}")))?,
        };
        let gz = has_word(q.headers.get("accept-encoding").unwrap_or(""), "gzip");
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Revalidate, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/json");
        h.set("etag", m.etag.clone());
        h.set("vary", "accept-encoding");
        if nfsu2_headers::etag_matches(q.headers.get("if-none-match"), &m.etag) {
            s.head(304, h.0);
            return finish(s).await;
        }
        let body = if gz { &m.gz } else { &m.body };
        h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
        if gz {
            h.set("content-encoding", "gzip");
        }
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            send(s, body).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }

    /// the manifest walked again: one walk at a time; a request while one is under way takes its result
    pub async fn refresh_manifest(&self) -> Result<Arc<manifest::Manifest>, String> {
        self.manifest.refresh(&self.o.data, &self.real_state, &self.etag_key).await
    }

    /// the manifest made last
    pub fn current_manifest(&self) -> Option<Arc<manifest::Manifest>> {
        self.manifest.current()
    }

    pub fn manifest_count(&self) -> usize {
        self.current_manifest().map_or(0, |m| m.count)
    }

    /// /players: how many play on this server now (the start page's Multiplayer settings): three counts, whether it
    /// is full and whether free roam is busy, nothing else, no names, addresses or times; online: in the game's Online
    /// mode (logged in, or racing an online race), null with --online off; roam: driving in free roam, or paused
    /// there, as of the hub's last tick (nfsu2-roam), null with --roam-hub off; full: a game that connects now waits in
    /// line (a connection without ?queue, which cannot wait: "LAN full"); queue: the pages waiting in line (nfsu2-lan queue.rs); roamBusy: the
    /// hub gives fewer than askCap links a player, so the page does not ask the free-roam question now (false with
    /// --roam-hub off).  ?room=<hash> (roam_core's rc_room_hash of a Room setting, decimal,
    /// not 0) adds room: how many of roam are in that room, its race tracks' spots too (with --roam-hub on).
    /// ?rooms=<hash>,<hash>,... (the worlds of the start page's World row and the page menu's: 0 the main world, then
    /// World 1 to 4 and a world of the player's own; the first ROOMS_ASKED that are numbers) adds rooms: how many of
    /// roam are in each world, at its race tracks' spots too (nfsu2_roam::world_count), in that order (with --roam-hub
    /// on, and one of them at least).  ?spots=<hash>,<hash>,... (the page menu's Tracks: a world's spots' rooms,
    /// nfsu2_roam::track_room; the first SPOTS_ASKED) adds spots: how many of roam are in each of those rooms, just
    /// that room, in that order.  ?crews=<hash>,<hash>,... (the
    /// rc_room_hash of each of the Crews setting's words, decimal; the first 4 that are numbers and not 0, the rest
    /// left out) adds crews: how many of roam are in each of those crews, in any room, in that order (with --roam-hub
    /// on, and one of them at least); both as of the hub's last tick, from its counts (nothing waits for its thread)
    async fn send_players(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, u: &url::Url) -> Res {
        let info = match &self.online {
            Some(h) => {
                let rx = nfsu2_util::Host::info(h.as_ref());
                tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(2), rx).await.ok().and_then(Result::ok)
            }
            None => None,
        };
        let players = self.lan.peer_count();
        let online = match info {
            Some(o) => {
                let n = |k: &str| o.get(k).and_then(serde_json::Value::as_f64).unwrap_or(f64::NAN);
                let x = n("personas") + n("racing");
                // Math.min: NaN when either is
                nfsu2_util::json::num(if x.is_nan() { f64::NAN } else { (players as f64).min(x) })
            }
            None => serde_json::Value::Null,
        };
        // (Math.min as online: the hub's last tick and the switch now, a player who just left may still be in it)
        let roam = self.roam.as_ref().map_or(serde_json::Value::Null, |r| serde_json::Value::from(r.in_roam().min(players)));
        let mut m = serde_json::Map::new();
        m.insert("players".into(), serde_json::Value::from(players));
        m.insert("online".into(), online);
        m.insert("roam".into(), roam);
        m.insert("full".into(), serde_json::Value::Bool(self.lan.full()));
        m.insert("queue".into(), serde_json::Value::from(self.lan.waiting()));
        m.insert("roamBusy".into(), serde_json::Value::Bool(self.roam.as_ref().is_some_and(|r| r.crowded())));
        let room = u.param("room").and_then(|r| r.parse::<u32>().ok()).filter(|&r| r != 0);
        if let (Some(room), Some(r)) = (room, &self.roam) {
            m.insert("room".into(), serde_json::Value::from(r.in_world(room).min(players)));
        }
        let rooms: Vec<u32> =
            u.param("rooms").map_or(Vec::new(), |c| c.split(',').filter_map(|h| h.parse::<u32>().ok()).take(ROOMS_ASKED).collect());
        if let Some(r) = self.roam.as_ref().filter(|_| !rooms.is_empty()) {
            let n = rooms.iter().map(|&h| serde_json::Value::from(r.in_world(h).min(players))).collect();
            m.insert("rooms".into(), serde_json::Value::Array(n));
        }
        let spots: Vec<u32> =
            u.param("spots").map_or(Vec::new(), |c| c.split(',').filter_map(|h| h.parse::<u32>().ok()).take(SPOTS_ASKED).collect());
        if let Some(r) = self.roam.as_ref().filter(|_| !spots.is_empty()) {
            let n = spots.iter().map(|&h| serde_json::Value::from(r.in_room(h).min(players))).collect();
            m.insert("spots".into(), serde_json::Value::Array(n));
        }
        let crews: Vec<u32> = u.param("crews").map_or(Vec::new(), |c| {
            c.split(',').filter_map(|h| h.parse::<u32>().ok()).filter(|&h| h != 0).take(nfsu2_roam::CREWS).collect()
        });
        if let Some(r) = self.roam.as_ref().filter(|_| !crews.is_empty()) {
            let n = r.in_crews(&crews).into_iter().map(|n| serde_json::Value::from(n.min(players))).collect();
            m.insert("crews".into(), serde_json::Value::Array(n));
        }
        let body = nfsu2_util::json::stringify(&serde_json::Value::Object(m));
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/json");
        h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            send(s, body.as_bytes()).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }

    /// /country: {"country":"nl"}, the country the browser's connection comes from as Cloudflare names it (a trusted
    /// proxy's CF-IPCountry, nfsu2_headers::client_country), lower case; null when there is none.  The start page's
    /// Your flag list puts it first (web/src/app/flags.ts): it goes to that browser only, and nowhere else.
    async fn send_country(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        let c = nfsu2_headers::client_country(q, &self.o.trust).map(|c| String::from_utf8_lossy(&c).to_ascii_lowercase());
        let mut m = serde_json::Map::new();
        m.insert("country".into(), c.map_or(serde_json::Value::Null, serde_json::Value::from));
        let body = nfsu2_util::json::stringify(&serde_json::Value::Object(m));
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/json");
        h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
        s.head(200, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            send(s, body.as_bytes()).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }

    /// /seen?at=page|play&id=<the page's id>: a browser opened the page or pressed Play, counted for the day
    /// (days.rs); a day's first Play also tells its device and changed settings, &k=<pc|phone|tablet>&s=<key=value,...>
    /// (settings_days.rs); 204, no body, whatever it said
    async fn send_seen(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, u: &url::Url) -> Res {
        let what = match u.param("at").as_deref() {
            Some("page") => Some(days::Seen::Page),
            Some("play") => Some(days::Seen::Play),
            _ => None,
        };
        if let (Some(what), Some(id), "GET") = (what, u.param("id"), q.method.as_str()) {
            let now = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
            self.days.seen(&id, what, now);
            if what == days::Seen::Play
                && let Some(r) = settings_days::Report::parse(u.param("k").as_deref(), u.param("s").as_deref())
            {
                self.days.told(&id, &r, now);
            }
        }
        let h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        s.head(204, h.0);
        finish(s).await
    }

    /// a test artifact (frame dump) from a page on this machine (--dev --artifacts only)
    async fn put_artifact(&self, q: &mut Request, s: &mut Response, name: &str) -> Res {
        let peer = nfsu2_headers::bare_ip(&q.conn.peer);
        let local = (peer == "::1" || is_loopback4(&peer)) && !present(q, "x-forwarded-for") && !present(q, "cf-connecting-ip");
        if !local || !artifact_name(name) {
            return self.plain(q, s, 403, "Forbidden", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        if js_to_number(q.headers.get("content-length").unwrap_or("0")) > limits::ARTIFACT_BYTES as f64 {
            return self.plain(q, s, 413, "Too large", &[("connection", "close")], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        let body = match q.read_body(limits::ARTIFACT_BYTES).await {
            Ok(b) => b,
            Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::TooLarge) => {
                return self.plain(q, s, 413, "Too large", &[("connection", "close")], Cache::Store, true).await;
            }
            Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::Broken) => {
                s.destroy();
                return Err(Fail::Gone);
            }
        };
        let path = crate::paths::join(&self.o.artifacts, name);
        tokio::fs::write(&path, body).await.map_err(|e| Fail::Error(format!("{path}: {e}")))?;
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-length", "0");
        s.head(201, h.0);
        finish(s).await
    }
}

/// `/^127\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`
fn is_loopback4(ip: &str) -> bool {
    let parts: Vec<&str> = ip.split('.').collect();
    parts.len() == 4 && parts[0] == "127" && parts[1..].iter().all(|p| !p.is_empty() && p.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()))
}

/// `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,127}\.png$/`
fn artifact_name(name: &str) -> bool {
    let ok = |c: u8, dot: bool| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'_' || c == b'-' || (dot && c == b'.');
    let Some(stem) = name.strip_suffix(".png") else { return false };
    let b = stem.as_bytes();
    !b.is_empty() && b.len() <= 128 && ok(b[0], false) && b[1..].iter().all(|&c| ok(c, true))
}

impl Service for App {
    /// connections at once per client and site, for TCP peers that are not trusted proxies (a proxy carries many
    /// clients); counted from the first byte, before any TLS, so stalled handshakes count too
    fn admit(&self, peer: &SocketAddr) -> Option<Box<dyn Send + Sync>> {
        let ip = nfsu2_headers::bare_ip(&peer.ip().to_string());
        if ip.is_empty() {
            return None;
        }
        if self.o.trust.trusts(&ip) {
            return Some(Box::new(()));
        }
        let key = address_key(&ip);
        let site = site_key(&ip);
        Share::take(&self.conns, &key, &site).map(|s| Box::new(s) as Box<dyn Send + Sync>)
    }

    /// Cloudflare's addresses (--trusted-proxies cloudflare) show Cloudflare's origin-pull certificate: any of its
    /// customers connects from them too (nfsu2_headers::ProxyTrust)
    fn client_certificate(&self, peer: &SocketAddr) -> bool {
        self.o.trust.must_prove(&peer.ip().to_string())
    }

    fn keep_alive(&self, peer: &SocketAddr) -> Duration {
        if !self.o.trust.cloudflare {
            return Duration::from_secs(limits::KEEP_ALIVE_S);
        }
        if self.o.trust.trusts(&peer.ip().to_string()) {
            return Duration::from_secs(limits::KEEP_ALIVE_CLOUDFLARE_S);
        }
        // the usual time for a peer that is not Cloudflare's: 65 s from the end of the answer.  The engine adds a
        // second to every keep-alive time (as Node does: nfsu2_http's KEEP_ALIVE_BUFFER), so a second less here: the
        // Node server set the socket's timeout to 65 s once an answer was finished, which replaced Node's own
        // keep-alive timer, its extra second and all.  (on_req says timeout=65 in the Keep-Alive header itself.)
        Duration::from_secs(limits::KEEP_ALIVE_S - 1)
    }

    fn request<'a>(&'a self, req: Request, res: &'a mut Response) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + Send + 'a {
        self.on_req(req, res)
    }

    /// Expect: anything but 100-continue
    async fn expectation<'a>(&'a self, req: Request, res: &'a mut Response) {
        let _ = self.plain(&req, res, 417, "Expectation failed", &[("connection", "close")], Cache::Store, true).await;
    }

    fn upgrade(&self, req: Request, up: Upgraded) -> impl Future<Output = ()> + Send {
        self.on_upgrade(req, up)
    }

    /// A request the engine could not read (a parse error, a head over max_header_size, a header or request that
    /// took too long) gets a short answer with this server's headers, then the connection goes.  A TLS handshake that
    /// failed or took too long has no HTTP to answer with: the engine closes the connection without a byte.
    fn client_error(&self, e: ClientError) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
        Some(self.raw_response(match e {
            ClientError::Parse => 400,
            ClientError::HeaderOverflow => 431,
            ClientError::Timeout => 408,
        }))
    }
}

//! /names: claimed names (nfsu2-claims), for this server's own pages only, with keyphrase saves (/vault) on: a name
//! is claimed by a keyphrase, so a server without them has none (404).
//!
//! - `GET /names?name=<name>[&alt=<name>]`, with the keyphrase's token as `Authorization: Bearer <43 characters>` when
//!   the page has one: what the name is to that keyphrase (and the second one, the page's choice of digits for it):
//!   `{"name":<its Online form>,"state":"free"|"yours"|"old"|"taken"|"default"|"blocked"|"invalid","until":<ms>,
//!   "alt":{...},"mine":{"name":...,"until":<ms>,"next":<ms of its next change, 0: now>},"captcha":<site key>}`.
//!   "old": the keyphrase's name before its last change (its for GRACE_DAYS); "mine": the keyphrase's own name;
//!   "captcha": Cloudflare Turnstile's site key, when claims ask for its check (turnstile.rs).
//! - `POST /names` with the token and `{"name":<name>,"captcha":<the widget's answer>}`: the keyphrase claims the
//!   name (a change when it had another).  200 with "mine"; 403 `{"error":"captcha"}` (the check failed); 404
//!   `{"error":"keyphrase"}` (the cloud has no such keyphrase: the page sends its saves first); 400 "invalid",
//!   "default" or "blocked"; 409 "taken"; 429 "soon" with "next" (one change a week) or plain (too many claims from
//!   one client: CLAIM_BURST, then CLAIM_PER_DAY a day); 507 "full"; 503 "captcha-down" (Cloudflare did not answer).
//!
//! Per client (and twice that per site): 120 reads, then 2 a second.  The console names the names claimed, never a
//! keyphrase or its token.

use std::sync::Arc;

use nfsu2_claims::{Claims, Refusal, Status, owner_of_id, owner_of_token};
use nfsu2_headers::Cache;
use nfsu2_http::{Request, Response};
use nfsu2_util::{Rate, log};
use nfsu2_vault::id_of;
use serde_json::{Map, Value, json};

use super::turnstile::Turnstile;
use super::{App, Fail, Res, finish, send, url};

pub const READ_BURST: f64 = 120.0;
pub const READ_RATE: f64 = 2.0;
pub const CLAIM_BURST: f64 = 10.0;
pub const CLAIM_PER_DAY: f64 = 10.0;
/// the most of a claim's body (a name and Turnstile's answer, at most 2 KB)
const MAX_BODY: usize = 4096;

/// The claimed names of an App: the store, Cloudflare's check, the limits.
pub struct NamesRoute {
    pub claims: Arc<Claims>,
    pub turnstile: Option<Turnstile>,
    reads: Rate,
    claimed: Rate,
}

impl NamesRoute {
    pub fn new(claims: Arc<Claims>, turnstile: Option<Turnstile>) -> NamesRoute {
        NamesRoute { claims, turnstile, reads: Rate::new(READ_BURST, READ_RATE), claimed: Rate::new(CLAIM_BURST, CLAIM_PER_DAY / 86_400.0) }
    }

    /// the buckets that are full again hold nothing worth keeping (every minute)
    pub fn prune(&self) {
        self.reads.prune();
        self.claimed.prune();
    }
}

/// `Bearer <43 characters of base64url>`: the token (as /vault takes it)
pub(super) fn token(q: &Request) -> Option<&str> {
    let t = q.headers.get("authorization")?.strip_prefix("Bearer ")?;
    (t.len() == 43 && t.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == b'-' || c == b'_')).then_some(t)
}

fn status_json(name: &str, s: &Status) -> Value {
    let (state, until) = match s {
        Status::Invalid => ("invalid", None),
        Status::Default => ("default", None),
        Status::Blocked => ("blocked", None),
        Status::Free => ("free", None),
        Status::Yours { until, current: true } => ("yours", Some(*until)),
        Status::Yours { until, current: false } => ("old", Some(*until)),
        Status::Taken => ("taken", None),
    };
    let mut m = Map::new();
    m.insert("name".into(), nfsu2_claims::clean(name).map_or(Value::Null, Value::from));
    m.insert("state".into(), state.into());
    if let Some(u) = until {
        m.insert("until".into(), u.into());
    }
    Value::Object(m)
}

fn mine_json(m: &nfsu2_claims::Mine) -> Value {
    json!({ "name": m.name, "until": m.until, "next": m.next_change })
}

impl App {
    /// a name's claim as `owner` sees it; one the operator took away (control.rs rename) as one that reads as a slur:
    /// nobody claims it
    fn name_status(&self, n: &NamesRoute, name: &str, owner: Option<&str>, now: i64) -> Status {
        match n.claims.status(name, owner, now) {
            s @ (Status::Invalid | Status::Default) => s,
            _ if self.bans.deny().has(name) => Status::Blocked,
            s => s,
        }
    }

    /// /names (claimed names): see this module's doc
    pub(super) async fn names(&self, q: &mut Request, s: &mut Response, u: &url::Url) -> Res {
        let Some(n) = &self.names else { return self.not_found(q, s).await };
        // only this server's own pages: a page of another site must not claim a player's name through their browser
        let site_ok = q.headers.get("sec-fetch-site").is_none_or(|f| f == "same-origin");
        if !self.own_page(q) || !site_ok {
            return self.plain(q, s, 403, "Forbidden", &[], Cache::Store, true).await;
        }
        let (_, key, site) = self.client(q);
        let now = nfsu2_util::now_ms();
        let owner = token(q).and_then(owner_of_token);
        match q.method.as_str() {
            "GET" => {
                if !n.reads.take(&key, &site) {
                    return self.too_many_names(q, s).await;
                }
                let name = u.param("name").unwrap_or_default();
                let mut v = status_json(&name, &self.name_status(n, &name, owner.as_deref(), now));
                let m = v.as_object_mut().expect("an object");
                if let Some(alt) = u.param("alt") {
                    m.insert("alt".into(), status_json(&alt, &self.name_status(n, &alt, owner.as_deref(), now)));
                }
                if let Some(mine) = owner.as_deref().and_then(|o| n.claims.mine(o, now)) {
                    let mut j = mine_json(&mine);
                    // (a name the operator took away from someone that reads as this claim: the page does not play it,
                    // claim-ui.ts, and its next claim is a change)
                    if self.bans.deny().has(&mine.name) {
                        j["blocked"] = true.into();
                    }
                    m.insert("mine".into(), j);
                }
                if let Some(t) = &n.turnstile {
                    m.insert("captcha".into(), t.site.clone().into());
                }
                self.json(q, s, 200, &v).await
            }
            "POST" => {
                let (Some(t), Some(owner)) = (token(q).map(str::to_string), owner) else {
                    return self.json(q, s, 401, &json!({ "error": "keyphrase" })).await;
                };
                let body = match q.read_body(MAX_BODY).await {
                    Ok(b) => b,
                    Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::TooLarge) => return self.json(q, s, 413, &json!({ "error": "large" })).await,
                    Err(nfsu2_http::BodyError::Broken) => {
                        s.destroy();
                        return Err(Fail::Gone);
                    }
                };
                let Ok(Value::Object(b)) = serde_json::from_slice::<Value>(&body) else {
                    return self.json(q, s, 400, &json!({ "error": "invalid" })).await;
                };
                let name = b.get("name").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("").to_string();
                // what would be refused anyway costs no claim, no check and no look into the cloud
                match self.name_status(n, &name, Some(&owner), now) {
                    Status::Invalid => return self.json(q, s, 400, &json!({ "error": "invalid" })).await,
                    Status::Default => return self.json(q, s, 400, &json!({ "error": "default" })).await,
                    Status::Blocked => return self.json(q, s, 400, &json!({ "error": "blocked" })).await,
                    Status::Taken => return self.json(q, s, 409, &json!({ "error": "taken" })).await,
                    Status::Yours { current: true, .. } => {
                        let mine = n.claims.claim(&name, &owner, now).map_err(|_| Fail::Error("claims: its own name".into()))?;
                        return self.json(q, s, 200, &json!({ "state": "yours", "mine": mine_json(&mine) })).await;
                    }
                    _ => {}
                }
                if let Some(m) = n.claims.mine(&owner, now)
                    && m.next_change > now
                {
                    return self.json(q, s, 429, &json!({ "error": "soon", "next": m.next_change })).await;
                }
                if !n.claimed.take(&key, &site) {
                    return self.too_many_names(q, s).await;
                }
                // a keyphrase the cloud has (the page sends its saves before it claims)
                let Some(v) = &self.vault else { return self.not_found(q, s).await };
                let (store, id) = (v.store.clone(), id_of(t.as_bytes()));
                let there = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || store.meta(&id, now))
                    .await
                    .map_err(|e| Fail::Error(format!("claims: {e}")))?
                    .map_err(|e| Fail::Error(format!("claims: {e}")))?
                    .is_some();
                if !there {
                    return self.json(q, s, 404, &json!({ "error": "keyphrase" })).await;
                }
                if let Some(ts) = &n.turnstile {
                    let answer = b.get("captcha").and_then(Value::as_str).unwrap_or("");
                    match ts.passed(answer).await {
                        Ok(true) => {}
                        Ok(false) => return self.json(q, s, 403, &json!({ "error": "captcha" })).await,
                        Err(e) => {
                            log::limited("names", "turnstile", "", &format!("[names] Cloudflare's check could not be asked: {e}"), 1);
                            return self.json(q, s, 503, &json!({ "error": "captcha-down" })).await;
                        }
                    }
                }
                match n.claims.claim(&name, &owner, now) {
                    Ok(mine) => {
                        let line = format!("[names] \"{}\" claimed ({} claimed)", mine.name, n.claims.count(now));
                        log::limited("names", "claims", &key, &line, 10);
                        self.json(q, s, 200, &json!({ "state": "yours", "mine": mine_json(&mine) })).await
                    }
                    Err(r) => {
                        let (code, e) = match r {
                            Refusal::Invalid => (400, json!({ "error": "invalid" })),
                            Refusal::Default => (400, json!({ "error": "default" })),
                            Refusal::Blocked => (400, json!({ "error": "blocked" })),
                            Refusal::Taken => (409, json!({ "error": "taken" })),
                            Refusal::TooSoon { next } => (429, json!({ "error": "soon", "next": next })),
                            Refusal::Full => (507, json!({ "error": "full" })),
                        };
                        self.json(q, s, code, &e).await
                    }
                }
            }
            _ => self.plain(q, s, 405, "Method not allowed", &[("allow", "GET, POST"), ("connection", "close")], Cache::Store, true).await,
        }
    }

    /// a keyphrase deleted from the cloud: its names are free (/vault's DELETE)
    pub(super) fn release_names(&self, vault_id: &[u8; 32]) {
        if let Some(n) = &self.names
            && n.claims.release(&owner_of_id(vault_id)) > 0
        {
            log::line("[names] a keyphrase deleted from the cloud: its name is free");
        }
    }

    /// a keyphrase used (its cloud saves read or saved, /vault): its claimed name lasts as long as it does
    pub(super) fn names_used(&self, vault_id: &[u8; 32], now: i64) {
        if let Some(n) = &self.names {
            n.claims.used(&owner_of_id(vault_id), now);
        }
    }

    async fn too_many_names(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response) -> Res {
        self.plain(q, s, 429, "Too many requests", &[("retry-after", "60")], Cache::Store, true).await
    }

    /// a JSON answer (never cached)
    pub(super) async fn json(&self, q: &Request, s: &mut Response, code: u16, v: &Value) -> Res {
        let body = nfsu2_util::json::stringify(v);
        let mut h = self.headers(q, Cache::Store, true);
        h.set("content-type", "application/json");
        h.set("content-length", body.len().to_string());
        s.head(code, h.0);
        if q.method != "HEAD" {
            send(s, body.as_bytes()).await?;
        }
        finish(s).await
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::super::testkit::Kit;
    use super::*;

    const A: (&str, &str) = ("Authorization", "Bearer AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA");
    const B: (&str, &str) = ("Authorization", "Bearer BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB");

    fn j(body: &[u8]) -> Value {
        serde_json::from_slice(body).unwrap()
    }

    async fn claim(kit: &Kit, who: (&str, &str), name: &str) -> (u16, Value) {
        let body = json!({ "name": name }).to_string();
        let a = kit.request("POST", "/names", &[who, ("Content-Type", "application/json")], body.as_bytes()).await;
        (a.status, j(&a.body))
    }

    // a claim lasts as long as its keyphrase: as long as the cloud keeps one nobody uses
    #[test]
    fn a_claim_holds_as_long_as_a_keyphrase() {
        let o = nfsu2_vault::VaultOptions::sized(std::path::PathBuf::from("/x"), 1.0);
        assert_eq!(nfsu2_claims::HOLD_DAYS * nfsu2_claims::DAY_MS, o.unused_ms);
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn names_checked_claimed_and_let_go() {
        let kit = Kit::start(&[], |_| {}).await;
        let g = kit.get("/names?name=Alex%20the%20Great", &[]).await;
        assert_eq!(g.status, 200);
        assert_eq!(g.header("content-type"), Some("application/json"));
        assert_eq!(g.header("cache-control"), Some("private, no-store, no-transform"));
        assert_eq!(j(&g.body), json!({ "name": "Alex_the_Great", "state": "free" }));
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=NAME", &[]).await.body)["state"], "default");
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Hitler", &[]).await.body)["state"], "blocked");
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=%21%21", &[]).await.body), json!({ "name": null, "state": "invalid" }));
        // a claim needs a keyphrase the cloud has
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, ("X-No", "token"), "Alex").await.0, 401);
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, A, "Alex").await, (404, json!({ "error": "keyphrase" })));
        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[A, ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"saves").await.status, 201);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/vault", &[B, ("If-None-Match", "*")], b"saves").await.status, 201);
        // refused before anything is asked
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, A, "NAME").await, (400, json!({ "error": "default" })));
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, A, "N1gg3r").await, (400, json!({ "error": "blocked" })));
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, A, "").await, (400, json!({ "error": "invalid" })));
        let (code, v) = claim(&kit, A, "Alex").await;
        assert_eq!((code, &v["state"], &v["mine"]["name"], &v["mine"]["next"]), (200, &json!("yours"), &json!("Alex"), &json!(0)));
        // to its keyphrase it is its own; to another, taken; the alt is the page's digits
        let g = j(&kit.get("/names?name=alex&alt=Alex4821", &[A]).await.body);
        assert_eq!((&g["state"], &g["alt"]["state"], &g["mine"]["name"]), (&json!("yours"), &json!("free"), &json!("Alex")));
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Alex", &[B]).await.body)["state"], "taken");
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Alex", &[]).await.body)["state"], "taken");
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, B, "ALEX").await, (409, json!({ "error": "taken" })));
        // its second form (co-op's second player, "Alex 2") is its own too, and another's claim of it is refused
        let g = j(&kit.get("/names?name=Alex%202", &[A]).await.body);
        assert_eq!((&g["name"], &g["state"]), (&json!("Alex_2"), &json!("yours")));
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Alex%202", &[B]).await.body)["state"], "taken");
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, B, "Alex 2").await, (409, json!({ "error": "taken" })));
        // a change: the first is free, the next waits a week; the old name stays its own
        let (code, v) = claim(&kit, A, "Speedy").await;
        assert_eq!((code, &v["mine"]["name"]), (200, &json!("Speedy")));
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Alex", &[A]).await.body)["state"], "old");
        let (code, v) = claim(&kit, A, "Racer").await;
        assert_eq!((code, &v["error"]), (429, &json!("soon")));
        assert!(v["next"].as_i64().unwrap() > nfsu2_util::now_ms() + 6 * 86_400_000);
        // its keyphrase deleted from the cloud: its names are free
        assert_eq!(kit.request("DELETE", "/vault", &[A], b"").await.status, 200);
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Speedy", &[B]).await.body)["state"], "free");
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Alex", &[B]).await.body)["state"], "free");
        assert_eq!(claim(&kit, B, "Alex").await.0, 200);
        // a name the operator takes away from someone else that reads as the claim: the page hears so
        assert_eq!(j(&kit.get("/names?name=Other", &[B]).await.body)["mine"].get("blocked"), None);
        kit.app.bans.rename("Alex", &["Alex".to_string()], &Default::default(), "", nfsu2_util::now_ms() as i64).unwrap();
        let g = j(&kit.get("/names?name=Other", &[B]).await.body);
        assert_eq!((&g["mine"]["name"], &g["mine"]["blocked"]), (&json!("Alex"), &json!(true)));
        // another site's page claims nothing
        let x = kit.request("POST", "/names", &[B, ("Origin", "https://evil.example")], b"{\"name\":\"Evil\"}").await;
        assert_eq!(x.status, 403);
        assert_eq!(kit.request("PUT", "/names", &[B], b"").await.status, 405);
    }
}

//! Questions this server asks other servers (Cloudflare's Turnstile: turnstile.rs; Last.fm: lastfm.rs; Discord's
//! webhook: autoban.rs): a form or JSON POSTed over HTTPS with the web's root certificates built in (webpki-roots: the
//! image has no certificate store), HTTP/1.1 with the connection closed after the answer.  The caller sets the time
//! limit.

use std::sync::Arc;

use tokio::io::{AsyncRead, AsyncReadExt, AsyncWrite, AsyncWriteExt};

/// the most of an answer read
const MAX_ANSWER: usize = 64 << 10;

pub struct Https {
    tls: tokio_rustls::TlsConnector,
}

impl Https {
    pub fn new() -> Https {
        let roots = rustls::RootCertStore::from_iter(webpki_roots::TLS_SERVER_ROOTS.iter().cloned());
        let provider = Arc::new(rustls::crypto::ring::default_provider());
        let config = rustls::ClientConfig::builder_with_provider(provider)
            .with_safe_default_protocol_versions()
            .expect("the ring provider's TLS versions")
            .with_root_certificates(roots)
            .with_no_client_auth();
        Https { tls: tokio_rustls::TlsConnector::from(Arc::new(config)) }
    }

    /// a form POSTed to `url` (https://, or http:// for the tests' own servers): the answer's status and body
    pub async fn post_form(&self, url: &str, body: &str) -> Result<(u16, Vec<u8>), String> {
        self.post(url, "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", body).await
    }

    /// JSON POSTed to `url` (Discord's webhook: autoban.rs), as `post_form`
    pub async fn post_json(&self, url: &str, body: &str) -> Result<(u16, Vec<u8>), String> {
        self.post(url, "application/json", body).await
    }

    async fn post(&self, url: &str, content_type: &str, body: &str) -> Result<(u16, Vec<u8>), String> {
        let (tls, rest) = match url.split_once("://") {
            Some(("https", r)) => (true, r),
            Some(("http", r)) => (false, r),
            _ => return Err(format!("not an http(s) address: {url}")),
        };
        let (hostport, path) = rest.split_once('/').map_or((rest, "/".to_string()), |(h, p)| (h, format!("/{p}")));
        let (host, port) = match hostport.rsplit_once(':') {
            Some((h, p)) if p.bytes().all(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()) => (h, p.parse::<u16>().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?),
            _ => (hostport, if tls { 443 } else { 80 }),
        };
        let req = format!(
            "POST {path} HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {hostport}\r\nUser-Agent: nfsu2-server\r\nContent-Type: {content_type}\r\n\
             Content-Length: {}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n{body}",
            body.len()
        );
        let tcp = tokio::net::TcpStream::connect((host, port)).await.map_err(|e| format!("{host}:{port}: {e}"))?;
        if tls {
            let name = rustls::pki_types::ServerName::try_from(host.to_string()).map_err(|e| format!("{host}: {e}"))?;
            let s = self.tls.connect(name, tcp).await.map_err(|e| format!("{host}: {e}"))?;
            exchange(s, req.as_bytes()).await
        } else {
            exchange(tcp, req.as_bytes()).await
        }
    }
}

/// the request written, the answer read to its end; its status and body
async fn exchange<S: AsyncRead + AsyncWrite + Unpin>(mut s: S, req: &[u8]) -> Result<(u16, Vec<u8>), String> {
    s.write_all(req).await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    s.flush().await.map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let mut buf = Vec::new();
    let mut chunk = [0u8; 8192];
    loop {
        match s.read(&mut chunk).await {
            Ok(0) => break,
            Ok(n) => {
                buf.extend_from_slice(&chunk[..n]);
                if buf.len() > MAX_ANSWER {
                    return Err("its answer is too long".into());
                }
            }
            // (a TLS server that closes without close_notify: what came is the answer)
            Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::UnexpectedEof => break,
            Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
        }
    }
    let end = buf.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n").ok_or("no answer")?;
    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&buf[..end]).to_ascii_lowercase();
    let status = head.split(' ').nth(1).and_then(|c| c.parse::<u16>().ok()).ok_or("no status")?;
    let body = &buf[end + 4..];
    if head.lines().any(|l| l.starts_with("transfer-encoding:") && l.contains("chunked")) {
        return Ok((status, dechunk(body)?));
    }
    Ok((status, body.to_vec()))
}

/// a chunked body's bytes
fn dechunk(mut b: &[u8]) -> Result<Vec<u8>, String> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    loop {
        let eol = b.windows(2).position(|w| w == b"\r\n").ok_or("a broken chunk")?;
        let size = String::from_utf8_lossy(&b[..eol]);
        let n = usize::from_str_radix(size.split(';').next().unwrap_or("").trim(), 16).map_err(|_| "a broken chunk")?;
        b = &b[eol + 2..];
        if n == 0 {
            return Ok(out);
        }
        if b.len() < n {
            return Err("a broken chunk".into());
        }
        out.extend_from_slice(&b[..n]);
        b = b.get(n + 2..).unwrap_or(&[]);
    }
}

/// application/x-www-form-urlencoded
pub fn form(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut o = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    for b in s.bytes() {
        if b.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(b, b'-' | b'_' | b'.' | b'~') {
            o.push(b as char);
        } else {
            o.push_str(&format!("%{b:02X}"));
        }
    }
    o
}

//! Threads of their own for the CPU work of the game data's runs (reading a chunk and compressing it, the probe):
//! a crowd of downloads queues here, never in front of the switch on the runtime's workers.  Half the cores, at least
//! two.  A job is a closure that owns what it works on (the encoder's state moves with it from chunk to chunk), and
//! its answer comes back through a oneshot.  The threads run at a lower priority (a nice value 10 above the process's,
//! nfsu2_util::cpu::lower_this_thread): a burst of downloads takes what the switch leaves of the cores, never the
//! other way round (a burst of 40 downloads put the switch's ping 20 % lower at p50 with it, at the same throughput).

use std::future::Future;
use std::panic::{AssertUnwindSafe, catch_unwind};
use std::sync::{Arc, mpsc};

use parking_lot::Mutex;

type Job = Box<dyn FnOnce() + Send>;

pub struct CpuPool {
    tx: mpsc::Sender<Job>,
}

impl CpuPool {
    pub fn new(threads: usize, name: &str) -> CpuPool {
        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Job>();
        let rx = Arc::new(Mutex::new(rx));
        for i in 0..threads.max(1) {
            let rx = rx.clone();
            std::thread::Builder::new()
                .name(format!("{name}-{i}"))
                .spawn(move || {
                    nfsu2_util::cpu::lower_this_thread(10);
                    loop {
                        // one thread waits on the queue at a time; the others wait for it to take a job
                        let job = rx.lock().recv();
                        match job {
                            // a job that panics loses its answer (the caller sees None), not the thread
                            Ok(job) => {
                                let _ = catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(job));
                            }
                            Err(_) => break,
                        }
                    }
                })
                .expect("a compression thread");
        }
        CpuPool { tx }
    }

    /// f queued for one of the pool's threads now (not when the answer is first awaited: a run's next chunk
    /// compresses while this one goes out); the answer is None if f panicked
    pub fn submit<T: Send + 'static>(&self, f: impl FnOnce() -> T + Send + 'static) -> impl Future<Output = Option<T>> + Send + 'static {
        let (otx, orx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel();
        let job: Job = Box::new(move || {
            // nobody waits for the answer any more (its client went, with the next chunk of its run queued): the work
            // is skipped, and what it holds (the open file, the encoder's state) goes now
            if otx.is_closed() {
                return;
            }
            let _ = otx.send(f());
        });
        let queued = self.tx.send(job).is_ok();
        async move {
            if !queued {
                return None;
            }
            orx.await.ok()
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn runs_jobs_and_survives_a_panic() {
        let p = CpuPool::new(2, "test-pool");
        assert_eq!(p.submit(|| 6 * 7).await, Some(42));
        let bad: Option<u32> = p.submit(|| panic!("a broken job")).await;
        assert_eq!(bad, None);
        let all = futures_util::future::join_all((0..32).map(|i| p.submit(move || i * 2))).await;
        assert_eq!(all.into_iter().map(Option::unwrap).sum::<u32>(), (0..32u32).map(|i| i * 2).sum::<u32>());
    }

    // A run's next chunk is queued before this one goes out, so a client that goes (or resets right after its request)
    // leaves a job behind: it compressed a chunk for nobody, holding the file open and the encoder's state until then.
    #[tokio::test]
    async fn a_job_nobody_waits_for_is_not_run() {
        use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering};
        let p = CpuPool::new(1, "test-pool");
        // the one thread busy until the gate opens, and jobs queued behind it
        let (gate, wait) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<()>();
        let busy = p.submit(move || wait.recv().is_ok());
        let ran = Arc::new(AtomicUsize::new(0));
        let held = Arc::new(());
        let gone: Vec<_> = (0..10)
            .map(|_| {
                let (ran, held) = (ran.clone(), held.clone());
                p.submit(move || {
                    let _held = held;
                    ran.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
                })
            })
            .collect();
        drop(gone);
        let wanted = p.submit(|| 7);
        gate.send(()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(busy.await, Some(true));
        assert_eq!(wanted.await, Some(7));
        assert_eq!(ran.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 0, "jobs whose answers nobody waits for");
        assert_eq!(Arc::strong_count(&held), 1, "what they held is let go");
    }
}
